Study sessions in October and November covered one-time budget items, changes from proposed to adopted budget, and a third amendment and supplemental appropriation to the 2026 budget.

adams-county/2.title: Development Standards Overhaul
adams-county/2.summary: The county is comprehensively rewriting its Development Standards and Regulations, with zoning map amendments to match the new standards. The commissioners discussed it in a September study session, and the Planning Commission hearing was set for October 22.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Study Session

adams-county/3.title: Balanced Housing Plan and affordable housing support
adams-county/3.summary: The county is developing a Balanced Housing Plan as a Comprehensive Plan amendment. It was reviewed in study sessions and Planning Commission sessions in October and November. The commissioners also approved rebating building permit fees for affordable housing and assigned the county's 2026 private activity bond cap to Maiker Housing Partners.

adams-county/4.title: Strategic Growth Element and Water Master Plan
adams-county/4.summary: The county is updating its Comprehensive Plan with a 2026 Strategic Growth Element and compliance work. It is also adding a Water Master Plan and Statutory Water Supply Element. These went through study sessions and Planning Commission hearings from September to November.

adams-county/5.title: Zoning violation penalties and graduated fines
adams-county/5.summary: The commissioners adopted a penalty payment process and a graduated fine schedule for civil infraction violations of zoning and land use rules in September. They adopted an amended fine schedule on October 27.

adams-county/6.title: Battery storage, substation and solar facility proposals
adams-county/6.summary: The Planning Commission heard conditional use permit requests for a battery energy facility and utility substation at 12500 Cavanaugh Road. It also heard requests for a major energy facility, transmission line and large-scale solar facility at 6301 Manilla Road.

adams-county/7.title: Irondale Mobile Home Park acquisition
adams-county/7.summary: Staff briefed the commissioners on a potential county acquisition of the Irondale Mobile Home Park in study sessions on October 28 and November 4. The county also considered cancelling mobile home property taxes.

adams-county/8.title: Homelessness programs and funding
adams-county/8.summary: The commissioners approved a $95,000 agreement with Brothers Redevelopment for a neighborhood stability project. They also approved transformational homelessness response agreements with Village Exchange Center, including an amended version in October.

adams-county/9.title: Park Central subdivision and Midtown at Clear Creek improvements agreement
adams-county/9.summary: The Park Central major subdivision preliminary plat at 6030 Washington Street went to the Planning Commission and was approved by the commissioners on October 13. The First Amendment to the Midtown at Clear Creek Filing No. 13 Improvements Agreement was moved to new business, continued to October 27, then continued again to November 10.

adams-county/10.title: Old Shooting Range water testing
adams-county/10.summary: The commissioners approved a $29,981.85 amendment for Quantum Water & Environment to do water testing and other services at the county's Old Shooting Range.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Public Hearing

akron/0.title: Washington County Housing Authority housing project, water review and MOU
akron/0.summary: The Council reviewed a County Housing Authority request for a water review of a Title 13 subdivision, held special housing meetings in August and September, and discussed a proposed MOU with the Washington County Housing Authority (drafts dated 9/8 and 11/6). It was on the agenda again for negotiation on Nov. 2 and for possible action on the MOU on Nov. 9.

akron/1.title: Water system improvements and DWRF loan, DOLA grant application
akron/1.summary: A Drinking Water Revolving Fund public hearing covered the aging cast iron, PVC and asbestos cement distribution system and problems with arsenic, nitrate and uranium in well water. The estimated rate increase is $13 to $18 per month. Council also considered a new DOLA Energy Impact grant application of up to $1,000,000 recommended by GMS.

akron/2.title: Sanitary sewer collection system replacement and WPCRF loan
akron/2.summary: A public hearing described replacing failing sewer lines, including a severely corroded cast iron line under the railroad that would get a new crossing. A DOLA CDBG grant of about $700,000 is already awarded, with more from principal forgiveness and a CDPHE loan. The average monthly sewer bill would need to be about $55, a $13 increase.
akron/2.where: Townwide, sewer line under the railroad

akron/3.title: Town Manager settlement and DOLA-funded position succession plan
akron/3.summary: Council took up a possible settlement with the Town Manager in executive session on Aug. 18. In November, DOLA told the Council that Energy Impact grant no. 9540, which funds the town manager position, steps down from 75% to 50% to 25% and requires a plan to keep funding the job. Mayor Bowin said Council needs more time to review the contract and plan.

akron/4.title: Title 14 Planning and Zoning ordinance 614
akron/4.summary: Council took up Ordinance 614, adopting a new Title 14 Planning and Zoning, on first read Sept. 14 and second read Oct. 5.

akron/5.title: 2027 budget and employee compensation
akron/5.summary: Council reviewed the 2027 budget on Oct. 12 and discussed employee compensation on Nov. 2.

akron/6.title: Sheriff's contract and code enforcement for 2027
akron/6.summary: Council was to review and possibly act on the Sheriff's contract, with a final revised 2027 town contract for code enforcement, on Nov. 9.

akron/7.title: E-bike ordinance discussion
akron/7.summary: Council discussed a possible e-bike ordinance on Oct. 5.

akron/8.title: Scott hangar lease at the airport
akron/8.summary: Council considered Ordinance 613 approving a lease of a hangar to Scott, on second read Sept. 14.

alamosa-county/0.title: Jeremiah Webb major site plan revocation at 6153 US Hwy 160
alamosa-county/0.summary: The Board of County Commissioners had a hearing on revoking Jeremiah Webb's major site plan for 6153 US Hwy 160 on its Nov. 10 agenda. The item was previously tabled; the documents do not state an outcome.

alamosa-county/1.summary: The commissioners scheduled a public hearing on a special use permit requested by Elson Miller for property at 5741 County Rd 15 S. The agenda does not describe the proposed use or the outcome.

alamosa-county/2.summary: A preliminary 2027 budget was presented to the commissioners at their Nov. 10, 2026 meeting. The documents give no figures or decisions.

alamosa-county/3.title: Sustainable Environmental and Economic Development Park
alamosa-county/3.summary: The Sustainable Environmental And Economic Development Park appeared on the Nov. 10 commissioners' agenda under appointments. The documents do not say what was decided.

arapahoe-county/0.summary: Commissioners got a data center overview (57 in Colorado) on Sept. 22 ahead of a Sept. 25 tour, then on Oct. 19 voted 5-0 for option 3, having staff draft permitted and/or special-use rules. The Land Development Code does not currently define "data center"; noise, air quality and water use were discussed. Commissioners also asked about Xcel energy costs and want data center land-use language in the county's legislative priorities.

The Executive Budget Committee and the 1A Resident Advisory Committee reviewed it, including whether it matches the intent of the 2024 Ballot Measure 1A. It went to Planning Commission study session Sept. 15, a commissioners' study session Sept. 21, and a Planning Commission hearing Oct. 20. A Strategic Growth Element is also being drafted.

arapahoe-county/3.summary: The Planning Commission held a study session on proposed county rezonings, with maps for the Federal Enclave, Dry Creek, a 4-square-mile area and Belleview. Dry Creek survey results and public comments were included in the materials.

arapahoe-county/4.title: Cease-and-desist hearing over septic system at 23900 E. Ohio Ave.
arapahoe-county/4.summary: The Board of Health held a hearing on an onsite wastewater system cease-and-desist case. The homeowner did not attend, and the Board discussed ways to gain compliance while sticking to its duty to enforce. An update was scheduled for September.

arapahoe-county/5.title: Gun Club Road widening and transmission line relocation
arapahoe-county/5.summary: Commissioners reviewed and approved a CORE transmission line relocation agreement tied to the C19-007 Gun Club Road widening, west of South Gun Club Road between the E-470 ramps and East Belleview Avenue. Right-of-way would grow from about 89 to 141 feet, with the county paying design and construction costs. A public use easement also came up.

Staff are also bringing expedited review policies for affordable housing in November. A group living Land Development Code amendment was also on the Nov. 10 agenda.

arapahoe-county/12.title: Swimming pool regulation resolution
arapahoe-county/12.summary: Public Health asked the Board of Health to adopt the existing state code as the local standard for aquatic venues and to start a stakeholder process on possible local rules based on the CDC Model Aquatic Health Code. The resolution itself adopts no new fees or licensing.

arapahoe-county/13.title: Domestic violence and firearms in the home
arapahoe-county/13.summary: During public comment at the Oct. 27 business meeting, a speaker raised domestic violence and the dangers of firearms in the home.

archuleta-county/0.title: Comprehensive Plan Update
archuleta-county/0.summary: Consultant HRGreen presented the purpose, timeline and status of the county's Comprehensive Plan update to the Planning Commission. Commissioners asked about outreach (only one public meeting is scoped) and state deadlines for water supply and growth elements, and the plan can be adopted in pieces. A resident argued the plan should focus on growth and affordability.

archuleta-county/1.title: LPEA transmission line to Trujillo Substation
archuleta-county/1.summary: La Plata Electric Association applied for a Board Conditional Use Permit for about 2,700 feet of 115 kV double-circuit line (initially run at 69 kV) with seven poles up to 75 feet tall, to power the approved Trujillo Substation. The land is zoned Agricultural Ranching and the commissioners held a public hearing.

archuleta-county/2.title: Housing Action Plan
archuleta-county/2.summary: The multijurisdictional housing coordinator was scheduled to brief the board on the Housing Action Plan.

archuleta-county/3.title: Draft 2027 budget and related transfers
archuleta-county/3.summary: The Town reviewed the draft 2027 budget, while county commissioners scheduled a work session on a budget transfer to the Road & Bridge Fund and on the Tourism Board budget.

archuleta-county/4.title: 2026 flood discussion
archuleta-county/4.summary: A discussion of the 2026 flood was on the Town agenda, and the county sought a letter of support for a Master Disaster Declaration request to the President.

archuleta-county/5.title: Cloman Blvd administrative rezoning (PLN-REZ-26-050)
archuleta-county/5.summary: The Planning Commission heard the staff report on an administrative rezoning on Cloman Blvd. The documents do not state the outcome.

archuleta-county/6.title: Upper San Juan Watershed Enhancement Partnership briefing
archuleta-county/6.summary: The board was scheduled to hear a briefing on the Upper San Juan Watershed Enhancement Partnership.

archuleta-county/7.title: Forest Health Timber Products 3-Phase Extension Project letter
archuleta-county/7.summary: Commissioners were asked to ratify the Chair's October 29 letter to the State Historic Preservation Office about the Forest Health Timber Products 3-Phase Extension Project.

archuleta-county/8.title: County fair and rodeo event planning
archuleta-county/8.summary: The fair and rodeo board planned entertainment, sponsorships including LPEA and Ally House, a beer garden with Rotary, and contractor RFPs, against a special services budget of about $58.5k.

arriba/0.title: Wastewater permit compliance and facility problems
arriba/0.summary: Arriba is studying its wastewater facility under new state permit rules, with GMS Inc. preparing an engineering report that found an infiltration problem. The facility has had repeated BOD and ammonia violations and flooding. In July the board approved paying $19,250 in GMS invoices, half from a DOLA grant. In September GMS said the state let the town revert to its old permit compliance; the permit expires in 2027.
arriba/0.where: Town wastewater ponds and sewer lines

arriba/1.title: Water and RV park sewer rates
arriba/1.summary: Resident Beverly Langley repeatedly asked that Big Ben's RV park and RV hookups pay more for water and sewer. The board raised the monthly RV sewer rate by $2 from $5 in January. In July it raised the base water rate by $5.50 to $55 effective Aug 1, 2026 to stay in compliance with the drinking water loan covenant.

arriba/2.title: Mandatory trash service ordinance and Rob's Trash contract
arriba/2.summary: The board adopted an ordinance requiring every occupied residential household to have trash service and approved a contract with Rob's Trash Service, renegotiable at end of 2026. Residents may use their own approved 3-yard dumpster for $45. Surveys of customers are planned for review in December.

arriba/3.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption (Ordinance 159)
arriba/3.summary: The board delayed adopting the state wildfire code for months over concerns about enforcement by the town clerk. After discussing insurance impacts and that Flagler had adopted it, the board adopted Ordinance 159 in July 2026.

arriba/4.title: 2026 budget, mill levy cut and sales tax ballot question
arriba/4.summary: The board adopted the 2026 budget and a 2025 supplemental sewer budget raising expenditures from $116,940 to $229,440. It certified a mill levy cut from 25.948 to 14.509 and put a sales tax question on the 2026 ballot to keep revenue above estimates ($30,000 vs. $14,000 estimated). A mail ballot election was also set.

arriba/5.title: 2027 budget and water meter replacement
arriba/5.summary: The board reviewed the proposed 2027 budget, including cost-of-living raises and higher insurance. It discussed replacing old water meters and charging new customers a non-refundable meter fee. A budget hearing is set for Dec. 1, 2026 at 6 p.m.

arriba/6.title: Speeding and speed bumps on College and Lincoln Avenues
arriba/6.summary: The board discussed truck route and speeding problems on College Ave and Lincoln Ave. In October it voted to buy 3 sets of speed bumps and 2 speed limit signs. A missing stop sign at Grant and Lincoln was also raised.

arriba/7.title: Pine Street drainage flooding
arriba/7.summary: Resident Beverly Langley reported stormwater running off Pine Street and flooding her house. The board agreed to let the maintenance worker dig a ditch on the west side of Pine Street and uncover the sidewalk.

arriba/8.title: July 4 Time Capsule event and park improvements
arriba/8.summary: The town held a Time Capsule event on July 4, 2026 with a beer garden on the park basketball court, funded partly by a $7,500 grant and a $2,500 tourism grant. Afterward the town planned a park sprinkler system using a $2,500 donation from Big Ben's RV Park and Conservation Trust funds.

arriba/9.title: RV and manufactured home permits
arriba/9.summary: The board approved a manufactured home permit at 521 Lincoln Ave for Brian and Sheri Mohr. An RV permit for Troy McCue at 214 Main Street was approved in September; no tap fee applies, only the permit fee and backhoe use.

arriba/10.title: Hooved animals ordinance (Ordinance 113)
arriba/10.summary: A request to allow hooved animals in town or on lots over 5 acres was discussed. The board decided to make no changes to the ban.

arvada/0.title: Data center moratorium (CB26-029)
arvada/0.summary: On Sept 15, 2026 Council took up first reading of an ordinance authorizing a moratorium on submitting and accepting applications for primary-use data centers, with a public hearing set for October 6, 2026 at 6:15 p.m.

arvada/1.title: Water Treatment Plant annexation and rezoning at 6809 SH 93
arvada/1.summary: The city is annexing two parcels (17.885 and 9.016 acres, 25.257 total) at 6809 SH 93 for its water treatment plant and rezoning them from Jefferson County PUD to city Open Space. The Planning Commission heard it Aug 19, and Council set hearings for Oct 6; written comments were received.

arvada/2.title: 2027-2028 budget, mill levy and pay plan
arvada/2.summary: The City Manager's proposed two-year budget totals $412,447,446 in 2027 appropriations, with 32 new positions requested and a new pay plan. Council scheduled adoption of the 2027 budget, capital fund, pay plan and 2026 mill levy for Oct 20.

arvada/3.title: 2027 water, wastewater and stormwater rates and drought surcharge
arvada/3.summary: Staff pulled the drought water surcharge ordinance (CB26-018) and plan to revisit surcharges in Spring 2027 in line with a possible drought declaration extension. Ordinances setting 2027 water, wastewater and stormwater rates were set for hearing Oct 20.

arvada/4.title: Hibernia Gold Strike Apartments, 240 units at 4800 W 60th Ave
arvada/4.summary: A conditional use permit is proposed for a five-story, 240-unit apartment building with a small coffee shop on 3.47 acres in the MX-T zone. About 20 residents attended a neighborhood meeting, the Planning Commission reviewed it Sept 16, and Council first reading was Oct 20 with a hearing set Nov 17.

arvada/5.title: Proposition 123 commitments and housing zoning changes
arvada/5.summary: Planning Commission heard zoning text amendments related to Proposition 123, and Council considered a resolution committing to Prop 123 obligations for the 2027-2029 cycle plus a residential land use table rewrite. The Housing Advisory Committee is also working on the housing strategic plan.

arvada/6.title: Paid parking in Olde Town
arvada/6.summary: Council held a study session on managing parking demand in Olde Town, reviewing studies from 2010, 2016 and 2025 and the Reinvestment Plan's proposal for paid metered parking. Council had earlier asked for more data and input from local businesses.

arvada/7.title: Wildfire early detection system
arvada/7.summary: The city agreed to accept up to $300,000 from the Arvada Urban Renewal Authority for cameras and chemical sensors to detect wildfires in the Urban Renewal Area. Data ownership concerns were raised in public comment, and staff gave an update Oct 27.

arvada/8.title: Homelessness response and Navigation Center funding
arvada/8.summary: Council recognized faith leaders in the homeless response, considered an agreement on operating funding for the Navigation Center, and scheduled a Homelessness Action Plan discussion for Oct 27.

arvada/9.title: Residency restrictions for registered sex offenders
arvada/9.summary: At a Sept 8 workshop Legal asked Council for direction on a possible ordinance restricting where registered sex offenders may live, noting Arvada has none now. Legal recommended a distance of no further than 1,000 feet and advised against retroactive application and applying it to juveniles.

arvada/10.title: Comprehensive Plan update
arvada/10.summary: Consultant Metta Urban Design is leading the update, with adoption targeted for Q3 2027. Phase 2 trends show home prices outpacing incomes, $732M in unfunded transportation projects, and a rising share of multifamily building.

arvada/11.title: Commercial drone delivery regulations
arvada/11.summary: Staff briefed Council on what the city can regulate regarding retail drone delivery and proposed conditional use rules for certain zones. Thornton is considering rules, and Castle Rock and Parker have imposed moratoriums.

arvada/12.title: City Attorney turnover and leadership agreements
arvada/12.summary: Council considered amended employment agreements for the City Attorney, Presiding Municipal Judge and City Manager, then an agreement for Nora Steenson as Interim City Attorney. A personnel executive session on the interim position was also scheduled.

arvada/13.title: Scenic Heights West Metropolitan District service plan
arvada/13.summary: Council held a public hearing on Sept 1 on a resolution approving the proposed service plan for the Scenic Heights West Metropolitan District.

aspen/0.title: Fee deferral program for qualified locals (Ordinance #11)
aspen/0.summary: Planning & Zoning reviewed a Title 2 fee deferral program for qualified locals in August and September 2026. Council took up Ordinance #11 for a continued public hearing and second reading on Oct 27.

aspen/1.title: Affordable housing fee-in-lieu 5-year update (Ordinance #18)
aspen/1.summary: The city reviewed two phases of a study on its affordable housing fee-in-lieu. It went from a council work session on Sept 14 to P&Z on Oct 7 and to first reading of Ordinance #18 on Oct 27.

aspen/2.title: CO 82 Entrance to Aspen reevaluation
aspen/2.summary: Council and the Historic Preservation Commission reviewed the refined preferred alternative for the Entrance to Aspen, including historic mitigation. Council asked for an amended information update in August.

aspen/3.title: Drought, Stage Three water restrictions and water supply
aspen/3.summary: Staff reported on a regional drought response using Ruedi Reservoir water, continued Stage Three water restrictions, and water use at special events. Council also discussed buying Twin Lakes water right shares and heard from the Ruedi Water and Power Authority. A resident noted low flows and nearby wildfires.

aspen/4.title: 2027 city budget, fees and fall supplemental
aspen/4.summary: Council held four budget work sessions in October covering capital spending, supplemental requests, fees and wrap-up. First readings followed on Nov 10 for the fall supplemental, the 2027 fee ordinance and community development fee changes.

aspen/5.title: Water treatment plant improvements and bond question
aspen/5.summary: Council considered an early work package amendment and a Holy Cross Electric contract for the Water Treatment Facility Improvements Project. It also considered Resolution #115, in support of the water treatment plant bond ballot question.

aspen/6.title: Conner Park stage and amplified sound
aspen/6.summary: A speaker at the Aug 25 meeting said a church near the Armory Hall redevelopment is concerned that amplified sound from a Conner Park stage would hurt the space. Council scheduled a Conner Park stage discussion for a Sept 22 work session.

aspen/7.title: E-bike and e-moto rules
aspen/7.summary: A resident asked council to align valley-wide e-bike and e-moto rules, with licensing and a minimum age of 16. The mayor said other towns face the same issues and that locals no longer feel comfortable walking on the Rio Grande Trail.

aspen/8.title: 121-123 East Hyman Avenue special review
aspen/8.summary: P&Z held repeated hearings on a special review for 121-123 East Hyman Avenue, including a reduced and amended application. Public comment about the Good Thunder Condos was submitted in October.

aspen/9.title: Marolt housing redevelopment and Armory Hall project
aspen/9.summary: Council reviewed redevelopment concepts for Marolt housing with AMFS. It also received an interior update on the Armory project, and a change order for the Armory Hall builder's risk insurance came up in September.

aspen/10.title: Wildfire fuel mitigation funding
aspen/10.summary: Council and county commissioners received a fuel mitigation update. On Nov 10 council considered funds to the Aspen Fire Protection District for fuels treatment.

aspen/11.title: Short-term rental program guideline changes
aspen/11.summary: Staff reported forthcoming amendments to the short-term rental program guidelines, referencing earlier council resolution and ordinance.

aspen/12.title: Golf clubhouse area master plan
aspen/12.summary: Council reviewed a clubhouse and campus master plan concept in September, with a follow-up report on Sept 28.

aspen/13.title: 420 West Francis Street transferable development rights
aspen/13.summary: HPC recommended creating three transferable development rights certificates for 420 West Francis Street. Council took up Ordinance #20 on first reading on Oct 27.

aurora/0.title: Data center moratorium and zoning standards
aurora/0.summary: Council took up a resolution (R2026-111) on a moratorium on accepting or processing development applications that include a data center as a primary use, with a waiver of reconsideration requested as time-sensitive. Council also held a Data Center Standards discussion and a public hearing on an ordinance (2026-51) amending the Unified Development Ordinance use table for data centers, which returned for final approval on the Oct. 26 consent calendar.

aurora/1.title: 2027 budget, tax levy, fees and rates
aurora/1.summary: Council held a day of budget deliberations on Oct. 3 covering city departments, the capital fund, proposed 2027 service fees, pay tables and general improvement district budgets. It then took up 2027 proposed rates and fees, a new self-funded health plan fund, and on Nov. 9 introduced the 2027 tax levy ordinance, which includes a temporary property tax credit, and the 2027 appropriations ordinance.

aurora/2.title: Nine Mile Station and Plaza urban renewal redevelopment agreements
aurora/2.summary: The Aurora Urban Renewal Authority considered amendments to the Point Crossing at Nine Mile Station agreement, a new agreement for Tempo at Nine Mile Station Apartments, and a restated Plaza 1 finance agreement, all within urban renewal areas. An intergovernmental agreement tied to the authority and a Nine Mile IGA with police also came up.
aurora/2.where: Nine Mile Station, Plaza 1 and Plaza 3 urban renewal areas

aurora/3.title: Homeless services funding awards
aurora/3.summary: Council reviewed a series of Homeless Services Notice of Funding Opportunity applications and recommendations, including Emergency Solutions Grants for Advance Pathways and the Aurora Housing Authority, HOME tenant-based rental assistance, and marijuana funds. They moved from the Oct. 12 agenda to the Oct. 26 consent calendar.

aurora/4.title: Mercy Housing affordable housing ground lease
aurora/4.summary: Council's consent calendar included a resolution (R2026-107) approving a ground lease with Mercy Housing Mountain Plains for an affordable housing project. An outside speaker was listed on the item.

aurora/5.title: Water rules: turf, ornamental features and water agreements
aurora/5.summary: Council finalized ordinances on new turf and ornamental water features and a related ordinance prohibiting certain permits. Aurora Water also brought a Lake County water deliveries and storage agreement, a South Adams water rights trade, and several flood and storm drainage agreements (Westerly Creek, Piney Lake Trails, Coal Creek at Picadilly Road).

aurora/6.title: Industrial zone district changes to the Unified Development Ordinance
aurora/6.summary: Council considered an ordinance amending the Unified Development Ordinance for industrial zone districts, presented by Planning staff.

aurora/7.title: Comprehensive Safety Action Plan and 38th Avenue interchange agreement
aurora/7.summary: Council approved a resolution adopting the Comprehensive Safety Action Plan, along with an amendment to the 38th Avenue Interchange maintenance and operation IGA.

aurora/8.title: Green Valley Ranch East metro district service plan amendments
aurora/8.summary: Council considered service plan amendments for Green Valley Ranch East Metropolitan Districts Nos. 6 through 14. It also handled 2027 operating plans and budgets for several business improvement districts, including Citadel on Colfax, Fitzsimons, Havana and Painted Prairie.

aurora/9.title: Oil and gas lease consideration
aurora/9.summary: Council had an item on its agenda to consider an oil and gas lease.

aurora/10.title: Bethel Lutheran Church historic designation
aurora/10.summary: A public hearing was scheduled on an ordinance (2026-52) to designate the Bethel Lutheran Church as a historic landmark.

avon/0.title: Flock license plate reader cameras
avon/0.summary: Residents repeatedly urged Council to end the Town's Flock Safety license plate reader contract, citing privacy concerns and petitions of 1,544 to 1,900 signatures. The Town Manager said the agreement had not been renewed and was under review, a discussion was set for October 6, and by October 27 Council voted to retain the cameras while asking Public Works to remove them if Flock's removal was delayed.

avon/1.title: 2027 budget review
avon/1.summary: Council held a work session on the 2027 budget for all funds, with a balanced General Fund and about $64.1 million in projected revenues. Topics included reserves, capital projects, recreation fees, staffing, wildfire mitigation, composting and housing, and Council gave direction to staff.

avon/2.title: Avon Whitewater Park and Bob the Bridge improvements
avon/2.summary: Residents asked Council to consider improvements near Bob the Bridge and the Avon Whitewater Park, including a standing river wave feature, better river access in low water, and a skate park that was approved but not funded.
avon/2.where: Avon Whitewater Park / Bob the Bridge

avon/3.title: Pedestrian crosswalk safety on Avon Road and Post Boulevard
avon/3.summary: A resident asked for flashing pedestrian beacons at the Avon Road crosswalks near Highway 6 after a near miss. Council also approved a CDOT Highway Safety Improvement Program grant agreement for Post Boulevard pedestrian improvements.
avon/3.where: Avon Road at Highway 6; Post Boulevard

avon/4.title: Piedmont Apartments trash and wildlife concerns
avon/4.summary: Residents raised trash, management and code enforcement problems at the Piedmont Apartments. Police reported receiving 27 calls about trash-related wildlife issues.

avon/5.title: Eagle County School District Ballot Issue 5B support resolution
avon/5.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-15 supporting a school district mill levy override for additional funding. Speakers opposed the tax increase while supporting higher teacher pay, and Council voted on the resolution.

avon/6.title: Community housing: Avondale Apartments and fast-track scheduling
avon/6.summary: Council approved a Construction Manager/General Contractor agreement for the Avondale Apartments and adopted Resolution 26-18, a fast-track priority scheduling policy for community housing projects.

avon/7.title: Lot B (The Summit) redevelopment and tree removal
avon/7.summary: A resident asked whether trees on Lot B could be affected by future development. Staff noted that trees may be removed as part of redevelopment and site excavation.

avon/8.title: Comprehensive Plan amendments for Senate Bill 24-174
avon/8.summary: Council approved on consent amendments to the Comprehensive Plan to comply with Colorado Senate Bill 24-174.

basalt/0.title: Public Works/Police facility and 0.5% sales tax ballot measure (Ballot Issue 3A)
basalt/0.summary: The Town plans a shared Public Works and Police facility at the end of East Valley Road, estimated at about $25 million. It is asking voters in November for a 0.5% sales tax with a 20-year sunset, and Council adopted a resolution supporting Ballot Issue 3A. Staff say the police department is spread across inadequate space, and have applied for a USDA loan and are considering selling some Town properties.
basalt/0.where: End of East Valley Road, adjacent to Highway 82

basalt/1.title: 218 E. Valley Road (Movieland) Residence Inn hotel proposal
basalt/1.summary: A revised proposal for a 93-key Residence Inn by Marriott with three deed-restricted rental affordable units on the former Movieland site, which requires PUD and annexation agreement amendments. Planning and Zoning held repeated hearings, and staff added conditions limiting use to the approved hotel. Council scheduled a site visit.

basalt/2.title: 555 Basalt Avenue mixed-use development and Master Plan amendment
basalt/2.summary: Council has repeatedly continued the hearing on Ordinance 18, which would grant special review and a PUD amendment for a mixed-use development at 555 Basalt Avenue, along with Resolution 34 amending the Master Plan's future land use map. The items were continued to October 27 and again appeared on the November 10 agenda.

basalt/3.title: Affordable housing financing: six condo units, Parcel 9 (Pitchview) and BACH decisions
basalt/3.summary: The Town is buying six housing units at Basalt Center Circle for $2.38 million and is moving a Certificates of Participation financing ordinance, with second reading set for August 25. Finance staff are also working through the pro forma for the Sopris Parcel 9 (Pitchview) project. BACH ruled on tenant requalification at Block 9 in Willits Town Center, letting the current tenant stay, and discussed leasing of Town-owned units.
basalt/3.where: Basalt Center Circle; Parcel 9, Sopris Meadows; 300 Robinson Street, Willits Town Center

basalt/4.title: Short-term rental rules and fees
basalt/4.summary: A resident asked Council to exempt on-site hosted primary residents who rent a spare room from the commercial fees and 60-day cap under Ordinance 3 of 2025. Council scheduled a work session on STR regulatory fees for October 22.

basalt/5.title: Tobacco tax ballot request
basalt/5.summary: Speakers urged Council to refer a tobacco tax increase to the ballot, noting Basalt's $2 per pack cigarette tax is below the $4 rate in Pitkin County, Eagle County and neighboring towns.

basalt/6.title: 2027 budget and sales tax trends
basalt/6.summary: Staff reported sales tax through May at $4.22 million, up 2.43% year over year, with cash generation in the first half of 2026 well below last year. A Two Rivers Road CDOT grant was deferred to 2027. Council held budget work sessions and heard the proposed 2027 budget on September 22.

basalt/7.title: Zoning, annexation and subdivision code rewrite
basalt/7.summary: Planning and Zoning is reviewing a consultant-led rewrite of Chapters 15, 16 and 17 to reorganize and simplify the code and make some substantive changes. The hearing was continued to October 20 with a recommendation to Council expected.

basalt/8.title: Midland Avenue streetlights and Southside traffic concerns
basalt/8.summary: Residents complained of inadequate lighting from new catenary streetlights on Midland Avenue, and the Town Manager said the lights are at maximum output while staff work with the contractor. Residents also raised the single egress for the Southside area and requested a stop sign at Alexander and Fiou Lane.
basalt/8.where: Midland Avenue; Southside; Alexander and Fiou Lane

basalt/9.title: Willits Lane roundabout and crossing to Crown Mountain Park
basalt/9.summary: A resident asked for a roundabout on Willits Lane so people can safely reach Crown Mountain Park, and asked the Town to define easement responsibilities with developers.

basalt/10.title: Lawn equipment and leaf blower restrictions
basalt/10.summary: After the 2025 ban on combustion leaf blowers on Town property, staff asked the Green Team for options to extend restrictions beyond Town-owned land, including possible effective dates.

basalt/11.title: 72 Sunset Drive event space
basalt/11.summary: Planning and Zoning will consider a minor PUD amendment to the Mid-Valley Business Center to allow an event space of about 1,000 square feet.

berthoud/0.title: Data center moratorium and land use rules
berthoud/0.summary: After trustees asked in August for a possible moratorium, the Board took up Emergency Ordinance 1391 on Sept. 22 to temporarily suspend applications for large data centers. Discussion focused on what size counts as large. Staff then held a Sept. 29 work session on land use concerns, which could lead to a Technical Memo and code amendments, with possible noise-consultant funding in 2027. A summary and next steps were set for Oct. 27.

berthoud/1.title: Legacy Park development agreement and final plat
berthoud/1.summary: The Board held a public hearing on Sept. 8 on revised vesting and improvement-guarantee language in the Legacy Park Development Agreement. Planning Commission considered the Final Plat on Sept. 10 and a motion to approve was made. HPAC was told the silos on the site will come down because of asbestos.

berthoud/2.title: Heron Lakes Marina neighborhood master plan
berthoud/2.summary: Planning Commission heard the Heron Lakes Marina Neighborhood Master Plan on Sept. 10 and sent a recommendation to the Board. The Board continued a public hearing on Resolution 2026-25 approving it on Oct. 27.

berthoud/3.title: Rewrite of Chapter 30 land use code
berthoud/3.summary: Staff proposed repealing and replacing Chapter 30 of the municipal code, covering impact fees, annexation, zoning, overlay districts, short-term rentals, oil and gas and more. It went to a Board work session Oct. 20, Planning Commission Oct. 22, and Board hearings Nov. 10 on Ordinances 1394 and 1395.

berthoud/4.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code and wildland-urban interface
berthoud/4.summary: The Board adopted Ordinance 1389 on Oct. 13, adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code and defining the wildland-urban interface boundary after the hearing was continued from September. A cooperative agreement with the Berthoud Fire Protection District covers code administration.

berthoud/5.title: 2027 budget and ballot measure
berthoud/5.summary: The Board approved Ordinance 1390 ballot language for the Nov. 3 election, with concern that it clearly say taxes would not increase. A preliminary 2027 draft budget was introduced Oct. 13 and presented Nov. 10, along with a Capital Improvement Program policy.

berthoud/6.title: Welch Avenue roadway and drainage design
berthoud/6.summary: The Board authorized issuing a request for proposals for design of roadway and drainage improvements on Welch Avenue after trustees asked questions. Separately, the 9th Street crossing improvements were presented.

berthoud/7.title: Affordable housing and Ordinance 1355
berthoud/7.summary: Planning Commission held a work session Oct. 8 with the regional housing director, and the Board scheduled discussion of Ordinance 1355 and possible expansion of affordable housing.

berthoud/8.title: Parks, open space and trails projects
berthoud/8.summary: The Board approved bid items for Jaskowski Open Space, bike park improvements and Mountain Vista Park revisions. Eagle Vista/Front Range Trail grant support, the Little Thompson River Trail plan and Parks Master Plan were also on agendas.
berthoud/8.where: Jaskowski Open Space; Mountain Vista Park; Eagle Vista

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Recreation, and Trails Committee

berthoud/9.title: Boards and commissions ordinance
berthoud/9.summary: Ordinance 1388 sets appointment rules, terms and duties for town boards and commissions. Advisory groups discussed it and Planning Commission considered it Oct. 22.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Recreation, and Trails Committee

berthoud/10.title: Historic preservation grants and AI opposition
berthoud/10.summary: HPAC reported funding for an elevated water tank interpretive sign and work on a survey grant. At the Sept. 22 meeting, residents asked the Board to support historic preservation and others spoke against artificial intelligence.

black-hawk/0.title: Education Enhancement Tax and the proposed Gilpin County sales tax
black-hawk/0.summary: Black Hawk's 1.5% Education Enhancement Tax for the Gilpin school has raised about $16.9 million since 2009 and ends automatically if a countywide sales tax is adopted. Council discussed the County Commissioners' possible November 2026 sales tax and passed Resolution 17-2026 on March 25 reaffirming that the tax would terminate.

black-hawk/1.title: Water supply: Four Mile Gulch Well #6 and Army Corps reservoir permit
black-hawk/1.summary: The city is pursuing an Army Corps of Engineers permit for a reservoir and approved a reimbursement agreement (CB12) covering review costs. Residents of unincorporated Aspen Springs and Chalet Park spoke on Sept. 9 against drilling Well #6 near Dory Hill Road, saying it could harm neighbors' water, and asked the council to pause additional wells.
black-hawk/1.where: Four Mile Gulch / Dory Hill Road

black-hawk/2.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption and fire restrictions
black-hawk/2.summary: Council adopted the 2025 Wildfire Resiliency Code into the municipal code on March 25 by a 5-1 vote. In July the city manager issued an administrative order imposing fire restrictions. The city also contracted Good People Tree Service for fire mitigation work.

black-hawk/3.title: City-owned land purchases and sales, including Resolution 48-2026
black-hawk/3.summary: Council approved a contract to buy land on Gregory Hill in June and accepted a property conveyance in July. A vacant land sale agreement (Resolution 48-2026) was repeatedly continued from August into September, with discussion of Central City's roadway permitting and traffic study.

black-hawk/4.title: Leadership turnover: new City Manager and Police Chief
black-hawk/4.summary: Police Chief Moriarty announced her retirement after 31 years, and the council met in executive session on City Manager matters. Lance Hillis's employment agreement as City Manager took effect May 2 (Resolution 22-2026), and Ely Reyes was introduced as the new Police Chief in July.

black-hawk/5.title: Capital projects: Bobtail Mine, Highway 119 culverts, Red Dolly electrical, Ballard House
black-hawk/5.summary: Council approved a $949,307 change order for Bobtail Mine Improvements Phase 2 and a $160,400 Bobtail wall excavation contract. It also approved relining two storm culverts under Highway 119 after a failure at Gregory Street, the Red Dolly Casino electrical relocation, storage sheds, and Ballard House renovation with a barn shed addition (Roche Constructors). Also streamlined the capital project approval process (CB10).

black-hawk/6.title: Historic preservation and Lace House designation
black-hawk/6.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission is working on the Lace House designation, a phased reconnaissance survey and an intensive survey property list. Council accepted the reconnaissance survey and the Five-Year HPC Work Plan in August to meet Certified Local Government requirements.

black-hawk/7.title: Rick Thomas Distillery trademark license and water fee waiver
black-hawk/7.summary: Council approved a trademark license agreement with Rick Thomas Distillery and extended a waiver of water fees for another year for its site on Lot 7 of the Black Hawk Park Subdivision.

black-hawk/8.title: Fee schedule update and 2025 audit
black-hawk/8.summary: Council accepted the 2025 audit and amended the fee schedule, aligning commercial electrical fees with state fees and moving SAFEbuilt's hourly rate to consultant fees, plus City Clerk fee changes.

black-hawk/9.title: Sanitation district agreement and ballot measure positions
black-hawk/9.summary: Council approved an amended and restated service agreement with the Black Hawk/Central City Sanitation District. The mayor also spoke against a County Commissioners property-tax measure (Initiative 1A) and proposed a resolution supporting Initiative 177 on natural gas purchases.

blue-river/0.title: Short-term rental moratorium, caps and new STR rules
blue-river/0.summary: The Board has spent several meetings working toward a new short-term rental ordinance, with a six-zone framework, caps by zone, license allocation, enforcement and possible nightly limits, aimed at taking effect in 2027. Residents urged stronger enforcement against unlicensed operators and repeat violators, and raised water and wastewater concerns.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/1.title: Exceptions to the STR moratorium for new and renewing license applicants
blue-river/1.summary: Ordinances 2026-10, 2026-11, 2026-12 and a draft 2026-13 would let owners who bought property intending to rent, or who nearly completed a license application or renewal, apply despite the moratorium. The 2026-10 exception has a November 1, 2026 application deadline, and the draft 2026-13 offers options for who qualifies for a renewal exception. Affected owners spoke, including one asking for reinstatement of an expired license.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/2.title: Transition Zone District lot size and setback amendments and Development Code
blue-river/2.summary: Ordinance 2026-06 sets minimum lot size, lot width and setbacks in the Transition Zone District, and Ordinance 2026-07 would put a Development Code into effect October 1, 2026 on condition that 2026-06 is in force. A resident commented on setbacks at the hearing, and the Board discussed wetlands and topography constraints.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/3.title: 2027 budget and property tax levy
blue-river/3.summary: The Board was scheduled to see and discuss the proposed 2027 budget on October 20. Financial reports show a mill levy of 10.459 after a temporary credit of 1.831.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/4.title: Planning Commission review of residence at 1253 Indiana Creek Road
blue-river/4.summary: The Commission gave guidance on a proposed home, covering the 35-foot height limit, recessed garage entrances, two separate living areas and possible future conversion, and garage area limits. It asked for revised exhibits and discussed possible restrictive covenants.

blue-river/5.title: Goose Pasture Tarn boat dock rules repealed
blue-river/5.summary: The Board considered Resolution 2026-10, repealing Resolution 13-05, which set rules and permits for private boat docks at Goose Pasture Tarn.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/6.title: Sewer, septic and traffic concerns raised by residents
blue-river/6.summary: Residents raised aging septic systems along Blue River Road and asked the Town to explore grants and financing for future sewer. Others raised speeding on Indiana Creek Road and asked for traffic calming.
blue-river/6.where: Blue River Road and Indiana Creek Road

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/7.title: Summit School District mill levy override presentation
blue-river/7.summary: District representatives presented Ballot Measure 4A, a local mill levy override raising up to $5.9 million a year, mostly for staff pay and retention, and the statewide Proposition NN.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/8.title: Detached garage and variance at 0809 Blue River Rd
blue-river/8.summary: The Planning Commission agenda includes a detached garage and variance application, plus a final draft of land use code shed provisions.

boone/0.title: New water treatment facility: startup, warranty and draws
boone/0.summary: The town's new water treatment plant moved from operator training in March and startup in May to warranty fixes and payment draws. By August there was a leak in the GreenSands room and a problem with chlorine pumps needing further investigation, and council asked for an itemized breakdown of the final draw under the 2-year warranty.

boone/1.title: Water/sewer billing procedure and tap fee ordinances
boone/1.summary: Council spent most of the year drafting ordinances on water bill dates, late, reconnect and disconnect fees, and water and sewer tap fees. The tap fee ordinance was signed and posted in July. The billing ordinance was held up over landlord/tenant wording in Section 9, then approved and signed on Oct. 14 with 30 days of posting before it takes effect.

boone/2.title: Fire protection: IGA with Edison Fire Protection District
boone/2.summary: Council reviewed an intergovernmental agreement, contract and lease with the Edison fire district. The IGA was accepted in April and a resolution adopting the Edison FPD IGA and contracts passed on May 7.

boone/3.title: Building code enforcement and Southern Colorado Building Department ordinances
boone/3.summary: The town has been revising its ordinances tied to the Southern Colorado Building Department (SCBD, formerly using Pueblo regional codes) for code enforcement. The department's attorney worked on revisions, and the ordinances were finalized and posted Oct. 14, though one was missed. An amended IGA was tabled to Nov. 18 so SCBD can add Rockvail.

boone/4.title: Refuse rate increase and utility billing changes
boone/4.summary: Council approved a refuse rate increase, a 3% trash fee increase under the contract, and signed the resolution in August. It also worked on a new utility billing system with credit card and ACH payments, and discussed switching internet from CenturyLink to Starlink at $280 a month.

boone/5.title: Water quality notice and lead line survey
boone/5.summary: The state health department lifted a bottled water advisory and the town sent letters to all residents. Some residents still questioned the safe water notice, and the operator advised checking test results online. Council also discussed the drinking water quality report and lead line survey notices.

boone/6.title: Town park playground and mower
boone/6.summary: Eight sprinkler heads were replaced after mowing damage and council approved buying a new mower. Council discussed that the playground needs new equipment, and the Edison fire chief suggested USDA or GOCO grants.

boone/7.title: Town administrator appointment and town governance
boone/7.summary: Council appointed a town administrator in August and completed related paperwork in September. It also approved a records retention policy, cancelled the spring election, swore in new council members, scheduled an employee handbook workshop, and took up the 2024 audit.

boone/8.title: Dispute with Secom contract and DOLA complaint
boone/8.summary: Council noted a complaint to the state Division of Local Government (DOLA) about the Secom contract in March. The documents give no further details.

boone/9.title: Dumping on roads and road work
boone/9.summary: A resident raised dumping on town roads and water bills. Pea gravel and road base were ordered in September to begin road work.

boulder-county/0.title: Proposed data center and detention center land use rules
boulder-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled to take up Land Use Code amendments that would define data centers as a specific use and set where and at what scale they may be permitted in unincorporated Boulder County (Docket DC-26-0003). A companion amendment (DC-26-0004) does the same for detention centers, with a recommendation going to the commissioners.

boulder-county/1.title: 2027 Boulder County budget
boulder-county/1.summary: The commissioners held town halls, department budget presentations (Oct. 13, 15 and 22), a public hearing on the 2027 recommended budget on Oct. 22 and a Nov. 5 work session. Adoption is scheduled for Dec. 8. Allenspark resident Edward Yagi spoke at the hearing.

boulder-county/2.title: County joins amicus brief backing Cook County assault weapons ban
boulder-county/2.summary: Commissioners were asked to ratify Boulder County's participation in an amicus brief in Viramontes v. Cook County at the U.S. Supreme Court. The brief supports Cook County, Illinois's ban on certain semiautomatic firearms, including AR-15-style rifles.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/3.title: Ballot measure to expand the Board of Commissioners from 3 to 5
boulder-county/3.summary: The commissioners fixed the ballot title for a citizen initiative petition to increase the Board of County Commissioners from 3 to 5 members. The question goes on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot after the Clerk confirmed the petition was sufficient. The board also considered taking positions on other 2026 ballot measures.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/4.title: Eldorado Springs wastewater plant debt ballot question
boulder-county/4.summary: The Eldorado Springs Public Improvement District board referred a question to the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot asking voters to approve a multiple-year obligation to pay for wastewater treatment plant improvements required by the state health department.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/5.title: Riverside Cabins Lodge permit revocation hearing
boulder-county/5.summary: The commissioners held a hearing on revoking the Riverside Cabins Lodge special review approval (SU-23-0013) for violating conditions of approval. They declined to revoke now and continued the hearing to Jan. 7, 2027. If the owners meet all conditions before then, they can use the permit.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/6.title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan major update
boulder-county/6.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing and conditionally approved the BVCP major update, including Rural Lands text amendments. The commissioners then adopted a resolution approving it in October.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/7.title: Longmont 1st & Main urban renewal tax increment agreement
boulder-county/7.summary: Boulder County agreed to share tax increment financing with the Longmont Urban Renewal Authority for redevelopment of the 1st & Main corridor. The project includes a regional transit center, environmental cleanup and public infrastructure.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/8.title: Housing Authority plans, Willoughby Corner and housing funding
boulder-county/8.summary: The commissioners approved the Housing Authority's 2027 Annual Plan and Moving to Work supplement after a public hearing. They also awarded $1,084,000 in affordable housing grant funds for Willoughby Corner Phases II and III at 928 Canterbury Drive in Lafayette, and approved a $956,189 Continuum of Care rapid re-housing renewal.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/9.title: Energy Impact Offset Fund sunset and marijuana rules
boulder-county/9.summary: The commissioners held a hearing and approved Resolution 2026-0070. It sunsets the Energy Impact Offset Fund, which charged cultivators quarterly fees based on energy use, and amends marijuana regulations, including extending license terms from one to two years.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/10.title: Wildfire mitigation grants and fire restrictions
boulder-county/10.summary: The commissioners approved strategic fuels mitigation funding of $191,350 for Superior's grazing program and a $990,262.88 grant for Conifer Hill work by The Watershed Center. Stage 1 fire restrictions in the mountain area were rescinded effective Oct. 15.
boulder-county/10.where: Superior; Conifer Hill; mountain Boulder County

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/11.title: Open space water share purchases and Tucker Complex
boulder-county/11.summary: The county proposed buying 20 shares of the Boulder and White Rock Ditch company for $450,000 and one James Ditch share for $120,000 to support irrigation on agricultural open space. Commissioners also discussed an interim management proposal for the Tucker Complex.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/12.title: Eldora Resort cell tower
boulder-county/12.summary: The commissioners conditionally approved a 100-foot Verizon macro-cell tower on a 46-acre forestry-zoned parcel at Eldora Resort, and later adopted the resolution.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/13.title: Flagstaff Road boundary line adjustment appeal
boulder-county/13.summary: The commissioners tabled an appeal over a boundary line adjustment between 6808 and 7022 Flagstaff Road, which also denied recognition of 6808 Flagstaff Road. The hearing is set for Dec. 3, when public comment will be taken.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/14.title: Nurturing Futures cash assistance and school mental health funding
boulder-county/14.summary: The commissioners approved a $3.77 million contract with AidKit to run the Nurturing Futures direct cash assistance program through March 2028. They also approved $800,000 contracts each with Boulder Valley and St. Vrain Valley school districts for school mental health services, funded by the 1B tax.
