Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder/0.title: Emergency sales and use tax increase from 3.5% to 5.5%
boulder/0.summary: On Nov. 12 Council considered Emergency Ordinance 8791 to raise a 3.5% sales and use tax to 5.5%, to be adopted by emergency measure. The agenda does not state the outcome.

boulder/1.title: Annexation of 1275 Cherryvale Rd. and 5995 McSorley Ln.
boulder/1.summary: A petition to annex about 5.43 acres with initial Residential-Rural 2 zoning was set for first reading on Oct. 1 (Ordinance 8764). A Nov. 12 public hearing included a land use map change and findings of fact (Resolution 1384).

boulder/2.title: 2027 budget and special district budgets
boulder/2.summary: Council held a 2027 Recommended Budget study session on Sept. 10. On Oct. 15 it took up 2027 budgets and mill levies for the Central Area GID, University Hill GID, Boulder Municipal Property Authority and the Boulder Junction Access GID.

boulder/3.title: Wildfire resilience and home hardening
boulder/3.summary: Council held study sessions on Aug. 27 and Oct. 22 on a wildfire home hardening implementation hub. They also covered an assessment of existing city wildfire programs.

boulder/4.title: Harvest34 affordable housing bonds
boulder/4.summary: Council considered assigning $7,333,256 in 2026 private activity bonds to Boulder Housing Partners. It also considered approving revenue bonds to finance the Harvest34 permanently affordable rental housing project.

boulder/5.title: Frasier and Naropa campus redevelopment reviews
boulder/5.summary: Council considered a Site Review Amendment to redevelop the Frasier campus with a four-story, 55-foot, 96-unit independent living building and below-grade parking. A Site Review for the Naropa campus was also on the Oct. 1 agenda.

boulder/6.title: Arapahoe Avenue rezoning and Marine Street vacation
boulder/6.summary: Ordinances 8774 and 8775 would rezone about 3.72 acres at 2106 and 2130 Arapahoe Ave. to RH-5 and vacate part of Marine Street right-of-way. Ordinance 8782 on Nov. 12 would rezone 14.84 acres to MU-4 with a 55-foot height limit.

boulder/7.title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan 10-year update
boulder/7.summary: Ordinance 8784, adopting the 2025 major 10-year update to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan, had first reading on Oct. 1.

boulder/8.title: Power reliability and resilience forum; Xcel facility expansion
boulder/8.summary: Council held a community forum on Oct. 8 on its power reliability and resilience priority project. It also reviewed a concept plan to expand the Xcel Energy service facility at 2655 N. 63rd Street.

boulder/9.title: The Hill compliance, independent audit and restaurant task force
boulder/9.summary: Council sought a nod of five for legal research on the Grant property and broader Hill compliance. It also discussed an independent performance audit function and a possible restaurant/small business task force.

boulder/10.title: Pedal cab licensing and cannabis code changes
boulder/10.summary: Ordinance 8757 creates pedal cab agency and driver licenses with fees. Ordinance 8770 amends the medical and recreational marijuana chapters.

breckenridge/0.title: 2027 budget and 5.07-mill levy
breckenridge/0.summary: Council took up the 2027 mill levy ordinance (Council Bill 11), the 2027 budget (Resolution 22) and the 2026-2030 Capital Improvement Plan. The levy stays at 5.07 mills, unchanged since 2014, and is projected to generate $5.48 million.

breckenridge/1.title: Town-wide parking study and worker permit parking
breckenridge/1.summary: A consultant study concluded Breckenridge has a distribution problem rather than a parking shortage, since demand is concentrated downtown while peripheral lots have room. It proposes 13 management strategies, and Council was asked to set implementation priorities. Residents had earlier complained about limited permit parking for workers and residents and suggested gated permit lots, towing and use of the South Gondola lots.

breckenridge/2.title: Flock license plate camera concerns
breckenridge/2.summary: Residents spoke to Council about Flock cameras, raising privacy and data-use concerns and asking for better communication on camera placement and contracts. They pointed to the contract renewal in March 2027.

breckenridge/3.title: Housing Helps program and workforce housing density
breckenridge/3.summary: Residents thanked Council for the Housing Helps program, which buys units and keeps them as local housing, and urged continued robust funding. Planning Commission reviewed the Comprehensive Plan's underutilized parcels analysis and staff's recommended workforce housing densities, including 30 units per acre along Park Avenue. Commissioners worried about density near Carter Park and the Breckenridge Elementary parcel. Council also took up a Proposition 123 agreement with Silverthorne and an ADU policy discussion.
breckenridge/3.where: Townwide, including Carter Park and Park Avenue corridor

breckenridge/4.title: Trails at Berlin Placer development and water service
breckenridge/4.summary: Council met in executive session on water service and legal advice for the Trails at Berlin Placer development and on buying property in the Upper Blue area. The Town Attorney was told to begin negotiating bond money for the development. A resident at 10944 Highway 9 also asked about partnering with the Town for water service to build housing.

breckenridge/5.title: Little Red Schoolhouse expansion and childcare leases
breckenridge/5.summary: The Little Red Schoolhouse expansion at 600 Reiling Rd went through a Planning Commission work session and a hearing, then to a Council hearing. Council also considered a surrender and acceptance agreement and lease ordinances for the schoolhouse, Carriage House and Timberline Learning Center. Executive session discussed possible negotiations with Summit School District over real property.

breckenridge/6.title: City Market #430 fuel center redesign
breckenridge/6.summary: Planning Commission held preliminary hearings on a new City Market fuel center at 430 N. Park Ave. The redesign uses mountain-style materials, adds Park Avenue evergreen screening and removes trees at Airport Road and Park Avenue. Existing fuel center demolition and remediation would come later, and signs will be reviewed separately. Commissioners called the redesign much better and asked for a stone sample board at the final hearing.

breckenridge/7.title: Mamba Trust retaining wall variance
breckenridge/7.summary: Planning Commission considered a variance to let part of an unpermitted retaining wall remain outside the platted disturbance envelope at 219 Glen Eagle Loop. About 75 feet would otherwise need removal, and commissioners questioned how disturbance envelopes work and whether the wall is justified.

breckenridge/8.title: Quandary trailhead, Aspen Alley shuttle and open space trails
breckenridge/8.summary: Open Space commission reviewed the Quandary Peak trailhead design, with the Town pledging $400,000 in matching funds to a coalition grant, and the Aspen Alley seasonal parking and shuttle plan. It also covered the Peak 10 social trail inventory and new trail construction. A resident urged steeper hand-built downhill trails, and the commission recommended 2027 grants including $25,000 to Friends of the Dillon Ranger District.
breckenridge/8.where: Quandary Peak trailhead, Aspen Alley, Peak 10

breckenridge/9.title: Wellington-Oro water treatment and 2029 water quality hearing
breckenridge/9.summary: Staff are budgeting for engineers to optimize the French Gulch treatment plant for cadmium and zinc. They are working toward a critical 2029 Water Quality Control Commission hearing, where the Town and County aim to show good-faith progress.

breckenridge/10.title: School funding ballot measures and Strong Futures
breckenridge/10.summary: Council passed resolutions supporting Summit County's referred measure 1A and the Summit School District mill levy override 4A (Strong Futures). It also supported the statewide Proposition NN on school funding.

breckenridge/11.title: Refunding of 2016 certificates of participation
breckenridge/11.summary: Council passed on first and second reading an ordinance to refund the Series 2016 certificates of participation, with $4.6 million outstanding. The refunding proceeds only if savings justify the costs.

breckenridge/12.title: Breckenridge Grand Vacations Parcel 2 density transfer
breckenridge/12.summary: Council's October 27 agenda included a resolution on a density transfer for Breckenridge Grand Vacations Parcel 2.

brighton/0.title: 180-day data center moratorium
brighton/0.summary: Council took up an ordinance pausing acceptance, processing or approval of any permit, license, zoning or land use application where a data center is a proposed use, for 180 days. It was introduced Oct 6 and an amended version came up for final consideration Oct 20.

brighton/1.title: 2027 budget, 6.650-mill levy and 2027 fees
brighton/1.summary: Council reviewed the proposed 2027-2028 budgets in August, heard a 2027 rate and fee proposal in September, then took up adoption of the 2027 budget, a 6.650-mill property tax levy and the 2027 fee schedule on Nov 10. The Q2 2026 financial update and a third 2026 budget amendment were also considered.

brighton/2.title: Case Farms PUD rezoning (232 acres)
brighton/2.summary: Council considered a first-reading ordinance to rezone about 232 acres from the Case Farms PUD to R-2 and open space and parks designations, following Planning Commission Resolution 26-09.

brighton/3.title: Bromley Park PUD 38th and 39th amendments
brighton/3.summary: Council reviewed the 38th amendment to the Bromley Park PUD near the I-76 frontage road and North 60th Avenue in September, October and again Oct 20. A 39th amendment for about 5.92 acres near Bromley Business Parkway and the BNSF railroad followed in October and November.
brighton/3.where: I-76 frontage road and North 60th Avenue; Bromley Business Parkway

brighton/4.title: Water system: 2016 bond refunding, chemicals and well contamination lawsuit
brighton/4.summary: Council considered refunding the 2016 water revenue bonds as Series 2026 refunding bonds and awarded master price agreements for water treatment chemicals to Univar Solutions and PVS DX. It also approved filing an amended complaint adding defendants in a case over contamination of a city drinking water well.

brighton/5.title: Lochbuie to Metro lift station and pipeline contract
brighton/5.summary: Council considered a contract of about $4.7 million with Garney Companies for the Lochbuie to Metro Water Recovery Northern Treatment Plant lift station and pipeline project.
brighton/5.where: Lochbuie to Metro Water Recovery Northern Treatment Plant

brighton/6.title: Lupton Meadows reservoir and Cherry Meadows pond work
brighton/6.summary: Council discussed Cherry Meadows pond maintenance and approved Change Order No. 3 with Engineering Analytics for the Lupton Meadow Reservoir design project.

brighton/7.title: Land use code amendments: floodplain, parks and open space, administration
brighton/7.summary: Council took up amendments to the Land Use and Development Code covering administration (Articles 1 and 11), Article 10 floodplain rules (Section 10.02), and parks and open space provisions.

brighton/8.title: Police JAG grant and Flock cameras
brighton/8.summary: Council considered accepting an Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant and authorizing the police chief to sign grant agreements. Materials reference a Flock presentation.

brighton/9.title: East Ridge Addition PUD major amendment
brighton/9.summary: A public hearing was set on a major amendment to the East Ridge Addition PUD covering about 1.34 acres north of Egbert Street and south of East Bridge Street.
brighton/9.where: North of Egbert St, south of E Bridge St, east of S 22nd Ave

broomfield/0.title: Broomfield Town Square site plan revocation
broomfield/0.summary: Councilmembers Twiss and Peterson asked in September to consider starting a revocation hearing for the Broomfield Town Square Site Development Plan. The Land Use Review Commission held a hearing on Oct. 26 with public speakers; its recommendation vote was 5 to 2 (the minutes show motions both for and against revocation). Council took up a Notice to Show Cause (Resolution 2026-133) on Oct. 13.

broomfield/1.title: AdventHealth and UCHealth hospital developments
broomfield/1.summary: The Land Use Review Commission recommended approval 6 to 0 of final plats and site development plans for an AdventHealth hospital in North Park Filing No. 8 and a UCHealth hospital in Northlands Filing No. 1. A resident from Anthem Ranch spoke on the AdventHealth request. A commissioner asked for an added condition on the UCHealth plan. City Council and the urban renewal authority were scheduled to consider the plans on Nov. 10.
broomfield/1.where: North Park Filing No. 8 and Northlands Filing No. 1

broomfield/2.title: 2026 revised and 2027 city budget
broomfield/2.summary: Council reviewed the proposed revised 2026 and 2027 budgets through department presentations in study sessions, a public hearing on Oct. 13, and budget resolutions on Oct. 27. Budgets for the Urban Renewal Authority, Arista Local Improvement District and Flatiron Improvement District were also up. The library board noted the 2027 budget is flat and worried about longer-term erosion.

broomfield/3.title: Lodging tax increase and Xcel franchise ballot measures
broomfield/3.summary: Council considered resolutions supporting November ballot items 1A on lodging tax and 1B on the Broomfield-Xcel franchise agreement. A first reading of an ordinance increasing the lodging tax was set for Nov. 10.

broomfield/4.title: Housing: Proposition 123, inclusionary housing and needs assessment
broomfield/4.summary: Council took up opting into Proposition 123 affordable housing financing Cycle 2 and a first reading of a Proposition 123 fast-track review process. A study session covered the 2026 housing needs assessment and the inclusionary housing ordinance. Council also heard from the Broomfield Housing Alliance and a youth housing presentation.

broomfield/5.title: Enterprise Utility ordinance
broomfield/5.summary: Council considered Ordinance 2308 on an enterprise utility, with first reading Oct. 13 and a public hearing and second reading Oct. 27.

broomfield/6.title: Electronic bike enforcement
broomfield/6.summary: Council took up Ordinance 2311 on enforcing rules for electric bikes, with first readings on the Aug. 25 and Nov. 10 agendas.

broomfield/7.title: Protecting outdoor recreation facilities in site plan changes
broomfield/7.summary: Ordinance 2305 would require a public hearing for site development plan amendments that reduce or eliminate outdoor recreation facilities. It had first reading Aug. 25 and second reading Sept. 22.

broomfield/8.title: Chipotle at Palisade Park and EV charging rules
broomfield/8.summary: Council and the urban renewal authority held hearings on the final plat and site plan for a Chipotle at Palisade Park. Council also held second reading of Ordinance 2301 allowing EV charging as a primary use in non-residential districts.

broomfield/9.title: Nordstrom Silo landmark nomination
broomfield/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-111 to nominate the Nordstrom Silo as a landmark.

broomfield/10.title: Councilmember requests: 311 line and regional transportation
broomfield/10.summary: Councilmember Cohen asked to implement 311 as a non-emergency number. Councilmember Ward asked for a resolution supporting H.R. 5356, the National Infrastructure Bank Act, which was on the Oct. 13 agenda, and for a study session on Regional Transportation Authorities.

buena-vista/0.title: Data center moratorium and proposed prohibition
buena-vista/0.summary: Planning staff updated the Planning and Zoning Commission on the town's data center moratorium. Code amendments must be adopted by mid-December. Staff recommends prohibiting data centers, noting the County code already prohibits them, with room to revisit once the State acts.

buena-vista/1.title: R-2 OT duplex and small multifamily code amendment
buena-vista/1.summary: Residents including a developer at The Crossing asked the Commission to allow two-family and small multifamily housing, including over/under duplexes across lot lines, in the R-2 OT zone. The Commission discussed party walls, 3-foot side setbacks, and special use permits for larger lots. The Historic Preservation Commission gave feedback and a public hearing on the amendment was set for Nov. 4.

sources.body: Planning and Zoning Commission - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)
Planning and Zoning Commission - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/2.title: Regional Housing Needs Assessment and Proposition 123 commitments
buena-vista/2.summary: Buena Vista is part of a regional Housing Needs Assessment with Chaffee County, Salida and Poncha Springs, due to the state by the end of 2026. Trustees held work sessions and a public review on Nov. 10. Trustees also considered a Prop 123 regional affordable housing MOU and the town's 2027-2029 housing commitment.

sources.body: Board of Trustees - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/3.title: 2027 town budget and fee schedule
buena-vista/3.summary: Trustees held multiple hearings on the 2027 budget, including a $400,000 General Fund transfer to capital improvements, advisory board budget requests and public-support funding for community groups. The Water Fund keeps its current rate structure pending the rate study. The 2027 fee schedule and budget resolutions were set for adoption Oct. 27.

sources.body: Board of Trustees - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/4.title: Water rate study and water efficiency planning
buena-vista/4.summary: The Water Advisory Board and Trustees reviewed the utility rate study technical memos, including 10-year financial planning. An Urban Land Institute water efficiency presentation looked at local development and landscaping practices. Trustees thanked staff for addressing unaccounted-for water in the Ivy League neighborhood.

sources.body: Board of Trustees - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/5.title: Short-term rental ordinance
buena-vista/5.summary: Trustees considered ordinances amending Article VII of Chapter 6 of the town code on short-term rentals (Ordinance 2026-14, later 2026-16). The documents do not state the outcome.

buena-vista/6.title: Boys & Girls Club new facility at 710 Cedar Street
buena-vista/6.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on the major site plan for a new Boys & Girls Club facility on a vacant 0.729-acre town-owned lot, after Trustees considered a ground lease amendment and assignment to Great Futures BV. Staff found the plan meets approval criteria, and a neighbor wrote in support while asking about Cedar Street parking. A motion to approve was made.

buena-vista/7.title: Carbonate Street Early Childcare Center
buena-vista/7.summary: Trustees were asked to approve a construction contract with Adena Construction and a commercial lease with Shining Mountain Montessori School to operate the childcare center.

sources.body: Board of Trustees - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/8.title: Transportation Master Plan
buena-vista/8.summary: Consultant KLJ and staff introduced the new Transportation Master Plan to Planning and Zoning and Trustees. Top public priorities are safe crossings of major roads and the railroad, paved multimodal trails and a parking strategy.

buena-vista/9.title: Airport projects: AWOS, safety plan and hangars
buena-vista/9.summary: AWOS weather system bids came in high, but state funding was increased and contractors cut prices to fit available funds. The board is drafting a safety plan, tracking prairie dogs as a hazard, and planning for the 2027 Aspen airport closure. Trustees also considered a hangar improvement agreement with PCS Hangar LLC.

sources.body: Board of Trustees - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/10.title: Fire district impact fees and Ballot Issue 6A
buena-vista/10.summary: Trustees considered a resolution supporting Ballot Issue 6A to include all town property in the Chaffee County Fire Protection District. A resident raised concerns that fire district impact fees, over $9,000 for some homes, could hurt housing affordability.

sources.body: Board of Trustees - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/11.title: Law enforcement agreements and co-response program
buena-vista/11.summary: Trustees considered intergovernmental agreements with the Sheriff's Office for a regional tactical response team and law enforcement mutual aid, and ending participation in another special team agreement. They also heard an update on the Chaffee County Co-Response Program.

buena-vista/12.title: Recreation and Outdoors Master Plan
buena-vista/12.summary: Trustees reviewed the draft Recreation & Outdoor Master Plan and were asked to adopt it on Nov. 10. A softball field staircase replacement contract was also bid.

sources.body: Board of Trustees - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/13.title: Historic landmark reviews and Chapter 19 changes
buena-vista/13.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission scheduled hearings on 213 N. Colorado and 124 S. San Juan for possible landmark designation after a window replacement permit, and discussed code changes on integrity as a landmark criterion.
buena-vista/13.where: 213 N. Colorado Ave and 124 S. San Juan

buena-vista/14.title: Sangre de Cristo Electric tree permit
buena-vista/14.summary: Trustees and the Tree Advisory Board reviewed the electric association's right-of-way tree work permit. A permit was approved only for 15 trees on S. Pleasant, with the rest of the southwest quadrant to come later.

burlington/0.title: 2027 city budget
burlington/0.summary: The council received a presentation of the proposed 2027 Budget on Oct. 26, with department heads including police, activities, the treasurer, Old Town and economic development listed as presenters. A public hearing introducing the proposed budget was on the Nov. 9 agenda.

burlington/1.title: City administrator executive search
burlington/1.summary: The council scheduled a closed-door personnel discussion about the city administrator executive search. The documents give no details on candidates or outcome.

burlington/2.title: Unpaid utilities certification to the County Treasurer
burlington/2.summary: The council was asked to approve the mayor's signature on a certification to the Treasurer regarding unpaid utility bills on Nov. 9. The documents do not list amounts or properties.

burlington/3.title: Special event permit for fundraiser at The Midway Theater
burlington/3.summary: The council was to consider a special events permit for Our Hometown Charitable Foundation for a fundraising event at The Midway Theater on Saturday, Nov. 21.

campo/0.title: 2055 Metropolitan Transportation Plan and Capital Blvd/US 1 North tolling
campo/0.summary: CAMPO held public hearings on the 2055 Metropolitan Transportation Plan, with the Board approving the draft in November 2025 and final adoption set for February. Staff recommended removing the U-5307 Capital Blvd/US 1 North project as a tolled project, reversing the Board's earlier action authorizing tolling to speed it up.
campo/0.where: Capital Boulevard / US 1 North, Wake County

campo/1.title: Triangle Bikeway East design alignment
campo/1.summary: The TCC and Executive Board were asked to endorse a technical alignment for the Triangle Bikeway East to carry forward to 30% design. A resident spoke against the project in November, citing mining regulations, zoning and active lawsuits on the property.

campo/2.title: FY 2027 Wake Transit Work Plan and Wake Bus Plan 2035
campo/2.summary: The draft and recommended FY 2027 Wake Transit Work Plan went through public hearings and TCC and Board approval in May and June. The Board also approved a Wake Bus Plan 2035 contract with Nelson\Nygaard in January, and a speaker in November backed the 2035 Wake Transit Plan.

campo/3.title: Regional Transit Technology Plan
campo/3.summary: The TCC and Executive Board approved the Regional Transit Technology Plan as a guiding document for future transit technology investment. It covers real-time passenger information, integrated payments, data standards and an open data portal, and an extra 30-day comment period drew no comments.

campo/4.title: Triangle Mobility Hub locally preferred alternative
campo/4.summary: GoTriangle sought approval of the Locally Preferred Alternative for the Triangle Mobility Hub. After a public hearing in June, where comments generally supported the project, the Executive Board moved to approve it. The Triangle West board approved it the day before.

campo/5.title: FFY 2027 LAPP projects and Crabtree Creek Greenway funding
campo/5.summary: CAMPO reviewed 19 submitted projects for FFY 2027 Locally Administered Projects Program funding and recommended the top roadway projects, including Rolesville at Riley Hill and Holly Springs Road. Raleigh also requested additional funding for the Crabtree Creek Greenway at Lassiter Mill, which requires a 50/50 match. The FFY 2028 target modal mix and call for projects are coming in August 2026.
campo/5.where: Wake County; Crabtree Creek Greenway at Lassiter Mill, Raleigh

campo/6.title: NC 540 bonus allocation projects and TIP amendments
campo/6.summary: CAMPO worked with NCDOT Division 5 to refine costs for 16 projects selected for the NC 540 bonus allocation, including a Neuse River bridge and Benson Road widening. They were included in TIP Amendment #3, approved after a May public hearing with no public comments received. The amendment also added an RDU interchange project at Aviation Boulevard and removed a Cary trail project. Amendment #4 is up for a public hearing in August.
campo/6.where: Johnston and Wake Counties; Aviation Blvd, RDU

campo/7.title: NCDOT cost estimate requirement and project delivery deadline
campo/7.summary: NCDOT is requiring cost estimates (CSCE) for prioritized projects, with all to be completed by September 30, 2027. CAMPO has 27 projects programmed that need plans to meet the deadline. TCC members questioned the status of projects such as the Western Boulevard Tunnel, and the Chair asked for more frequent updates.

campo/8.title: FAST Transit and Wake BRT corridor projects
campo/8.summary: Consultants presented FAST Transit concepts such as transit priority lanes on Blue Ridge Road and options on I-540 and I-40. The Wake BRT update noted that Raleigh has had difficulty getting bids on the New Bern Avenue project, which is under construction.
campo/8.where: New Bern Avenue, Blue Ridge Road, I-40, I-540

campo/9.title: NCDOT Division resurfacing and safety projects
campo/9.summary: NCDOT Division 5 and 6 staff briefed the TCC on resurfacing and safety projects, including the Angier Bypass, scheduled for April 2028. CAMPO staff asked whether FY 2028 resurfacing projects could be expanded to add intersection improvements through LAPP.

canon-city/0.title: Community pool sales tax and agreement with the Recreation and Park District
canon-city/0.summary: Council took up an intergovernmental agreement with the Cañon City Area Metropolitan Recreation and Park District and Resolution 12 on keeping the 0.3% pool sales and use tax and collected revenue. The draft agreement caps bonds at $18 million for a community pool facility, to be operated as an extended seasonal pool, and says the tax would end if the 2026 ballot question fails.

canon-city/1.title: 2027 city budget
canon-city/1.summary: Council held budget hearings on Oct 21 and Nov 2-4 and moved to adopt the 2027 budget by resolution and ordinance in mid-November. Committees held budget workshops on police, parks, stormwater and raw water, and discussed 2026 underspending. The budget covers street projects funded by the 2A tax, water and stormwater funds, parks and the pool tax fund.

sources.body: Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee
