Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee

canon-city/2.title: City compensation and classification study, including police pay
canon-city/2.summary: Staff presented a compensation and classification plan that moves many positions up pay grades, such as parks and streets crew leaders, water plant operators and police records technicians. Council was asked whether to fund phase 1 for police officers or the full plan in the 2027 budget. A committee also reviewed compensation and retention for police.

sources.body: Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee

canon-city/3.title: Water and stormwater rate increases
canon-city/3.summary: The Water Committee discussed a 7% water rate increase and a 3.9% stormwater rate increase, along with water conservation and which tier to use for the shortage response plan. Ordinances 19 (water rates) and 20 (stormwater rates) went to council in November.

canon-city/4.title: Royal Gorge Lease Agreement termination and park trails
canon-city/4.summary: Council repeatedly met in executive session on negotiation strategy and the termination of the Royal Gorge Lease Agreement with Royal Gorge Company of Colorado. A Royal Gorge Mountain Park Trails Committee is also planning trails, including the South Rim Trail, and a state grant application resolution was pulled from the Sept 21 agenda.

sources.body: Royal Gorge Mountain Park Trails Committee
Royal Gorge Mountain Park Trails Committee

canon-city/5.title: City Attorney resignation and search for a replacement
canon-city/5.summary: Council discussed next steps after the city attorney resigned. A relationship study committee and a City Attorney Search Committee met repeatedly through the fall, and a proposed RFP was discussed in November.

canon-city/6.title: Police impound lot fence variances at 161 Justice Center Road
canon-city/6.summary: The Board of Adjustment heard a request for four variances from fence standards to build a 6-foot galvanized chain link security fence around the expanded police impound lot. The hearing was continued from Oct 6 to Nov 3, and staff had received no public comment letters as of Sept 30.

canon-city/7.title: Western Gateway Park Framework Plan and Main Street plaza design
canon-city/7.summary: Planning Commission reviewed a resolution adopting the Western Gateway Park Framework Plan, west of South 1st Street and north of the Arkansas River, and it went to council in November. Council also weighed two design options for a plaza and parking site, with bids of about $939,600 and $971,300 and a cheaper redesign that drops the stage and restroom.
canon-city/7.where: Western Gateway property, south 1st Street and Arkansas River

canon-city/8.title: Sales tax rules, including food for home consumption
canon-city/8.summary: The Economic Development Committee heard a presentation from Ken Rief of Sally's Bakery on whether city sales tax should apply to food for home consumption. Council then took up sales tax rules and ordinances amending the sales tax code and the 2A street tax sections.

canon-city/9.title: Ditch and culvert maintenance rules
canon-city/9.summary: Council and the Water Committee reviewed proposed code language defining culverts, ditches and obstructions. Property owners would maintain private culverts and stormwater-only ditches, and ditch companies would maintain irrigation ditches. The Water Committee also took up Title 19.

canon-city/10.title: Urban Renewal Authority grants and 4-Mile Ranch agreements
canon-city/10.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority discussed grant programs, a special project grant for 111 N. Cottonwood, and its 2027 budget. Council also met in executive session on renewal plan revenue sharing agreements and a proposed Master Development Agreement for 4-Mile Ranch.

canon-city/11.title: Public restroom design recommendations
canon-city/11.summary: The Public Safety and Quality of Life Committee reviewed recommendations for a public restroom, such as locally made metal-frame construction, preventing gutter clogging with trash and needles, and police opening and closing it.

sources.body: Public Safety and Quality of Life Committee

canon-city/12.title: Historic Preservation Commission: Saving Places hosting bid and Section 106 comments
canon-city/12.summary: The commission set a 2027 budget of $5,400, formed a committee to apply to host Colorado Preservation Inc.'s Saving Places On the Road conference, now targeting summer 2028, and planned a 2027 Project Archaeology workshop. It also drafted a letter of concern about proposed changes to Section 106 review.

castle-pines/0.title: Citizen-initiated charter amendment on annexation votes and the city's Annexation Policy
castle-pines/0.summary: On Aug. 25 the council adopted an Annexation Policy (Resolution 26-49, with a minor three-word addition moved by Council Member Mulvey) and passed Resolution 26-53 opposing a citizen-initiated ballot measure that would amend the Home Rule Charter to require voter approval for certain large annexations. Resolutions 26-50 and 26-51 also dealt with placing the citizen-initiated amendment on the ballot. The Chamber of Commerce spoke in favor of the policy and the opposition resolution.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/1.title: Canyonside development: preliminary plan, replat and South Havana Street vacation
castle-pines/1.summary: The Planning Commission recommended approval of the Canyonside Preliminary Plan No. 1, 2nd Amendment (PFP-2026-001) on Sept. 24, and Council approved it Oct. 13 as Resolution 26-62 with a condition on the Subdivision Improvement Agreement. Follow-on items include a replat (Canyonside Filing No. 1, 3rd Amendment, Resolution 26-65) and Ordinance 26-11 vacating part of South Havana Street, set for Oct. 27 and a Nov. 10 hearing. Related ordinances 26-12 and 26-13 accept deeds and easements for Canyons tracts.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/2.title: Happy Canyon Road/I-25 interchange project agreements
castle-pines/2.summary: Council approved several intergovernmental agreements and contracts for the Happy Canyon Road/I-25 interchange, including an amendment to the state IGA (Resolution 26-57), an agreement with the Board of Construction, Maintenance and Operations (26-58), and estimating services (26-61). Further IGAs on bridge enterprise funds (26-72) and CDOT maintenance and operations (26-73) were on the Oct. 27 agenda. A design contract for an interchange monument at I-25 (26-69) was also scheduled.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/3.title: Proposed 2027 city budget
castle-pines/3.summary: The City Manager presented the proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 20, with a plan to adopt the budget and mill levies later. Projections include 104 new home permits, sales tax up 5%, and construction use tax down 36% after a 26% bump in 2026. Priorities include the Road Solutions Plan, a second Parks foreman, a Trails Master Plan update, a pavilion, and research on lodging and admissions taxes.

castle-pines/4.title: Development notification and resident participation in planning
castle-pines/4.summary: At the Sept. 22 meeting, residents asked for adjacent-property-owner notification, a central online source for development information, and longer than three minutes of public comment. A Castle Rock resident asked that The Village at Castle Pines HOA be included in the city's referral process.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/5.title: Site improvement plan zoning amendment (Ordinance 26-06)
castle-pines/5.summary: After a public hearing on Aug. 25, Council considered adopting Ordinance 26-06 amending Section 27 (Site Improvement Plan) of the zoning ordinance. Speakers said comprehensive plan elements should stay in the process and asked for a holistic review and an amendment; another speaker said it provides a clear, predictable process.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/6.title: Comprehensive plan, land development code update and affordable housing review
castle-pines/6.summary: The Planning Commission held a kickoff for the 2026 Comprehensive Plan and a study session on an affordable housing expedited review and overlay project. Council also had a Nov. 10 agenda item for a professional services agreement with Goebel Partners for a Unified Land Development Code update.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/7.title: Conveyance of recreation properties and tracts from Castle Pines North district
castle-pines/7.summary: Ordinances 26-08 and 26-09 approve conveying recreation properties and tracts of land to the city under an intergovernmental agreement with the Castle Pines North district. After a combined public hearing on Oct. 13, Council moved to adopt both.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/8.title: Trail signage, Soaring Hawk Park and Coyote Ridge Park
castle-pines/8.summary: The Parks and Recreation Advisory Board worked on signage for 35 trail segments, including trailhead kiosks, directional signs and mile markers, and discussed phasing for Soaring Hawk Park and the Coyote Ridge Park renovation. Staff asked the board to settle remaining questions on sign options and budget.
castle-pines/8.where: City trails, Soaring Hawk Park, Coyote Ridge Park

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting
Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting
Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting

castle-pines/9.title: Council redistricting into three districts
castle-pines/9.summary: Ordinance 26-10 amends the boundaries of the city's three council districts. It passed consent on first reading Oct. 13 and had a public hearing on second reading Oct. 27.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/10.title: Campaign finance ordinance and 2026 building code updates
castle-pines/10.summary: Ordinance 26-07 amending Chapter 2, Article 1 on campaign finance had second reading on Nov. 10. A study session that day covered building code updates, including fire separation for two-family dwellings, water heaters and EV-ready parking.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

centennial/0.title: Elevation Volleyball annexation and initial zoning
centennial/0.summary: Council accepted an annexation petition in August, then took up Ordinance 2026-O-12 (annexing the Elevation Volleyball property) and 2026-O-11 (initial zoning from Arapahoe County mixed use). Planning and Zoning reviewed the zoning on Sept. 9, and public hearings were set for Oct. 6, 2026.

centennial/1.title: Rezoning of Business Park land to Employment Center districts
centennial/1.summary: The city is rezoning property from Business Park (BP75, BP100) to Employment Center districts, including land south of E. Nichols Ave and east of S. Akron St and west of S. Chester St. Planning and Zoning reviewed the rezonings on Nov. 4. Council set first readings on Nov. 2, with hearings proposed for Nov. 17, and discussed legislative zoning opportunities. A Sept. 15 closed-door legal session covered regulation of industrial and business park uses.
centennial/1.where: South of E. Nichols Ave / east of S. Akron St; west of S. Chester St

sources.body: Special Meeting of the Planning and Zoning Commission

centennial/2.title: Rezoning north of E. Fremont Ave and east of Potomac St
centennial/2.summary: Ordinance 2026-O-14 would rezone property north of East Fremont Avenue and east of Potomac Street from Planned Unit Development to Employment Center - Light Industry 50 (Case RZONE-26-00001). It went through Planning and Zoning on Aug. 26, first reading on Sept. 1 and a public hearing on Sept. 15.
centennial/2.where: North of E. Fremont Ave and east of Potomac St

centennial/3.title: 2027/2028 biennial budget
centennial/3.summary: Council and the Budget Committee reviewed revenues, fund balance and the City Manager's proposed 2027/2028 budget in September and October workshops. A related ordinance on Nov. 2 amends provisions of Chapter 4 involving a tax rate increase, with a hearing proposed for Nov. 17.

centennial/4.title: Opting out of the state graywater program
centennial/4.summary: Ordinance 2026-O-15 would opt Centennial out of the state graywater program and prohibit graywater treatment works and graywater use. It had first reading Sept. 1 and was set for a hearing Sept. 15.

centennial/5.title: Land Development Code amendments
centennial/5.summary: Council and Planning and Zoning discussed proposed amendments to the Land Development Code in October. In November, Planning and Zoning also looked at potential code amendments on utility-related matters.

sources.body: Special Meeting of the Planning and Zoning Commission

centennial/6.title: Livable Streets residential collectors next phase
centennial/6.summary: Council discussed the next phase of the Livable Streets program for residential collector streets at its Oct. 20 meeting.

centennial/7.title: Westray Business Improvement District 2027 plan and budget
centennial/7.summary: Council considered a resolution approving the Westray Business Improvement District 2027 operating plan and budget.

centennial/8.title: Changes to Investment and Budget Committees
centennial/8.summary: Ordinance 2026-O-17 would amend the Investment and Budget Committees, including member appointment dates. A hearing was proposed for Nov. 17.

centennial/9.title: Cisco's All In One Auto Repair conditional use
centennial/9.summary: Planning and Zoning considered a resolution approving a conditional use for Cisco's All In One Auto Repair on Sept. 9.

chaffee-county/0.title: Corrigan Rezone near Hwy 50 in Garfield
chaffee-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission heard an application to rezone Corrigan properties so they could apply for commercial lodging zoning. Staff described it as remediation of a land use code violation; neighbors raised spot zoning, noise, septic, driveway safety and unpermitted structures. Commissioners discussed spot zoning, and the County Commissioners' Nov. 10 agenda lists Resolution 2026-37 granting the rezone.

chaffee-county/1.title: The Meadows concert permit and capacity increase
chaffee-county/1.summary: The county held post-event reviews of the August and September concerts at The Meadows and a hearing on amending the multi-year special event permit to raise maximum attendance above 10,000. Commissioners also planned legal advice on the permit.
chaffee-county/1.where: The Meadows, 14998 County Road 350, Buena Vista

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/2.title: Housing needs assessment, Housing Trust and River Village grant
chaffee-county/2.summary: Commissioners reviewed the final 2026 Regional Housing Needs Assessment done with Buena Vista, Poncha Springs and Salida. They agreed to serve as applicant and fiscal sponsor with the Chaffee Housing Trust for a DOLA asbestos removal grant to rehabilitate units at River Village Mobile Home Park, and a 2027-2028 Chaffee Housing Authority funding agreement was on the Nov. 10 agenda. The Planning Commission scheduled an affordable housing work session.
chaffee-county/2.where: Countywide; River Village Mobile Home Park

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/3.title: Airport land lease, 2027 budget and new development area
chaffee-county/3.summary: The airport advisory board discussed at length a new land lease and the 2027 airport budget, including old fuel farm removal (about $48,000 eligible), a well for the new development area, a drainage plan and Taxiway A rehabilitation. Residents including Ray Plumb commented.

chaffee-county/4.title: Tourism marketing budget and Destination Management Council
chaffee-county/4.summary: The Destination Management Council reviewed the 2027 tourism budget, lodging tax revenue, a five-year strategic plan and a response to the Colorado Tourism Office on a perceived conflict of interest. Commissioners approved its FY27 marketing allocation for website and AI enhancements.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/5.title: Wildfire preparedness and utility wildfire letter
chaffee-county/5.summary: Commissioners backed several Forest Restoration and Wildfire Risk Mitigation grant applications and discussed and ratified a letter to the Public Utilities Commission about Xcel and Black Hills Energy wildfire issues. Emergency services groups reported on dry conditions, the Willow fire and community wildfire planning.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/6.title: EMS medical director, ambulance billing and regional tactical team
chaffee-county/6.summary: Commissioners contracted Dr. Michael Mandrell as EMS medical director, approved an intergovernmental agreement with Buena Vista for a regional tactical team, and had an ambulance billing agreement with Systems Design West on the Nov. 10 agenda. The 911 board also discussed replacing aging Motorola consoles.

chaffee-county/7.title: Hwy 50 roundabout support letter to CDOT
chaffee-county/7.summary: Commissioners discussed on Oct. 20 and ratified on Nov. 10 a letter of support to CDOT for a proposed roundabout on Highway 50.

chaffee-county/8.title: Archery range ground lease with Colorado Parks & Wildlife
chaffee-county/8.summary: Commissioners approved entering a ground lease with CPW for operation of the Chaffee County archery range, with staff to finalize terms.

chaffee-county/9.title: Sheriff's budget, county audit and 2027 budget hearings
chaffee-county/9.summary: Commissioners held 2027 budget hearings including the Sheriff's Office, and received the 2025 annual audit and a sheriff update. Human Services reviewed its quarterly budget.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/10.title: County fleet electrification and Colorado Charge Ahead
chaffee-county/10.summary: A CSU fellow presented on electric vehicle conversion for the county fleet, including costs, grant funding and the pending Colorado Charge Ahead application.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/11.title: Appeals of building official decisions and building code amendments
chaffee-county/11.summary: The Board of Review heard a variance request over emergency escape window requirements and denied it because other solutions were available. Appeals from Joe Cooper on permit extensions and amendments to the county building code were also on its agenda.

cherry-hills-village/0.title: 2027 budget and temporary property tax mill levy reduction to 0 mills
cherry-hills-village/0.summary: The draft 2027 budget temporarily cuts the Village property tax mill levy to 0 mills for 2027, about $8.5 million in relief (roughly $3,800 for the average homeowner), with the adopted levy restorable from 2028. Council held a study session on Oct. 20 and a public hearing on the budget ordinance was to follow; the draft also adds a Planner I position and a 10% compensation placeholder.

cherry-hills-village/1.title: Council positions on November 2026 ballot measures (2C home rule zoning and 7A rail district tax)
cherry-hills-village/1.summary: Council approved Resolution 29 supporting Ballot Question 2C, a Charter amendment on home rule authority over zoning and land use, with added language on state land-use legislation. It also took up Resolution 30 opposing Ballot Issue 7A, a Front Range Passenger Rail District tax increase, over how the district was structured.

cherry-hills-village/2.title: Institutional zoning designation and lot frontage rules
cherry-hills-village/2.summary: Staff told the Planning and Zoning Commission that Council plans to create an institutional zoning designation, mainly for schools and churches, and rezone those properties from residential. Staff are also drafting lot frontage requirements, including for private streets such as in Glenmoor and Sunset Drive, after recent subdivision applications raised questions.

cherry-hills-village/3.title: Ebike enforcement and park, trail and safety work plan
cherry-hills-village/3.summary: Police increased enforcement of existing ebike rules at Council's direction, producing 26 written warnings and a lot of public feedback by phone and email. The Parks, Trails & Recreation Commission's 2027 Work Plan adds items like a Trail Passport Program, Parks & Trails Visioning with safety improvements, bike lane improvements on Colorado, Quincy and Mansfield, and a pilot trail map sign at John Meade Park. Safety at High Line Canal crosswalks was also raised.
cherry-hills-village/3.where: Parks and trails, High Line Canal crossings

cherry-hills-village/4.title: Planning and Zoning Commission vacancies and 2027 work plan
cherry-hills-village/4.summary: Council reappointed two Planning and Zoning members to partial terms, both running unopposed for Council, and left a third seat vacant. Interviews are planned for December with new appointments on Jan. 5, 2027. Council also received the Commission's 2026 report and 2027 Work Plan on Nov. 3.

cherry-hills-village/5.title: Police body-worn and in-car cameras purchase
cherry-hills-village/5.summary: The Nov. 3 Council agenda includes a purchasing agreement with Axon Enterprise to equip the Police Department with body-worn and in-car cameras.

cherry-hills-village/6.title: Día de los Muertos family event and Art Commission programs
cherry-hills-village/6.summary: The Art Commission planned a family-oriented Día de los Muertos event on Oct. 24 with a food truck, crafts, an author reading and loaned sculptures. It also worked on the Art in Public Places Master Plan, the 2027 Sculpture-on-Loan cycle, a Snow Plow Painting program with local schools, and whether to brighten the logo's red.

cherry-hills-village/7.title: Wireless infrastructure, cell coverage and Centennial Airport noise
cherry-hills-village/7.summary: Council discussed the limited scope of what the city can regulate for wireless infrastructure up to fifty feet. A resident proposed a municipal satellite resiliency plan for poor cell coverage. Councilor Heller is working to notify the public about a Centennial Airport noise plan rulemaking.

clear-creek-county/0.title: Short-term rental ordinance No. 21 replacing Ordinance 19
clear-creek-county/0.summary: On Nov. 3 the commissioners held a public hearing and first reading of Ordinance No. 21, a rewrite of the county's short-term rental rules (Ordinance 19). The packet includes a summary of October community feedback, written public comments, and a list of substantive changes.

clear-creek-county/1.title: Open fire ban ordinance No. 20
clear-creek-county/1.summary: The commissioners held a second-reading public hearing on Ordinance No. 20, which repeals and replaces Ordinance 16 and sets the county's regulations for banning open fires. A related work session covered Public Safety Power Shutoffs and the 2026 wildfire mitigation plan.

clear-creek-county/2.title: 2027 county budget
clear-creek-county/2.summary: The commissioners took up 2027 budget requests in September, held a proposed budget workshop on Oct. 20, and discussed capital requests on Nov. 10. A public hearing on the 2027 budget for the county, the Emergency Services General Improvement District and the Housing Authority was held Nov. 3, along with a supplemental 2026 budget appropriation (R-26-61).

clear-creek-county/3.title: Lodging tax increase ballot question
clear-creek-county/3.summary: The board considered Resolution R-26-55 to send voters a question on raising the county's lodging tax. Proceeds would go to tourism-related road maintenance, public safety, childcare and housing. The question covers unincorporated areas and the municipalities except Georgetown.

clear-creek-county/4.title: Fire Authority, Housing Authority and emergency services agreements
clear-creek-county/4.summary: The county worked on potential amendments to the Clear Creek Fire Authority intergovernmental agreement, discussed the Housing Authority IGA with municipalities, and nominated Bruce Hohne to the Fire Authority board. It also handled an Emergency Services GID resolution.

clear-creek-county/5.title: Georgetown purchase of Waldorf inholding with Open Space funds
clear-creek-county/5.summary: The Open Space Commission discussed Georgetown's purchase of a Waldorf inholding parcel (No. 2091-034-00-645). The commissioners then considered Resolution R-26-60 to contribute county Open Space Trust Fund money to the purchase.

clear-creek-county/6.title: Alvarado Open Space Park and open space rules
clear-creek-county/6.summary: Staff gave an update on the Alvarado Open Space Park concept, and the Open Space Commission discussed a memorial concept for the park. The commission also began updating its rules and regulations, using Jeffco's park rules as a model, and the board discussed parking on county roads to reach open space.

clear-creek-county/7.title: I-70 Floyd Hill and CDOT requirements
clear-creek-county/7.summary: The commissioners held work sessions on CDOT reporting on the I-70 Floyd Hill project and on CDOT requirements for Condition 9.

clear-creek-county/8.title: Prop 123 affordable housing credits and childcare support
clear-creek-county/8.summary: The board approved an intergovernmental agreement on sharing Proposition 123 affordable housing credits. It also amended an agreement supporting childcare in the county.

clear-creek-county/9.title: Road easements and road projects
clear-creek-county/9.summary: The board accepted U.S. Forest Service public road easements for Little Bear Creek Road, Raven Ridge Road, Van Eden Road, Morrison Lane, South Spring Gulch Road and Sinton Road. It also approved a pavement marking contract, drainage improvements and a FASTER grant agreement, and an IGA for the Trails to Town phase two grant project.

clear-creek-county/10.title: County manager and attorney employment agreements
clear-creek-county/10.summary: The board approved employment agreements for the county attorney and the county manager on Sept. 1.

colorado-springs/0.title: Project Taurus data center appeal at 1565 High Tech Way
colorado-springs/0.summary: City Council held a special hearing on Sept. 17, 2026 on appeals of the administrative approval of the Project Taurus development plan modification at Corporate Ridge Filing No. 1 Lot 4, 1565 High Tech Way, a facility with operational similarities to a data center. Public comment was capped at 120 speakers, and noise impacts and a sound monitoring plan were reviewed. By October the appeal had been postponed at Council's request, with a hearing expected in November, and planning staff are working on data center definitions in the zoning code.

colorado-springs/1.title: Homelessness Response Action Plan and car-camping ban
colorado-springs/1.summary: Council received a briefing on the Homelessness Response Action Plan and heard that 335 vehicles have been addressed since the ban on sleeping in cars took effect. Members asked about the Safe Parking program, housing vouchers, and whether the housing and homelessness officer role should be split in two. Funding requests are expected in budget planning.

colorado-springs/2.title: 2027 city budget, tax levy and furlough day cancellation
colorado-springs/2.summary: Council reviewed mid-year finances showing 2026 revenue running above budget, including strong retail marijuana tax growth, and discussed police and fire turnover and park restroom funding. It took up a supplemental appropriation to eliminate the November furlough day, held budget work and markup sessions, and scheduled a 2027 tax levy of 3.209 mills plus a 2027 salary schedule.

colorado-springs/3.title: Business license rewrite and 2027 fee schedule
colorado-springs/3.summary: Council passed ordinances 26-52, 26-53 and 26-54 rewriting the business license, sales of goods and services, and adult use business codes. A resolution sets new 2027 general business license fees to reach full cost recovery by 2029, bringing in about $81,000 in year one.

colorado-springs/4.title: Banning Lewis Ranch and east-side rezonings
colorado-springs/4.summary: Council advanced the Banning Lewis Ranch Village B2 rezone near Tamlin Road and Dublin Boulevard and approved a slate of 16 Banning Lewis Ranch items. Related east-side items include rezones for the Cherokee Metro District 3-million-gallon water tank (4.88 acres at Tamlin and Marksheffel), the Creekbend rezone, Wagner Equipment at East Platte Avenue, and a 10.06-acre multifamily rezone at Villages at Waterview North.
colorado-springs/4.where: Banning Lewis Ranch, Tamlin Road, Marksheffel Road, East Platte Avenue

colorado-springs/5.title: Kettle Creek Metropolitan District and right-of-way vacation
colorado-springs/5.summary: Council approved a service plan for the Kettle Creek Metropolitan District north of Old Ranch Road and east of Voyager Parkway. It also approved vacating about 2.42 acres of Kettle Creek Road at 2060 Old Ranch Road, and the Planning Commission reviewed a seven-foot front setback adjustment.

colorado-springs/6.title: Utilities bonds and electric rates
colorado-springs/6.summary: Council passed ordinances for Colorado Springs Utilities refunding bonds and for Series 2026A and 2026B system improvement revenue bonds. It also considered a resolution setting electric rates and approved a lease term for CSU property.

colorado-springs/7.title: Planning updates: ADU heights, annexation policy and Historic Preservation
colorado-springs/7.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed an ordinance on height allowances for accessory dwelling units. Staff are working on AnnexCOS amendments to discourage flagpole annexations and on a Housing Action Plan, while the Historic Preservation Board discussed rewriting the preservation ordinance and its meeting time.

colorado-springs/8.title: Park System Master Plan and sale of Meadows Park
colorado-springs/8.summary: Council went into closed session on the sale of Meadows Park Community Center and on a property interest in Wilson Ranch Park. A resolution adopting the 2026 Park System Master Plan was scheduled for Nov. 9.

colorado-springs/9.title: Downtown districts, BIDs and special maintenance district levies
colorado-springs/9.summary: Council reviewed the Downtown Development Authority 5.000-mill levy and 2027 budget, the Briargate GID levy of 4.409 mills, and business improvement district budgets. Mill levies for several special improvement maintenance districts were also set, and dissolution of the Barnes & Powers South BID was on the agenda.
colorado-springs/9.where: Downtown Colorado Springs, Briargate, Barnes & Powers

colorado-springs/10.title: Redevelopment and appeals: 21st & Cucharras, Patriot Park, Vineyards Research Park
colorado-springs/10.summary: The Planning Commission's November agenda includes a 5.44-acre rezone and land use plan at 21st Street and Cucharras Street, a Patriot Park rezone and land use plan modification, and an appeal of the Vineyards Research Park subdivision development plan. Public comments are attached to several items.
colorado-springs/10.where: S 21st St & W Cucharras St; 3070 Vineyard Park Drive

colorado-springs/11.title: Code of Ethics update and Internal Audit Charter
colorado-springs/11.summary: Council passed amendments to the Code of Ethics and adopted a charter for the Office of the City Auditor's internal audit function. It also repealed the Civic Engagement Program resolution, dissolving that program.

columbine-valley/0.title: E-bike and e-scooter ordinance
columbine-valley/0.summary: After trustees raised concerns in January, police described their approach to e-bikes and e-scooters in April and the board directed staff to draft an ordinance. A resident spoke in support in June, and trustees later reported positive support for the ordinance.

columbine-valley/1.title: Recreational lighting rules and moratorium at Columbine Country Club
columbine-valley/1.summary: A resident at 8 Driver Lane raised concerns about Planning and Zoning lighting regulations and asked for a moratorium and a clear process for sharing plans. Trustees approved first reading of zoning code amendments, including the Country Club (CC) District lighting section, in October. In November a study session on recreational, sports and parking lighting led to a directive to draft a moratorium ordinance.

columbine-valley/2.title: Pickleball noise and Columbine Country Villas development
columbine-valley/2.summary: A resident at 7 Fairway raised pickleball noise concerns in February and asked trustees to act before future development of Columbine Country Villas. He gave an update in March, and the pickleball discussions were noted again in May.

columbine-valley/3.title: Annexation of 8 Hunter Run Lane
columbine-valley/3.summary: Trustees discussed annexation with an HOA in May. They approved Resolution #14 on the annexation of 8 Hunter Run in August and Trustee Bill #11 on first reading in October.

columbine-valley/4.title: Platte Canyon Road sidewalk project
columbine-valley/4.summary: Trustees approved additional spending on the sidewalk in June. In August a required design change was discussed and trustees directed staff to proceed. In September staff said the sidewalk would not proceed because the design had changed too much.

columbine-valley/5.title: 2027 Town budget and long-range financial forecast
columbine-valley/5.summary: Staff presented a draft long-range financial forecast in August, a first draft of the 2027 budget in September, and a second draft in October. A public hearing on the 2027 budget has been set. A town-wide fee schedule was approved in August, and a permit fees bill passed first reading in October.

columbine-valley/6.title: Housing Needs Assessment
columbine-valley/6.summary: The town is conducting a Housing Needs Assessment, with a community survey expected to exceed its 20% response target. A first draft was presented in October and a public hearing on feedback has been set.

columbine-valley/7.title: Jake brake ordinance
columbine-valley/7.summary: Trustee Bill #8 on engine compression brakes (Jake Brakes) passed first reading in July and second reading in August.

columbine-valley/8.title: Smoking and vaping ban in Town Park
columbine-valley/8.summary: Trustee Bill #4 prohibiting smoking and vaping in the Town Park passed first reading in March and second reading in April.

columbine-valley/9.title: Building, traffic and fire code updates
columbine-valley/9.summary: Trustees adopted updates to the building codes in 2025 and amended the Model Traffic Code in early 2026. The 2024 Fire Code was adopted in June. A proposed ordinance on the Building Commissioner was tabled indefinitely in March.

commerce-city/0.title: Data center moratorium and research
commerce-city/0.summary: Residents asked Council on Oct. 19 to extend the Data Center Moratorium and spoke about water restrictions. The Environmental Policy and Innovation Commission held data center discussions and was scheduled to bring a recommendation on Oct. 22. A council member said a study session on data centers is coming.

commerce-city/1.title: 2027 city budget, fees and mill levies
commerce-city/1.summary: Council held a 2027 budget workshop on Sept. 14 and a public hearing on adopting the 2027 city budget and tax levy on Nov. 2. Golf and recreation fee increases for 2027 were reviewed by the Parks commission and Council. Several improvement districts (E-470 Commercial, E-470 Residential, Northern Infrastructure) and the Urban Renewal Authority took up their 2027 budgets and mill levies, with hearings continued to Nov. 2.

sources.body: E-470 Commercial Area General Improvement District
E-470 Residential Area General Improvement District
E-470 Commercial Area General Improvement District
E-470 Residential Area General Improvement District

commerce-city/2.title: Colorado Blvd. and Chambers Road traffic, truck and road conditions
commerce-city/2.summary: Residents told Council on Oct. 19 about truck traffic, speeding, drainage and poor road conditions on Colorado Blvd. Council directed work on prohibiting jake brakes by Q1 2027 and on restoring two travel lanes each way on 120th Avenue between Sable and Chambers Road before winter. A Chambers Road widening update and a 120th/Buckley cost-sharing agreement also came before Council.
commerce-city/2.where: Colorado Blvd., 120th Avenue, Chambers Road, Buckley Road

commerce-city/3.title: Land Development Code rewrite and citywide legislative rezoning
commerce-city/3.summary: Planning Commission and Council reviewed the legislative rezoning of the city under the 2025 Land Development Code, with proposed zoning maps and public comment. Ordinance 2811 would repeal and reenact the official zoning map, with a hearing Nov. 3. Tier 2 code amendments and other code ordinances (2795, 2803) were also taken up.

commerce-city/4.title: Annexations: Third Creek East, South Platte Crossing Phase 2, and surrounded enclaves
commerce-city/4.summary: Council found the Third Creek East annexation petition substantially compliant and set an eligibility hearing. South Platte Crossing Phase 2 (0.61 acres at 7110 Colorado Blvd.) was found compliant and went to Planning Commission Nov. 3 with a zoning request. Council also discussed annexing surrounded enclaves.

commerce-city/5.title: Reunion Filing 39 plat and Hogan Property PUD amendment
commerce-city/5.summary: Oakwood Homes asked Planning Commission to approve a final plat creating 84 lots in the Reunion PUD, with public comment on file. Council adopted on second reading the Hogan Property PUD amendment covering 16.82 acres at 15955 E. 101st Way.

commerce-city/6.title: Housing Action Plan and Commerce City Housing Authority
commerce-city/6.summary: Council and Planning Commission were to hear consultant presentations on a Housing Action Plan, and Council discussed the Housing Authority's projects and affordable developments. A state grant for pre-approved accessory dwelling unit plans was also recognized in the budget.

commerce-city/7.title: Oil and gas development north of the city and Suncor
commerce-city/7.summary: A Chevron-hosted meeting reviewed a proposed oil and gas development north of the city, and Council took up a request for a study session with Suncor.

commerce-city/8.title: Municipal court, noise and police matters
commerce-city/8.summary: Council reviewed draft court ordinances on jury trials and compliance and enforcement (2806, 2807) and options on a municipal noise ordinance. Police bought a mobile command unit with Ordinance 2796 and amended the Axon agreement, while a resident complained about police response.

commerce-city/9.title: I-3 rezoning at East 52nd Avenue and Ivy Street
commerce-city/9.summary: Council introduced an ordinance rezoning property at the southwest corner of E. 52nd Ave. and Ivy St. from I-2 to I-3 industrial, with a public hearing on Nov. 16.
commerce-city/9.where: SW corner of E 52nd Ave and Ivy St

commerce-city/10.title: Parks, trails and public art projects
commerce-city/10.summary: Pioneer Park renovations were awarded a construction contract, and golf renovation water funding was budgeted. Commissions reviewed the trail system and Prairieways plan, public art at the police substation, 96th Ave and Second Creek Farm Park, and a council directive to study pump tracks.
commerce-city/10.where: Pioneer Park, Second Creek Farm Park, 96th Ave

commerce-city/11.title: City charter amendments and Council governance
commerce-city/11.summary: Council discussed charter amendments on administrative and departmental matters, board and commission practices, and the order of business policy. A 2027 City Manager performance standards and salary increase resolution was before Council.

sources.body: City Council Policy and Governance Committee

cortez/0.title: Park Village on 7th affordable rental housing and 7th Street property
cortez/0.summary: Council received an update on the city-owned 7th Street property in August. In October it considered authorizing Mayor Spruell to sign CHFA's notification form for Park Village on 7th, a proposed affordable rental development on the former high school property. A Housing Needs Assessment was presented in November.

cortez/1.title: 2027 city budget
cortez/1.summary: Council took up first reading of Ordinance No. 1378, the proposed City of Cortez budget for fiscal year 2027, on November 10. Council also updated spending authority limits for staff (Resolution No. 14).

cortez/2.title: Comprehensive Plan update, water supply and stormwater planning
cortez/2.summary: Council adopted the 2026 Water System Master Plan (Resolution 16) in September. It considered awarding the Comprehensive Plan Update covering strategic growth and water supply to SE Group in October. It also discussed a Storm Water Master Plan and awarded Phase 2 of the Montezuma-Sligo drainage project to D&L Construction.

cortez/3.title: Historic designations: Garland Home and 209 West Main
cortez/3.summary: Council moved Ordinance 1376 to designate the Garland Home at 120 East North Street, and Ordinance 1377 to designate the building at 209 West Main Street, to the City Register of Historic Resources. It also accepted $50,000 in supplemental state funding on a historic grant agreement, and the Planning Commission reviewed Land Use Code revisions for historic designation.
cortez/3.where: 120 East North Street; 209 West Main Street

cortez/4.title: Cortez Municipal Airport contracts and projects
cortez/4.summary: Council considered an asbestos abatement contract, extending the TSA terminal lease through June 2031, and a five-year engineering services agreement starting December 1, 2026. A youth seat on the Airport Advisory Committee was also filled.

cortez/5.title: Mobile food vendor licensing rules
cortez/5.summary: Council reviewed Ordinance No. 1371, revising the annual licensing process for mobile food vendors in the city, after a work session discussion in August. It was on the agenda in October.

cortez/6.title: Land Use Code changes and local zoning permits
cortez/6.summary: Council passed Ordinance 1374 amending the Land Use Code on first and second reading. Site plan and conditional use permits were considered for 127 N. Market Street, 1411 Montelores Avenue and a carport encroaching on setbacks.

cortez/7.title: Parks and Recreation Master Plan and ash tree pests
cortez/7.summary: Council chose a representative for the Parks and Recreation Master Plan committee and held a community listening session in October. Staff also briefed council on the green ash beetle's impact on park ash trees.

cortez/8.title: Municipal judge contract
cortez/8.summary: Council discussed the municipal judge's contract in closed session and considered a 2027 services contract with Padilla Law, PC.

cortez/9.title: Police Proposition 130 training fund resolution
cortez/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 18, committing to spend Peace Officer Training and Support Fund (Proposition 130) money as state law requires so the police department can receive its distribution.

craig/0.title: 2027 city budget and property tax levies (Ordinance 1186)
craig/0.summary: Council gave first reading to Ordinance No. 1186 on Oct. 27, adopting the 2027 budget, appropriations and property tax levies. A public hearing was scheduled for Nov. 10, with a second reading to follow. The Craig Urban Renewal Authority also set a hearing to adopt its own 2027 budget on Nov. 10.

craig/1.title: Water, wastewater and refuse rate increases
craig/1.summary: Ordinances 1187 and 1188 would raise water and wastewater rates and refuse collection fees to keep the enterprise funds balanced. Both were set for public hearing on Nov. 10.

craig/2.title: RWE solar facility land lease option amendment
craig/2.summary: Ordinance 1189 would amend the land lease option for a solar facility between the city and RWE Solar Development. It was set for public hearing on Nov. 10.

craig/3.title: Meadows Apartments HUD and DOLA grant agreements
craig/3.summary: Council unanimously approved Resolution 34 on Oct. 27, authorizing subrecipient agreements for HUD and DOLA grant funding for the Meadows Apartments project. Alex Gano of New Communities Law provided additional information.

craig/4.title: Tunatua RV Resort agreements
craig/4.summary: Planning and Zoning considered a deferred recreational amenities and certificate of occupancy agreement for the resort. Council took up Resolutions 35 and 36 on Oct. 27, covering that agreement and a subdivision improvements agreement.

craig/5.title: Craig Business and Industrial Park sketch plan
craig/5.summary: Planning and Zoning reviewed a major subdivision sketch plan for the business park. Commissioners raised concerns about vagueness, infrastructure capacity and missing sidewalks. The recommendation to Council was conditioned on adding sidewalks to comply with the Land Use Code or obtaining a variance. Staff also said a site plan and two annexations may come forward.
craig/5.where: West 1st Street, Craig Business and Industrial Park

craig/6.title: Mike Thompson hobby shop site plan
craig/6.summary: Mike Thompson sought site plan approval to build a personal hobby shop at 791 Industrial Ave. After Planning and Zoning review, Council approved it on Oct. 13.
craig/6.where: 791 Industrial Ave, Green Tree Business Park Lot 6

craig/7.title: Local Marketing District fund awards and Business Plan Competition
craig/7.summary: Council approved Economic Development Advisory Committee recommendations for Local Marketing District dissolution funds, including $15,000 for the Moffat County Balloon Festival, $4,000 for a Young Life car show and $15,000 for Powderbound Adventure. Winners of the 2026 Business Plan Competition were announced Oct. 13, with prizes up to $12,000.

craig/8.title: Timberg vacant land plan at Pine and East 12th
craig/8.summary: Bruce Timberg was scheduled to present a tentative plan for his vacant land east of Pine Street and East 12th Street to the Planning Commission.

crawford/0.title: Town water and sewer rate overhaul
crawford/0.summary: A Water Rate Committee formed in spring 2026 found current rates ($35–$41) far below sustainable levels, with the $3 reserve fee covering none of the required reserves. A consultant suggested about $125/month; the June work session modeled base rates, tiers, higher bulk water rates ($2–$3 per 100 gallons vs. $1.50) and a tap fee increase from $5,000 to roughly $11,230. Council authorized sewer rate analysis in June, and by October a notice that water rates change November 1 was discussed.

crawford/1.title: Crawford State Park water rate structure
crawford/1.summary: Council is working out how to bill the state park, which has roughly 76–78 points of use modeled as about 31 equivalent taps and is billed as a rural commercial tap. Staff found about a million gallons of use and a 2024 billing discrepancy; a park representative described budget impacts of higher costs. Options such as a separate customer class, virtual taps and guaranteed base revenue were discussed, but no rate was adopted.

crawford/2.title: Water tank replacement and state review
crawford/2.summary: The town is replacing its potable water tank; the site has been backfilled and the state health department (CDPHE) must approve the final design before bidding. CDPHE requires a full project review before bids can be split, and bidding was targeted for July. Grant reimbursements for the spring project and planning grant were being pursued.

crawford/3.title: Town Clerk vacancy and finance staffing transition
crawford/3.summary: The board advertised the Town Clerk vacancy, held executive sessions to pick finalists, and considered an offer to Ruben Santiago. It also considered hiring Jeff Blanton as a financial consultant during the transition, at an unstated amount.

crawford/4.title: 2026 and 2027 budget
crawford/4.summary: The 2026 budget hearing in November 2025 covered billing software ($10,000), a wastewater jetter, investments and a 2025 surplus. Budget talks for 2027 began in fall 2026, including water accounts with multiple uses that reportedly were not billed for all uses. Lagoon liner deterioration needs long-term planning for 2027.

crawford/5.title: Fire-damaged property cleanup and Town Hall concerns
crawford/5.summary: Staff followed up on two properties damaged by fire (on Dogwood and Elm) and sent letters requesting cleanup plans. A fire department auxiliary member raised Town Hall kitchen cleanliness, grease trap and pest issues.

crawford/6.title: Speeding, traffic safety and sheriff coverage
crawford/6.summary: At the October 26 meeting the Undersheriff discussed patrol coverage, staffing and fraud complaints. The board discussed speeding near the school, speed bumps and additional signs; no expenditure was approved.
crawford/6.where: Near the school and town streets

crawford/7.title: F Street driveway access at 410 Highway 92
crawford/7.summary: Rael Forsberg asked for driveway access from F Street. The board approved F Street access with a drainage culvert, clarifying it was an access approval rather than a variance.

crawford/8.title: Cemetery land boundary adjustment
crawford/8.summary: The Cemetery District seeks to buy land from Ann Landreth; survey and title work indicate an old cattle-drive easement was abandoned. Town staff will process the amended plat, scheduled for June 22, 2026.

crawford/9.title: Region 10 economic development and campus planning
crawford/9.summary: Region 10 presented on broadband, small business support and Enterprise Zone credits ($19,000 reinvested locally). Council discussed collaborating on a master plan for town-owned property and grants from DOLA and USDA.

crawford/10.title: 2026 municipal election
crawford/10.summary: Three council seats are up in 2026, with petitions due January 26. Staff reviewed the intergovernmental agreement with the County Clerk.

crested-butte/0.title: Zoning code rewrite and new Chapter 16 land development code
crested-butte/0.summary: Council and BOZAR held joint work sessions from February to June 2026 on a full zoning and subdivision update covering residential, commercial and mixed-use districts, incentives, and PUDs. Ordinances 12-16 of 2026, including a new zoning map and Chapter 16 amendments, had second readings August 17; staff had proposed a September 1, 2026 effective date.

crested-butte/1.title: Non-primary home excise tax and long-range financial planning
crested-butte/1.summary: Facing structural budget pressures that rely heavily on sales tax, Council worked through 2026 financial planning sessions on new revenue, including an excise tax on vacant or underused homes and a longevity-based property tax rebate at $1.0M-$1.5M revenue levels. Draft ballot language was reviewed August 4, and a resolution calling a November 3, 2026 election was on the August 17 agenda. A 2027 Budget Advisory Committee was also discussed.

crested-butte/2.title: Five-year Housing Strategy and town housing purchases
crested-butte/2.summary: Council reviewed the town's affordable housing portfolio, then took up adoption of the 5-year Housing Strategy in May. The town also approved purchases of units and properties on Gothic Avenue (816, 818, 810, 806 #5A), 16 Ninth Street, sale of 16 Ninth Street #3A, and amended affordable housing guidelines.
crested-butte/2.where: Gothic Avenue and other town housing sites

crested-butte/3.title: Red Lady Avenue and Sixth Street roundabout
crested-butte/3.summary: The town is designing a roundabout at Red Lady Avenue and Sixth Street on Highway 135, where the intersection operates at LOS E in peak hours, below CDOT standards. In June 2026 Council considered a cost-sharing request from the Gunnison Watershed School District, a partner in design cost sharing.
crested-butte/3.where: Red Lady Avenue and Sixth Street (Highway 135)

crested-butte/4.title: Gunnison to Mt. Crested Butte Corridor Plan
crested-butte/4.summary: Council has been working out its values and priorities for the Corridor Plan and Transportation Strategy led with Gunnison County, including an MOU, county presentations and a listening session on August 4.
crested-butte/4.where: Gunnison to Mt. Crested Butte corridor

crested-butte/5.title: Drought water restrictions and water/sewer penalties
crested-butte/5.summary: Council considered changes to water restrictions to address drought conditions in June, then passed Emergency Ordinance No. 10 in July amending violations and penalties for water and sewer regulations. Council ratified it July 20.

crested-butte/6.title: PROST Plan for parks, recreation, open space and trails
crested-butte/6.summary: Council reviewed the Parks, Recreation, Open Space and Trails plan through work sessions on open space definitions, success measures, cost recovery philosophy, and a parks decision-making framework and survey, and scheduled plan adoption for May 4, 2026.

crested-butte/7.title: Community Spaces Strategy and Lower Verzuh proposal
crested-butte/7.summary: The 5-year Community Spaces Strategy, one of three Community Plan implementation items, was reviewed in December and brought for adoption in May. Council also considered a referral letter on an amended Lower Verzuh proposal.

crested-butte/8.title: Wildfire code and hazard planning
crested-butte/8.summary: Council discussed the Wildfire Ready Action Plan update, adopted the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code as Chapter 18, Article 6.5 and adopted the Gunnison County Hazard Mitigation Plan.

crested-butte/9.title: Special event policy, food trucks and sanitation bin fees
crested-butte/9.summary: Council reviewed special event permitting changes, single-use plastic reduction for events, extended the suspension of food truck rules, and discussed Save-As-You-Throw bin fees for 2026-2027 to fund sanitation.

dacono/0.title: Northern Lot CNS Annexation and zoning
dacono/0.summary: Council took up the petition to annex the Northern Lot CNS property, finding it eligible and passing annexation Ordinance 1026 and zoning Ordinance 1027 on first reading on Oct. 26, with second reading scheduled for Nov. 9. The Planning and Zoning Commission also considered a site plan and industrial use for Northern Lot CNS.

dacono/1.title: 2027 city budget and Flock Safety contract
dacono/1.summary: Council discussed the 2027 budget in October and held a public hearing on Nov. 9 to adopt it, with appropriations and an employee pay plan. The budget resolution specifies no appropriation for the Flock Safety contract.

dacono/2.title: City Center Park design and master feasibility plan
dacono/2.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority received a City Center Park presentation from Wenk Associates and approved a first amendment to Wenk's design services agreement. It also considered hiring Hunden Strategic Partners for a City Center master feasibility plan and implementation strategy, and a third amendment to the reimbursement agreement with the city for capital projects.

dacono/3.title: Sharpe Farms Towne Center public finance agreement
dacono/3.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority held an executive session for legal advice and discussed a public finance agreement with EVT Dacono Marketplace, LLC for developing the Sharpe Farms Towne Center. Council also considered Ordinance 1025 creating a sales tax credit for transactions within a boulevard-area property.
dacono/3.where: Sharpe Farms Towne Center / Dacono urban renewal area

dacono/4.title: Water rate changes and water dedication
dacono/4.summary: Ordinance 1028 amending water service fees and charges was introduced Nov. 9, with a public hearing set for Dec. 14. Council also approved a water dedication agreement for additional water purchase for Strata Filing 2 and toured the United Water and Sanitation District.

dacono/5.title: Impact fee changes
dacono/5.summary: Council held an impact fee discussion on Oct. 26 and introduced Ordinance 1030 amending impact fees in the municipal code on Nov. 9.

dacono/6.title: Silver Peaks Warehouse site plan
dacono/6.summary: Council held a public hearing on a site plan and industrial use application for the Silver Peaks Warehouse.

dacono/7.title: Strata Dacono Filing 2 subdivision
dacono/7.summary: Council took up a subdivision agreement amendment and probationary acceptance of street and utility improvements for Strata Dacono Subdivision Filing 2, along with a water dedication agreement.

dacono/8.title: PUD and subdivision code rewrite
dacono/8.summary: Ordinance 1029 would repeal and reenact the planned unit development chapter and allow administrative approval of final subdivision plats. It was introduced on first reading Nov. 9.

dacono/9.title: Police Advisory Board complaint investigation
dacono/9.summary: The Police Advisory Board met in September and October to review results of an investigation into a complaint filed with the board and make a determination and recommendation. Council also heard a police analytics presentation and discussed a therapy dog program.

de-beque/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center development
de-beque/0.summary: The Council was set to discuss and give direction on a temporary moratorium on data center development within the town. The agenda does not state an outcome.

de-beque/1.title: Pivot Energy solar farm in unincorporated Mesa County
de-beque/1.summary: The Council continued discussing a proposed Pivot Energy solar farm in unincorporated Mesa County that borders the town. It also planned further discussion and direction on the development.
de-beque/1.where: Unincorporated Mesa County bordering De Beque

de-beque/2.title: CDBG housing abatement and demolition grant application
de-beque/2.summary: The Board of Trustees held a public hearing on a Community Development Block Grant application to the state Division of Housing for a housing abatement and demolition program. It also considered Resolution 2026-32 authorizing staff to apply.

de-beque/3.title: Automated license plate readers
de-beque/3.summary: The Council scheduled a discussion on using automated license plate readers. No decision is recorded in the agenda.

de-beque/4.title: Updated 2027 preliminary budget
de-beque/4.summary: Staff submitted an updated 2027 preliminary budget for the board's review.

de-beque/5.title: Sanitary sewer agreement and dedication/acceptance resolution
de-beque/5.summary: The Council was to consider Resolution 2026-34 on the dedication and acceptance of infrastructure tied to a sanitary sewer agreement between the Town of De Beque and another party. It also considered Resolution 2026-33 directing staff to enter a contract.

de-beque/6.title: DOLA Local Capacity Grant and timelines
de-beque/6.summary: The Council received a presentation on the DOLA Local Capacity Grant and its timelines.

del-norte/0.title: Outdoor Entertainment Overlay District (Ordinance 789)
del-norte/0.summary: The town held public hearings, first in September and again on October 14 at the Rio Grande Hospital Wellness Center, on creating an Outdoor Entertainment Overlay District. The ordinance would set the district boundaries and amend the use chart (Table 16-4A) of the municipal code. It was on the October 14 agenda for action.

del-norte/1.title: Moratorium on Flock Safety cameras
del-norte/1.summary: The council discussed a temporary moratorium on Flock Safety license-plate cameras in September. Resolution 13-2026 for a moratorium on Flock cameras was on the October 14 agenda.

del-norte/2.title: 2027 town budget
del-norte/2.summary: The council accepted the proposed 2027 town budget for review and set a work session. A public hearing on the 2027 budget was set for November 5 or 11, with a budget work session on November 18.

del-norte/3.title: Police Department policy manual
del-norte/3.summary: The council discussed adopting police department policies and procedures. Resolution 12-2026 would adopt the Police Department Manual as a stand-alone policy.

del-norte/4.title: Lookout Mountain annexation and GOCO grant
del-norte/4.summary: Gary Blakley spoke to the council about annexing the Lookout Mountain property and about GOCO grant funding.

del-norte/5.title: Nuisance violations and civil abatement process
del-norte/5.summary: The council discussed how the town handles nuisance violations and its civil abatement process.

del-norte/6.title: River Park changing stall
del-norte/6.summary: Patti Kelly of D Mountain Recreation presented to the council about a changing stall at River Park.

del-norte/7.title: Rio Grande County Comprehensive Plan outreach
del-norte/7.summary: The town and Rio Grande County scheduled an open house on October 27 and a town board stakeholder meeting on November 4 about the county comprehensive plan.

del-norte/8.title: Library request for computer funding
del-norte/8.summary: The Del Norte Library asked the town for funding for computers.

delta-county/0.title: Land Use Code amendments: battery storage (BESS), natural medicine businesses and general cleanup
delta-county/0.summary: The commissioners held a continued public hearing on Land Use Code amendments and on Sept 15 considered resolutions adopting rules for natural medicine businesses and battery energy storage systems, which would repeal earlier moratorium resolutions. The Planning Commission took public comment in October on setbacks, temporary special events, intensive agricultural setbacks and site plan review, and a final adoption hearing was set for Nov 3.

delta-county/1.title: CAFO land use regulations working group
delta-county/1.summary: The commissioners considered forming a working group to evaluate, review and draft amendments to the county's rules for concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs).

delta-county/2.title: Clear Water Enterprises rezone (PLN26-022, Peter Edwards)
delta-county/2.summary: A public hearing on Sept 15 considered rezoning a parcel from A-35 to RES-1 for Peter Edwards (Clear Water Enterprises LLC). Separately, the Planning Commission set an Oct 14 hearing on rezoning a 2.03-acre parcel from A-35 to A-5.

delta-county/3.title: Proposed 2027 county budget
delta-county/3.summary: The commissioners received a presentation of the proposed 2027 Delta County budget at a special meeting on Oct 13. The Assessor also presented the 2026 property assessment study on Oct 6, and a tax lien discussion was scheduled for Oct 27.

delta-county/4.title: Fire Mountain speed limit change and road safety items
delta-county/4.summary: The board considered a speed analysis and resolution to change the speed limit on Fire Mountain, and a School Bus Ahead sign on G Road west of the railroad tracks. It also took up a driveway spacing variance (PLN26-013) for a parcel on 3260 Road near Highway 92, where standards require 200 feet from an arterial.
delta-county/4.where: Fire Mountain; G Road; 3260 Road at Highway 92

delta-county/5.title: Hotchkiss skate park request at the fairgrounds
delta-county/5.summary: Hotchkiss resident Tanner Wilson asked the commissioners to support a skate park, suggesting the county fairgrounds as a site, and offered to help with fundraisers.

delta-county/6.title: 2001 Roadless Rule comment letter and Forest Service road agreement
delta-county/6.summary: The board discussed a county comment letter on the 2001 Roadless Rule and a Delta County road agreement with the U.S. Forest Service.

delta-county/7.title: Resolution supporting Amendment 83
delta-county/7.summary: On Oct 20 the board considered a resolution in support of Amendment 83, a proposed constitutional right measure.

delta-county/8.title: Property tax appeals and senior exemptions
delta-county/8.summary: The Board of Equalization heard 2026 tax appeals, including one on Fruitland Mesa Road in Crawford where the value was kept at $449,341, and considered senior exemption applications and a stipulation for Meadow Brook Boulevard LLC.

delta-county/9.title: Portable chemical toilet policy and septic variance
delta-county/9.summary: The Board of Health discussed a public health policy on portable chemical toilets and an on-site wastewater (septic) variance request.

delta-county/10.title: Fire Mountain Canal landslide emergency and grant requests
delta-county/10.summary: The board took up late items: Colorado River District emergency landslide help for the Fire Mountain Canal, and grant applications for a Sheriff's office generator, security hardening at the North Fork Annex, and campus alert beacons.
delta-county/10.where: North Fork Annex; Fire Mountain Canal

delta/0.title: 2027 budget, TABOR projections and capital plan
delta/0.summary: Council reviewed historical budget trends, a 2026 financial update, TABOR projections and a 5-year Capital Improvement Plan, then held 2027 budget discussions in October. The agendas do not state any decisions.

delta/1.title: South Main Street Gateway traffic and Main Street discussions
delta/1.summary: Council scheduled a South Main Street Gateway traffic conversation in September and a Main Street discussion on October 13. The agendas give no details of outcomes.

delta/2.title: Unhoused Task Force
delta/2.summary: Council considered appointing Carrie Boyd to the Unhoused Task Force, which met October 7 at the Delta Police Department with a public comment period.

delta/3.title: Proposition 123 resolution
delta/3.summary: Council took up Resolution #20, 2026 on Proposition 123 (affordable housing funding) on October 20, with staff report and public comment slots on the agenda.

delta/4.title: Unified Development Code and DOLA planning grant
delta/4.summary: Council discussed the Unified Development Code on October 6 and a Comprehensive Elements DOLA grant on October 20.

delta/5.title: Subdivision approvals: Stone Mountain Filing 10, Quintana Minor, O'Connor extension
delta/5.summary: Council considered the Stone Mountain Filing No. 10 final plat (Resolution #17), the Quintana Minor Subdivision (Resolution #18) and an extension request for the O'Connor Subdivision. The Stone Mountain and Quintana items had public comment slots.

delta/6.title: Water and wastewater projects
delta/6.summary: Council considered awarding the North Delta Waterline Project contract and accepting construction of the wastewater treatment facility digester improvements (Resolution #19).

delta/7.title: Mobile emergency generator purchase
delta/7.summary: Council considered buying a mobile emergency generator on October 20, with public comment on the agenda.

delta/8.title: Riverbend Resource Center conference and office space
delta/8.summary: Council considered an item on conference and office space at the Riverbend Resource Center on August 18.

denver/0.title: Mayor's proposed 2027 budget and council amendments
denver/0.summary: Council received the Mayor's Proposed 2027 Budget on Oct. 19 with a public hearing, then voted on a series of amendments on Nov. 2, some carried and some failed. The 2027 annual appropriation, a $16.1 million rescission of unused capital funds, and several special-fund changes moved through Finance on Nov. 3. The budget is back on the Nov. 9 agenda with a public hearing.

sources.body: Operations Meeting of the City Council

denver/1.title: Data center moratorium update
denver/1.summary: The Community Planning and Housing Committee heard an update on Denver's data center moratorium on Aug. 18. The documents give no details on what was reported.

denver/2.title: Council rejects Citibot and Slalom contract increases
denver/2.summary: Contract amendments adding $3.9 million for Citibot and $5 million for Slalom were called out at full Council. On Oct. 13 both resolutions failed to carry.

denver/3.title: Wheeler Trigg O'Donnell legal contract increase
denver/3.summary: A $500,000 increase to the city's outside legal counsel contract with Wheeler Trigg O'Donnell went to committee on Aug. 25. On Sept. 15 it was postponed to a later date and then approved for filing.

denver/4.title: Homeless shelter, rapid rehousing and housing contracts
denver/4.summary: Council approved many contracts for rapid rehousing and rapid resolution services (Salvation Army, Volunteers of America, St. Francis Center, Delores Project, Urban Peak and others). Other items include pallet shelters at 3815 N Steele St, a micro-community shelter at 1375 N. Elati St, emergency shelter at the Sand & Sage/Westerner Motel, and a congregate shelter presentation. The Department of Housing Stability also got a one-year 2027 continuation plan.

denver/5.title: Affordable housing loans and rezonings
denver/5.summary: Council took up affordable housing loans, including one creating 118 income-restricted units and a loan for 3755 Tennyson St. It also took up a Loretto Heights middle-income row home contract and rezonings at 3418 W. 14th Ave and 1371 N Julian St, 3343-3351 N Mariposa St, and 76 N Hazel Ct and 4519 area. A regulatory reform and HUD PRO Housing presentation was heard.

denver/6.title: Denver Health sales tax and Caring for Denver spending limits
denver/6.summary: Council reviewed spending of the .34% Denver Health sales tax passed in 2024 and amended a contract with Denver Health. Ordinances would bar Caring for Denver, Preschool Program and college affordability tax money from being spent on alcohol and other administrative costs. A Care Over Incarceration grant of $2.7 million for the STAR program was also accepted.

denver/7.title: Airline use and lease agreements at Denver International Airport
denver/7.summary: Council approved a block of three-year use and lease agreements with ten airlines, including Air Canada, Alaska, Lufthansa and WestJet. DEN also had contracts for taxiway, gate apron, and a bond anticipation note.

denver/8.title: Minority and women-owned business contracting ordinance rewrite
denver/8.summary: Council Bill 26-1216 revises Denver's contracting rules for minority-owned, women-owned and small business enterprises. It was approved for filing in committee and placed on final consideration on Sept. 21.

denver/9.title: Downtown Development Authority boundaries and funding agreements
denver/9.summary: Council amended the Downtown Development Authority boundaries several times. It also approved DDDA project funding agreements for the Midland Condominiums, University Building and 101 W. Colfax Ave, plus a city lease of about 64,654 square feet at 101 W. Colfax.

denver/10.title: Business improvement district budgets and Colfax Mayfair expansion
denver/10.summary: Council reviewed 2027 operating plans and budgets for many business and general improvement districts and set a Nov. 9 hearing on adding property to the Colfax Mayfair BID. Annual maintenance cost approvals for streetscapes and pedestrian malls went to a Board of Equalization hearing.

denver/11.title: Public safety: ShotSpotter, automated vehicle ID and District 6 police station
denver/11.summary: A ShotSpotter contract was reduced by $147,421. Council advanced an ordinance changing Denver's automated vehicle identification system rules. Contracts were approved for a new District 6 police facility at 1566 N Washington St.

denver/12.title: Amendment 81 and 82 ballot measure positions
denver/12.summary: A proclamation opposing Colorado Amendment 81 (law enforcement) was taken up in committee and Council. Council also considered a resolution on Amendment 82 on a constitutional right to purchase and sell natural gas.

denver/13.title: Parks capital projects and fees
denver/13.summary: Council approved Vibrant Denver bond funding for theatre and museum projects, Red Rocks improvements, Boettcher Concert Hall renovation, a new DPR NW facility at Cuernavaca Park, and on-call parks contracts worth up to $20 million each. Golf and Mountain Parks fee schedules were advanced.

denver/14.title: Flood control and infrastructure projects
denver/14.summary: Council approved agreements for the Globeville Levee project, Harvard Gulch and Valverde drainage, Tower Road sanitary interceptor, and Civic Center Park (Studio Gang). Other items include Welton Street, a Broadway Station pedestrian bridge and the East Colfax sidewalk project land acquisition.

dolores/0.title: Broc's Development PUD and rezoning of 206 and 207 South Third Street
dolores/0.summary: KKV Development's Broc's Development concept plan drew neighbor concerns about density, three-story buildings, parking, infrastructure and spot zoning. The Board reviewed the concept in May. Ordinance 592, rezoning 206 and 207 South Third Street from Downtown Mixed Use, had a first reading in August and was moved for approval on second reading on September 14.

dolores/1.title: Phase 2 water project and main line replacement funding
dolores/1.summary: The Town is funding the Phase 2 water infrastructure project and the water main replacement through a DWRF loan (Resolutions 700 and 719) and about $700,000 in DOLA funding. Phase 2 construction is expected to start in spring 2027. The Town manager also got Board consensus to hire a water law attorney on river water rights.

dolores/2.title: 2026 fee schedule, business license fees and Ordinance 591
dolores/2.summary: Staff proposed a fee schedule overhaul and Ordinance 591, which lets fees be set by resolution and sets renewal, late-fee and enforcement procedures. Trustees debated business license and short-term rental permit fees. The Board agreed on a $30 business license fee with a $50 late fee, and Ordinance 591 passed on second reading August 10. A business owner later protested a late fee.

dolores/3.title: 2027 budget
dolores/3.summary: The Board began 2027 budget planning in August. The preliminary budget was presented October 12 and reviewed in full at an October 26 workshop. Residents urged finishing park improvements and funding the Community Center.

dolores/4.title: Montezuma County Sheriff's contract
dolores/4.summary: The Board reviewed a draft Sheriff's contract in August, discussing metrics to measure the value of law enforcement service. Resolution 728 for the 2027 contract was moved on November 9.

dolores/5.title: Comprehensive Plan update
dolores/5.summary: The Town is updating its Comprehensive Plan with a consultant, a community questionnaire and outreach events that ended July 10. Public comments closed July 31 and a draft plan is expected in October.

dolores/6.title: 2024 International Codes adoption
dolores/6.summary: Ordinance 594 adopts the 2024 International Codes. It passed first reading October 12 and had a hearing and second reading November 9. A resident asked about triple-pane windows and was told they would not be required. Residents also thanked the Board for not adopting the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code.

dolores/7.title: Dog licensing ordinance
dolores/7.summary: The Board reworked dog licensing rules to make them more enforceable. Ordinance 589 was approved on first reading in March and on second reading in April.

dolores/8.title: Town attorney resignation and public comment rules
dolores/8.summary: Town Attorney Ethan Sumrall resigned and the Board accepted it October 12, then approved a legal services agreement with Holligan Westendorff, PLLC. The Board also discussed limiting personal attacks on staff in public comment, and a resident objected on First Amendment grounds.

dolores/9.title: Community Center funding and boundary issue
dolores/9.summary: The Board gave direction to move forward on a Community Center boundary issue and to review its funding in the budget process. The Community Center Advisory Board asked for direction and residents asked the Board to weigh community priorities.

dolores/10.title: Fall rain event flooding
dolores/10.summary: Residents described excess water on their properties during a rain event and asked for an after-action plan. Neighboring Mancos remained under a boil-water order.

dolores/11.title: Parks, Flanders Park structure and Search and Rescue property request
dolores/11.summary: The Board handled requests for use of park space, including the Galloping Goose Historical Society's proposed structure in Flanders Park and a request to waive the softball tournament park fee. Montezuma Search and Rescue asked to use or lease Town-owned property, and the request was later removed from the future-agenda list.

douglas-county/0.title: Ballot measure to expand the Board of County Commissioners from 3 to 5
douglas-county/0.summary: The commissioners wrote and refereed a ballot measure on expanding the board from three to five members, fixing the ballot title on Aug 28 and approving an amended referral resolution (R-026-062) on Aug 31 after dozens of residents spoke. A ballot title protest administrative hearing was scheduled for Sept 3 and 4.

douglas-county/1.title: Nonfunctional turf and artificial turf zoning rules
douglas-county/1.summary: The county is amending its zoning resolution (DR2026-001) to regulate nonfunctional turf and nonfunctional artificial turf. It went through a Planning Commission work session and hearing in September and was set for Board hearings on Oct 27 and Nov 3.

douglas-county/2.title: Training lessons and exercising of non-owned animals zoning amendment
douglas-county/2.summary: A proposed zoning resolution change (DR2026-004) would set rules for training lessons and exercise sessions involving animals not owned by the property owner. It moved from a Planning Commission work session through hearings to the Board hearings in late October and early November.

douglas-county/3.title: Special review uses at 6685 South Highway 83 and 2485 South Russellville Road
douglas-county/3.summary: Two Use by Special Review applications (US2023-011 and US2025-010) went from the Planning Commission in October to the Board of County Commissioners hearings on Oct 27 and Nov 3.
douglas-county/3.where: 6685 S. State Highway 83; 2485 S. Russellville Road

douglas-county/4.title: Sterling Ranch Filing 6A, 2nd Amendment
douglas-county/4.summary: The Board approved this minor development with two conditions on Sept 22 after two speakers addressed it.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing

douglas-county/5.title: Castle Pines North Metropolitan District service plan amendment
douglas-county/5.summary: The district's 2nd service plan amendment went to the Planning Commission on Oct 5 and appeared on the Nov 3 and Nov 10 Board agendas. Roxborough Village Metropolitan District also had a service plan amendment before the Planning Commission on Nov 2.

douglas-county/6.title: Meribel Village Filing 1, 10th Amendment replat and rezoning
douglas-county/6.summary: The Board approved a replat with two conditions on Sept 8, followed by a zone map change heard at the Planning Commission on Oct 5 and the Board on Oct 20.
