Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing

douglas-county/7.title: Meridian Village Parcel P-7 land disposal
douglas-county/7.summary: A land disposal request for Parcel P-7 (MI2026-017) appeared at Board land use hearings on Oct 20 and Nov 10.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing
Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing

douglas-county/8.title: Road and traffic projects: signals, bridges and highway improvements
douglas-county/8.summary: The Board approved contracts including the Dakan Road Bridge replacement (Volkert, up to $534,840), University Blvd and Post Office traffic signal (total $481,914.25), a $279,320 transportation safety action plan, and Woodmoor drainage and road repair ($106,463). Later agendas include Waterton Road improvements ($2.15M design), Hilltop Road and County Line Road/Inverness Parkway funding of $2.875M.

douglas-county/9.title: Vacation of Pine View Circle
douglas-county/9.summary: The Board approved vacating Pine View Circle (SB2026-017) with two conditions on Aug 25, with no public comment.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing

douglas-county/10.title: Wildcat Regional Park and parks projects
douglas-county/10.summary: The county backed a Great Outdoors Colorado grant request for Wildcat Regional Park and a Colorado Parks and Wildlife trails grant, and a memorial open space renaming (Mark Weston) with up to $30k was approved. Macanta Regional Park pedestrian bridge contracts and the Rueter-Hess Incline Trailhead improvements were also on agendas.

douglas-county/11.summary: The county received a DRCOG Metro Vision Award for the Greenland Ranch Wildlife Overpass, and the Board approved a major agritourism permit for Gilly's Pumpkin Patch with six conditions.

douglas-county/12.title: Older adult grants, TANF and human services funding
douglas-county/12.summary: The Board gave out 2026 Older Adult Initiative grant checks and approved human services contracts including a $2.4M Colorado Works amendment, Manna TANF case management and transit grants.

douglas-county/13.title: 2027 budget and 2026 budget supplement
douglas-county/13.summary: The Board of Health reviewed the 2027 health department budget, and a resolution on Nov 10 supplements the 2026 county budget with new revenues. Certificates of participation underwriting with Piper Sandler was also on the agenda.

dove-creek/0.title: Sewer usage fee ordinance (Section 24-85)
dove-creek/0.summary: The town board held a public hearing and first reading on October 27, 2026 of an ordinance replacing Section 24-85 of the Dove Creek Code, which sets sewer usage fees. Second reading and possible adoption were scheduled for November 10, 2026. The documents do not state the new rates or the outcome.

dove-creek/1.title: Town Manager hiring and contract
dove-creek/1.summary: The board reviewed applications for the Town Manager position and held an executive session on the Town Manager contract and offer. It then scheduled possible action on the contract and offer for its August 25, 2026 meeting.

dove-creek/2.title: Town Clerk/Treasurer and Town Attorney selection
dove-creek/2.summary: The board has been filling several staff posts: a contract for the Treasurer, review of Town Clerk/Treasurer applications, and a selection discussion. It also reviewed Town Attorney legal-services RFP submissions and planned interviews with candidates.

dove-creek/3.title: Foundational ordinance draft and proposed ordinance changes
dove-creek/3.summary: On September 22 the board reviewed a draft foundational ordinance and considered approving it for public release. An October 15 meeting included an overview of a proposed ordinance, formal presentations, discussion and proposed changes. The documents do not say what the ordinance covers.

dove-creek/4.title: Sinclair sewer negotiations, DOLA meter grant and capital plan
dove-creek/4.summary: The October 27 agenda included a DOLA meter grant, the Capital Improvement Plan, and a Sinclair sewer item tied to a negotiations executive session. The documents give no details or outcomes.

dove-creek/5.title: Preliminary budget and trench box safety purchase
dove-creek/5.summary: The board took up a preliminary budget on October 13, 2026. On September 22 it also considered buying a trench box for worker safety.

durango/0.title: 2027 city budget and appropriations
durango/0.summary: Council is holding a public hearing on the City Manager's 2027 proposed budget and introducing ordinances for the 2027 operating and capital appropriations. A resolution would also amend the 2026 capital budget and the city's investment policy, and a study session includes budget reconciliation.

durango/1.title: Water and sewer rate changes and water shortage planning
durango/1.summary: Council is introducing an ordinance amending water charges and sewer service rates in the city code. A study session covers updates to the Water Efficiency Plan and Water Shortage Response Plan.

durango/2.title: Lake Nighthorse water pipeline agreement
durango/2.summary: Council is asked to authorize the City Manager to sign a four-party agreement for design and construction of a 200-foot pipeline conveying Lake Nighthorse water.

durango/3.title: South Durango and Durango Crossings urban renewal areas
durango/3.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority is considering forming the Durango Crossings and South Durango URA plan areas. It will hear a presentation on the South Durango Multi-Sport Facility and go into executive session for legal advice on negotiations related to the South Durango plan.

durango/4.title: Regional housing and child care funding
durango/4.summary: Council will hear from the Regional Housing Alliance of La Plata County about 2027 and beyond. It will also get an update on the Child Care Investment Fund city grant and a 2027 support proposal.

durango/5.title: Remote parking rules and downtown parking wayfinding
durango/5.summary: Council is giving final reading to a land use code amendment on remote parking. A study session working session covers the parking wayfinding project.

durango/6.title: Animas Air Park and La Posta economic development
durango/6.summary: A council study session includes a staff presentation on Animas Air Park and La Posta economic development.

durango/7.title: Court case executive session
durango/7.summary: Council called a special meeting with an executive session on a La Plata County District Court case (2026 CV 030147) filed against the city.

eagle/0.title: Proposed pickleball courts at Town Park
eagle/0.summary: Neighbors near Town Park, including residents 68 feet from the proposed site, spoke against new pickleball courts at Council meetings, citing noise, park space, cost and maintenance. Staff presented feedback from an August 25 open house and online survey. Residents asked Council to move the money elsewhere and keep courts at least 500 feet from homes, while others supported pickleball as an attraction.

eagle/1.title: 2026 supplemental and 2027 town budget
eagle/1.summary: Council worked through the 2026 supplemental and 2027 budgets, with a draft General Fund operating surplus of $466,340 and $350,000 in assumed vacancy savings. A capital work session was held Sept. 29 and a public hearing Oct. 27 drew no comment and no revisions. Budget resolutions 66-68 were set for adoption Nov. 10.

eagle/2.title: Eagle River Park funding and Coalition requests
eagle/2.summary: The Eagle River Park Coalition asked Council to fund ongoing maintenance and a river park engineering project in the 2027 budget. Residents urged more pathways and asked Council to work with the Coalition rather than a third-party contractor. Council planned a site visit to the park at 200 Fairgrounds Rd.

eagle/3.title: Eagle Bike Park maintenance funding
eagle/3.summary: Council reviewed who pays for Bike Park upkeep. The Town owns the land and Vail Valley Mountain Trails Alliance runs it under a 2023 license that sets no Town contribution. The Town approved $44,500 for 2026 from the Sales Tax Capital Improvement Fund, and VVMTA submitted a similar 2027 request.

eagle/4.title: Red Mountain Ranch Metropolitan District service plan
eagle/4.summary: Council held a public hearing on Resolution 52 approving the consolidated service plan for Red Mountain Ranch Metropolitan Districts 1 and 2. Discussion covered financial risks and utility ownership and maintenance responsibilities.

eagle/5.title: Land use code amendments: variances, appeals and mixed-use step-backs
eagle/5.summary: The Planning & Zoning Commission reviewed code changes that would remove financial hardship as a basis for variances and create a two-tier review. It also reviewed changes to mixed-use step-back standards (Section 4.10.050) and to appeals, referrals and call-ups of land use decisions. Council directed that parties who participated could appeal and that the director may refer administrative decisions to the Commission.

eagle/6.title: Capitol Flats rezoning at 123 and 137 Howard Street
eagle/6.summary: A request to continue the public hearing on rezoning two properties at 123 and 137 Howard Street to November 17, 2026 was on the Planning Commission agenda.

eagle/7.title: Downtown Development Authority expansion and 2027 budget
eagle/7.summary: The DDA approved Resolution 05 to include 212 E. Third Street, and Council approved Ordinance 16 adding a vacated alley on Block 13 to the DDA boundary. The DDA also reviewed a draft 2027 budget with a commercial activation rebate program and a $10,000 EV charging grant carryover, and worked to fill two alternate seats. Other possible additions include 214 Capitol Street and the Big Bear building.
eagle/7.where: Downtown Eagle, 212 E. Third St and Block 13

eagle/8.title: Right-of-way parking rules
eagle/8.summary: Council asked about parking in the public right-of-way. Police reported that Town Code does not prohibit parking in the right-of-way as such, though vehicles left over 24 hours or violating other provisions can be tagged. A Grand Avenue right-of-way map was part of the discussion.

eagle/9.title: Marketing and Events funding requests for 2027
eagle/9.summary: The Marketing and Events Advisory Committee reviewed 45 event funding requests totaling $246,000. Staff proposed moving away from very small awards and weighing visitor impact, sales tax and sports tourism. Applications included Eagle Arts Second Friday events, a bouncy-house festival at Town Park and the Runoff Rodeo.

eagle/10.title: Economic Vitality Committee priorities and EVC-MEAC merger
eagle/10.summary: The committee set priorities including sports tourism, permitting reform, civic branding and small business support. It also discussed capitalizing on Aspen Airport closure traffic at Eagle Airport and merging with MEAC. A joint EVC-MEAC sports travel initiative was on the agenda.

eagle/11.title: Open Space trails, Haymaker restroom and river restoration
eagle/11.summary: The Open Space committee reviewed the Haymaker Trailhead restroom, whose cost grew from $90,000 to about $160,000 against a single bid near $380,000. It also discussed trail signs, the Open Space operating budget, a seasonal position, enforcement of off-leash dogs and a five-year capital plan, with Nottingham Excavation proposed for river work.

eagle/12.title: Council support for Eagle County School District Ballot Issue SB
eagle/12.summary: Council passed Resolution 61 supporting the school district's Ballot Issue SB on the November 3, 2026 ballot after several residents urged support. Council then agreed to set an approach for responding to future requests to take positions, discussed at a Nov. 3 work session.

eagle/13.title: Automated license plate readers and police
eagle/13.summary: A resident asked Council to avoid automated license plate readers and later thanked Council for not taking them up. Council also asked for a detailed Police Department budget review at a future work session.

eagle/14.title: Capital projects: Brush Creek Road extension, Grand Ave. and St. Mary's Church
eagle/14.summary: The 2027 capital priorities include Brush Creek Road extension right-of-way acquisitions, Grand Ave. grill demolition and parking, and Nogal Park updates. The Town is under contract to buy St. Mary's Church, which can operate until January 2028.
eagle/14.where: Brush Creek Rd, Grand Ave, Nogal Park

edgewater/0.title: Zoning code rewrite and new residential districts
edgewater/0.summary: The city is rewriting its zoning code with a Technical Focus Group. Its June 8, 2026 meeting reviewed proposed RLI, RMLI and RMHI residential districts, rear-lot intensification, and duplexes and cottage clusters, aiming to add housing while keeping Edgewater's cottage-scale character. The Planning and Zoning Commission and Board of Adjustment have both had it on their agendas.

edgewater/1.title: Transit-Oriented Communities housing study (HB 24-1313)
edgewater/1.summary: A consultant, Matrix Design Group, is running a Transit-Oriented Communities planning project to shape Edgewater's response to state law HB 24-1313. In August 2026 it presented existing conditions, housing market and economic feasibility findings to the Planning and Zoning Commission as it moves toward housing, land use and transportation strategies.

edgewater/2.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing fast-track review policy
edgewater/2.summary: Staff proposed a resolution adopting an expedited review policy for qualifying affordable housing, with a 90-day review period after a complete application. Adopting it by June 30, 2026 would make Edgewater eligible for about $45,000 in state incentive funding, to be used in the zoning code update.

edgewater/3.title: Sheridan Boulevard safety improvements with CDOT
edgewater/3.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission was briefed on the updated Sheridan Corridor Multimodal Plan between 17th and 26th Avenues, a high-injury corridor. The city and CDOT are working on safety and ADA improvements, and construction is expected to begin in late 2026.

edgewater/4.title: 2026 budget, 2025 tax levy and audit findings
edgewater/4.summary: Council set the 2025 tax levy and adopted the annual budget in December. The city manager called the 2026 budget very tight. The 2024 audit prompted talk of water, sewer and trash losses, possible rate increases, and segregation of duties.

edgewater/5.title: Local minimum wage ordinance 2025-23
edgewater/5.summary: Council took up Ordinance 2025-23 amending the local minimum wage and tip provisions of the municipal code, effective January 1, with first reading on Nov 25 and second reading on Dec 16, 2025.

edgewater/6.title: Right-of-way funding sales tax ballot measure
edgewater/6.summary: A sales tax ballot measure for right-of-way funding was scheduled for presentation to the HARP board in August and to the Board of Adjustment in September 2026.

edgewater/7.title: Rezoning of 2403 Fenton Street
edgewater/7.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission held a public hearing and recommended that Council approve rezoning 2403 Fenton Street from Residential One (R-1) and Residential Three (R-3).

edgewater/8.title: Height and parking variances at Board of Adjustment
edgewater/8.summary: In November 2025 the Board approved a variance allowing rear-lot parking access closer than five feet to the side lot line. It also considered a separate variance for an accessory structure 20 feet 2 inches tall, 5 feet 2 inches over the 15-foot limit.

edgewater/9.title: Foothills Animal Shelter intergovernmental agreement
edgewater/9.summary: Council considered an amended agreement with Jefferson County, Arvada and others on animal sheltering, licensing and funding for the Foothills Animal Shelter, including a funding calculation and a future agreement with the shelter as a party.

el-paso-county/0.title: 2027 county budget hearings
el-paso-county/0.summary: The commissioners held budget hearings on the 2027 budget, including department critical-needs presentations on Oct. 27 and final direction on the original adopted budget on Nov. 10. A third-quarter 2026 budget report was also on the Nov. 3 agenda.

el-paso-county/1.title: Weeds, rubbish and unsafe structures ordinances (HB 26-1239)
el-paso-county/1.summary: The county took up Ordinances 26-02, 26-03 and 26-04 on weed and brush removal, rubbish accumulation and unsafe structures. They update enforcement procedures and legal remedies to comply with state House Bill 26-1239. First reading was Oct. 22 and second reading was Nov. 12, along with a related Land Development Code amendment on enforcement procedures.

el-paso-county/2.title: Markets at Bent Grass rezoning, preliminary plan and metro district
el-paso-county/2.summary: A request to rezone 17.17 acres along Woodmen Frontage Road from I-2 industrial to CR commercial regional, plus a 53.91-acre preliminary plan for 14 commercial lots. A hearing was also set for Nov. 17 on the Bent Grass Commercial Metropolitan District service plan.
el-paso-county/2.where: Woodmen Frontage Road and Bent Grass Meadows Drive

el-paso-county/3.title: Triple H Ranch 244-lot preliminary plan
el-paso-county/3.summary: P760 Land, LLC requested approval of a 752.68-acre preliminary plan for 244 single-family lots in the RR-2.5 district, with 40.57 acres of tracts and 67.92 acres of right-of-way.
el-paso-county/3.where: Triple H Ranch, El Paso County

el-paso-county/4.title: Mayberry Phase 2 PUD rezoning and preliminary plan
el-paso-county/4.summary: Mayberry Communities, LLC asked to convert 18.70 acres from a conceptual PUD to a site-specific PUD with a preliminary plan.

el-paso-county/5.title: Siesta Grove and Bradley Point land use requests
el-paso-county/5.summary: Siesta Grove: a request to rezone 35.08 acres at 15850 Siesta Grove from RR-5 to RR-2.5. Bradley Point Filing No. 1 amendment: a request to establish a water sufficiency finding for a 9.7-acre minor subdivision. Hardy Road Properties also sought final plat approval for two lots on 19.34 acres.
el-paso-county/5.where: 15850 Siesta Grove; Bradley Point; 1054 Hardy Road area

el-paso-county/6.title: Road and pedestrian safety projects
el-paso-county/6.summary: The county approved contract changes for pedestrian crossing improvement packages, multi-year paving (about $948,543 to Martin Marietta), and North Calhan Highway design. It also advanced the CDOT agreement for Woodmoor Dr/Lake Woodmoor Dr intersection improvements and easements for Misty Acres Boulevard pedestrian improvements.
el-paso-county/6.where: Countywide; Woodmoor Dr; Misty Acres Blvd; North Calhan Highway

el-paso-county/7.title: Sheriff's Northeast Substation and Sheriff grants
el-paso-county/7.summary: The county approved a contract amendment for architecture of the Sheriff's Northeast Substation and accepted a $135,000 VALE grant and small donations for the Sheriff's Office.

el-paso-county/8.title: McLaney federal lawsuit executive session
el-paso-county/8.summary: The county attorney requested an executive session about litigation filed by Stuart Patrick McLaney in U.S. District Court (Case No. 2025-cv-00815).

elizabeth/0.title: Gold Creek Commons Sketch Plan (Resolution 26R28)
elizabeth/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a quasi-judicial hearing on the Gold Creek Commons Sketch Plan from applicant Alexandra Cramer and was to consider recommending Resolution 26R28 to the Board of Trustees. The Board of Trustees listed a public hearing and possible action on the same resolution on Oct. 13. The documents do not state the outcome.

elizabeth/1.title: 2027 Town budget
elizabeth/1.summary: The Board of Trustees took up the 2027 draft budget on Oct. 13 and held budget workshops on Sept. 26 and Oct. 17. On Oct. 27 it discussed 2027 budget modifications, and a public hearing on the proposed 2027 budget was set for Nov. 10 along with the 2026 budget, the town investment policy and FY2027 projects and objectives.

elizabeth/2.title: Extending town water restrictions
elizabeth/2.summary: The Board of Trustees was to discuss and possibly act on extending water restrictions on Oct. 13, with a presentation by Travis Scurlock. The documents do not say what was decided.

elizabeth/3.title: E86 Annexation Agreement (Resolution 26R29)
elizabeth/3.summary: The Board of Trustees had the E86 Annexation Agreement, Resolution 26R29, on its Oct. 13 agenda. Details of the terms are not in the agenda.

elizabeth/4.title: Town fire regulations
elizabeth/4.summary: Fire chiefs TJ Steck and Jeff Engel were scheduled to discuss town fire regulations with the Board of Trustees on Oct. 27.

elizabeth/5.title: Housing planning grant for Comprehensive Plan elements
elizabeth/5.summary: On Oct. 27 the Board was to consider Resolution 26R32, a grant agreement with the Colorado Department of Local Affairs for a Housing Planning Grant (HPLN-H26084) for the Elizabeth Comprehensive Plan Elements Project.

elizabeth/6.title: Main Street Station site plan agreement extension
elizabeth/6.summary: Resolution 26R31 would approve a first amendment to the site plan agreement between the town and Main Street Station Elizabeth, LLC, extending it. The Board was to consider it on Oct. 27.

elizabeth/7.title: Road contracts with NexCivil and Hillside Village paving scope change
elizabeth/7.summary: On Oct. 27 the Board was to consider Resolutions 26R33 and 26R34 amending trade contractor agreements, one with NexCivil Engineering and Construction. It was also to discuss a change of scope on the Hillside Village paving project.

elizabeth/8.title: Metropolitan districts and Depot parking lot restrooms
elizabeth/8.summary: The Oct. 27 workshop included a metropolitan district discussion led by Corey Hoffmann and a discussion of the Depot parking lot restrooms. A facilities discussion was also on that agenda.

elizabeth/9.title: Friday Night Markets 2026 recap and Main Street events
elizabeth/9.summary: Tony Briggs of Elizabeth Brewing Company was to present a recap of the 2026 Friday Night Markets to the Board on Oct. 13. The Main Street Board also planned to discuss recent events on Main Street and a communication plan on Sept. 14.

erie/0.title: Sale vs. lease of Town mineral rights to SM Energy (Draco pad)
erie/0.summary: Council approved Ordinance 26-028 on June 23 to sell Town-owned minerals to SM Energy, but SM terminated the contract Aug. 19 and Council repealed the ordinance Aug. 25. On Sept. 1 Council discussed leasing the minerals instead (an offer at $12,000 per net mineral acre, about $1.36M bonus) and how the Town should take part in the state ECMC drilling and spacing process for the Draco pad.

erie/1.title: 2027 budget and revenue slowdown
erie/1.summary: Staff told Council that sales tax growth is under 2% and use tax and building permits are down over 40%, so the 2027 budget limits new staff to health-and-safety needs. Study sessions ran Aug. 18 and Oct. 6, with first reading of the proposed 2027 budget set for Oct. 27; advisory boards such as Tree and Sustainability saw their budgets cut.

erie/2.title: Oil and gas regulations update (Title 10, Chapter 12)
erie/2.summary: Planning Commission reviewed proposed revisions to the Town's oil and gas rules, including doubling inspection fees, per-well fees, notification periods, legacy wells, noise and air quality. A resident commented on the proposed changes; the commission was asked to recommend revisions to Council.

erie/3.title: Short-term rental rules and permit fees
erie/3.summary: Planning Commission considered a new UDC Chapter 16 on short-term rentals, and Council set an application fee for STR permits and a special-event STR permit period for 2027.

erie/4.title: Comprehensive Plan amendments and Prop 123 affordable housing
erie/4.summary: Planning Commission and Council discussed amending the 2024 Elevate Erie Comprehensive Plan and Erie's Prop 123 commitment, with the Town seeking a reduction of its unit requirement to 30 units. Residents spoke against any Comp Plan changes on Sept. 8, and a medium-low density amendment was later approved.

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/5.title: Town trees removed for new water meters
erie/5.summary: Several residents told Council they objected to the Town digging up trees to install new water meters. Council also approved temporary water meter standards tied to the end of residential fire sprinkler requirements.

erie/6.title: Colliers Hill Urban Renewal tax increment agreements
erie/6.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority and Council approved an amendment with Weld County removing the requirement that tax increment between $10M and $14M go to Weld County Road 5, and adding parks and recreation facilities as eligible improvements. The URA also adopted its 2027 budget ($5.75M revenue) with Briggs Alleyway stormwater as the main capital project.
erie/6.where: Colliers Hill plan area / Weld County Road 5

erie/7.title: Downtown Briggs Street improvements and alleyways
erie/7.summary: The URA paid for design amendments for downtown infrastructure and bridge work, and Council approved a contract amendment for downtown alleyway improvements, revocable licenses for businesses on Briggs Street, and a disposition and development agreement for 150 Briggs.

erie/8.title: New Town Manager appointment
erie/8.summary: After a search that opened in August, Council scheduled a vote on Resolution 2026-214 appointing Kelli Johnson as Town Manager starting Jan. 4, 2027, with an employment agreement.

erie/9.title: Airport noise and fees, and charter change for longer hangar leases
erie/9.summary: A resident complained about early-morning touch-and-go flights. The airport board discussed residential through-the-fence fees (staff proposal to Council in December), commercial fees, hangar development, and a possible ballot question to allow land leases longer than 20 years.

erie/10.title: Open space protection and zoning
erie/10.summary: Planning Commission and the Open Space and Trails board prepared a joint study session on how open space is zoned and protected, including the Reserved Open Space district and the voter approval required to sell or rezone open space. The OSTAB also supported a rezoning at 1025 Weld County Road 1 1/2 and discussed trail connections.

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board
Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/11.title: Vista Ridge golf course PD Amendment No. 9
erie/11.summary: Planning Commission held a hearing on Vista Ridge PD Amendment No. 9 for the golf course, and Council held a public hearing on the ordinance Oct. 13 with presentations from Gauge Land Development and the golf course manager.

erie/12.title: Compass Park and safe sidewalks
erie/12.summary: Residents spoke to Council in favor of Compass Park and safe sidewalks.

erie/13.title: Flock Safety technology and security executive session
erie/13.summary: Council scheduled an executive session on security arrangements and Flock Safety technology.

estes-park/0.title: 2027 Town budget and 2027–2031 Community Improvement Plan
estes-park/0.summary: Budget study sessions in October reviewed the 2027 budget, which plans to use $1.775 million of fund balance for capital items and projects revenue 5% over 2025 actuals. The CIP holds $37.66 million in projects, including Events Center lighting, Wonderview Avenue trail extension, Children's Park remodel and stormwater work. Staff pay raises and a 15% health insurance increase were also covered.

estes-park/1.title: Workforce housing, Housing Action Plan and 6E funding
estes-park/1.summary: The Board heard public concern about housing and seasonal workforce needs, received the Housing Assessment Addendum and Housing Action Plan, and approved Resolution 105-26, the 2027 Workforce Housing and Childcare Funding Plan for 6E lodging tax funds. The Estes Park Housing Authority is also gathering data on seasonal housing and has board vacancies being filled.

estes-park/2.title: Development Code rewrite: housing density bonuses and rezoning criteria
estes-park/2.summary: The 50% draft Development Code would set housing definitions, density and height bonuses, and lower parking minimums for qualifying projects; EPHA said 1.2 to 1.4 spaces per unit suffices for its properties, while some board members worried about fewer than two per unit. The Board also reviewed new rezoning criteria tied to the Estes Forward Future Land Use Plan. The rewrite continues into 2027.

estes-park/3.title: Annexation of Fawn Valley and Highway 7 enclaves
estes-park/3.summary: Staff reported costs and benefits of annexing two enclaves: about $50,000 for a consultant map, plus $12,750 per year in sales tax and $1,900 in property tax revenue, and $2,400 a year for 25 years to bring Chalet Ridge Court up to Town standard. Four responses opposed and one favored annexation of the Highway 7 enclave; staff will research an unowned gap parcel. Olympus Lodge annexation and water access also came up in budget talks.

estes-park/4.title: Public safety facility cost debate
estes-park/4.summary: Residents questioned the cost of a proposed new public safety facility, citing population data and a cheaper alternative, and suggested raising officer pay instead so more officers live in town.

estes-park/5.title: Parking license plate recognition policy
estes-park/5.summary: Staff presented a draft policy for license plate readers in paid parking, with data kept one day unless tied to a citation. It bars use for immigration enforcement, First Amendment monitoring or data sales. The Board asked for the policy to return and discussed limiting private LPR use.

estes-park/6.title: Water: administrative penalties, Colorado-Big Thompson subcontract and NCWCD incorporation
estes-park/6.summary: The Board reviewed an administrative fine policy to enforce repair of leaking surface water lines. It also pulled the Colorado-Big Thompson subcontract extension with YMCA of the Rockies for discussion, along with the plan to incorporate Water Division customers into the Northern Colorado Water Conservancy District. Water rate hearing dates were set and a Trout Haven water lease approved.

estes-park/7.title: Fall River Trail final segment construction
estes-park/7.summary: The Board approved a $3,553,992.20 construction contract with FNF Construction and $114,500 for construction management. A trustee questioned the wide range of bids, and the engineer said the Town's estimate was conservative and half the bids exceeded it.

estes-park/8.title: Parks and Open Space Master Plan
estes-park/8.summary: The final draft plan covers 11 parks, two natural areas and two town parcels, drew feedback from about 890 people, and found 76% of households are within a 15-minute walk of a park. Board members asked for an urban forestry element, dog parks and ongoing updates; implementation depends on funding.

estes-park/9.title: Visit Estes Park 2027 operating plan
estes-park/9.summary: VEP presented its 2027 operating plan with proposed revenues of $11.68 million, $6.45 million of it 6E funds passed to the Town. The Town Board and County Commissioners commended it; the Town Board is to act on November 10.

estes-park/10.title: Micromobility, e-bike rules and youth tobacco policy
estes-park/10.summary: Staff proposed four Municipal Code changes to clarify rules for micromobility devices. A resident and Larimer County representatives urged the Town to consider policies on youth tobacco and nicotine use, and e-bike accidents involving youth were discussed.

estes-park/11.title: Feather flag sign rules
estes-park/11.summary: The Board discussed whether to extend or make permanent the temporary allowance for feather flags under Ordinance 15-25, with one flag per lot, 12-foot height limit, and a ban in residential zones and downtown. Members were split on whether to require a fee and permit.

fairplay/0.title: Gemenskap development sewer dispute and lawsuit
fairplay/0.summary: The Board has repeatedly gone into executive session, including a joint session with the Park County commissioners on Sept. 15, about the sewer system at the Gemenskap development. The agendas mention mediation with the developer on July 27, a related claim and a lawsuit the developer filed against the Town. The documents do not state any outcome.

fairplay/1.title: 2026 amended and 2027 budget, fee schedule and staffing
fairplay/1.summary: The Town reviewed the 2027 budget through the fall. This included preliminary staffing and salaries, a proposed police department budget, capital projects and the events budget. The amended 2026 and proposed 2027 budgets had a first hearing on Nov. 2 and a second on Nov. 16. The Board also reviewed changes to the 2027 fee schedule and year-end employee bonuses.

fairplay/2.title: Park County use of Town water for landfill-area wells
fairplay/2.summary: The Board discussed Park County's use of Fairplay water for wells contaminated by the landfill. On Nov. 2 it discussed fees for the County's use of Town water for parcels outside Town related to the landfill.
fairplay/2.where: Landfill area outside Town limits, Park County

fairplay/3.title: Fairplay Police Station construction and police matters
fairplay/3.summary: The Town paid for a structural assessment of the police station and on Nov. 16 considered Resolution 38 on a spending award for construction of the Fairplay Police Station. Executive sessions also covered legal advice and personnel matters involving Chief Jeff Worley and an officer. The Town is also revising its automated vehicle identification system ordinance (Ordinance 6), which had first reading Nov. 2 and second reading Nov. 16.

fairplay/4.title: Land swap with Park County
fairplay/4.summary: The Board took up first reading of Ordinance 5, which would authorize a land swap in which the Town conveys Park County parcel no. 32670 to the County in exchange for County property.

fairplay/5.title: Property Improvement Incentive Program (PIIP) agreements downtown
fairplay/5.summary: The Town approved or considered incentive agreements for exterior and window projects. These included 711 Front Street (Andrew Schofield, with an architectural review), 305 4th Street and 402 Hathaway Street (Greg Johnson), and reimbursement for a 601 Main painting project.
fairplay/5.where: 711 Front St, 305 4th St, 402 Hathaway St, 601 Main St

fairplay/6.title: Wastewater lagoon project and water resource planning
fairplay/6.summary: The Town is paying for engineering on a wastewater lagoon liner and new lagoon, plus a new pump and motor for the treatment plant. It held a work session on water rights and the utilities capital plan. Colorado Rural Water presented on the Source Water Protection Plan.
fairplay/6.where: Fairplay wastewater treatment plant and water system

fairplay/7.title: Funding requests from community groups and events
fairplay/7.summary: The Board weighed funding for the Burro Days request from South Park School District RE-2, the Halloween Spooktacular, Rocky Mountain Rural Health and the Park County Senior Coalition. It also considered Boys & Girls Club facility needs, and chose a Mardi Gras fundraiser beneficiary. It donated $1,000 to the South Park High School football car show fundraiser after a resident's request.

fairplay/8.title: Records request policy and fee schedule changes
fairplay/8.summary: Resolutions amend the Town's schedule of fees. The Nov. 2 version adds a policy on responding to records requests under the Colorado Open Records Act and the Criminal Justice Records Act.

fairplay/9.title: Park County E-911 communications center agreement
fairplay/9.summary: The Board reviewed a proposed intergovernmental agreement on operating, administering and financially supporting the Park County Communications (E-911) Center.

firestone/0.title: Comprehensive Plan update
firestone/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on Resolution PC-26-03 to approve an update to the town's Comprehensive Plan on October 1, 2026. The documents do not state the outcome.

firestone/1.title: Barefoot Lakes Filing 5, 2nd Amendment preliminary plat
firestone/1.summary: In July the Planning and Zoning Commission held a hearing on Resolution PC-26-02 recommending approval of the Barefoot Lakes Filing 5, 2nd Amendment preliminary plat. Resident Steve Trunk raised concerns about impacts on neighboring properties, including views and buffering.

firestone/2.title: Parks and trails priorities and 2027 budget recommendations
firestone/2.summary: The Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission discussed trail connections to St. Vrain Park via the Legacy trail and trail improvements at Birch and Firestone Blvd, Cotton Hollow and Sable, and Pinecone and Frontier. It also noted rotting bridge boards south of Gateway Park and looked into adding pickleball courts, as input to the 2027 budget. A proposed PTROC projects list is on the October 7 agenda.
firestone/2.where: Trails and parks townwide, including Gateway Park and St. Vrain Park

sources.body: Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission

firestone/3.title: Arts in Public Places program
firestone/3.summary: The Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission discussed the Colorado Arts in Public Places (AIPP) program in July, with staff gathering commissioner input.

sources.body: Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission

firestone/4.title: Summer Hours Pilot Program
firestone/4.summary: The Board of Trustees has a discussion item on a Summer Hours Pilot Program at its October 14 meeting. The documents give no details of the proposal.

florence/0.title: Transfer of 100 East Front Street museum property and end of 1964 trust
florence/0.summary: Council held a public hearing and second reading of Ordinance 11-2026 to end a 1964 trust agreement and convey the property at 100 East Front Street to the museum that operates it. The museum would take on all maintenance, insurance, utilities, structural repairs and capital improvements. The property was originally conveyed to the City by the Fraternal Order of Eagles.

florence/1.title: Handover of the July Fourth Festival
florence/1.summary: Council was asked to consider transferring ownership and management of the City of Florence July Fourth Festival. The agenda does not say who would take it over.

florence/2.title: 2027 compensation and classification plan
florence/2.summary: Council was asked to adopt the Compensation and Classification Plan for budget year 2027.

florence/3.title: Water rights, utility service and billing negotiations
florence/3.summary: The agenda lists a closed session to instruct negotiators on water rights, municipal utility service and billing, and PUD compliance. The water consultant, planning director and water superintendent were named as attending.

fort-collins/0.title: 2027-2028 biennial budget
fort-collins/0.summary: Council held a series of work sessions in September and October on the City Manager's Recommended 2027-2028 Budget, the first under a new Priority Based Budgeting approach. Staff identified a gap between ongoing revenues and expenses and asked service areas to find 8% in cost reductions. Council was to give direction on changes and adopt the budget in November, and residents objected to higher rental rates and user fees at the Lincoln Center and other city facilities.

fort-collins/1.title: Joining the Northern Integrated Supply Project (Glade Reservoir) instead of enlarging Halligan
fort-collins/1.summary: The Water Utility Enterprise board adopted 6-1 (Nelsen opposed) a resolution authorizing agreements for the city to become a participant in NISP and store some of its own water rights in Glade Reservoir. Staff cited permitting uncertainty around the Halligan Reservoir enlargement and projected lower rate increases, and plan to notify the Army Corps and withdraw the Halligan Section 404 permit application.

fort-collins/2.title: Montava wholesale water agreement with ELCO
fort-collins/2.summary: At an Aug. 25 work session, staff reviewed a wholesale water arrangement with East Larimer County Water District to serve Montava, a 4,000+ unit mixed-use development in northeast Fort Collins. Councilmembers supported advancing it, while asking about fee differences, utility revenue, water supply sufficiency and the non-potable system; a long-term Integrated Water Resources Plan is proposed for 2027.

fort-collins/3.title: Housing Action Plan and affordable housing land and funding
fort-collins/3.summary: Council reviewed draft Housing Action Plan strategies on supply, affordability, preservation, stabilization and funding, which would replace the 2021 Housing Strategic Plan. Council also moved to convey city-owned land at 314 North Howes Street for affordable housing (a speaker called it a giveaway) and appropriated leftover CCIP sales tax reserves to the Affordable Housing Capital Program.

fort-collins/4.title: North College Urban Renewal: property purchases, Bristlecone loan and community coalition
fort-collins/4.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority approved items including a redevelopment agreement for façade and community-use improvements at 1505 North College (about $1 million project), a $250,000 acquisition at 1630 North College, and a proposed $2 million loan for the 112-unit income-restricted Bristlecone Affordable project. It also discussed a community coalition charter for 1636 North College and the remaining TIF funding, and held executive sessions on property purchases including eminent domain.

fort-collins/5.title: College and Drake urban renewal plan amendment
fort-collins/5.summary: The URA considered funding an existing conditions study of the College and Drake intersection area to amend the existing urban renewal plan, saying the original plan's intent is no longer viable. A second resolution would fund a property acquisition settlement to secure possession for redevelopment.

fort-collins/6.title: Safe Parking Pilot Program
fort-collins/6.summary: At a Sept. 8 work session, staff outlined a possible safe parking pilot and asked Council whether to allow one and what code and enforcement updates would be needed. Input was mixed on whether to pursue an ordinance to ensure neighbor voices are heard.

fort-collins/7.title: Economic Development Investment Program
fort-collins/7.summary: Council gave broad support to a proposed Economic Development Investment Program, favoring uses for community vitality and micro-business proof-of-concept over jobs or sales tax. Members discussed an after-the-fact review role, discomfort with ongoing annual commitments, and staffing; the program ties to 2027-28 budget adoption.

fort-collins/8.title: Platte River Power Authority rollback of 2030 carbon-free goal
fort-collins/8.summary: Several residents spoke against discussion by the Platte River Power Authority board of rolling back its goal of 100% non-carbon electricity by 2030.

fort-collins/9.title: Pedestrian safety and intersection projects (Vision Zero)
fort-collins/9.summary: Council appropriated funds for the Pedestrian Intersection Improvements project at five locations, bringing total funding to $2,460,856, and for the Lemay and Drake intersection, including $1,549,760 to acquire property and install a signal. A resident urged more downtown pedestrian safety and others raised downtown parking fees.
fort-collins/9.where: Lemay and Drake; downtown Fort Collins

fort-collins/10.title: Election Code Committee changes and campaign finance
fort-collins/10.summary: The committee reviewed the 2025 election (cost about $176,300), campaign finance enforcement, and proposed Code changes including precinct boundary updates, direct fines by the City Clerk for late reports, and longer-term public campaign funding.

fort-collins/11.title: Ethics rules and Code of Conduct changes
fort-collins/11.summary: Council took up an ordinance requiring reporting of contacts with staff about non-routine city mailers and amendments to the Code of Conduct recommended by the Ethics Review Board; a resident raised ethics concerns.

fort-collins/12.title: Automated vehicle ID corridors and surveillance policy
fort-collins/12.summary: A November work session sought Council feedback on a draft surveillance policy and on automated vehicle identification corridors adopted under Ordinance No. 098, including code changes to align with Colorado law.

fort-lupton/0.title: Comprehensive Plan update, Housing Action Plan and Strategic Growth Element
fort-lupton/0.summary: The city is updating its Comprehensive Plan with consultant Ayres Associates, whose scope was amended to add a water supply element. The Planning Commission (Oct. 22) and City Council (Oct. 27) reviewed the draft Housing Action Plan, Strategic Growth Element and proposed future land use categories. The city also backed a DOLA Local Planning Capacity Grant application.

fort-lupton/1.title: Western Midstream buried gas gathering pipeline special use permit
fort-lupton/1.summary: The Planning Commission considered a Western Midstream request for a special use permit for a buried gas gathering pipeline crossing I-2 industrial and agricultural parcels. Nearby property owners, including Joseph and Sue Hubert and Leeroy Sack, asked about pipe size, property access and impacts; Western Midstream said it would be the responsible party.
fort-lupton/1.where: South Denver Ave and County Road 10 area, Fort Lupton

fort-lupton/2.title: Ewing Annexation Agreement amendment
fort-lupton/2.summary: Council took up a first amendment to the Ewing Annexation Agreement approved April 16, 2024, as an ordinance, with a second reading on Sept. 29 (Ordinance 2026-1202).

fort-lupton/3.title: Water and sewer plant investment (tap) fee increases
fort-lupton/3.summary: Council approved a resolution revising the water and sewer infrastructure investment fee schedule effective Dec. 1, 2026, after staff surveyed regional tap fees. Fees are tied to upgrades at the water and wastewater treatment plants, and METRO Water Recovery is raising its own tap fee to $6,290. 2027 plant investment fee changes were also on the Sept. 8 agenda.

fort-lupton/4.title: Water system projects: water tower, Colorado-Big Thompson assessment
fort-lupton/4.summary: Water tower construction continues, with a contract amendment, a change order with HPM and an easement from Murray Farms on the October 13 agenda, and large construction management invoices. Council also approved the 2027 Colorado-Big Thompson assessment of up to $191,000.70 and ongoing treatment plant upgrades.

fort-lupton/5.title: Street reconstruction design contracts funded by CR 12 UPRR money
fort-lupton/5.summary: Council awarded design contracts for reconstruction of 5th Street and Broadway Avenue (JVA, up to $143,095), Homestead Drive and Columbine Avenue (IMEG), and 3rd and 5th Streets (HKS), paid from CR 12 UPRR project funds. A JVA contract amendment came up on Oct. 13.
fort-lupton/5.where: 5th St & Broadway Ave; Homestead Dr & Columbine Ave; 3rd & 5th Streets

fort-lupton/6.title: Koshio Park renovation
fort-lupton/6.summary: The park is being renovated, with a temporary irrigation change order, a second change order, an update and a gazebo discussion on council agendas. The Urban Renewal Authority also noted the groundbreaking.

fort-lupton/7.title: 2027 budget and mill levy limit exclusion
fort-lupton/7.summary: Council received the 2027 requested budget on Sept. 29, held a Budget Retreat Oct. 17, and scheduled 2027 budget approval Nov. 10. It also considered an application for exclusion from the 5.5% assessed valuation limit, plus 2027 golf green fees and health plan items.

fort-lupton/8.title: Fort Lupton Urban Renewal Authority grants and TIF projects
fort-lupton/8.summary: FLURA reviewed its 2027 draft budget, an El Rey Del Taco grant extension request, and a resolution to fund 50% of a city survey and engineering project with a total cost of $86,820. It also handles TIF reimbursements and may get a request for grant help from the Odd Fellows historic building.

fort-lupton/9.title: Metropolitan district service plans: Lancaster Crossing and 277
fort-lupton/9.summary: Council took up a resubmitted service plan for Lancaster Crossing Metropolitan District Nos. 1-5 and a service plan for the 277 Metropolitan District on Sept. 29. Murata subdivision improvement agreements for Filings 2 and 3 were also considered.

fort-lupton/10.title: Energy feasibility MOU and Xcel/PSCO access agreement
fort-lupton/10.summary: Council approved an MOU with Performance Services for feasibility studies on solar, water, wastewater and infrastructure improvements. It also approved a temporary PSCO access agreement for boring and testing on the city parcel east of the South Platte River and north of the Fort site.
fort-lupton/10.where: City parcel east of the South Platte River, north of the Fort site

fort-lupton/11.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment
fort-lupton/11.summary: Council considered the city's Proposition 123 commitment for affordable housing for 2027-2029.

fort-lupton/12.title: Parks and Trails Vision Plan
fort-lupton/12.summary: Design Workshop presented an update on the Parks and Trails Vision Plan to council on Sept. 29.

fort-morgan/0.title: Police Chief Loren Sharp's departure and interim chief
fort-morgan/0.summary: Residents packed public comment on Oct. 6 and Oct. 20 to criticize how former Chief Loren Sharp left and to ask that he be rehired or a new chief be hired promptly. Council unanimously appointed Deputy Chief Steve Brown as Interim Chief on Oct. 20. One speaker urged revisiting the 2019 2E initiative on police oversight.

fort-morgan/1.title: Electric rate increase (Ordinance No. 1338)
fort-morgan/1.summary: Following a rate study presented in May, council passed first reading on Aug. 18 and held a public hearing Sept. 1. Resident Cynthia Ruppel opposed the increase, and council approved second reading of Ordinance No. 1338, saying the city passes on its power purchase costs.

fort-morgan/2.title: 2027 budget, mill levy and fee schedule
fort-morgan/2.summary: Council reviewed department expense budgets in August and September, with the City Manager adjusting direction after Cargill and Teamsters agreed on a labor contract. The Nov. 3 agenda includes the 2027 fee schedule and first reading of the budget and mill levy ordinance, with a public hearing set for Nov. 17.

fort-morgan/3.title: New aquatic facility and certificates of participation financing
fort-morgan/3.summary: The aquatic facility design was updated Oct. 6, with budget and timeline unchanged and excavation set to begin this fall. Council also took first reading of an ordinance authorizing certificates of participation to obtain funding.

fort-morgan/4.title: Pointe Village Commercial Park lot sale for grocery store
fort-morgan/4.summary: Council approved selling three lots (1.5 acres) in Pointe Village Commercial Park and a development agreement with K&M LLC on Sept. 1. The sale resolution appears again on the Nov. 3 agenda.

fort-morgan/5.title: Water supply: Riverside Irrigation lease and Southern Water Supply Project pipeline
fort-morgan/5.summary: On Oct. 20 council extended the Riverside Irrigation and Quality Water lease, which gives the city water during drought years. It also took up amending the allotment contract for the Southern Water Supply Project pipeline that carries CBT water to the treatment plant.

fort-morgan/6.title: Special use permit for apartment above 305-307 Main St.
fort-morgan/6.summary: Council approved a special use permit for new upstairs living space above a tattoo shop at 305-307 Main St. in the downtown corridor. The state health department requires a separate outdoor entry. No public comments were received.

fort-morgan/7.title: Northeast Colorado Health Department development agreement extension
fort-morgan/7.summary: Council extended the development agreement with the Northeast Colorado Health Department for two more years to help secure funding, which has been slow to come through grants.

fort-morgan/8.title: Airport apron expansion naming
fort-morgan/8.summary: The Airport Advisory Board continued discussing naming the aircraft parking apron expansion in honor of a person, and an obstruction light project update was on the October agenda.

foxfield/0.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption (Ordinance 2026-03)
foxfield/0.summary: The Board worked through the State-required Wildfire Resiliency Code from spring to summer 2026, with insurance implications and enforcement through building and fire officials discussed. Ordinance 2026-03 was approved after an Aug. 6 public hearing with no public comments. Trustees also pushed wildfire education with South Metro Fire, including grass height rules and a fire prevention meeting.

foxfield/1.title: Land Use Code update (Ordinance 2026-02)
foxfield/1.summary: The Board held a public hearing on rewriting Articles 1-6 of Chapter 16, continued it several times and postponed it, partly using an AI (Copilot) review of the code. It passed unanimously on Aug. 6, 2026 after a hearing with no public comments.

foxfield/2.title: Speeding data and radar speed signs
foxfield/2.summary: Trustees debated speed data, monitor placement and traffic calming after resident concerns. In July they moved to buy four solar radar signs with tracking software for Hindsdale and Waco. The roughly $22,373 purchase (Resolution 2026-08) was reconsidered in September, with a majority favoring a resident speeding-report tool on the website instead. Trustee Pakanati asked to bring it back when all Trustees could attend.

foxfield/3.title: Road maintenance: crack seal and pavement program
foxfield/3.summary: The Board approved the 2026 SEH engineering fee estimate and pavement repair program. In October it considered a Vance Brothers bid of $11,800 for additional crack seal, an added $6,300, after the first 2 tons did not cover all roads. It was approved in November after SEH explained the estimating shortfall. Emergency repairs on Arapahoe Road with Terracare were also ratified.

foxfield/4.title: Waco Street drainage, erosion and culvert repairs
foxfield/4.summary: Staff presented engineering recommendations on erosion and roadway deterioration near Waco Street and Arapahoe Road. The Board debated riprap versus seeding. In September it approved a revised Terracare quote that dropped the culvert cleanout, with work scheduled for fall.

foxfield/5.title: Home rule charter process
foxfield/5.summary: After a presentation from Town Attorney Corey Hoffmann, Trustees debated whether to start the home rule process, with some feeling it was being rushed. Staff laid out a timeline with a possible special election to form a charter commission in 2026 and a charter vote in 2027. Home rule authority and land use also came up in July.

foxfield/6.title: 2026 and 2027 budgets, taxes and falling sales tax
foxfield/6.summary: The 2026 budget, with general fund spending up about 25% mainly for speed-related items, was adopted after a hearing with no public attendance, and the property tax levy was approved (mill levy 4.982). Trustee Hodge noted sales tax has dropped significantly over four years and vacancies at Foxfield Village Center. A 2027 budget study session was set for November.

foxfield/7.title: Law enforcement (ACSO) and code enforcement contracts
foxfield/7.summary: The Board approved the 2026 Arapahoe County Sheriff's law enforcement agreement and a new SafeBUILT code enforcement agreement with revised rates. A 2027 ACSO agreement was on the November agenda.

foxfield/8.title: Street and tunnel lighting repairs
foxfield/8.summary: Trustees pursued repairs to non-working streetlights and tunnel lights, including S Lewiston Way and Parker Road. In August the Board approved a CLI Services proposal to replace three fixtures and a fuse kit.

foxfield/9.title: Short-term rental litigation
foxfield/9.summary: In July the Board discussed a Summary Judgment ruling in the town's short-term rental lawsuit and future steps.

foxfield/10.title: AI use policy for town staff
foxfield/10.summary: Staff proposed a policy governing AI use by employees and contractors, noting AI chats can be requested under the open records law (CORA).

fraser/0.title: Chapter 18 & 19 land development code rewrite (Ordinance 340/540)
fraser/0.summary: Planning Commission workshopped sweeping amendments to Fraser's land development and building codes, aiming for adoption by January 1, 2027 to meet the Proposition 123 fast-track requirement for affordable housing. Changes include plat-before-site-plan sequencing, water/sewer proof of service before building permits, fee waiver criteria, and drought/fire-resilient landscaping. The commission recommended adoption of the ordinance and it went to the Trustees in November; annexation policy was split off for separate discussion.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/1.title: St. Louis Landing workforce housing and New Markets Tax Credit financing
fraser/1.summary: Trustees and the Fraser Housing Authority approved resolutions authorizing New Markets Tax Credit actions, with financing going toward a playground and early childhood buildout. The Housing Authority then took up housing regulations, community rules, and initial rents and fees for the St. Louis Landing workforce housing development.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/2.title: Cornerstone v. Fraser litigation mediation
fraser/2.summary: The Board met in executive session on upcoming mediation in a conservation-related dispute, and a resolution approving a mediation submission agreement with Cornerstone was on the October 21 agenda. A November executive session again covered the mediation procedure for the litigation.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/3.title: Reassessment of water and sewer tap fees for changed water use
fraser/3.summary: The Board discussed legal options for reassessing water and sewer service fees on properties whose water usage has expanded or changed since the original tap fee. It was removed from one agenda but held in executive session on September 16 and listed again on October 7.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/4.title: 2027 Town budget and priorities
fraser/4.summary: The Trustees held budget workshops on the 2027 draft budget, presented October 7 by Finance Director Lorraine Waters. Staff expect the Town to be over budget in 2027, with sales tax revenue running about 6-7% below last year and big projects like Clayton Court and a planned public works building. A KFFR radio funding request was also on the agenda.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/5.title: Water restrictions, watershed and wastewater plant permit
fraser/5.summary: Trustees amended mandatory watering restrictions, issued a Water Supply Protection District permit for the public works fuel station at 150 County Road 72, and considered Windy Gap Environmental Fund and Upper Colorado Watershed Environment Team groundwater study resolutions. The joint wastewater committee is negotiating with the state over an appeal of the Upper Fraser Valley Wastewater Treatment Facility discharge permit.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/6.title: Transit budget and service options
fraser/6.summary: Trustees reviewed transit budget and service options and voted on one of the options; the documents do not say which.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/7.title: Meyer Lot No. 1 preliminary plat and encroachment license
fraser/7.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled a public hearing on the Meyer Lot No. 1 preliminary plat, with public comment attached to the packet. An encroachment license agreement was also recommended by the Planning Commission and moved to the Trustees on November 4.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/8.title: Downtown Development Authority 2027 budget and tax increment
fraser/8.summary: The DDA reviewed its preliminary 2027 budget, tax increment financing calculations with the County Assessor, and an intergovernmental agreement with the Town. Resolutions approving the 2027 budget and IGA were on the November 10 agenda.

fraser/9.title: Mural Fest, public art budget and Fire & Ice 2027
fraser/9.summary: The Public Arts Committee reported all 30 murals sold and discussed shifting toward building wall murals, which would need a larger budget. The roughly $91,000 art budget is unapproved and the committee agreed to hold off on 2027 sculpture purchases. Planning for the Fire & Ice festival covered logistics, fire safety, vendors and fireworks.

fraser/10.title: Ordinance 539 amending Chapters 2, 7 and 10
fraser/10.summary: Ordinance 539, Series 2026, amending Chapters 2, 7 and 10 of the municipal code, was listed for the November 4 meeting with an executive session on legal questions. The documents give no details on its content.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

frederick/0.title: Roads & Routes transportation sales tax and debt ballot measures
frederick/0.summary: The Board set ballot language for a sales and use tax for transportation infrastructure (Ordinance 1422) and for issuing debt for transportation projects (Ordinance 1423), and took up a Resolution 26-R-46 in support of a road tax. Staff and a Roads & Routes Taskforce ran a communications campaign with a potential 1% transportation tax, including videos, FAQs and signage.

frederick/1.title: 2027 budget process and 2026 budget amendment
frederick/1.summary: The Board held a budget introduction and workshops, adopted a budget amendment (Ordinance 1424), and held the first budget public hearing on Nov. 4. Action on the budget is expected after a second public hearing on Dec. 2, 2026.

frederick/2.title: Land Use Code bi-annual amendments (Ordinance 1425)
frederick/2.summary: The Planning Commission recommended amendments to the Land Use Code covering zoning, signs, parking, annexation, oil and gas and definitions. They include creating a marijuana retail use that is prohibited in all zoning districts and changing the permitted animals list. The Board scheduled a public hearing on Ordinance 1425 on Oct. 21.

frederick/3.title: Water rights, leases and reservoir treatment
frederick/3.summary: Water staff arranged a water lease with Wyndham Hill Metropolitan District, filed a Statement of Opposition in water court case 2026CW3081, and worked on Lower Boulder change-of-use. The town received a discharge permit effective Sept. 1, 2026 for phosphorus treatment to reduce algae in a reservoir. Large payments went to Central Weld County Water District for tap fees and to Northern Water for assessments.

frederick/4.title: Public Works & Parks Campus / Municipal Service Center construction
frederick/4.summary: Phase 1 (Building A and site improvements) is near completion on the new Public Works & Parks Campus, and Phase 2 (Fleet Shop and Warehouse) is underway. Monthly payment applications for the construction continue to be a major part of town spending.

frederick/5.title: Engineering Building mural and public art
frederick/5.summary: The Arts Committee wrote an RFP with a $19,000 budget and chose Laurie Cullum as the artist for the Engineering Building mural, with payment of 50% at signing, 25% at install start and 25% at completion. It also approved wood carvings in Crist Park and discussed hiring balloon artists for Frights on Fifth.

frederick/6.title: Parks, open space and trails planning and PROST role
frederick/6.summary: Parks staff presented design standards to the Planning Commission and are finishing the Parks Water Management, Golf Course and Urban Forestry plans for adoption this fall. The new PROST commission was onboarded and will discuss its future role.

sources.body: Parks, Recreation, Open Space & Trails Commission (PROST)
Parks, Recreation, Open Space & Trails Commission (PROST)

frederick/7.title: Historic preservation plan and Certified Local Government status
frederick/7.summary: The Historic Preservation Committee is working on plan goals and action items, a 2027 work plan, state historic fund grants, and the town's application to become a Certified Local Government. Resident Mike Sindelar spoke to the committee, and plaques for founding families were discussed.

frederick/8.title: Community grants and rent/utility assistance funding
frederick/8.summary: The Board reviewed a community grant application from a rent and utility assistance program, and the town applied for a state public health grant. Staff also presented a grants quarterly report and a Resolution 26-R-47 agreement with the St. Vrain Education Foundation.

frederick/9.title: Property and easement actions: KO Industrial conveyance, Wheatlands plat, utility easements
frederick/9.summary: The Board considered conveying Tract B of Del Camino South to KO Industrial LLC and vacating easements (Ordinance 1421), extending the Wheatlands preliminary plat expiration, and granting easements to United Power and St. Vrain Sanitation District.

frederick/10.title: Youth Commission funding and Youth Day
frederick/10.summary: The Youth Commission failed to secure grant funding and must seek sponsors, including from Erie, Firestone and Dacono. Youth Day was postponed over budget limits, and its mental health and bullying discussion was moved to later meetings.

fremont-county/0.title: 152-lot Planned Unit Development at 1337 County Road 3A
fremont-county/0.summary: A public hearing was scheduled for the Oct. 13 agenda on a Planned Unit Development proposing 152 lots at a minimum of 3 acres each, at 1337 County Road 3A near Cañon City. The documents do not state the outcome.

fremont-county/1.title: Cañon Dolomite Quarry truck traffic permit amendment
fremont-county/1.summary: Amrize asked to amend the truck traffic condition (Section K) of Conditional Use Permit 11-001 to use the "Annual Average Daily Traffic" wording from the original CDOT approval. The company says the quarry operates only a day or two per month and needs room for random sales surges, not more operating days.

fremont-county/2.title: Proposed 2027 county budget
fremont-county/2.summary: The commissioners scheduled public hearings on the proposed 2027 Fremont County budget for Oct. 27 and Nov. 10. Related items include the 2027 MotivHealth employee insurance proposal and a DHS building roof replacement bid.

fremont-county/3.title: Extra review fees billed to a developer who requested an outside consultant
fremont-county/3.summary: Planning & Zoning asked the board to bill an applicant for outside consultant review costs exceeding the application fee. The applicant had asked for the consultant after alleging staff bias, and Section 306 of the county resolution lets the board assess such fees.

fremont-county/4.title: Commissioners' positions on November ballot measures
fremont-county/4.summary: The Oct. 13 agenda included resolutions supporting Amendment 83 and opposing Amendment 87 (graduated income tax) and Proposition NN. The documents do not give votes.

fremont-county/5.title: Zone change from Business to Residential for a personal-use unit
fremont-county/5.summary: At a hearing on Aug. 25, an owner asked to rezone a lot from commercial to Residential One (R1) so a unit can be used personally and a full bathroom added.

fremont-county/6.title: Colorado River shortage and Lower Basin cuts
fremont-county/6.summary: A commissioner reported on Colorado Counties Inc. discussions about the Colorado River. The federal government, acting through the Bureau of Reclamation, required the Lower Basin to cut water use by 1.25 million acre-feet after the states failed to agree.

fremont-county/7.title: New liquor license and CDOT highway access for a restaurant/bar/mercantile
fremont-county/7.summary: Commissioners considered a new malt, vinous and spirituous license for a restaurant, bar and mercantile in a building with 134-person occupancy. The business needs a new CDOT highway access permit because the old one allowed only 20 trips a day, and a CDOT traffic study delayed by construction is now complete.

fremont-county/8.title: Airport consultant award and advisory board
fremont-county/8.summary: The board planned to approve an airport consultant services award and reappoint two Airport Advisory Board members. It also ratified a signature on an airport land document.

frisco/0.title: Fast-track affordable housing review (Prop 123) and Unified Development Code changes
frisco/0.summary: The Planning Commission held hearings in August on Unified Development Code amendments (allowed uses, accessory uses, parking) and a new fast-track review process for affordable housing to meet Proposition 123 requirements. Council took up Ordinances 26-17 and 26-18 on first reading Sept. 8 and second reading Sept. 22.

frisco/1.title: Short-term rental cap and licensing changes
frisco/1.summary: Staff asked Council on Oct. 13 whether income-restricted housing such as the Scout should count toward the total housing units used to calculate the cap on short-term rental licenses. Ordinance 26-14 amending STR licensing was on first reading Oct. 27 and second reading Nov. 10.

frisco/2.title: 2027 budget, mill levy and tax code changes
frisco/2.summary: Council discussed the 2027 budget Sept. 8, then took up the appropriation ordinance and mill levy ordinance in October and adopted-budget resolution Oct. 27 including a 2027-2031 plan. On Nov. 10 Council considered an ordinance revising town tax code, including eliminating the sales tax vendor's fee.

frisco/3.title: Ballot measures: Summit County Strong Future mill levy and school district 4A
frisco/3.summary: Council considered resolutions in support of Summit County's referred reauthorization of the Strong Future mill levy (not a new or increased tax) and of Summit School District Ballot Measure 4A, a mill levy override for teacher and staff pay. The Summit County Education Association presented on Oct. 13.

frisco/4.title: AC Marriott / CDOT I-70 Exit 203 settlement requests
frisco/4.summary: CDOT submitted three requests from AC Frisco to facilitate a settlement over parking modifications required on the hotel property due to the I-70 Exit 203 project. They cover snow storage, landscaping and confirmation of property matters, and Council was asked for direction.

frisco/5.title: Residential in Light Industrial district and ADU incentives
frisco/5.summary: Planning Commission scheduled hearings Nov. 5 on code changes to permit residential uses in the Light Industrial District and one or two dwelling units in mixed-use, and on incentives for accessory dwelling units.

frisco/6.title: 207 Granite Street eight-townhome sketch plan
frisco/6.summary: Commissioners reviewed a sketch plan for eight townhomes at 207 Granite Street. Issues included waivers for dumpster access and access from 2nd Avenue, a sidewalk along Granite, and fit with the historic park across the street. The CC zoning allows the use by right.

frisco/7.title: Sixth Degree Townhomes at 121 E Main Street
frisco/7.summary: Planning Commission conducted final review of a mixed-use project with six residential and two commercial units. Questions included parking lifts without a covenant, lighting compliance, and an unlocated water line.

frisco/8.title: Pioneer Park right-of-way vacation and 101 W Main telecom facility
frisco/8.summary: Planning Commission considered vacating a portion of right-of-way next to Pioneer Park, north of 99 N, and a special use permit for a new freestanding telecommunication facility at 101 W Main Street. Council also had an executive session on vacating town rights of way.

frisco/9.title: Council strategic plan retreat and water system update
frisco/9.summary: Council held an Aug. 25 retreat reviewing the strategic plan: infrastructure, water rates set for five years, housing, wildfire trail work and Terrain Park ski hill expansion. A strategic plan briefing and water systems update followed Oct. 27.

frisco/10.title: Downtown winter parking and Unsheltered in Summit license
frisco/10.summary: Council received a downtown winter parking update Sept. 22 and considered a revocable license agreement for Unsheltered in Summit on Oct. 13.

fruita/0.title: 2027 City Manager's recommended budget and Fremont Street/18 1/2 Road spending
fruita/0.summary: City Manager Shannon Vassen presented the 2027 budget on Sept. 29, with few big surprises and fewer, smaller capital projects. The largest is about $2 million to build J Road from Wildcat Avenue to Skiff Road, with grant funding being sought. On Oct. 20 resident Paul Schultz asked Council to halt the roughly $2.2 million Fremont Street to 18 1/2 Road expenditure, citing eminent domain use and cost overruns on 19 Road.

fruita/1.title: Metropolitan districts ordinance (Title 18)
fruita/1.summary: Ordinance 2026-20 would enact a new Title 18 of the municipal code on metropolitan districts, with a public hearing set for Nov. 17, 2026. A resident asked Council to pull it from the consent agenda on Oct. 20.

fruita/2.title: Fruita Co-op annexation and industrial rezone
fruita/2.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled on Oct. 13 to hear a request to annex about 40.16 acres into the city and rezone it to Industrial. The Co-op silo project is also being celebrated with art and tourism promotion.

fruita/3.title: Myers annexation and rezone at 1903 J Road
fruita/3.summary: A request to annex about 8.89 acres at 1903 J Road and rezone it to Community Residential (CR) was on the Planning Commission's Nov. 10 agenda.

fruita/4.title: Wake Harbor Houseboat Campground conditional use permit
fruita/4.summary: The Planning Commission was to consider a conditional use permit for a campground and RV park at 1081 16 Road on Nov. 10.

fruita/5.title: Water supply and strategic growth elements of the comprehensive plan
fruita/5.summary: State law requires Fruita to adopt Water Supply and Strategic Growth elements in its comprehensive plan. Staff sought Council feedback on community engagement and a water survey. A draft is due Dec. 31, 2026 for the city to be considered 'compliance in progress'. The mayor noted it is an unfunded state mandate, and the city is seeking a grant for a consultant.

fruita/6.title: CDOT US 6 West / SH 139 access control plan amendment
fruita/6.summary: CDOT presented an amendment to the access control plan for Highway 6 from 18 Road to 22 Road ahead of a future widening project. Concepts include right-in/right-out intersections with U-turns and alternate access for properties. An updated intergovernmental agreement is expected in January 2027.

fruita/7.title: Raptor Crossing PUD major amendment
fruita/7.summary: Council introduced Ordinance 2026-17 on first reading to amend the Raptor Crossing PUD guide to allow certain residential and other uses, with a public hearing set for Sept. 15, 2026.

fruita/8.title: Park conditions, drought water use and Farmers Market location
fruita/8.summary: The Parks and Recreation Commission discussed worn grass at Civic Center Park and possibly moving or alternating the Farmers Market with Reed Park. Salt Wash soccer fields are turning to dust as watering is reduced during drought. It also discussed e-scooter and off-road vehicle rules and community requests for more lap lanes at the community center.
fruita/8.where: Civic Center Park, Reed Park, Salt Wash fields

fruita/9.title: Bee City USA designation
fruita/9.summary: Council heard a proposal for Fruita to become the county's first Bee City, requiring a $200 annual fee and a Council resolution. Staff suggested the Livability or Parks and Recreation Commission take responsibility for the application.

fruita/10.title: Request for regular town halls
fruita/10.summary: Resident Jeffrey Louden asked Council on Sept. 15 to hold town halls regularly so residents can have two-way conversations rather than just public comment.

fruita/11.title: Municipal court judge appointment
fruita/11.summary: After final interviews in executive session on Sept. 22, Council recommended that the City Manager negotiate a contract with the preferred candidate for municipal court judge. Ordinance 2026-16 on municipal judges' powers was also introduced in August.

garden-city/0.title: New police station construction (Mark Young Construction)
garden-city/0.summary: The Board repeatedly approved Mark Young Construction change orders (Nos. 004-010) and monthly invoices, including a $301,598.32 invoice for November billing and a June 2026 invoice, for the Police Department project. The documents list the items but do not give a total project cost.

garden-city/1.title: 2026 budget, tax levy and employee raises
garden-city/1.summary: The Board held a public hearing on the 2026 budget in November, then on December 9 considered a 4% cost-of-living raise, a larger health insurance stipend for employees, and resolutions adopting the budget, appropriating funds and levying the general property tax.

garden-city/2.title: Town Administrator/Clerk transition and Cheryl Campbell's resignation
garden-city/2.summary: In July 2026 the Board discussed the transition of the Town Administrator/Town Clerk position once Linda Blackston starts, approved Cheryl Campbell's resignation letter, and took up an employment agreement and a related resolution. The Board also considered alternate attorney options.

garden-city/3.title: Revitalization grant programs for businesses and homes
garden-city/3.summary: The Board extended the Commercial Revitalization Grant Program and the Single Family Residential Revitalization Grant Program for 2026 and reviewed the final grant for El Rodeo Night Club LLC. A pavement-related program was also extended.

garden-city/4.title: Incentive for Award Alliance
garden-city/4.summary: Award Alliance's Paul Hlad presented to the Board in November, and in December the Board considered Resolution 13-2025 providing an incentive for the company.

garden-city/5.title: Electric and solar ready building code adoption (Ordinance 11-2025)
garden-city/5.summary: The Board introduced Ordinance 11-2025 adopting the 2023 Electric and Solar Ready Code and the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code by reference, and held a public hearing on December 9, 2025.

garden-city/6.title: Marijuana business licenses and Star Buds ownership change
garden-city/6.summary: The Board reviewed several retail marijuana store, cultivation and manufacturing licenses and renewals. It approved the change of ownership of Star Buds (Vireo Health of Noco, 2502 8th Ave) in January and considered a further license for that business in July.

garden-city/7.title: Special review use approval, Northern Colorado Driveline and election planning
