garden-city/7.summary: In July 2026 the Board adopted Resolution 10-2026 granting a Use by Special Review, discussed Northern Colorado Driveline, and discussed the coordinated election and an intergovernmental agreement for it. The minutes do not give details of the property or decisions.

garden-city/8.title: Weld County Community Development Block Grant agreement
garden-city/8.summary: The Board approved an intergovernmental agreement for the conduct of the Community Development Block Grant program in Weld County.

garfield-county/0.title: 2027 county budget hearings and supplemental appropriations
garfield-county/0.summary: Commissioners held 2027 proposed budget hearings in October, heard an MGT workforce analysis, and took up 2026 Budget Supplement #4 and a $234,039 supplement in November. Requests included $150,000 for Garfield Clean Energy, a $90,000 Housing Authority request and Human Services Commission grants.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session
Board of County Commissioners - Budget Hearings

garfield-county/1.title: Affordable housing: USDA programs, Housing Authority, Cavern Springs and Oak Meadows
garfield-county/1.summary: The board heard USDA Rural Development on affordable housing, a Housing Authority update and annual report with a $90,000 2027 request. A letter of support was requested for the Cavern Springs Mobile Home Park partnership, the Oak Meadows Ranch Filing 4B affordable housing plan amendment was signed, and a Glenwood Springs Association housing summit whitepaper was presented.
garfield-county/1.where: Countywide; Cavern Springs Mobile Home Park; Oak Meadows Ranch

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session

garfield-county/2.title: Mitchell Creek Community PUD rezoning on Highway 6/24
garfield-county/2.summary: Planning Commission held a public hearing on rezoning from Rural to PUD and a major subdivision sketch plan for the Mitchell Creek Community PUD at 50235 Highway 6/24 near Glenwood Springs. The owner is AMICHAUX Limited Partnership LLLP.

garfield-county/3.title: McClure River Ranch PUD amendment and 12-lot preliminary plan
garfield-county/3.summary: Commissioners were asked to sign resolutions approving a substantial PUD amendment for the 98-acre McClure River Ranch and a preliminary plan dividing 48.96 acres into 12 lots and 2 tracts, east of Carbondale. The applicant is Aspen Polo Partners.

garfield-county/4.title: Lake Springs Ranch PUD amendment and Hogback View Estates subdivision
garfield-county/4.summary: Planning Commission considered a substantial PUD amendment, preliminary plan and rezoning for Lake Springs Ranch off County Road 114. Commissioners also were asked to sign the preliminary plan resolution for Hogback View Estates east of New Castle.
garfield-county/4.where: 4001 County Road 114, Glenwood Springs; 24 County Road 138, east of New Castle

garfield-county/5.title: Xcel Hopkins to Basalt transmission line rebuild
garfield-county/5.summary: Planning Commission reviewed the location and extent of Xcel's Hopkins to Basalt Line 9256 rebuild, starting at the Hopkins Substation near Red Canyon Road. Xcel also gave a presentation to commissioners in October.
garfield-county/5.where: Hopkins Substation, Red Canyon Road and Fisher Cemetery Road, east of Carbondale

garfield-county/6.title: Parachute road and transit funding
garfield-county/6.summary: Parachute requested $600,000 toward the 1st Street/US 6 reconstruction (Parachute MOVES), plus disbursement of $200,000 in 2026 funding and a 2027 request for the Parachute Area Transit System. A draft RFTA Traveler IGA and senior programs MOU were also under review.

garfield-county/7.title: Madison AI assistant for county staff
garfield-county/7.summary: Commissioners were asked to approve a $43,200 supplemental appropriation and a Carahsoft contract for a 12-month Madison AI subscription, with a countywide assistant and a Community Development assistant.

garfield-county/8.title: Sheriff's Office early retirement incentive and grants
garfield-county/8.summary: Commissioners considered a resolution for a voluntary early retirement incentive program for the Sheriff's Office. They also considered applying for a $39,903 opioid grant for inmate MAT medications and a $12,100 bulletproof vest grant.

garfield-county/9.title: Garfield County School of Innovation lease at 949 Railroad Avenue
garfield-county/9.summary: Judy Brannberg asked to lease a county-owned property at 949 Railroad Avenue to house the planned Garfield County School of Innovation.

garfield-county/10.title: Colorado River District update and Shoshone water rights
garfield-county/10.summary: The Colorado River District gave an annual update including the Shoshone Water Rights Preservation project. The county also considered a letter of support for the Rifle Creek watershed restoration project.

garfield-county/11.title: Rifle Garfield County Airport repairs and contracts
garfield-county/11.summary: The county ratified an emergency roof repair contract, awarded fuel tank cleaning and concrete improvement contracts at the airport.

gilpin-county/0.title: Rollinsville area fire-protection cistern projects
gilpin-county/0.summary: The county considered Resolution 26-085 to develop a fire-protection cistern for the Rollinsville area, choosing between the East/Gold Dirt and West/Public Works sites. By Sept. 8 the resolution covered coordinated procurement of both cistern projects.

gilpin-county/1.title: Ordinance 26-01 on rental regulations
gilpin-county/1.summary: Commissioners held a first reading of Ordinance 26-01 on Aug. 25 and a second reading at a public hearing on Sept. 22. The ordinance concerns rental regulations and was presented by Community Development and the County Attorney.

gilpin-county/2.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing credits and commitment
gilpin-county/2.summary: The county considered an intergovernmental agreement on Proposition 123 affordable housing unit credits (Resolution 26-086) and later authorized filing an affordable housing commitment (Resolution 26-098).

gilpin-county/3.title: Wildfire mitigation, restrictions and grants
gilpin-county/3.summary: The county reduced Stage 2 fire restrictions to Stage 1 on Sept. 8 and removed restrictions on Oct. 26. It also committed $51,000 over three years to the Clear Creek Watershed & Forest Health Partnership's wildfire grant application, and discussed wildfire defense grant coordination, the Community Wildfire Protection Plan and a letter of support for the Dove Creek Ranch fuels reduction project.

gilpin-county/4.title: County roadway designation and road manual
gilpin-county/4.summary: A public hearing on Aug. 25 covered Resolution 26-084 designating and classifying county roadways and Resolution 26-088 adopting the county roadway manual.

gilpin-county/5.title: 2027 budget and 2026 supplemental appropriations
gilpin-county/5.summary: Commissioners saw the proposed 2027 draft budget on Sept. 22 and later considered supplemental appropriations to the 2026 budget. Employee benefits renewal for 2027 and the 2026 compensation plan were also on agendas.

gilpin-county/6.title: Comprehensive fee schedule and parks fee/equipment plan
gilpin-county/6.summary: The county reviewed its comprehensive fee schedule on Sept. 8 and Resolution 26-093 updating it was on the Sept. 22 agenda. A parks and recreation fee structure and equipment purchase plan was also discussed.

gilpin-county/7.title: November ballot issues
gilpin-county/7.summary: The county referred a ballot issue to voters (Resolution 26-077) and discussed upcoming ballot propositions. A resolution also dealt with the November election involving the City of Central and Timberline Fire.

gilpin-county/8.title: Veterans Service Officer shared role and IGA
gilpin-county/8.summary: Commissioners discussed a shared Veterans Service Officer role and then considered Resolution 26-096, an intergovernmental agreement for the VSO.

gilpin-county/9.title: Code enforcement policy and public records request process
gilpin-county/9.summary: A draft code enforcement process policy was discussed. The county also amended its public records request policy (Resolution 26-090) and heard an update on the CORA process and fees.

gilpin-county/10.title: COMBA bike trail outside I-70 project
gilpin-county/10.summary: A bike trail project by COMBA outside the I-70 corridor was on the Aug. 18 agenda.

glendale/0.title: 2027 city budget and 2026 tax levy
glendale/0.summary: Council introduced Ordinances 6, 7 and 8 on Oct. 6 to adopt the city budget, appropriate money and levy 2026 taxes, then held public hearings on them Nov. 10. The documents do not state the final votes or amounts.

glendale/1.title: Water and sewer rate and fee increases
glendale/1.summary: On Nov. 10 council took up Ordinance 9 revising water rates and fees, and Ordinance 10 revising sewer user and connection fees. Ordinance 11 amends Chapter 13.06 of the city code. These were introduced and no outcome is recorded.

glendale/2.title: Xcel Energy franchise agreement
glendale/2.summary: Council considered a resolution on the franchise granted to Public Service Company of Colorado (Xcel) under ballot Question 2B, approving a franchise agreement.

glendale/3.title: Four Mile Project legal advice
glendale/3.summary: Council went into executive session for legal advice on the Four Mile Project at both its Oct. 6 and Nov. 10 meetings. The agendas give no further detail.

glendale/4.title: Entertainment Advisory Board activities and budget
glendale/4.summary: The Entertainment Advisory Board reviewed its Sept. 1 presentation to council, held team discussions and discussed its budget and plans for proposed activities. Infinity Park also appeared as a council discussion item.

glendale/5.title: Ordinance 5 correcting reference numbers in Ordinance 1
glendale/5.summary: Council introduced an ordinance amending and correcting reference numbers from Ordinance No. 1 of 2026, with a public hearing on Nov. 10.

glenwood-springs/0.title: Short-term and accessory tourist rental rules
glenwood-springs/0.summary: Planning and Zoning reviewed a code amendment requiring permit holders to actually rent and remit lodging tax in order to renew short-term rental and accessory tourist rental permits. Council took up Ordinance 2026-22 on Sept. 17, with an amendment to a minimum of 20 nights and $150 in sales tax remitted over two years, and it returned on the Oct. 1 consent agenda.

glenwood-springs/1.title: Xcel transmission line rebuild (6584 line)
glenwood-springs/1.summary: Xcel Energy is replacing aging wood poles on the 6584 transmission line with steel monopoles and widening easements to reduce wildfire risk. Planning and Zoning considered the Location and Extent permit and a 1041 recommendation, and the 1041 application went to City Council on Nov. 5.
glenwood-springs/1.where: Glenwood Springs portion of the 6584 transmission line

glenwood-springs/2.title: Canyon Vista affordable housing at 51993 Hwy 6 & 24
glenwood-springs/2.summary: The 80-unit affordable multifamily project on about 4 acres between Highway 6 and Donegan Road needed a preliminary plat to merge three parcels into one lot. Planning and Zoning reviewed it with six recommended conditions, then Council took up the plat and a right-of-way encroachment license on Oct. 15. Revised water service agreements followed on Nov. 5.
glenwood-springs/2.where: 51993 Hwy 6 & 24, between Highway 6 and Donegan Road

glenwood-springs/3.title: 130 Midland affordable homeownership funding request
glenwood-springs/3.summary: Council considered a funding request for the 130 Midland affordable homeownership project on Oct. 1 and continued it on Oct. 15. A tour of the Habitat project, The Confluence at 8th and Midland, was planned for Nov. 5.
glenwood-springs/3.where: 130 Midland Avenue / The Confluence at 8th and Midland

glenwood-springs/4.title: Bennett Avenue parking and 1600 Bennett fee-in-lieu request
glenwood-springs/4.summary: Five residents spoke at the Sept. 3 council meeting about parking on Bennett Avenue. Council later had a parking fee-in-lieu request for 1600 Bennett on its Oct. 1 agenda.

glenwood-springs/5.title: 2027 city budget and fees
glenwood-springs/5.summary: Council received the 2027 budget presentation on Oct. 1, held a public budget hearing on Oct. 15, and had a resolution approving the 2027 budget on the Nov. 5 agenda. Related items included a 2026 appropriation amendment, the 2027 Tourism Promotion Fund budget, 2027 landfill fees and the 2027 parks and recreation fee schedule.

glenwood-springs/6.title: Fire tax ballot issue and coordinated election
glenwood-springs/6.summary: Council took up a resolution certifying a ballot issue and setting its ballot title, and held public comment. It also approved an intergovernmental agreement with Garfield County for the 2026 coordinated election. The mayor spoke in support of the fire tax.

glenwood-springs/7.title: Pay as You Throw trash contract and haul route weight limits
glenwood-springs/7.summary: Council discussed and then scheduled action on a Pay as You Throw contract with Mountain Waste and Recycling. A councilor also asked for support to study street weight limits and designated haul routes.

glenwood-springs/8.title: Ride Glenwood on-demand pricing and transportation planning
glenwood-springs/8.summary: Council scheduled action on pricing for the Ride Glenwood on-demand service on Oct. 15, alongside a comprehensive transportation discussion. A joint work session with the Transportation Commission was set for Oct. 1.

glenwood-springs/9.title: Electric vehicle charging regulations
glenwood-springs/9.summary: Council considered Ordinance 2026-18 amending the municipal code on regulating and permitting electric vehicle charging projects. It later appeared on the Sept. 3 consent agenda.

glenwood-springs/10.title: Water litigation and Hot Springs Pool raw water contract
glenwood-springs/10.summary: Council went into executive session on litigation involving the Mitchell-Cooper Ditch and Pipeline Company and JG Housing Solutions, LLC. Another executive session concerned negotiations on the Hot Springs Pool raw water delivery contract.

golden/0.title: The Junction urban renewal plan and tax increment financing
golden/0.summary: GURA is weighing a new urban renewal area for The Junction, a 51-acre light industrial business park at 5079 State Highway 93. The developer says it is not feasible without tax increment financing. About $59 million in public improvements are needed, including a Highway 93 roundabout and a pedestrian bridge to the North Table Mountain trailhead. Staff proposed revenue-sharing with the county and city, and a subcommittee recommended explicitly excluding data centers from the plan.

sources.body: City Council Exec Session 4:30pm-Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm
City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm

golden/1.title: Fire Department incident, independent investigation and City Manager separation
golden/1.summary: Council hired outside counsel to oversee an independent investigation of an incident at the Fire Department, with closed legal sessions and a contract amended on September 15. Council also approved a City Manager separation agreement and an acting city manager agreement in August. The REDI Task Force discussed community concerns about racial profiling and healing.

sources.body: City Council Exec Session 4:30pm-Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm
City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm
City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 6:30pm

golden/2.title: Flock Safety cameras and data retention
golden/2.summary: Council took up the police department's use of Flock cameras and its contract. Staff gave a presentation on data retention, and Council considered deactivating the cameras or terminating the contract.

sources.body: City Council Exec Session 4:30pm-Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm

golden/3.title: 2027-2028 biennial budget and revenue outlook
golden/3.summary: The Citizens' Budget Advisory Committee reviewed the proposed 2027-28 operating and capital budget. Sales tax is projected to grow about 1% a year while property tax and use tax are expected to dip. Council planned final adoption on December 8, 2026. The advisory committee also recommended more marijuana tax money for rent assistance and food insecurity.

sources.body: City Council Exec Session 4:30pm-Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm

golden/4.title: 2122 Jackson Street development and alley spur
golden/4.summary: Council called up the site plans for 2122 Jackson Street so the Planning Commission could review the alley spur and the whole project. Neighbors raised concerns about the narrow alley, parking, trash, lighting and green space. In October a Jackson Street resident objected to the approval, citing snow removal and other concerns.

sources.body: City Council Study Session & Regular Business Meeting

golden/5.title: South Golden Road speeding and complete street project
golden/5.summary: Residents urged Council to slow traffic on South Golden Road, which they called the 'South Golden Speedway.' They asked that the complete street project be split so the first segment moves ahead before the budget is approved in November. They cited about 18,000 vehicles a day, a petition and difficulty turning left.

sources.body: City Council Study Session & Regular Business Meeting

golden/6.title: Clayworks natural gas amendment
golden/6.summary: The Clayworks development asked to amend its Official Development Plan to allow limited natural gas for pool and spa heating, fireplaces and communal grills. The sustainability board heard residents urge the project to keep its all-electric commitments. The request is under staff review and will go to Planning Commission and Council. The mobility board also tracked its parking and travel demand plan.

golden/7.title: Lions Park playground, GOCO grant and public art
golden/7.summary: The Lions Park nature play and outdoor playground redesign advanced, with a Great Outdoors Colorado grant resolution approved. The Arts and Culture Commission picked 'Pollinators at Play' by Alexander Bond from three finalists for the park's public art.

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting
ACC Lion's Park Art Selection Panel Meeting - No Recording

golden/8.title: Special events impacts and grants
golden/8.summary: A west 10th Street resident asked for a broader review of how events affect parking and traffic. The Special Events Review Committee also reviewed 2026 grant requests of about $37,800 against a $40,000 budget and a new event grant request of up to $5,000 for shuttles. The Community Marketing Board planned satellite parking and shuttles for a summer event.

golden/9.title: Visit Golden marketing contract and budget
golden/9.summary: Council approved a services agreement with DVA Advertising for community marketing. The Community Marketing Board reviewed its 2027-28 budget and strategic plan, and asked for more itemized detail. The program is funded by suspending the sales tax vendor fee credit. The DDA was asked to contribute $7,500 to a KOSI and Golden Hotel holiday promotion.

golden/10.title: Nazarene affordable housing plan area and TIF agreement
golden/10.summary: GURA is reviewing a draft tax increment agreement for the Nazarene project at 17455 West 16th Avenue. Changes focus on making affordable housing commitments survive any sale and raising the income cap from 30% to 35% to match state grant definitions. Council also approved Proposition 123 and housing intergovernmental agreements, and heard a Rental Housing Inventory Report.

sources.body: City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm

golden/11.title: Downtown DDA grants, parking and tree planting
golden/11.summary: The Downtown Development Authority considered emergency repair grants for 807 13th Street and a $25,000 sewer repair grant at 1200 Washington Avenue. It also began a downtown parking data review and planned street tree planting on Arapahoe Street. Staff recommended a two-year holiday lights contract extension.

golden/12.title: Sustainability programs: water conservation, recycling and energy benchmarking
golden/12.summary: The sustainability board reviewed 2026 water conservation and drought response, a universal recycling ordinance starting with hauler licensing, EV charging fees and overnight overstay rules, and a proposed commercial energy benchmarking program. The board favored a voluntary pilot, and recommended raising rebates to $200,000 in 2027.

golden/13.title: 2027 recreation service fees
golden/13.summary: Staff proposed 2027 fee changes for athletic fields, Splash, the community center, the RV park and the golf club. Credit card users would pay a processing fee of up to 3% starting in early 2027. Council reviews the full fee schedule in early December.

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Study Session

golden/14.title: Historic preservation cases
golden/14.summary: The Historic Preservation Board approved a certificate of appropriateness for a new cottage at 2024 Ford Street, and reviewed demolition requests for 612 10th Street and 403 18th Street.

granby/0.title: Data center workshop
granby/0.summary: The Board of Trustees held a data center workshop led by the Town Manager at its August 25, 2026 meeting. The documents do not say what was decided.

granby/1.title: Zoning code rewrite and new zoning map (Ordinance 1041)
granby/1.summary: The Board held public hearings on August 25 and September 22 on Ordinance 1041. It would comprehensively amend Chapter 16 of the municipal code (the zoning regulations) and adopt a legislative update to the official zoning map.

granby/2.title: Ten Mile Crossing planned development
granby/2.summary: The Planning Commission heard the preliminary plat and preliminary plan for the Ten Mile Crossing Planned Development Overlay District on October 5. The Board of Trustees took up the preliminary plan, subject to conditions, in a public hearing on October 13.

granby/3.title: Nuche Village apartments agreement, funding and hearing board
granby/3.summary: The Board dealt with the Nuche Village apartment project repeatedly. It considered extending the agreement on September 8, funding on October 13 and the contract on October 27, and also appointed a Nuche Village hearing board member.

granby/4.title: Town Manager separation and recruitment
granby/4.summary: The Board ratified and considered a Town Manager separation agreement on September 8, after executive sessions on the manager's employment. It then discussed interim manager and recruitment arrangements on October 13 and the transition on October 27.

granby/5.title: New police chief contract and oath
granby/5.summary: The Board considered a contract for the Police Chief on September 22. The chief's oath of office was scheduled for October 13.

granby/6.title: Annexation proceedings and GRCO annexation
granby/6.summary: On September 22 the Board considered a resolution initiating annexation proceedings and setting a hearing on whether certain lands are eligible to be annexed. On October 27 it took up an annexation consideration for GRCO.

granby/7.title: 2027 town budget and Grand Elk and Granby West improvement district budgets
granby/7.summary: The Board discussed the 2027 Town budget on October 13, and the Grand Elk General Improvement District budget the same day. On November 10 it took up budget, appropriation and mill levy ordinances for the Grand Elk and Granby West improvement districts.
granby/7.where: Grand Elk Ranch and Granby West

granby/8.title: Grand Elk property conveyance and metro district dissolution
granby/8.summary: The Grand Elk Ranch GID considered Ordinance 81 on October 27, authorizing the conveyance of real property related to the Village at Buckhorn. The Board also considered consenting to the dissolution of Granby West Metropolitan District No. 7 and conditionally accepting public improvements for the Granby Elementary School project.
granby/8.where: Grand Elk Ranch / Village at Buckhorn

granby/9.title: Parks planning, Bark Park pond and parks staffing
granby/9.summary: The Board discussed the Bark Park pond on October 13. On October 27 it discussed parks planning and a Parks and Rec position.

granby/10.title: Alley traffic concerns and Mediate Colorado
granby/10.summary: On September 8 the Board discussed alley traffic concerns and a possible arrangement with Mediate Colorado. The documents give no details.

granby/11.title: 843 Saddle Ridge hearing for Granby Sanitation District
granby/11.summary: A public hearing was scheduled September 22 on 843 Saddle Ridge for the Granby Sanitation District.

granby/12.title: Revegetation and CSFS grant update
granby/12.summary: Resident Daniela Gosselova gave the Board an update on revegetation and a Colorado State Forest Service grant on August 25.

grand-county/0.title: 2027 county budget hearings and final budget approval
grand-county/0.summary: Commissioners held departmental budget hearings Oct. 5-9, with a five-year projection and rebuttals on Nov. 4. A final budget determination and approval was scheduled for Nov. 10. The Middle Park Fair and Rodeo board also scheduled its own 2027 budget approval for Nov. 9.

grand-county/1.title: Ridge Point Townhomes sketch plan near Winter Park
grand-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a request to turn an earlier 8-unit approval into a 6-unit townhome subdivision on Lot 27, Winter Park Ranch Second Filing Replat, with access from County Road 834. Staff recommended approval with eight conditions, including a landscape plan, radon mitigation and paved, engineered roads. Separately, commissioners were to consider a partial release of funds for Ridgeview Townhomes.
grand-county/1.where: Lot 27, Block 1, Winter Park Ranch Second Filing Replat, off County Road 834

grand-county/2.title: Departmental fee changes and subdivision regulation amendments
grand-county/2.summary: Commissioners scheduled a public hearing on Grand County departmental fee changes on Oct. 20 and a hearing on amendments to the county Subdivision Regulations on Oct. 27. A building permit fee refund request was also on the Nov. 10 agenda.

grand-county/3.title: Planning Commission special use permits: auto repair shops, Summit Trail Townhomes and event rules
grand-county/3.summary: The Nov. 12 Planning Commission agenda included special use permits for Guz's Auto and Wyatt's Performance Auto and Diesel, a sketch plan for Summit Trail Townhomes, and zoning amendments that would require a special use permit for events and gatherings in unincorporated Grand County.

grand-county/4.title: Self-storage building code appeals on U.S. Highway 34
grand-county/4.summary: The Board of Appeals was set to hear two appeals over how the county's adopted building code applies to Stillwater Storage at 9405 U.S. Highway 34 and the Storage at the Fort/Uplift project at 10393 U.S. Highway 34.

grand-county/5.title: Historic Preservation Board seeks to restore Certified Local Government status
grand-county/5.summary: The newly organized board named restoring the county's Certified Local Government status as its top priority, and the chair will contact History Colorado about requirements. It also discussed historic surveys, landmark designations and a countywide preservation plan. A resident asked what resources can qualify for designation.

grand-county/6.title: Special use permits and temporary use hearings: St. Joseph's retreat camping and Grand Lake Skijoring
grand-county/6.summary: Commissioners scheduled a public hearing on a camping special use permit for the St. Joseph's Foundation Retreat on Oct. 20. A temporary use permit for Colorado Skijoring (Grand Lake Skijoring) was continued from Oct. 13 to Oct. 27.

grand-county/7.title: Road hearings, traffic code and plow truck purchase
grand-county/7.summary: Commissioners were to hold a second reading of the Model Traffic Code amendment (Ordinance 23) on Oct. 20. County road hearings continued from Sept. 22 were set for Nov. 10 along with a plow truck purchase order.

grand-county/8.title: Master plan update and blight penalty certification
grand-county/8.summary: Commissioners planned a Nov. 10 workshop on the county Master Plan update. They also had a resolution certifying blight violation penalties for a property at 115 CR 6421.

grand-junction/0.title: 2027 city budget and structural deficit
grand-junction/0.summary: Staff reported a $6 million General Fund structural gap and presented a $317.4 million 2027 budget ($120.8 million General Fund) with about $2 million in personnel cuts, reduced Lincoln Park Pool hours, and some housing programs moved to community partners. It adds six police officers and three fire battalion chiefs, and utility and golf fee increases were discussed. The first appropriation hearing was set for Nov. 4 with a second on Nov. 18.

grand-junction/1.title: Temporary moratorium on large data centers
grand-junction/1.summary: Staff proposed an ordinance pausing applications for large data centers while the city writes land-use rules, since current code doesn't address them and their electricity and water demands could be large. No applications are pending. Council wanted coordination with Mesa County and utilities and asked about other high-water industries. An ordinance with a 365-day maximum was introduced Oct. 7 for a hearing Oct. 21.

grand-junction/2.title: Significant Tree Ordinance removed from development code
grand-junction/2.summary: At the Housing Affordability Code Task Force's request, Council considered repealing the significant tree and mature tree protections in the Development Code, and voted to remove them. The Forestry Board expressed disappointment, noting strong public support, and a consultant review may bring an alternative, possibly incentive-based, later. The board is considering focusing on public trees.

grand-junction/3.title: Housing Affordability Code Task Force and Housing Action Plan
grand-junction/3.summary: The task force is working with consultant KLJ to simplify the Development Code and TEDS manual to cut housing costs, with the effort aimed to finish in the first quarter of 2027. Council also reviewed a revised Housing Action Plan, which dropped a proposed Housing Advisory Board and moved exploring new housing revenue to years four to six. It goes to a public hearing for adoption after DOLA review.

grand-junction/4.title: 2911 D 1/2 Road annexation, mixed-use rezone and apartments
grand-junction/4.summary: Anthony Properties and Davenport and Company seek annexation of 14.88 acres, MU-2 zoning, and a Comprehensive Plan change from Residential Medium to Mixed Use for a potential multi-unit apartment complex. A Circulation Plan amendment to relocate planned roads is expected later. Council set a public hearing for Dec. 16; the Planning Commission was to consider it Nov. 10.

grand-junction/5.title: Lincoln Park Barn and Certified Local Government
grand-junction/5.summary: The Historic Preservation Board is weighing whether to pursue Certified Local Government status, which could require design standards in historic districts. Residents asked the board to nominate the Lincoln Park Barn for designation, and members asked staff to schedule a special meeting on it.

grand-junction/6.title: Rural fire and EMS costs and regional fire district
grand-junction/6.summary: Staff cited the cost of providing rural fire and EMS service as a major budget pressure and plan to give the Rural Fire District the required two-year notice to renegotiate. The city is pursuing a regional fire district as a long-term funding solution.

grand-junction/7.title: Water supply plan and turf conversion/water conservation
grand-junction/7.summary: Staff presented the state-required Water Supply Element for the Comprehensive Plan, saying current supplies meet current and projected needs. Separately, the Forestry Board discussed turf conversion's effect on mature trees, and Council supported a Bureau of Reclamation grant for piping the Juniata Enlarged Ditch, which loses about 1,400 acre-feet annually.

grand-junction/8.title: Persigo sewer budget and lift station
grand-junction/8.summary: The recommended 2027 Persigo wastewater budget totals $69.9 million, about $49.7 million of it for capital projects, with delayed projects and $4.5 million in unplanned needs. Council also authorized buying property at 354 Bonny Street for a new sewer lift station.

grand-junction/9.title: HomewardBound shelter funding request
grand-junction/9.summary: HomewardBound of the Grand Valley asked Council for $225,000 for operating its 29 Road consolidated shelter, then submitted an updated pay-for-performance proposal including $1,500 per person moved into non-shelter housing. It is not in the recommended budget, and staff want more time to evaluate it.

grand-junction/10.title: Matchett Park bike park future
grand-junction/10.summary: A survey showed strong support for keeping the unsanctioned bike park at Matchett Park. Given budget challenges, the Parks board moved to hold off on further development.

grand-junction/11.title: Rezones and right-of-way vacations (24 Road area, Inland Avenue, 2324 Hwy 6 & 50)
grand-junction/11.summary: Council passed a rezone of 13.04 acres at 675 26 Road and Galley Lane from R-1R to RL-4, and moved on vacating Inland Avenue right-of-way near Westgate Drive. A rezone of 2.88 acres at 2324 Hwy 6 & 50 from I-1 to commercial advanced with Planning Commission approval.

grand-junction/12.title: Materials Recovery Facility financing
grand-junction/12.summary: Council passed Ordinance 5338 authorizing an additional $9.3 million in Certificates of Participation to finish acquisition of the city's Materials Recovery Facility. No public comments.

grand-junction/13.title: Arts commission funding overhaul and Riverfront murals
grand-junction/13.summary: The Arts & Culture Commission moved to general operating support with a $4,500 cap, dropped its "does not fund" list, and selected artists for Riverfront Trail murals. A Las Colonias firefighter memorial was also proposed.

grand-lake/0.title: Land Use Code overhaul: definitions, shoreline rules and development review (Ordinances 13-2026 to 27-2026)
grand-lake/0.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed amendments (Resolutions 08-2026 and 10-2026) to Chapter 12 of the town code. They move definitions out of several sections, drop the certified-mail notice requirement, create a new Certifications section and clarify development review thresholds and procedures. The Board of Trustees scheduled a public hearing and first reading of Ordinances 13-2026 through 27-2026 for Nov. 9.

grand-lake/1.title: 2027 town budget and public hearing
grand-lake/1.summary: The Board held workshops on Sept. 28 and Oct. 8 and reviewed the draft 2027 budget on Oct. 12 and 26, including wages and benefits compared with other municipalities. The preliminary budget shows $7.51M of General Fund revenue, of which $2.87M is grant money tied to four specific projects. A public hearing on the FY 2027 budget was set for Nov. 9, with final approval planned for Nov. 23.

grand-lake/2.title: Major subdivision at 120 County Road 663
grand-lake/2.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on the final development application and final plat for a major subdivision on property annexed in 2025. Staff flagged concerns about fire and emergency access, the road improvements needed, protecting the water main under County Road 663 that supplies all of Grand Lake, and stormwater and flood risk after the post-fire flooding.

grand-lake/3.title: Shoreline and side/front yard setback variances
grand-lake/3.summary: The Board of Adjustment heard variance requests for 536 Cairns Avenue, including a side yard setback for a separate staircase, which neighbors spoke in support of, and a front yard setback for an elevator. A shoreline setback variance (Resolution 08-2026) had a notice error naming the wrong hearing body, since shoreline variances go to the Planning Commission. The Trustees were set to hear a shoreline variance (Resolution 87-2026) for a property on Mad.

grand-lake/4.title: Boots, Bass & Big Air downtown winter event
grand-lake/4.summary: Trustees discussed a proposed downtown winter event on Saturday, January 30, 2027, with a working budget of $40,000 and a snowmobile jump on a closed Grand Avenue. Staff raised concerns about public safety and liability, street closures, parking and staff time on the same weekend as skijoring. No action was requested, only Board direction.

grand-lake/5.title: Town Council retreat agenda: marketing, housing, parking and governance
grand-lake/5.summary: Multi-day Board sessions covered the What Makes Us Grand marketing campaign, events policy (fee waivers, food trucks, mobile stage), Mary Drive next steps and workforce housing, downtown property acquisition and parking direction. They also covered home rule versus statutory town, the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, reserves policy and a five-year capital plan.

grand-lake/6.title: $175,000 promissory note for Space to Create Grand Lake
grand-lake/6.summary: Trustees were asked to approve Resolution 91-2026, a $175,000 promissory note with The Grand Foundation for the Space to Create Grand Lake project.

grand-lake/7.title: Little Columbine Creek restoration and fire mitigation contracts
grand-lake/7.summary: The Board considered a construction contract with Frontier Environmental Services for Little Columbine Creek restoration (Stormwater Plan Phase 2). It also considered a fire mitigation contract for the Mathews Property at 195 County Road.

grand-lake/8.title: Public comment and meeting recording policy
grand-lake/8.summary: Trustees considered Resolution 94-2026 adopting a public comment and meeting recording policy.

grand-lake/9.title: Town Square Park marquee sign
grand-lake/9.summary: The Board considered a revised proposal from SALT Workshop and MetalMorphic Methods for the Town Square Park marquee sign. A sign code waiver (Resolution 92-2026) was also on the Nov. 9 agenda.

greeley/0.title: Global AI data center campus: pre-annexation agreement and interim water service
greeley/0.summary: Global AI (Colorado) LLC bought about 438 acres east of Highway 257 (the former Kodak/Carestream campus) and is evaluating a data center there. Council's Sept. 8 agenda had a Pre-Annexation Agreement requiring annexation by March 31, 2028, and the Water & Sewer Board took up a bridging interim water service agreement. Residents spoke against the AI data center and asked for a moratorium.
greeley/0.where: East of State Highway 257, south of Eastman Park Drive, Weld County

greeley/1.title: Sales tax ballot question 2F and the Catalyst/Cascadia project debt
greeley/1.summary: Council backed Ballot Question 2F, a 0.60% sales and use tax increase for capital projects on the Nov. 3 ballot. Many residents objected to the tax, to tying it to the Catalyst project and the Civic Campus, and to debt tied to earlier projects. Council also held executive sessions on the tax and on economic development including Catalyst.

greeley/2.title: 2027 city budget, cuts and the budget retreat
greeley/2.summary: The City Manager's recommended 2027 budget was released Sept. 4, discussed at a Sept. 11 council retreat, and had first reading Oct. 20. It rests on reductions, voluntary separations (67.75 FTE), a lagging sales tax and a temporary 25 percent cut to capital maintenance. The Citizen Budget Advisory Committee backed staff's work.

greeley/3.title: Museum and cultural budget cuts
greeley/3.summary: Proposed cuts to the Culture, Parks and Recreation Department would reduce museum staffing and research access. The Museum Advisory Board, which passed a resolution, and the Historic Preservation Commission, drafting a letter to Council, objected. The budget later includes $150,000 added for museum part-time staff. Residents also objected to cuts to natural areas and the Union Colony Civic Center.

sources.body: Union Colony Civic Center Advisory Board

greeley/4.title: Flock license plate readers and police drones
greeley/4.summary: Residents asked Council to end the Flock Safety contract for license plate readers, citing no public vote, cost, misuse and Fourth Amendment concerns. A Sept. 8 work session covered the police use of ALPRs (17 Flock cameras with 30-day retention) and drones as first responders.

greeley/5.title: Great Western Industrial Park annexations and Windsor's reconsideration motion
greeley/5.summary: Council went into executive session for legal advice on Great Western Industrial Park annexations 1-15 and a Motion for Reconsideration from the Town of Windsor. A related GWIP reconsideration motion was on the consent agenda.

greeley/6.title: Arroyos del Sol annexation and zoning
greeley/6.summary: Planning Commission held hearings on annexing about 1,000 acres northwest of Highway 257 Spur along the Cache la Poudre River and on zoning it Conservation District. Much of the land is under a conservation easement with a master plan focused on public recreation. A motion recommended annexation approval to Council.
greeley/6.where: Northwest of State Highway 257 Spur, west of Weld County Road 19, south of the Cache la Poudre River

greeley/7.title: Civic Campus and Judicial Center redevelopment
greeley/7.summary: Planning Commission reviewed subdivision plats for the Judicial Center and Civic Campus in downtown, with phased redevelopment starting with temporary juror parking displaced by the new City Hall. Council considered an alley vacation and Certificates of Participation for the campus.

greeley/8.title: MERGE highway project and transportation projects
greeley/8.summary: The MERGE project, with over $50 million in federal grants plus state funds, would build underpasses at 35th and 47th Avenues, with significant property impacts. Staff also updated on the Keep Greeley Moving tax, US 34 safety, 16th Street, 13th Street quiet zone (eminent domain) and the Sheep Draw Trail underpass.

greeley/9.title: Water supply, rate increases and park watering cutbacks
greeley/9.summary: Staff proposed 4.5% water and 3.0% sewer rate increases for 2027 and delayed the F Street facility to limit rate impacts. The Greeley-Loveland ditch shut off early, so parks cut watering at passive sites and golf expects tough restrictions. Council also authorized legal action over the Halligan Water Supply Project Clean Water Act certification.

greeley/10.title: Housing needs assessment, Prop 123 and housing funding
greeley/10.summary: Council considered a Housing Needs Assessment contract with Interval, LLC and a Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment. The Housing for All Advisory Board reviewed its first funding cycle and Hope Springs funding, and the housing authority took up voucher consolidation and waiting lists.

greeley/11.title: Westside Area Plan, form-based code and related rezonings
greeley/11.summary: Planning Commission considered the Westside Area Plan, a form-based code option for the development code, a 76.5-acre rezoning near 83rd Avenue and 28th Street, and an indoor storage facility east of 35th Avenue.

greeley/12.title: Golf course fee increases
greeley/12.summary: The Golf Course Advisory Board reviewed fee research and a motion raised nine-hole rates by $3. Cart revenue is about $800,000 yearly, and Highland Hills will use potable water after its ditch water ended.

green-mountain-falls/0.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code ordinance (Ordinance 2026-05)
green-mountain-falls/0.summary: The town introduced Ordinance 2026-05 to adopt the state-mandated Wildfire Resiliency Code, which must be in effect by July 1, 2026. A public hearing was held April 23, the board approved it May 5 with a correction, and in August it approved changing WUI references to the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. A resident questioned the penalties.

green-mountain-falls/1.title: Sales tax increase ballot question for capital projects
green-mountain-falls/1.summary: Staff presented a "Closing the Gap" plan for a sales tax increase to fund sidewalks, culverts, sewage, and pool and park updates. On April 7 the mayor moved to put a 0.05% sales tax increase for four years on the ballot for the Capital Improvement Fund, and ballot and TABOR resolutions followed in May. The board called the general election in August.

green-mountain-falls/2.title: Town-owned open space: land sales, rezoning to park, and enclave annexation
green-mountain-falls/2.summary: The board has debated selling town land, including an appraisal for the El Paso trail property. A resident urged rezoning open space to park, or an ordinance giving sales the same legal requirements as parkland. In June the board sent annexation of enclaves to the Planning Commission and notified owners. Enclave annexation (Resolution 2026-15) and updating the 1997 annexation plan are on fall agendas.

green-mountain-falls/3.title: 2027 budget, fee schedule and mill levy
green-mountain-falls/3.summary: In December 2025 the council handled the 2026 fee schedule, mill levy certification and 2026 budget adoption. A 2026 fee schedule resolution was approved in May. Work on the 2027 draft budget, work sessions and the 2027 fee schedule was scheduled for fall 2026.

green-mountain-falls/4.title: Short-term rental tax and rules
green-mountain-falls/4.summary: In December 2025 the council took up Ordinance 2025-06 on a short-term rental tax and Ordinance 2025-09 amending short-term rental rules.

green-mountain-falls/5.title: Comprehensive Plan addendum and 3-mile plan update
green-mountain-falls/5.summary: The town manager is updating the 1997 3-mile plan. A 2026 Comprehensive Plan addendum was on several agendas, with a work session set for August 18 and further review scheduled in the fall. A resident urged the board to follow the plan's goals.

green-mountain-falls/6.title: Downtown parking, paving and drainage
green-mountain-falls/6.summary: The town planned a roughly $96,000 paving contract focused on parking near the Blue Moose and Lake Street, and a Maple Street parking survey. By June the new paving was complete, giving 78 downtown parking spots. Trailhead parking and 2026 drainage improvements also came up.
green-mountain-falls/6.where: Downtown, Lake Street and Maple Street

green-mountain-falls/7.title: Wastewater, septic and water rights
green-mountain-falls/7.summary: The town manager said pumping septic for the Marshal's building and park would cost about $16,000. The board tabled hiring a water attorney for water rights until creek flows are measured. A wastewater feasibility study was announced in April, and a resident thanked staff for work on a water and cesspool issue.

green-mountain-falls/8.title: Municipal election date change and planning commission role
green-mountain-falls/8.summary: Ordinance 2026-03 moved the town election from the first Tuesday of April. A resident asked that the Planning Commission be involved in more decisions, and the board considered ordinances changing Planning Commission and board responsibilities, with one tabled in March.

green-mountain-falls/9.title: Marshal's office pay and equipment
green-mountain-falls/9.summary: The board approved a budget amendment for a Marshal's office wage increase, added another speed camera near the pool park, and the town manager applied for a grant to replace a patrol car.

green-mountain-falls/10.title: Trash contract and bear reduction grant
green-mountain-falls/10.summary: The November agenda includes a trash RFP and a grant for human-bear conflict reduction.

green-mountain-falls/11.title: Pool, park restrooms and events
green-mountain-falls/11.summary: The board approved Bronc Day fee waivers, the 4th of July event with a $600 fee and Green Box pool use at $1,200. Park restrooms were due in March, the pool opening was discussed, and Lake Street bathrooms were on a September agenda.

greenwood-village/0.title: Emergency permit parking districts near Cherry Creek High School
greenwood-village/0.summary: On Aug. 3, 2026 Council passed emergency ordinances 08-26 and 09-26 expanding the Cherry Creek Village North permit district and creating one in Village on the Lake, ahead of a student parking shortage from the Cherry Creek High School rebuild. By the Oct. 5 study session, police reported 88 warnings, 18 citations and permits issued to about 125 households; temporary permits were mailed to 208 households.
greenwood-village/0.where: Cherry Creek Village North and Village on the Lake neighborhoods

greenwood-village/1.title: 2027 budget and mill levy
greenwood-village/1.summary: Council held the first-reading public hearing on the 2027 budget and Capital Improvement Program (Ordinances 12-26 and 13-26, setting mill levies) and then put second reading on the Nov. 2 consent agenda. The amended budget added $164,000 for a citywide access control system after the budget workshop.

greenwood-village/2.title: Belleview Avenue and Franklin Street safety improvements
greenwood-village/2.summary: CDOT, which controls Belleview Avenue as a state highway, will present its recommended alternative for safety improvements at the Franklin Street intersection to Council on Nov. 16. The recommendation came out of a joint effort and scoring of several alternatives.

greenwood-village/3.title: Green Oaks and Orchard Road bridge repairs over budget
greenwood-village/3.summary: Bids to replace rails on the Green Oaks Drive Bridge over the Highline Canal and the Orchard Road Bridge, and to repair failing asphalt on the Orchard bridge, all exceeded the budget. Staff needs a $387,996 supplemental appropriation and is asking Council whether it supports the amendment.
greenwood-village/3.where: Green Oaks Drive Bridge (Highline Canal) and Orchard Road Bridge

greenwood-village/4.title: Drone delivery regulations
greenwood-village/4.summary: Staff briefed Council on how cities can regulate commercial drone delivery, citing moratoria and permit rules in Castle Rock, Parker, Northglenn and others. Greenwood Village is considering how drone hubs, landings and use of parks might be handled.

greenwood-village/5.title: Electric vehicle charging station rules
greenwood-village/5.summary: The Land Development Code has no specific EV charging language, and staff asked Council whether to add standards such as equipment screening for commercial chargers, in light of state law (HB 24-1173). Staff did not recommend changing approval processes. The Planning Commission also considered a 4-charger amendment at 7600 E Orchard Road, where two were previously approved.

greenwood-village/6.title: Carson Park public art installation
greenwood-village/6.summary: The Arts and Humanities Council and staff asked Council to approve fabrication and installation of three Kevin Shaffer sculptures in Carson Park, part of the park improvement project and the city's 75th anniversary. A public input meeting was held Aug. 26, 2026.

greenwood-village/7.title: High Line Canal irrigation phase two
greenwood-village/7.summary: Council considered a license agreement with Arapahoe County for the second phase of High Line Canal irrigation using well water, with work through the winter. Council discussed whether Curtis Park, on Denver Water, could be added, which would need a large booster pump.
greenwood-village/7.where: High Line Canal (Long Rd to Steele to Garden Ln)

greenwood-village/8.title: Grace Chapel special use permit at 8500 E Orchard Road
greenwood-village/8.summary: Council held a quasi-judicial hearing on a Special Use Permit and Site Development Plan to repurpose the existing building and parking lot at Grace Chapel.

greenwood-village/9.title: Brinkerhoff Landmark restaurant site plan
greenwood-village/9.summary: Council scheduled a hearing on the site development plan and a development improvement agreement for the Brinkerhoff Landmark Restaurant at 5390 Greenwood Plaza area.

greenwood-village/10.title: Side-yard setback variances before the Board of Adjustments
greenwood-village/10.summary: The Board heard a variance to the Monaco Heights PUD for a garage addition encroaching about 48 sq ft into the 20-foot side setback; staff found no hardship. A separate variance for a north side yard addition was also heard, and a neighbor spoke against one request on Oct. 22. Fence variances at 9150 E Radcliff Ave were also voted on.
greenwood-village/10.where: Monaco Heights PUD; 9150 E Radcliff Ave

gunnison-county/0.title: 0.50% countywide sales tax for roads and bridges on the November 2026 ballot
gunnison-county/0.summary: On August 18 the commissioners approved Resolution 2026-29 referring a 0.50% countywide sales tax for roads, bridges and related transportation infrastructure to the November 3, 2026 ballot, along with an agreement with the Clerk and Recorder to run the question. Commissioners stressed the money would go only to roads and bridges. In October a commissioner continued public outreach on the measure, and a Road and Bridge budget work session was scheduled.

gunnison-county/1.title: 2027 county budget and work sessions
gunnison-county/1.summary: The commissioners received the first draft of the 2027 budget on October 13 and chose departments for work sessions, including Road & Bridge, Public Health, Human Services, the Housing Authority, Whetstone and the capital improvement plan. A public hearing on the budget is set for December 8 at 5:30 pm. A $10,000 late-night taxi request could be added to a contract for services, and the Board agreed to invite an application.

gunnison-county/2.title: Whetstone housing budget and Housing Authority finances
gunnison-county/2.summary: The Housing Authority amended its 2026 budget and appropriation (Resolution 2026-005) for Whetstone because of how the bond documents work. Whetstone, the Housing Authority administration fund and the Whetstone business plan were set for 2027 budget work sessions. Whetstone also includes family childcare units.

gunnison-county/3.title: Mineral Point property agreements
gunnison-county/3.summary: The Housing Authority and commissioners went into executive session on September 15 to get legal advice on proposed Mineral Point Property agreements and to develop negotiating strategy. The documents state no outcome.

gunnison-county/4.title: Senior property tax exemption appeal denied
gunnison-county/4.summary: On September 1 the Board of Equalization heard an appeal of a senior property tax exemption. The county assessor's records and the owner's voter registration put her primary residence elsewhere. The board denied the appeal.

gunnison-county/5.title: Property valuation appeals and abatement petitions
gunnison-county/5.summary: On October 20 the Board of Equalization reviewed hearing officer recommendations on appealed properties. One property was reclassified as agricultural, and CBS Block 6 LLC and others reached agreements with the Assessor on values. On October 6 the board heard a petition for abatement or refund of taxes.

gunnison-county/6.title: Gunnison-Crested Butte Regional Airport projects
gunnison-county/6.summary: The county approved a $719,737 airfield pavement maintenance contract with Maxwell Asphalt and an amendment to the airport food, beverage and retail agreement. An Airport Master Plan update is on the November 10 agenda.

gunnison-county/7.title: Federal health grant award terms questioned
gunnison-county/7.summary: On October 20 commissioners pulled a federal Health and Human Services notice of award for separate discussion because of its terms. Staff said whether the award is worth the terms is a policy decision, and the discussion was held until later in the meeting.

gunnison-county/8.title: Regional mental health, suicide prevention and early childhood programs
gunnison-county/8.summary: The Human Services board and commissioners heard updates on early childhood scholarships (94 families served), caregiver support, and the 2027 budget reduced to meet federal guidelines. Public health staff described Whole Health Navigation, stigma reduction and the Regional Suicide Prevention effort, plus a community health strategic plan.

gunnison-county/9.title: Town of Crested Butte water and sewer extension agreement
gunnison-county/9.summary: The November 3 consent agenda included a second amended utility extension agreement with the Town of Crested Butte to provide water and sewer service. An executive session was also planned on negotiating over specific parcels and recovery of funds owed to the county under a contract.

gypsum/0.title: License plate reader cameras and calls for an investigation
gypsum/0.summary: Residents pressed Council over the Town's automated license plate reader cameras. One resident requested an independent investigation and raised possible legal claims, and a records request was filed. Staff gave presentations on the Town's camera technology and the contract with the Sheriff's Office, and Council held a dedicated public comment period on cameras on Sept. 22.

gypsum/1.title: Public comment policy changes
gypsum/1.summary: After legal background from the Town Attorney, Council decided to move to a general public comment period at the beginning of each meeting. Mayor Green explained the changes on Oct. 13, including liability considerations.

gypsum/2.title: Lodging tax ballot measure
gypsum/2.summary: Council approved Resolution No. 23 calling a special coordinated election on a Town lodging tax. The Town Manager said it would replace the existing county tax rather than add a new one. Council discussed a resident's letter asking about the measure and the ballot language.

gypsum/3.title: Tower Center Filing No. 2 plat and improvement agreements
gypsum/3.summary: Council held a public hearing and approved Resolution 22, the final plat and subdivision improvement agreements for Tower Center Filing No. 2. On Sept. 8 it approved Resolution 25, assigning and assuming the subdivision improvement agreement.

gypsum/4.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment and funding request
gypsum/4.summary: Council heard a project presentation and discussed the Town's Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment for the 2027-2029 cycle. Presenters asked for an in-kind partnership with the Town, and Council said it would consider the matter further at its budget meeting.

gypsum/5.title: 2027 budget and financial advisor
gypsum/5.summary: Staff are developing the draft 2027 budget, with a budget meeting held in late October. Council approved a contract with UMB Financial Services as municipal financial advisor, not to exceed $50,000. The 2025 audit was presented and the financial statements approved.

gypsum/6.title: Siena Lake settlement with JPJG
gypsum/6.summary: A speaker from Denver asked Council to consider a proposed settlement between the Town and JPJG over the Siena Lake project.

gypsum/7.title: Water system projects: Cooley Mesa generator, Mosher plant, Abrams Creek
gypsum/7.summary: Council awarded the Cooley Mesa Road Pump Station backup generator contract to Pinnacle Electric for $131,183.68. The Town Manager reported a lightning strike at the Mosher water plant. Council also heard an update on the Abrams Creek crossing project and water quality.
gypsum/7.where: Cooley Mesa Road pump station; Mosher water plant; Abrams Creek

gypsum/8.title: I-70 Eagle Airport Interchange grant application
gypsum/8.summary: Council authorized an application to the FHWA PROTECT competitive grant program for planning and design of the I-70 Eagle Airport Interchange project.

gypsum/9.title: Fire restrictions and wildfire mitigation
gypsum/9.summary: Council confirmed administrative orders moving the Town from Stage 2 to Stage 1 fire restrictions and later another fire restrictions order. Eagle Valley Wildland presented its 2026 projects and 2027 plan, including the chipping program.

gypsum/10.title: Bear-resistant trash cans
gypsum/10.summary: Colorado Parks and Wildlife gave statistics on bears in town, and Council discussed the availability and cost of bear-resistant cans.

gypsum/11.title: Street, recycling center and clubhouse construction change orders
gypsum/11.summary: Council approved Change Order 2 of $14,570.63 with A-1 Chipseal for street chipseal and slurry seal. It also approved Recycling Center change orders totaling $28,598.27, with Gypsum paying $12,111.63 and Eagle County the rest. The Clubhouse Restoration project is complete apart from a punch list.

gypsum/12.title: Amazon warehouse public improvements accepted
gypsum/12.summary: Council accepted the dedication of public improvements supporting Amazon's warehouse facility under Resolution 30.

haxtun/0.title: 2026 town budget adopted
haxtun/0.summary: After a public hearing on Dec. 1, 2025 with no public comment, the Council adopted the 2026 budget and appropriation resolutions (2025-9 and 2025-10). The general property tax levy brings in $189,144, and the final property assessment set the mill levy slightly above the estimate. Staff also raised a crack-filling machine for streets and a supplemental fund tied to the generator project.

hayden/0.title: Data center moratorium study and citizen advisory committee
hayden/0.summary: Council is running a study tied to a data center moratorium. A citizen committee was to be announced shortly, and the Data Center Citizen Advisory Committee appointment was on the Nov. 5 agenda. Council also asked staff to draft letters to state and federal representatives about data center bills.

hayden/1.title: 2027-2029 draft budget, COLA and proposed 32-hour work week
hayden/1.summary: The Town Council, the Northwest Colorado GID and the Housing Authority held their budget discussions in tandem. Staff presented the draft 2027-2029 budget and asked for direction on an additional COLA increase and a proposed 32-hour work week. The property tax sheets show a general fund mill levy of 25.067 and a debt service levy of 3.990, with about $1.54 million in budgeted property tax revenue.

hayden/2.title: Council endorsements of 2026 ballot measures (fire district, schools, CMC, regional transit)
hayden/2.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-14 endorsing ballot measures 6A (West Routt Fire mill levy override), 4B (Hayden schools joining Colorado Mountain College district), 7A (half-percent sales tax for the Yampa Valley Regional Transportation Authority) and 4A (Hayden RE-1 mill levy override). Councilmember Haight objected to the language on the transportation authority and moved to remove it. Resolution 2026-16 separately endorsed referral of Measure 7A.

hayden/3.title: Business park road to Highway 40 and new hotel lot
hayden/3.summary: The Northwest Colorado GID heard that design is starting for a new road from the business park to Highway 40. The GID is also closing on another business park lot that will be used for a hotel.

hayden/4.title: Colorado Main Street program presentation
hayden/4.summary: Council received a Main Street 101 presentation from the Colorado Main Street team on joining the program. It covers mini-grants, façade and building improvements, and a Main Street manager for downtown Hayden.

hayden/5.title: Outdoor pickleball court and 3rd Street Park
hayden/5.summary: The Parks & Recreation board discussed building an outdoor pickleball court, possibly splitting the court, with a cost near $260,000. Staff are looking for grants, and a pickleball co-op was suggested. The board also received 3rd Street Park updates at each meeting, and one project has a $5,000 grant.

hayden/6.title: Parks & Recreation board bylaws on members who move
hayden/6.summary: The board discussed amending its bylaws on members who move away during their term. The bylaw discussion was also placed on the Nov. 5 Council agenda.

hayden/7.title: Animal ordinance 752 and emergency fee schedule change
hayden/7.summary: Council held a second reading and public hearing on Ordinance 752, a new ordinance on animals within the town. No one commented. Council also considered Resolution 2026-15 adopting an emergency fee schedule change.

hayden/8.title: Routt County Hazard Mitigation Plan adoption
hayden/8.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-17 adopting the 2026 Routt County Hazard Mitigation Plan.

hayden/9.title: Parks & Rec revenue ideas and events planning
hayden/9.summary: The Parks & Rec board reviewed ways to generate revenue and planned events, including a farmers market with pumpkins in October and vendor fees. Other items were food trucks, drink service and volunteer incentives. The board also reviewed budget work that takes effect January 2027.

hooper/0.title: 2026 budget, property tax levy and attorney contract
hooper/0.summary: At the December 3, 2025 meeting the Town held a public hearing on the 2026 budget. Trustees were also set to consider Resolutions 6, 7 and 8-2025 to adopt the budget, levy property taxes and appropriate funds. The agenda also listed an attorney contract rate increase and a legal services contract (Resolution 5-2025).

hooper/1.title: Town park safety concerns and 2026 park improvements
hooper/1.summary: Ramona Smith presented park safety concerns in December 2025. In March 2026 the Board planned to discuss a 2026 park grant led by Trustee Mimi Dolan, hiring a park and town maintenance employee, and placing a library box in the town park.

hooper/2.title: Public nuisance and ground fowl ordinances
hooper/2.summary: The March 18, 2026 agenda included Ordinance 1-2026 amending public nuisance provisions and Ordinance 2-2026 amending standards for ground fowl in the municipal code.

hooper/3.title: 2026 regular town election
hooper/3.summary: Resolution 4-2025 on the December 2025 agenda called the town's regular election.

hotchkiss/0.title: Drought restrictions, water rates and the bulk water standpipe
hotchkiss/0.summary: Council passed an emergency moratorium on new out-of-town water taps and limits on standpipe sales in February 2026, then discussed drought restrictions and Resolution 2026-04 in April and May. Trustees noted Hotchkiss water rates are among the lowest around and set the standpipe and rates for a separate work session. In August the Town reported a $10,000 WaterSmart grant and talks with neighboring water users about a regional agreement.

hotchkiss/1.title: Hiring a Town Administrator and Town Attorney
hotchkiss/1.summary: After months of interim leadership, the Town used a search firm (KRW Associates) and executive sessions to recruit an administrator. Kimberly States was appointed on June 25, 2026 and her appointment was ratified in October. The Town also sought proposals for and appointed a new Town Attorney (Sarah Ross), and passed Ordinance 2026-04 defining the administrator's powers.

hotchkiss/2.title: Ordinance 2026-07 on demonstrations and special events in public rights-of-way
hotchkiss/2.summary: The Town considered and later approved an ordinance setting content-neutral safety, access and permit rules for demonstrations and special events. Residents spoke on it, and one asked whether it could override state statute. The new permit process later required a waiver for the homecoming parade while procedures were set up.

hotchkiss/3.title: Proposed park on Bridge Street lots and skate park request
hotchkiss/3.summary: Don Foster proposed a park on the empty lots at 171 and 191 E Bridge Street, possibly run with a non-profit, and the Board agreed to form a research committee. One resident opposed it, preferring a revenue-generating business. Separately, Tanner Wilson asked for a skate park, and the Town offered a letter of support. In October a resident proposed a Train Station Pocket Park.

hotchkiss/4.title: Wage study, benefits and budgets
hotchkiss/4.summary: The Board heard Graves Consulting's wage compensation study in April, with raises proposed to start June 1, 2026, plus increased vacation and insurance benefits. Trustee Edstrom had budget concerns. The updated 2026 budget was adopted in September and ratified in October after staff corrected errors, and the first draft of the 2027 budget was presented with a work session on October 22.

hotchkiss/5.title: Flock camera contract cancellation
hotchkiss/5.summary: The Board considered canceling two Flock camera contracts, a trailer kit expiring December 11, 2026 and three town cameras expiring December 18. Cancellation could cost $500 per hardware unit.

hotchkiss/6.title: Master Plan, housing and accessory dwelling units
hotchkiss/6.summary: The Planning Commission approved the final Master Plan in April. Trustees discussed the difficulty of finding housing, and the Planning Commission is drafting possible accessory dwelling unit requirements for R-1 zoning, expected after the new year.

hotchkiss/7.title: Wildland-Urban Interface Code and wildfire planning
hotchkiss/7.summary: The Western Slope Conservation Center presented a Wildfire Ready Action Plan in December. Ordinance 2026-03 adopting a Wildland-Urban Interface Code was heard in July, with a fire-risk map covering the whole Town and no public comments. In August the Town also discussed the risk that a fire at its water source would cut off water, and funding for a study.

hotchkiss/8.title: Broadband franchise with DMEA and purchase of Delta County Tele-Com
hotchkiss/8.summary: A franchise agreement with Delta Montrose Electric Association for broadband was planned in December. In July the Board took up Ordinance 2026-05, a franchise agreement tied to the purchase of Delta County Tele-Com, Inc., on second reading.

hotchkiss/9.title: Variance requests for sheds and fences
hotchkiss/9.summary: In June the Board heard variances for a shed replacement setback at 159 E. Orchard, an 8-foot fence at 791 Barrow Mesa Road, and a 6-foot fence at 319 Knob Hill Circle Drive. The Planning Commission recommended approval of the shed with conditions for a metal, fire-resistant structure on skids.
hotchkiss/9.where: 159 E. Orchard; 791 Barrow Mesa Road; 319 Knob Hill Circle Drive

hotchkiss/10.title: Police vehicle transfer and training tuition agreement
hotchkiss/10.summary: The Board debated transferring decommissioned Police Department vehicles in exchange for a training arrangement. Chief Green said the vehicles were untrustworthy. The Board directed him to ask Technical College of the Rockies to amend the contract so the Town avoids extra tuition fees. Vehicle use policy revisions for the Police Department were later approved.

hotchkiss/11.title: Piñon Road alley dispute and unplatted property claim
hotchkiss/11.summary: A resident said property near 4th Street and Lorah Lane is in the Dukes Unplatted area with no legal plat or title, and had filed a complaint with the police chief. In October the Board considered executive session on the Piñon Road alley dispute, involving threatened litigation and settlement negotiations.
hotchkiss/11.where: 4th Street and Lorah Lane; Piñon Road alley

hudson/0.title: Canterbury Meadows settlement with Prestige Builder Group
hudson/0.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-118, a settlement of litigation and a multi-million-dollar hardship takings claim over a 32-lot conservation subdivision on about 94.56 acres at Ravenna Street and Stow Road. Residents objected that it bypasses the Planning Commission and the Land Development Code and raised water run-off and high water table concerns. The Planning Commission also discussed the settlement and asked for separate legal counsel; the documents do not state a final vote.

hudson/1.title: Clinton Crossing downtown development
hudson/1.summary: Staff and Council reviewed the Clinton Crossing concept plan, including housing unit counts, a market hall, railroad proximity, parking studies and public finance tools such as TIF and new community authorities. Residents worry about traffic at Owen Brown Street and Morse Road and the one-lane railroad underpass, and about consistency with the Comprehensive Plan. A concept site plan hearing was set before the Planning Commission on Nov. 9.
hudson/1.where: Clinton Street, Owen Brown Street and Morse Road area

hudson/2.title: Owen Brown Street and Clinton Street townhome project
hudson/2.summary: A townhome project by Fairmont, reduced from 22 to 18 units, went through Architectural & Historic Board of Review and variance reviews. The developer appealed a denial of the design to the Board of Zoning & Building Appeals for the corner of Clinton Street and Morse Road.
hudson/2.where: 86 Owen Brown Street; Clinton Street and Morse Road

hudson/3.title: Hudson Innovation Park and salt barn at 996 Hines Hill Road
hudson/3.summary: Council received an update on the former YDC site, covering relocation of the salt barn, excess soil, property tax abatement options and Hines Hill Road improvements. Council asked for abatement details and road cost estimates. A salt barn site plan and an excess soils resolution followed.

hudson/4.title: 2027-2031 Five-Year Capital Plan and unfunded infrastructure
hudson/4.summary: Council reviewed the five-year capital plan, including streets, storm water, sidewalks, trails, Fiber-to-the-Home broadband and debt service. Discussion included whether to fund the Barlow Road sidewalk and reduce storm water allocations. A resolution adopting the plan in concept was on the Nov. 10 agenda, along with a GAI contract for the Barlow Road sidewalk re-design.

hudson/5.title: Low-speed vehicle rules, Ordinance 26-113
hudson/5.summary: Council amended Chapter 478 on low-speed vehicles such as golf carts. Residents objected to the ban on 35 MPH roads and to lighting rules that don't allow night use, and suggested equipment requirements instead.

hudson/6.title: Short-term rental rules, Chapter 876
hudson/6.summary: Ordinance 26-78, amending short-term rental regulations after workshops from March to May, had three readings and was ready for action on Nov. 10, with amendments from Councilor Goetz.

hudson/7.title: Hudson's Restaurant sidewalk and outdoor seating proposal
hudson/7.summary: The restaurant at 80 N Main Street proposed widening the sidewalk and expanding outdoor seating, which would remove some on-street parking. Council asked staff to study parking, accessibility, crosswalks and precedent, and to get a legal opinion. A discussion on removing the mid-block crosswalk and beacon was requested for early 2027.

hudson/8.title: 88 N Main Street door and Executive Session appeal
hudson/8.summary: The owner of 88 N Main Street appealed an Architectural & Historic Board of Review decision on a door installed without a permit. The attorney argued the board's executive session was improper and asked for a remand or continuance. The matter returned to the historic board on Sept. 23 and Oct. 14.

hudson/9.title: School-hours turn restriction at SR 303 and N. Hayden Parkway
hudson/9.summary: Council took up Ordinance 26-134, restricting a turn at the westbound intersection of E. Streetsboro Street and N. Hayden Parkway during school hours. Staff also discussed truck restrictions and turn radius at SR 91 and SR 303.
hudson/9.where: E. Streetsboro Street (SR 303) and N. Hayden Parkway

hudson/10.title: Veterans Way open space parcel
hudson/10.summary: Staff recommended keeping a 34.37-acre parcel south of Veterans Parkway as open space while options such as a park, outdoor pool or recreation center are considered. Designating it parkland could limit future changes.

hudson/11.title: Standard Shop Company site plan extension
hudson/11.summary: The Planning Commission subcommittee questioned the long-delayed industrial park project at Terex Road, approved in 2020 with approval expiring in October 2026. It asked for proof of financing, a bond and window changes before approval.

huerfano-county/0.title: GroAway LLC conditional use permit (LU-26-000154)
huerfano-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on the GroAway, LLC conditional use permit on Sept. 10, continued it twice to Oct. 8 and Oct. 22, and weighed Colorado Parks and Wildlife input and late public comments. On Nov. 3 the commissioners voted to deny the permit after residents raised concerns about the project, including its "cat sanctuary" aspect.

huerfano-county/1.title: 2027 county budget
huerfano-county/1.summary: County Administrator Carl Young presented a preliminary balanced 2027 budget that includes a 3.6% cost-of-living raise and extra pay increases for Human Services and Road and Bridge. It warns County General will need cost cuts amid fuel and jail housing costs. Department budget workshops were set for Nov. 10.

huerfano-county/2.title: Housing programs: pre-approved home plans, Prop 123 down payment help, revolving loan fund
huerfano-county/2.summary: The county adopted pre-approved home designs, including tiny home and barndominium plans, codified a Housing Authority dormant since 2021, and adopted a land banking and donation policy. It also took up Prop 123 down payment assistance and an affordable housing revolving loan fund, with Impact Development Fund presenting and a resident asking how the program works.

huerfano-county/3.title: Rec and cultural mill levy and voter survey
huerfano-county/3.summary: Commissioners heard a Magellan Strategies county voter survey and approved Resolution 26-34 on a recreation and cultural mill levy, tied to parks and rec and jail renovation projects.

huerfano-county/4.title: Fox Theater loan guaranty
huerfano-county/4.summary: The county approved a guaranty of a First Southwest Bank loan for the Fox Theater in Walsenburg, to be repaid from tax credit sales (Resolution 26-41, with a further guaranty in Resolution 26-48). Change Order #2 with McKinstry for the theater was also approved.

huerfano-county/5.title: Water augmentation lease-purchases and bulk water permits
huerfano-county/5.summary: The county approved lease-purchase financing for eight acre-feet of augmentation water for the Gardner Public Improvement District and three for Road and Bridge. Bulk water permits and monthly volume reports came up at most meetings, and a marijuana license hearing drew a resident's drought and water-use concerns.

huerfano-county/6.title: Gardner Sewer Project and Gardner Main Street revitalization
huerfano-county/6.summary: The Gardner sewer project bid tabulation was moved to correspondence. Commissioners also approved the Gardner Main Street Revitalization Plan and Rio Cucharas plan resolutions, with the County Revitalization Authority discussing outreach to taxing entities.

huerfano-county/7.title: Camping ordinance and trash dumping
huerfano-county/7.summary: Commissioners approved the second reading of Ordinance 26-04, the camping ordinance. The sheriff and county administrator also discussed illegal trash dumping and what a future ordinance could add, and a resident asked about requesting dumpsters.

huerfano-county/8.title: Land Use Code Chapter 11 amendments
huerfano-county/8.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 26-38 amending Chapter 11 of the Land Use Code, covering overlay districts, development rights, planned unit developments, non-conforming lots and the use table. The Planning Commission later reviewed conditional use approval provisions in Sec. 11-18.

huerfano-county/9.title: Wildfire protection, fire restrictions and forest grants
