huerfano-county/9.summary: The county approved its 2026 Community Wildfire Protection Plan and an amended Community Wildfire Defense Grant subaward. It sent support letters for forest restoration grants, and stepped down from Stage 2 to Stage 1 fire restrictions before lifting them in October.

huerfano-county/10.title: Spanish Peaks Regional Airport budget and capital plan
huerfano-county/10.summary: The airport advisory board discussed a budget running in the red, a turnaround taxiway, a 2027-2036 capital plan, land acquisition advised by the FAA, and frustration with commercial tax assessments. Commissioners also approved an agreement with Airport Monitoring Systems.
huerfano-county/10.where: Spanish Peaks Regional Airport, County Road 101

huerfano-county/11.title: Cuchara Mountain Park: liquor license denial and ski pond dam study
huerfano-county/11.summary: The Liquor License Authority recommended against a special event liquor license for Cuchara Mountain Park. Commissioners approved a $10,600 geotechnical services agreement for the ski pond dam, and the park is upgrading snowmaking equipment and aging pipe.

huerfano-county/12.title: Tourism board budget and lodging tax
huerfano-county/12.summary: The Tourism Board finalized its 2027 budget and tracked lodging tax, which was down about 2% in September. It also paid for winter advertising, discussed EV charger signage, and handled board appointments.

huerfano-county/13.title: Road and Bridge staffing and projects
huerfano-county/13.summary: The Road and Bridge Department saw terminations, new hires and wage increases, an announcement about its superintendent position, and KLJ contract amendments for Peak Gravel and the Huerfano River Bridge closeout. Commissioners also approved county road use for the Grassroots Gravel event.

hugo/0.title: Water and sewer rate study: 40% water and 28% sewer increases proposed
hugo/0.summary: Colorado Rural Water Association's rate study found Hugo is spending savings to service debt in both enterprises. It estimates a 40% water rate increase and 28% sewer rate increase, plus annual inflation increases, to cover operations and debt. The council also adopted a resolution amending water, wastewater and refuse rates in October and reviewed a rate study timeline in August.

hugo/1.title: Water restrictions and water share limits
hugo/1.summary: With LAWMA explaining that Hugo owns only common (not preferred) shares, the town imposed Level One watering restrictions, leased two preferred shares, and replaced the restriction ordinance (Ordinance 300). In July council adopted emergency Ordinance 302 changing permitted watering days and hours after residents such as Tom Lee objected to watering three days in a row. Restrictions lift automatically October 1, and staff report the town is on track to stay under its allotment.

hugo/2.title: Water system improvements, CDBG and state loans for water and sewer
hugo/2.summary: The town held public hearings on a CDBG grant and a Water Pollution Control Revolving Fund project, took on a water loan of up to $5,395,767, and is moving a Water System Improvements Project toward bidding in December. Water tank repair, well pump replacement and sewer loans (including one up to $1,559,900 and a principal forgiveness loan) are also in progress.

hugo/3.title: Solomon Addition / Roundhouse Estates infrastructure problems and impact fees
hugo/3.summary: Staff and engineers reported that infrastructure in the Solomon Addition/Roundhouse Estates was improperly constructed, mostly sewer, roads and drainage, and presented repair options in October. The town also discussed charging system impact fees per lot on new development, and ordered a lift station for Roundhouse Estates.

hugo/4.title: Photo radar (automated vehicle identification) with DacraTech
hugo/4.summary: Council approved Ordinance 296 establishing an automated vehicle identification system and an agreement with DacraTech in March. A November agenda has a DacraTech presentation and a resolution repealing the earlier agreement and approving a new one.

hugo/5.title: New Hugo firehouse and Fire Protection District land
hugo/5.summary: A plan for a new firehouse was presented in March. Council denied adding the fire department driveway to the CDOT sidewalk project, then approved Ordinance 301 disconnecting Fire Protection District land from the town and waived one water and one sewer tap at the district's property at 5th Street and 9th Avenue.

hugo/6.title: Hugo Main Street program
hugo/6.summary: The town has been working with Colorado Main Street to form a Hugo Main Street board, including a steering committee, a board retreat on August 17 and a resolution in September supporting becoming an official Main Street Community.

hugo/7.title: Ordinance updates: trash, wildfire code, abandoned buildings and code enforcement
hugo/7.summary: Council tabled the 2025 Wildfire Resiliency Code (Ordinance 295), raised maximum code-violation penalties, authorized a code enforcement officer, and worked on a revised trash ordinance due in August. It approved a Willdan agreement for code enforcement services and applied for a DOLA Local Planning Capacity Grant to update the abandoned and deteriorated property ordinance.

hugo/8.title: Affordable housing, daycare and Housing Authority
hugo/8.summary: Council adopted Resolution 2026-07 on expedited review for affordable housing projects. County economic development reported on possible new housing and a child care mini-center, and a land donation for daycare was discussed. The Hugo Housing Authority sought help with plumbing repairs and is working toward compliance before asking for a grant partnership with the town.

hugo/9.title: Culture, recreation and pool sales tax ballot issue
hugo/9.summary: The January 2026 agenda included discussion of Ballot Issue #2, an additional 1% sales tax for culture, recreation and the pool.

hugo/10.title: Street maintenance, pothole repair and CDOT sidewalk project
hugo/10.summary: A street assessment is planned to determine pavement and structural conditions for a maintenance plan, and council approved a Millan Asphalt pothole proposal in June. The CDOT sidewalk project was waiting on asphalt approvals in April.

hugo/11.title: Parks, playground and football field safety
hugo/11.summary: The town sought quotes and grants for playground equipment, approved a BYO Recreation proposal in June, and discussed the safety of kids playing on a hard football field in August.

hugo/12.title: 2027 budget workshops and strategic plan
hugo/12.summary: The council scheduled a 2027 budget review and workshop in October, with the strategic plan draft to be reviewed at the November 30 budget workshop.

idaho-springs/0.title: Roberts Brothers Garage arts center: fee waivers, parking and historic designation at 121 15th Avenue
idaho-springs/0.summary: The Clear Creek Center for Arts & Education won a $1.538 million state grant that requires a 1:1 match and asked the city for up to $729,307 in in-kind contributions and fee waivers. Council took up Resolution 27 on fee waivers and contributions with Four Bairs, Inc., Ordinance 20 on designating the property, and a parking fee-in-lieu request. A parking arrangement with the adjacent city-owned property was also discussed.

idaho-springs/1.title: Affordable and senior housing: incentives, Prop 123 and DOLA application
idaho-springs/1.summary: Council authorized a DOLA Division of Housing predevelopment funding application for the Idaho Springs Affordable Senior Housing Project. It also discussed affordable housing incentives and the Proposition 123 commitment for 2027-2029. The Miner Street Apartments multifamily plan and a Fair Housing Act code amendment (Ordinance 17) also came up.

idaho-springs/2.title: Proposed 2027 city budget
idaho-springs/2.summary: Staff called the 2027 budget extremely difficult to prepare, with General Fund revenue only about $100,000 above 2024. Measures include moving community promotion costs to the Parking Fund and pausing some employee benefits. City property tax is projected to fall from $282,237 to $267,546 at the same 6.310 mill levy. The Business & Community Promotions Board recommended a $211,109 baseline for its own budget, and council also considered a fee schedule update.

idaho-springs/3.title: Recreational occupation tax on outdoor recreation providers
idaho-springs/3.summary: Council referred a ballot issue to create a new occupation tax on outdoor recreation providers such as rafting companies, with up to $5 per customer. Revenue would go to impacts on streets, parking, public safety, water and parks. Rafting businesses made requests to council about the tax.

idaho-springs/4.title: Downtown parking: paid-lot moratorium, parking study and library parking
idaho-springs/4.summary: Council considered Ordinance 18, a temporary moratorium on permits and licenses for private paid parking facilities. Planning reviewed preliminary parking study results and council received final results, while library parking was also on the agenda. Council amended the name and scope of the parking, transportation and mobility enterprise.

idaho-springs/5.title: Two-way traffic on Miner Street and the Miner Street Market
idaho-springs/5.summary: Miner Street was closed for the seasonal Miner Street Market and Halloween events, with reopening to traffic set for November 5. Public works asked to return it to a two-way street, and council was asked to approve two-way vehicle traffic downtown.

idaho-springs/6.title: 2026 Comprehensive Plan adoption
idaho-springs/6.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing recommending the 2026 Comprehensive Plan, and council took up Resolution 31 approving it on October 26. Council also adopted its five-year strategic plan by Resolution 30.

idaho-springs/7.title: Noise ordinance with decibel limits
idaho-springs/7.summary: Staff proposed adding objective decibel standards, such as 55 dB daytime and 50 dB nighttime in parks and recreation areas, so police can enforce noise rules with a professional dB reader. The current code has no maximum decibel level.

idaho-springs/8.title: New development rules and public concerns on buffers and parking
idaho-springs/8.summary: Residents asked the Planning Commission for clear zoning restrictions, buffer zones, lot-line and parking rules for new developments. The commission heard a minor subdivision of Lots 1-12, Block 57 near vacated Sixth Avenue, which council also approved by plat resolution. Code amendments on nonconforming buildings (Ordinance 22) and exterior lighting were also in progress.
idaho-springs/8.where: Lots 1-12, Block 57/75 near vacated Sixth Avenue

idaho-springs/9.title: Water restrictions and city landscaping
idaho-springs/9.summary: A resident said the city should follow the residential water restrictions, criticizing the waterfall running and sprinklers on city property, and urged native plants.
idaho-springs/9.where: Citywide; city property near Miner Street

idaho-springs/10.title: I-70 Floyd Hill project and Exit 240 agreement
idaho-springs/10.summary: Council received an I-70 Floyd Hill project update and considered a resolution approving an agreement related to the project near Exit 240, along with a RAISE planning grant for downtown. A letter of support was proposed for the US 40 Empire wildlife crossing.

idaho-springs/11.title: Golddigger Park and Fieldhouse park conveyance
idaho-springs/11.summary: Council discussed a new park conveyed by Fieldhouse Development and then accepted Lot 3 of the former Golddigger Field subdivision as a city park named Golddigger Park.

idaho-springs/12.title: E-mobility planning grant and Ameresco facility assessment
idaho-springs/12.summary: Council considered a $78,750 proposal from The Antero Group for the Community Accelerated Mobility Program e-mobility planning grant, plus a steering committee. A preliminary facility assessment agreement with Ameresco was also on the agenda.

jefferson-county/0.title: 2027 proposed county budget
jefferson-county/0.summary: The Commissioners received the 2027 Proposed Budget presentation and budget book on October 27, 2026. Earlier in the fall they also handled the August and September supplementary 2026 appropriations and an ARPA budget revision.

jefferson-county/1.title: Lakewood Navigation Center operating costs agreement
jefferson-county/1.summary: The Board approved an intergovernmental agreement and memorandum of understanding with Arvada, Edgewater, Golden, Lakewood, Westminster and Wheat Ridge to share the operating costs of the Lakewood Navigation Center. It was discussed in a September 29 work session and approved October 13 as Resolution CC26-277.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/2.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing agreements and incentives
jefferson-county/2.summary: The county worked on a JeffCo-Denver-Arvada Prop 123 unit-sharing agreement and an assignment of private activity bond allocation for the Belveron project. It also reviewed its 15-year affordable housing plan and a supplemental funding request for the Prop 123 expedited review incentive bonus.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/3.title: Rezoning to allow up to 143 dwelling units
jefferson-county/3.summary: After staff and applicant presentations and public testimony, the Board approved by majority vote (CC26-234) a rezoning from Agricultural-Two and Commercial-One to Planned Development to allow a maximum of 143 dwelling units.

jefferson-county/4.title: Junction Urban Renewal Plan tax-increment revenue sharing
jefferson-county/4.summary: The Board held closed-door discussions and an October 27 briefing on negotiating how tax-increment revenue from The Junction urban renewal plan will be shared with the Golden urban renewal authority.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/5.title: Red Rocks transportation hub and Planning Commission land-use cases
jefferson-county/5.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled hearings on a transportation hub with 397 parking spaces serving Red Rocks Amphitheatre (Jurassic Road and Trading Post Rd). It also had rezonings and plats at 22339 S Platte River Road in Sedalia, 33871 Golden Gate Canyon Road, and 10446 Ammons Street in Westminster. The Board approved a preliminary and final plat (Resolution CC26-266) after public testimony.
jefferson-county/5.where: 17355 Jurassic Road and 17900 Trading Post Rd, Golden

jefferson-county/6.title: Parks and Open Space projects
jefferson-county/6.summary: The Board approved the Meyer Ranch Park forestry contract. It approved a $3.22 million North Table Mountain Park improvements contract with American West Construction and a Lakewood Bear Creek Greenbelt easement subordination. It also approved a bus stop agreement and trails funding at West 32nd Avenue and Kipling, utility easements at Pleasant View Community Park, and agreements for Long Lake and Van Bibber parks.
jefferson-county/6.where: Meyer Ranch, North Table Mountain, Bear Creek Greenbelt and other county parks

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/7.title: Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport contracts and lease policy
jefferson-county/7.summary: The Board approved the $-contract with Amrize West Central for the Taxiway D Phase II reconstruction. It also amended the airport lease agreement policy and approved Premier Hangar Group C-2 ground leases.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/8.title: Wildfire, pine beetle and hazard mitigation planning
jefferson-county/8.summary: Commissioners hosted the statewide Ponderosa Mountain Pine Beetle Task Force and discussed wildfire mitigation. Staff briefed on the 2026 Hazard Mitigation Plan for adoption, and the Board approved the Conifer and Elk Creek fire districts' 2024 fire codes.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/9.title: Head Start funding and expansion
jefferson-county/9.summary: The Board approved the Head Start continuation grant application and welcomed a Head Start expansion in Lakewood. The county also prepared public comment on federal proposed changes to Head Start performance standards.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/10.title: Position resolutions on 2026 ballot measures
jefferson-county/10.summary: At a special meeting the Board adopted positions on 2026 ballot measures, supporting Amendment 87 and Front Range Passenger Rail Measure 7A by majority votes and opposing Amendment 84 on mail ballot voter ID.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Special Meeting

jefferson-county/11.title: Special district service plan
jefferson-county/11.summary: After public testimony, the Board unanimously approved Resolution CC26-224 for a special district service plan, continued from July 28.

jefferson-county/12.title: Denver Water purchase and sale agreement
jefferson-county/12.summary: The Board reviewed and then approved a purchase and sale agreement with Denver Water.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

johnstown/0.title: Permanent 8-mill property tax cut and FY 2027 budget
johnstown/0.summary: Council reviewed the FY 2027 preliminary budget, which recommended keeping the 23.947-mill levy, and then took up Ordinance 2026-299 to permanently cut the mill levy by 8.000 mills in four annual 2-mill steps. Any later increase would need new voter approval. The 2027 proposed budget came up for public hearing in November, and a resident asked for trees at Clearview Park.

johnstown/1.title: Housing needs assessment and comprehensive plan updates (SB 24-174)
johnstown/1.summary: Staff presented a draft Housing Needs Assessment by ECOnorthwest plus new Strategic Growth and Water Supply elements of the comprehensive plan, required by state law. Planning and Zoning is to consider them November 18 and Council adoption is slated for December 2. A Housing Action Plan follows in mid-2027.

johnstown/2.title: Water supply projects and water rates
johnstown/2.summary: Council approved a $326,400 Water System Master Plan Update with J-U-B Engineers, a $150,645 raw water transmission services agreement with Connell Resources, 15 more CBT units, and the Northern Integrated Supply Project interim agreement. A resident wrote in about water usage at town facilities and water rates.

johnstown/3.title: New Senior Center construction and YMCA agreement
johnstown/3.summary: Council awarded the construction contract for the Town senior center building to Fransen Pittman Construction. It also considered an amended facility management agreement with the YMCA of Northern Colorado, tied to a settlement and release agreement.

johnstown/4.title: Town Attorney selection
johnstown/4.summary: Council interviewed law firms, including Hoffmann Parker Wilson & Carberry, for the appointed Town Attorney post, then considered a legal services agreement with Wilson Williams Fellman Dittman.

johnstown/5.title: West Parish Alley construction contract
johnstown/5.summary: Council awarded Krische Construction a $1,874,329 contract for the West Parish Alley project, with a 10% contingency the Town Manager can use for unforeseen conditions.

johnstown/6.title: Vista Commons rezoning and plat
johnstown/6.summary: Council considered a change of zone (Ordinance 2026-301) and a preliminary plat for the Vista Commons subdivision.

johnstown/7.title: Diamond Ridge Metropolitan District service plan
johnstown/7.summary: Council held a hearing on approving the service plan for Diamond Ridge Metropolitan District Nos. 1 and following.

johnstown/8.title: Town property deals: Quality Liquid Feeds, Gillam, old library
johnstown/8.summary: Council considered a purchase and sale agreement with Quality Liquid Feeds, one with Gillam Development Corporation, and a lease of the Old Library Building at 1011 Jay Avenue. Executive sessions covered real property sales.
johnstown/8.where: 1011 Jay Avenue and other town parcels

johnstown/9.title: Downtown Development Authority fund and I-25 frontage road
johnstown/9.summary: Council took up Ordinance 2026-298 establishing a DDA Fund, and an ordinance accepting a stretch of the I-25 East Frontage Road between mile markers 253.2 and 257.1 under an IGA. A new DDA executive director was introduced.

kersey/0.title: Ballot Issue 2B: ten-year extension of the 17.205-mill property tax levy
kersey/0.summary: The Board referred Ballot Issue 2B to voters, a ten-year extension (2028 through 2037) of the Town's existing 17.205-mill property tax levy without raising the rate, and passed a resolution of support. A related ordinance (2026-0012) would fix the rate at 12.000 mills. A resident disputed how the Clerk handled a public comment submitted in opposition to 2B.

kersey/1.title: 2027 Town budget
kersey/1.summary: Town Manager Stacy Brown presented a preliminary 2027 budget in October that reflected direction from the September 22 work session. A public hearing to adopt the budget (Resolution 2026-0027) was set for the November 10 meeting.

kersey/2.title: Water Blueprint Plan and long-term water supply
kersey/2.summary: The Board began the first of three working sessions with Brendle Group on a $50,000 Water Blueprint, funded by a $37,500 DOLA grant, $10,000 from Northern Water and a $2,500 Town match. Northern Water now requires a native water supply for new development, and buy-and-dry pressure means the Town's Colorado-Big Thompson water may not support future growth.

kersey/3.title: Water rate increase options and General Fund subsidy
kersey/3.summary: The November 10 agenda included a discussion of options for raising water rates and of possibly subsidizing water costs from the General Fund.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/November 10, 2026 Regular Meeting Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202611061226010

kersey/4.title: Clark Street Storm Sewer Project contract
kersey/4.summary: The Town got 13 bids and awarded the construction contract to Mountain Constructors, Inc., the second-lowest bidder, after staff raised concerns about the lowest bidder's references and bid items. The bid came in well below the engineer's estimate and is held for 180 days while the Town waits on FEMA funding.

kersey/5.title: Renaming duplicate streets in Berryman Farms
kersey/5.summary: Several streets east of 1st Street in Berryman Farms share names with other streets, which could slow police, fire and EMS response. Staff asked the Board for authority to start renaming them, working with residents, Weld County and emergency agencies.
kersey/5.where: Berryman Farms subdivision, east of 1st Street

kersey/6.title: Kohler Farm P.U.D. zoning amendment
kersey/6.summary: A public hearing was set on Ordinance 2026-0013, which would amend the Kohler Farm P.U.D. to a P.U.D. overlay with Industrial (I) zoning for Lots 1-20 and Outlots N and O.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/November 10, 2026 Regular Meeting Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202611061226010

kersey/7.title: Adoption of the 2024 International Fire Code
kersey/7.summary: After a public hearing with no public comment, the Board considered Ordinance 2026-0010 adopting the 2024 International Fire Code. The Deputy Fire Marshal said it streamlines the Town's fire code requirements and aligns them with the previously adopted code.

kersey/8.title: Sign removal and code enforcement complaint
kersey/8.summary: Resident Bill Cannon told the Board that signs had long been allowed in a location despite a Town ordinance. He called their removal discriminatory and questioned how consistently the ordinance is enforced. The October 13 agenda also covered a code compliance approach centered on voluntary compliance.

kiowa/0.title: New 2026 Zoning Code replacing Chapter 16
kiowa/0.summary: The Planning Commission was asked on July 15 to approve the 2026 Zoning Code Update as the town's official zoning ordinance. On Oct. 13 the Board of Trustees held a public hearing on Ordinance 2026-08, which would repeal and replace Chapter 16 and adopt a new zoning code.

kiowa/1.title: Proposed 2027 town budget and Main Street funding request
kiowa/1.summary: The Board of Trustees took up the proposed 2027 budget in October and held a second presentation on Nov. 10. The Water and Wastewater Authority also had its own 2027 budget presented on Nov. 10, and Kiowa Main Street made a 2027 funding request to the town.

kiowa/2.title: Purchase of property at 319 Comanche Street
kiowa/2.summary: Trustees were asked to approve Resolution 2026-25, a contract to buy the vacant land at 319 Comanche Street. An executive session on Oct. 13 was also noticed to discuss real property purchase and negotiation strategy.

kiowa/3.title: Affordable housing commitment filing
kiowa/3.summary: On Oct. 13 trustees considered Resolution 2026-19 authorizing the Town Administrator to file an affordable housing commitment with the state.

kiowa/4.title: Floodplain permit fee
kiowa/4.summary: The Oct. 13 agenda included discussion of the Town's floodplain permit fee established by Resolution 2026-18.

kiowa/5.title: Trustee compensation and new town staff policies
kiowa/5.summary: On Nov. 10 trustees considered Ordinance 2026-10 amending and setting compensation of the Board of Trustees. They also considered new remote work and cell phone policies (Policies 26-02 and 26-03).

kiowa/6.title: Colorado Plains Project presentation
kiowa/6.summary: The Nov. 10 trustees meeting included a presentation on the County's Colorado Plains Project.

kit-carson-county/0.title: Engie Resources conceptual site plan and setback variance
kit-carson-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission's October 20, 2026 agenda lists a conceptual site plan from Engie Resources and a request for a variance for setbacks. The documents give no details on the project's size or location, and no outcome is recorded.

kit-carson-county/1.title: County road easement for water line trenching (Isenbart / Pace Dirt Works)
kit-carson-county/1.summary: On November 10, 2026 the County Commissioners were to consider a county road easement for Ed Isenbart, submitted by Pace Dirt Works. It would allow trenching a 6-inch-wide water line for animals.

kit-carson-county/2.title: Harper Borrow Pit structure agreement
kit-carson-county/2.summary: The Commissioners' November 10, 2026 agenda includes a structure agreement with Harper Brothers Construction, LLC for the Harper Borrow Pit. The documents give no terms or outcome.

la-junta/0.title: Pueblo sewage spill and Arkansas River safety
la-junta/0.summary: After a major raw sewage spill in Pueblo reached the river near Confluence Park, the Water Director told Council not to use untreated river water for food preparation or cooking. Local drinking water was reported safe and the treatment plant working properly, with reservoir releases raised to 60 cfs to help flush the river.

la-junta/1.title: 2027 city budget and mill levy
la-junta/1.summary: Finance Director Aliza Libby presented the 2027 budget in September. Council adopted the proposed budget by resolution on Oct. 19 and passed the mill levy and annual appropriation ordinances on first reading, with second readings on the Nov. 2 agenda.

la-junta/2.title: 2027 electric, water, wastewater and sanitation rate increases
la-junta/2.summary: The Board of Utilities adopted resolutions changing 2027 prices for electric, water, wastewater and sanitation and recommended the utility fund budgets to Council. Staff noted rate increases are not done lightly but costs keep rising.

la-junta/3.title: Water system loan from the Colorado Water Resources and Power Development Authority
la-junta/3.summary: Council took up an ordinance authorizing a loan from the state water authority to pay for water distribution system improvements, along with a supplemental appropriation to the Water Fund. First reading was Nov. 2 and second reading on Nov. 16. Utility crews are also continuing a system expansion on 24th Street.

la-junta/4.title: Urban Renewal Authority grants and Chestnut Apartments
la-junta/4.summary: The URA tabled a Spark Grant request from Sangre de Cristo Community Care for a storefront sign at 207 Colorado Ave because the work was done before approval; it was later denied for that reason. It approved a roof-repair application from Arkansas Valley CASA and has another application from La Junta Associated Charities pending. The Chestnut Apartments project by Rikhof ran about 52 days past its 180-day contract.

la-junta/5.title: Urban Renewal 2027 budget and TIF district question
la-junta/5.summary: The URA tabled its 2027 budget for a work session, with the budget approval on the Oct. 22 agenda. A resident asked whether the TIF district will expand and what it covers.

la-junta/6.title: New Economic Development Board
la-junta/6.summary: Council passed an ordinance creating an Economic Development Board as an arm of the city, rather than a nonprofit, after IRS-related problems with the earlier structure. The ordinance passed on first and second readings, and the City Clerk will call for letters of interest for board vacancies.

la-junta/7.title: Residents' complaints over handling of an assault case
la-junta/7.summary: Residents told Council that an assault case was dismissed without notifying the family, and cited confusion over city versus county jurisdiction. A family member alleged unprofessionalism within the police department and questioned the Mayor's endorsement of a sheriff candidate.

la-junta/8.title: Street flooding and drainage at Lewis Avenue and 2nd Street
la-junta/8.summary: A Ward 1 resident said only two drains serve the area, causing road flooding and water in business basements after recent rainstorms, and asked the city to address it.

la-junta/9.title: Temporary event ordinance for side-by-sides and low-speed vehicles
la-junta/9.summary: Council passed on first and second readings a temporary ordinance allowing side-by-sides and other low-speed vehicles during an event, with concerns about the ordinance discussed. Such vehicles are used by committee members for events like Tarantula Fest and Early Settlers Day.

la-junta/10.title: Naming Potter Park field for Jim Sullivan
la-junta/10.summary: A request asked Council to name the field Jim Sullivan Field at Potter Park, honoring a long-time school district figure, without renaming the park. It follows the city's community naming procedure.

la-junta/11.title: Arkansas Valley Emergency Communications intergovernmental agreement
la-junta/11.summary: Council approved an intergovernmental agreement establishing an authority for towns and agencies in the Arkansas Valley, funded by a fee on cell phones statewide.

lafayette/0.title: New Land Use Code and Old Town OTX-3 zoning
lafayette/0.summary: Council took up Ordinance No. 15, a full rewrite of the Land Use Code and zoning map, with first reading Aug. 18 and second reading Sept. 15. Residents objected to the OTX-3 district along South Public Road south of Emma Street, citing building height and size. A joint Planning Commission/Council workshop on Sept. 9 reached general agreement on changes such as cutting the OTX-3 footprint cap from 25,000 to 10,000 sq. ft. and rezoning the 700 block to OTX-1, with height and other items left for a second ordinance.

lafayette/1.title: Boulder Ranch annexation and housing proposal
lafayette/1.summary: Residents wrote in against the proposed Boulder Ranch development, about 78 acres near Baseline Road and Burlington. They cited density, traffic and bike safety on Baseline, loss of open space, and an agreement not to annex between cities, and said over 2,000 people signed petitions. On Nov. 2 Council considered a resolution finding the annexation petition in substantial compliance and setting an eligibility hearing.
lafayette/1.where: Southeast of Baseline Road and Nyland Way

lafayette/2.title: Flock license plate cameras and the 2027 budget
lafayette/2.summary: Residents repeatedly asked Council to end the Flock Safety license plate reader contract and to exempt surveillance contracts from administrative approval. Council considered two budget versions, 2026-24A and 2026-24B, the latter with no Flock funding, and a separate appropriation ordinance for the Flock contract. Council also discussed a formal policy on automatic license plate readers.

lafayette/3.title: 2027 budget, mill levy and fee changes
lafayette/3.summary: Staff introduced a 2027 recommended budget with $128 million in revenue, a 3% sales tax increase assumption to $26.2 million, and no General Fund balance use. Council adopted the budget and mill levy and the 2027 pay plan, and considered fee updates to Chapter 4 (Ordinance 19). Discussion included utility rates, the Urban Renewal Authority sunset and the Open Space Ranger position.

lafayette/4.title: Moratoria on data centers and advanced air mobility
lafayette/4.summary: Council considered an 18-month moratorium on land use applications and building permits for data centers (Ordinance 21, second reading Oct. 20) and an emergency 18-month moratorium on advanced air mobility facilities (Ordinance 22).

lafayette/5.title: Naming the 701 S. Public Road pocket park for Rosebelle Lueras
lafayette/5.summary: Many residents spoke in favor of naming the new pocket park at 701 S. Public Road "Rosebelle Park" for Rosebelle Lueras. A naming motion was on the Oct. 20 agenda.

lafayette/6.title: Capital bond projects: recreation center, service center, civic center
lafayette/6.summary: Voters approved $74 million in bonds in November 2025 for the Bob L. Burger Recreation Center, Service Center and Civic Center. Council held first and second readings of the General Obligation Bonds ordinance (No. 16), with the first tranche expected in October 2026, and approved a Service Center design-build guaranteed maximum price contract. A Sept. 22 bus tour covered related projects including LaMont Does Park and the water park.

lafayette/7.title: Church parcel zoning at Highway 287 and South Boulder Road
lafayette/7.summary: Council amended its August 18 direction so church parcels at Highway 287 and South Boulder Road would be zoned consistently with Immaculate Conception (NC). Residents spoke both for and against the rezoning, and some urged Council to wait.

lafayette/8.title: Douglass Elementary School future
lafayette/8.summary: Council directed staff to work with Councilor Jensen on a letter asking BVSD to consider whether it had a sufficient record of Lafayette input on Douglass Elementary. A resident wrote that Lafayette families had no representation in the engagement process.

lafayette/9.title: Affordable housing: bond allocation, expedited review and inclusionary housing
lafayette/9.summary: Council assigned its 2026 private activity bond allocation to the Boulder County Housing Authority. It considered a resolution supporting expedited review for affordable housing projects and heard inclusionary housing and affordable housing impact fee recommendations on Nov. 2.

lafayette/10.title: Oil and gas regulation workshop
lafayette/10.summary: Following public comment on low-producing wells, staff briefed Council on local authority over oil and gas under Colorado law, existing city rules and state regulatory developments. The session was informational with no action.

lafayette/11.title: Street racing near Avalon Flatirons on South Public Road
lafayette/11.summary: A resident wrote that street racers fill the Flatirons Church parking lot across from Avalon Flatirons, with loud engines and speeding, and that police drove by without responding.
lafayette/11.where: South Public Road near Flatirons Church

lafayette/12.title: SH7 / 95th Street intersection agreement and 709 S. Public Road right-of-way
lafayette/12.summary: Council approved an intergovernmental agreement with CDOT for the SH7 corridor 95th Street intersection project. On Nov. 2 it considered buying part of 709 S. Public Road for right-of-way improvements.
lafayette/12.where: SH7 at 95th Street; 709 S. Public Road

lake-city/0.title: Phase 1 Hinsdale County & Lake City Housing Plan implementation
lake-city/0.summary: In August the council approved the PC-IN-922 Phase 1 Housing Plan Implementation grant agreement and picked a consultant by RFP. The consultant name shifted across documents (Collegiate Peaks Law & Mediation, then Western Space/Spaces LLC). A professional services agreement with Western Spaces LLC was approved on Nov. 4.

lake-city/1.title: Elk Fire response and emergency water agreement with USDA Forest Service
lake-city/1.summary: Council discussed the Elk Fire on the Lake City border and approved an emergency facilities and land use agreement letting the Forest Service use town potable water and grey water disposal at $0.03 per gallon. On Oct. 21 it considered Resolution 2026-13 ending the local disaster emergency. Backup generators lent by Estes Park and Windsor were also thanked.
lake-city/1.where: Lake City and unincorporated Hinsdale County

lake-city/2.title: 2027 budget, water and sewer rates, and capital projects
lake-city/2.summary: Council worked through the 2027 draft budget in October and November, including 2027 water and sewer rates, capital improvement projects, donations funding, and health insurance plan options. The town manager was appointed budget officer, and a budget workshop was set for Nov. 11.

lake-city/3.title: ADU grant and Armory apartment rules
lake-city/3.summary: Council approved a DOLA ADU grant application of $107,000 with a $13,910 match for pre-approved accessory dwelling unit designs and financial assistance. It also discussed rent and applicant criteria for Armory apartments.
lake-city/3.where: Lake City; Armory, 230 N. Bluff Street

lake-city/4.title: Colorado Ride 2027 tent camping in Memorial Park
lake-city/4.summary: Summit Cycle Solutions asked to use Memorial Park for tent camping Aug. 11-13, 2027 for about 70 participants. Council approved the request and then Resolution 2026-12 permitting it.

lake-city/5.title: Dark Sky Community certification
lake-city/5.summary: Council discussed requirements and the application for International Dark Sky Community designation.

lake-city/6.title: Wildfire resiliency code and 2026 audit
lake-city/6.summary: Council discussed CML and DOLA responses on the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption and future grant funding. It also moved to draft an RFP for the 2026 audit and approved an engagement letter with Green & Associates LLC.

lake-city/7.title: Pickleball courts public engagement and Town Park dogs
lake-city/7.summary: Council discussed public engagement on pickleball courts for spring/summer 2027. It approved Resolution 2026-11 permitting dogs in Town Park for the Chamber's Dog Days of Summer event on Sept. 5.

lake-county/0.title: Rural Lodging and Camping moratorium and Land Development Code amendments
lake-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on 26-17 on Oct. 12 on new rules for rural lodging, campgrounds and accessory special events, meant to protect Backcountry zoning. Standards cover water, access, parking, lighting, noise and event management plans. The commissioners were scheduled to consider Resolution 2026-35 amending the code on Oct. 20, lifting the moratorium imposed by Resolution 2026-06.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/1.title: E911 Authority budget, restructuring and PUC surcharge application
lake-county/1.summary: The E911 Authority worked through its 2027 budget (Resolutions 26-02 and 2026-03), a dispatch reorganization, and an application to the Colorado PUC to raise the emergency telephone charge. It also weighed a CentralSquare software proposal against the current Motorola/Flex contract and exit costs. The county also discussed an offsite dispatch office.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Work Sessions

lake-county/2.title: Leadville–Lake County fire IGA and firefighter pay
lake-county/2.summary: A new intergovernmental agreement between the City of Leadville and the County for Leadville-Lake County Fire Rescue was considered Oct. 20 and later noted as approved by City Council and the commissioners. At the Fire Management Board, the union president said firefighters earn about 25% less than sheriff deputies and proposed raising pay to 90% of deputy pay. Highway 91 safety concerns were also raised.
lake-county/2.where: Leadville fire stations, 816 Harrison Ave and 141 County Road 10

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/3.title: Colorado Mountain College housing project
lake-county/3.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing and moved to approve a CMC housing project on its existing campus, with 48 parking spaces, access from existing roads and wildfire-resiliency compliance. Staff said it is not subject to zoning review under state statute, and commissioners voiced support, citing Leadville's tight housing market.

lake-county/4.title: Affordable housing, Prop 123 IGA and Housing Authority
lake-county/4.summary: The Regional Housing Authority gave its semi-annual report to commissioners on its strategic plan, housing pipeline and 2027 budget. Commissioners also considered a first amendment to the Prop 123 IGA on affordable housing commitments, which calls for a cumulative 9 percent increase in affordable housing inventory and expedited review.

lake-county/5.title: 2027 county budget and capital requests
lake-county/5.summary: Commissioners held work sessions on departmental 2027 budgets (administration, planning, animal shelter, fire), elected officials' requests, and capital requests including a Certificate of Participation. A preliminary budget was presented Oct. 13. Audited 2025 financial statements were also reviewed.

lake-county/6.title: Leadville–Lake County joint comprehensive plan
lake-county/6.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the joint comprehensive plan, including water augmentation and future code amendments drawing on the Housing Needs Assessment. It was slated for November hearings.

lake-county/7.title: Hayden Ranch rezoning to PUD
lake-county/7.summary: Commissioners considered Resolution 2026-38, written findings conditionally approving the rezoning of Hayden Ranch, 5801 S. Highway 24, from Rural to Planned Unit Development. The public hearing had already been held.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/8.title: Aurora water deliveries and storage IGA
lake-county/8.summary: Commissioners considered an amended and restated IGA between the City of Aurora and Lake County on water deliveries and storage, presented by the Water and Natural Resources Director.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/9.title: County–City shared services and efficiencies
lake-county/9.summary: Lake County and Leadville held a joint work session on operational efficiencies and shared services, including forming a joint task force and coordinated legislative advocacy.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/10.title: Highway safety and Gateway Mobility Plan
lake-county/10.summary: Commissioners discussed transportation and safety on state highways and the Lake County Gateway Mobility Plan. Highway 91 safety measures such as guardrails, signs and speed enforcement were raised with CDOT.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Work Sessions

lake-county/11.title: Animal shelter staffing, budget and IGA changes
lake-county/11.summary: The Animal Shelter Advisory Board discussed staffing, hours, 2027 budget, a possible Ark Valley partnership and modifications to the shelter IGA.

lake-county/12.title: Willow Fire debrief and wildfire restrictions
lake-county/12.summary: Commissioners held a debrief on the Willow Fire and lessons learned, and later ratified rescinding all fire restrictions in unincorporated areas.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings
Board of County Commissioners Work Sessions

lakewood/0.title: Ballot Issue 2G: half-cent sales tax for public and traffic safety
lakewood/0.summary: Council adopted Resolution 2026-58 on Aug. 24 to put Ballot Issue 2G on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot. It would raise the sales and use tax rate by one-half percent, with revenue dedicated to public safety and traffic safety. On Oct. 12 council considered a resolution formally supporting the measure.

lakewood/1.title: Automated license plate readers and red-light/speed camera vendor safeguards
lakewood/1.summary: Police presented on the 17 fixed Flock Safety license plate cameras the city has run, and council discussed safeguards and how they relate to the proposed automated vehicle identification system for red-light and speed enforcement. In November staff brought draft accountability language to guide contracts as the city seeks a new vendor for both technologies.

lakewood/2.title: Affordable Housing Fund study session
lakewood/2.summary: On Nov. 16 council reviewed the Housing Policy Commission's 2026 discussions on creating a local Affordable Housing Fund, including housing need data and homelessness trends, and the steps toward an ordinance establishing the fund. A separate item sets 2026 neighborhood and affordable housing preservation funding, including a 3% increase to affordable housing stock.

lakewood/3.title: West Colfax LRA investment strategy
lakewood/3.summary: Staff presented an updated strategy for spending West Colfax urban renewal tax increment funds, which expire in 2030. Ten potential projects were scored, including the Quail Street Center, and the Colfax transportation safety project would narrow Colfax from three lanes to two each direction.
lakewood/3.where: West Colfax corridor, Pierce Street to Simms Street

lakewood/4.title: 2027 city and LRA budgets
lakewood/4.summary: Council saw the revised 2026 and proposed 2027 city budget in a September study session. The Lakewood Reinvestment Authority reviewed its revised 2026 and proposed 2027 budget, with approval sought Oct. 19. Council also approved 2027 budgets for the Alameda Corridor and West Colfax business improvement districts.

lakewood/5.title: Public benefit agreement to keep Natural Grocers headquarters in Lakewood
lakewood/5.summary: Council considered a performance-based incentive agreement to keep Natural Grocers' national headquarters in Lakewood, with 50 new jobs and repayment if it moves. It follows a 2023 agreement for up to $500,000 that did not proceed because required public improvements grew beyond its scope.
lakewood/5.where: Natural Grocers headquarters, 12612 W. Alameda Parkway

lakewood/6.title: Rezonings on Kipling, Mansfield and Duquesne
lakewood/6.summary: Council took up a series of rezoning ordinances in fall 2026: 2555 S. Kipling St. and 7201 W. Mansfield Ave. (first reading Oct. 26, second reading Nov. 9), and 7801 W. Duquesne and 2501 S. Kipling St. (first reading Nov. 9).
lakewood/6.where: 2555 and 2501 S. Kipling St.; 7201 W. Mansfield Ave.; 7801 W. Duquesne

lakewood/7.title: Purchase of 1081 Vance Street for open space and parks
lakewood/7.summary: Council moved an ordinance authorizing the city to buy the property at 1081 Vance Street for municipal open space and park purposes, with first reading Sept. 28 and second reading Oct. 12.

lakewood/8.title: 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption
lakewood/8.summary: Council took up an ordinance adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code with local deletions and amendments, with first reading Aug. 24 and second reading Sept. 28.

lakewood/9.title: Permanent police committee
lakewood/9.summary: Council amended Resolution R-2026-6 to revise the ad-hoc committee working toward a permanent police committee and considered appointing a member to it on Sept. 28.

lakewood/10.title: City manager contract
lakewood/10.summary: Council's Aug. 24 agenda included a resolution on the city manager's contract; the condensed agenda gives no details of the terms.

lamar/0.title: Data center moratorium and development standards
lamar/0.summary: Council discussed data centers in September, then heard residents' concerns in October and November. It also debated a proposed 24-month moratorium so the city has time to write community benefit and responsible development standards. The mayor said no agreement or NDA has been signed and that a company contacted the city first.

lamar/1.title: Main Café brownfield cleanup
lamar/1.summary: The city held a pre-bid walk-through for the EPA-funded cleanup and awarded Bid 46-002 for $483,299 to Rockies Environmental on Oct. 12. The contract has since been signed, and staff are starting a third assessment grant and closing out the second.

lamar/2.title: 2027 city budget adoption
lamar/2.summary: Staff began budget meetings with directors in August and held a council work session on revenue projections on Aug. 24. Council approved Ordinance No. 1290 adopting the 2027 budget on Nov. 9.

lamar/3.title: Ward I council vacancy filled
lamar/3.summary: Robert Seay was the only applicant for the vacant Ward I seat. He was interviewed in open session and appointed to serve until November 2027.

lamar/4.title: Subdivision regulations rewrite (Ordinance 1287)
lamar/4.summary: Council approved on second reading Ordinance No. 1287 amending Chapter 22, Subdivisions, of the municipal code.

lamar/5.title: Land Use Board seat and outside counsel review
lamar/5.summary: The administrator said an appointment to the Land Use Board seat will wait until outside counsel completes a document and internal review it was engaged to do.

lamar/6.title: Parks and recreation upgrades
lamar/6.summary: Escondido Field was topsoiled, reseeded and treated for weeds and fungus. Council members discussed replacing the community building carpet and looking for grants for ADA-accessible playground equipment. Kolby Brubacher was made permanent Park, Cemetery & Recreation Director.

lamar/7.title: Willow Valley water line project
lamar/7.summary: A councilmember reported the water line project should be finalized within weeks. The Street Department will then make street repairs.

lamar/8.title: Resident complaints on law enforcement response and affordable housing
lamar/8.summary: At the Nov. 9 meeting Donna Smith said law enforcement keeps refusing to respond to her calls and submitted a formal written request. Another resident asked about affordable housing.

lamar/9.title: Donated Colorado State Patrol Taser equipment
lamar/9.summary: Council accepted Taser X26P units and equipment donated by the Colorado State Patrol, worth about $50,000.

lamar/10.title: Tyler software system rollout
lamar/10.summary: The city is moving sales tax, court, utility billing, parks and recreation, accounts receivable and cemetery functions into the Tyler system. Most modules are close to done, with sales tax and cemetery still pending in November.

limon/0.title: 2026 budget, property tax levy and appropriations
limon/0.summary: Council held a budget workshop on Nov. 18, 2025, then a public hearing on Dec. 10 to adopt the 2026 budget (Resolution 25-12-20), set the property tax levy (25-12-21) and appropriate funds (Ordinance 648). A 2025 budget supplement and supplemental appropriations were heard Dec. 29.

limon/1.title: Water and sewer projects
limon/1.summary: Council received a GMS report and recommendations for water and sewer projects in April 2026, followed by project reports and discussions in August and November 2026.

limon/2.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption
limon/2.summary: Council held a public hearing in March 2026 on adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code (Ordinance 649). The ordinance appeared again on the April agenda.

limon/3.title: Municipal code changes on driver licensing and penalties
limon/3.summary: Council took up ordinances to enforce state vehicle rules (Ordinance 650), require a valid license or permit when driving (651), and amend municipal penalties (652).

limon/4.title: Affordable housing project review policies
limon/4.summary: In June 2026 council considered Resolution 26-06-12 establishing review policies for affordable housing projects. A Housing Authority board appointment followed in August.

limon/5.title: Limon Municipal Airport
limon/5.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-04-07 on transferring airport entitlements to Archuleta County in April 2026, and received a presentation on the airport in August.

limon/6.title: Chip sealing of city streets
limon/6.summary: Council considered a proposal from A-1 Chipseal to chip seal designated streets (Resolution 26-05-10).

limon/7.title: Tamarack Golf Club user rates
limon/7.summary: Council set user rates for Tamarack Golf Club through Resolution 26-03-06.

littleton/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center applications
littleton/0.summary: Council took up Ordinance 22-2026 on first reading Oct. 20 and second reading Nov. 3. It would temporarily halt acceptance, processing and approval of data center applications while staff study and recommend land use regulations.

littleton/1.title: 2027 budget and tax levies
littleton/1.summary: On Nov. 3 council had first reading of ordinances appropriating the 2027 annual budget, adopting enterprise fund budgets and amending the 2026 budget, plus tax levies for the city and the Downtown Development Authority. Council also discussed the 2027 fee schedule on Nov. 10, and approved 2027 operating plans for the Aspen Grove and Mineral business improvement districts.

littleton/2.title: Public authority for jointly owned wastewater treatment facility
littleton/2.summary: Resolution 81-2026 expresses council support for forming a public authority to operate the city's jointly owned wastewater treatment facility and directs staff to take next steps.

littleton/3.title: Economic Partnership Incentive Policy and developer agreements
littleton/3.summary: Council amended the Economic Partnership Incentives Policy (Resolution 61-2026) and considered sales tax share-back agreements with RIG Mineral LLC and Scheels. It also discussed an incentive agreement for Chachi's and held follow-up policy talks and incentive strategy sessions.

littleton/4.title: Geneva Village redevelopment
littleton/4.summary: Council heard the Geneva Village Redevelopment Advisory Team's recommendation on Oct. 27.

littleton/5.title: E-bike safety ordinance and 25 mph speed limit
littleton/5.summary: Council discussed a draft e-bike and e-motor safety ordinance. Ordinance 17-2026 would set a maximum lawful speed limit of 25 mph and moved to second reading Sept. 1. Council also received a Safer Streets update.

littleton/6.title: Hauler licensing, waste diversion and recycling rules
littleton/6.summary: Council discussed hauler licensing and an equal space ordinance proposal, approved a subaward with Circular Action Alliance, and moved Ordinance 19-2026 amending Title 3 through two readings, citing the South Metro Waste Diversion Plan.

littleton/7.title: Bear Valley Bible Institute master plan
littleton/7.summary: Planning Commission held a hearing on a Conceptual Master Development Plan for Bear Valley Bible Institute.

littleton/8.title: Sign variances for 2450 W Main Street
littleton/8.summary: The Appeals & Adjustment Commission considered seven variances for signs at the address, including a marquee sign projecting 6 ft instead of 4 ft, 30 ft clearance versus 25 ft, exposed bulb lighting and extra window signs.

littleton/9.title: Street projects, Main Street and transportation planning
littleton/9.summary: Council approved a 2026 mill and overlay contract with Chavez Construction, a surface sealing IGA, and a Transportation Master Plan update contract. It also reviewed the Elati Street corridor study and Main Street investment strategies.

littleton/10.title: Land use code update and joint study sessions
littleton/10.summary: Planning Commission previewed the Unified Land Use Code update and discussed joint study session topics with council.

logan-county/0.title: South Platte Metropolitan District wastewater violations and rental treatment unit
logan-county/0.summary: The district serving an HOA community has about 170 discharge violations to groundwater and a cease-and-desist order. It is paying roughly $28,000 to $78,000 a month for a rental temporary treatment unit, is raising rates, and is struggling to get loans or grants. The Commissioners reviewed its finances and plan on Oct. 27.

logan-county/1.title: Sterling splash pad proposed downtown
logan-county/1.summary: The Sterling Community Fund asked the Commissioners for advice and possible approval of a concrete splash pad downtown near an urban park, to draw foot traffic and build the tax base. A private donor has offered $100,000, and the fund would cover water, sewer and upkeep. Concerns raised include parking, aesthetics and restroom cleanup.

logan-county/2.title: Sterling road-maintenance sales tax ballot question
logan-county/2.summary: Sterling plans a ballot question to raise its sales tax from 3% to 4% for five years, with the money dedicated to city road maintenance. A similar measure failed last year. The Commissioners can't spend public money on it but the county attorney will draft a resolution they could pass encouraging a vote.

logan-county/3.title: Rural Health Transformation Program grant for ambulance interfacility transports
logan-county/3.summary: Sterling Fire/EMS was approved for a federal Rural Health Transformation Program grant to advance EMS and handle interfacility transports. The contract needed county and city attorney review and a special meeting by Oct. 27-28. Concerns include missing wellness funding for paramedic positions and whether the county audit covers the federal funds.

logan-county/4.title: EMS and ambulance budget for 2027
logan-county/4.summary: The Sterling Fire Department EMS battalion chief asked for guidance on moving a $14,000 RETAC training grant into 2027 and pursuing a CDPHE ambulance grant (about $40,000 match on a $337,000 ambulance). The city and county are also sorting out how to split costs, and the city wants a 3% cost-of-living raise included.

logan-county/5.title: Prairie dog proposal before Colorado Parks and Wildlife
logan-county/5.summary: The Commissioners discussed a petition and proposed rules on prairie dogs before the Colorado Parks and Wildlife Commission. Speakers questioned whether local voices would be heard and said the proposal lacks compensation for landowners, and people were urged to submit written comments.

logan-county/6.title: CR 26 bridge and county bridge grants
logan-county/6.summary: The Road and Bridge department weighed applying for a bridge planning and engineering grant for the CR 26 bridge but decided not to pursue it, since the board didn't want the bridge closed for a 2-3 year project. The board decided to hold a public meeting on the bridge's future, and discussed other narrow bridges and an engineer for a cheaper design.

logan-county/7.title: Permit Gateway for oversize and overweight transport permits
logan-county/7.summary: Road and Bridge staff described how manual oversize/overweight permits are slow, especially for weekend requests. The Board supported moving to Permit Gateway, which is free to the county, with carriers paying a service fee, and provides road maps and restrictions.

logan-county/8.title: DOLA grants and comprehensive plan update
logan-county/8.summary: A DOLA regional manager warned that state grant funding is uncertain but pointed to CDBG and REDI grants and a possible $50,000 housing-planning award for a Sterling/county comprehensive plan, which would need a county match. The county's plan dates from 2013 or earlier.

logan-county/9.title: Battery storage, wind and solar energy projects
logan-county/9.summary: Commissioners toured a battery energy storage facility and noted its fire suppression and three-year safety record. Niyol Wind sought road access and temporary sign removal at County Roads 67 and 24 to replace blades on two towers. A solar developer wanted to discuss county solar regulations she finds limiting.

logan-county/10.title: Fairgrounds master plan and Fair Board finances
logan-county/10.summary: The fairgrounds manager sought direction on capital spending from last year's master plan for next year's budget. The Fair Board found about $22,000 lost to ticket-service fees, and is weighing a porta cooler purchase, sponsorship renewals and a bull riding contract.

logan-county/11.title: County employee health pool rates
logan-county/11.summary: County Health Pool rates dropped this year, with the employee-only plan down $11 and the family plan down $26, and dental moves to Ameritas at the same rates. Staff asked about separate tier rates and a stipend for older employees; the county pays 65% of family premiums.

logan-county/12.title: Railroad crossing closure near Peetz at Highway 138
logan-county/12.summary: The railroad is considering closing a crossing at Highway 138 near Peetz, and the Board planned to meet the railroad about it.

lone-tree/0.title: Fidelity Office Building site improvement plan (SP26-0017)
lone-tree/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on the Fidelity Office Building site improvement plan on Oct. 27. City Council opened its Nov. 3 hearing only to continue it to Nov. 17, with no testimony taken that night.

lone-tree/1.title: Hillcamp Drive/Cabela Drive extension plat and water booster pump station
lone-tree/1.summary: City Council's Nov. 3 agenda included public hearings on the Hillcamp Drive/Cabela Drive Extension Final Plat (SB25-0014) and a water booster pump station at Hillcamp (USR25-0002, SP25-0023). The plat hearing was set to be continued to Nov. 17.

lone-tree/2.title: Colorado Transportation and Housing Investment Zone application
lone-tree/2.summary: Council considered an engagement letter with Beck Rivera LLP for legal and advocacy services on the city's 2027 Colorado Transportation and Housing Zone application. A program update was given at the Nov. 3 study session.

lone-tree/3.title: Southwest Village plan and parks master plan amendments
lone-tree/3.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on Oct. 27 on amendments to the Southwest Village Preliminary Plan (RG26-0003) and the Southwest Village Parks Master Plan (RG26-0002).

lone-tree/4.title: Business improvement district 2027 budgets
lone-tree/4.summary: Council took up resolutions 26-47 and 26-48 approving the 2027 operating plans and budgets for the Park Meadows and Lone Tree Business Improvement Districts.

lone-tree/5.title: Unified Development Code review
lone-tree/5.summary: Council's Oct. 26 strategy session featured an overview and preliminary discussion of a Unified Development Code.

lone-tree/6.title: Parks, Open Space and Trails Master Plan and Entertainment District Park
lone-tree/6.summary: The Recreation Advisory Committee worked on the Parks, Open Space, and Trails Master Plan and discussed the Entertainment District Park, High Note Park and the South Suburban strategic plan.

lone-tree/7.title: Council strategy session on staffing, police and capital plans
lone-tree/7.summary: The Oct. 5 strategy session covered compensation and a 5-year staffing plan, the police department, the capital projects 5-year plan and community development. No votes or public comment occur at these sessions.

longmont/0.title: 1st and Main urban renewal plan, transit center and parking garage financing
longmont/0.summary: The Longmont Urban Renewal Authority took up tax increment revenue agreements for the 1st and Main plan area with the city, Boulder County, Northern Water, the St. Vrain Valley School District and the Downtown Development Authority. City Council also considered the urban renewal plan, a lease-purchase financing of a parking garage, and a development agreement with Main Street Tebo, LLC for the 1st and Main Transit Center and a transit-oriented project.

sources.body: City Council Joint Meeting with Boulder County Commissioners

longmont/1.title: 2027 city budget and capital improvement program
longmont/1.summary: Council received the 2027 proposed budget and 2027-2031 Capital Improvement Program, held public hearings on Sept. 29 and Oct. 6, and gave final direction. Related items include the Downtown Development District tax levy.

longmont/2.title: November ballot measures: public safety tax, open space sales, ranked choice voting
longmont/2.summary: Council took up a resolution calling a special election on a city sales and property tax increase for public safety and on charter amendments requiring voter approval to sell open space and providing for ranked choice voting. It also considered resolutions urging a yes vote on these and on a Boulder County property tax ballot issue.

longmont/3.title: Annexations: Dry Creek, 8513 St. Vrain Road, Gateway Northwest and 8979 Nelson Road
longmont/3.summary: Council moved through several annexations. Dry Creek (Airport Road and Clover Basin Drive) and 8513 St. Vrain Road were to be zoned Residential Mixed Neighborhood. The Longmont Gateway Northwest annexation at U.S. 287 and Park Ridge Avenue includes a comprehensive plan amendment. A neighborhood meeting notice covered a proposed annexation of a 0.88-acre church parcel at 8979 Nelson Road.
longmont/3.where: Airport Road/Clover Basin Drive; 8513 St. Vrain Road; US 287 and Park Ridge Ave; 8979 Nelson Road

longmont/4.title: Longmont Housing Authority: Briarwood sale, Zinnia Apartments and bonds
longmont/4.summary: The Housing Authority board dealt with a purchase and sale agreement with All Roads for Briarwood Apartments and commercial space at 1227 Kimbark Street. It also discussed Zinnia Apartments (property manager resignation, sale of the general partner's interest), multifamily housing revenue bonds, and the city's assignment of its 2026 private activity bond allocation to the Authority.

sources.body: Longmont Housing Authority Board of Commissioners
Special LHA Board of Commissioners Meeting
Longmont Housing Authority Board of Commissioners

longmont/5.title: Housing needs, vouchers and affordable housing funding
longmont/5.summary: The Housing and Human Services board reviewed an update to the housing needs assessment required by state law SB 24-174. The Housing Authority adopted a voucher administrative plan and 2027 budgets and discussed the countywide affordable housing tax review. Council and Boulder County commissioners also planned to discuss affordable housing funding and for-sale housing demand.

sources.body: Housing and Human Service Advisory Board
Longmont Housing Authority Board of Commissioners Meeting
City Council Joint Meeting with Boulder County Commissioners

longmont/6.title: Human services funding hearings
longmont/6.summary: The Housing and Human Services Advisory Board held a series of agency hearings in September and October on funding requests from local service providers, and discussed the application process and challenges at HOPE, Our Center and All Roads.

longmont/7.title: Airport vision and noise monitoring
longmont/7.summary: Council held a vision session on the future of the airport, covering governance models and building trust with the community. Staff also presented options for implementing airport monitoring systems.

longmont/8.title: Water service for Hygiene Fire Protection District and Water Board items
longmont/8.summary: Council considered extraterritorial water service for the Hygiene Fire Protection District's fire house (larger tap) and a fire suppression system. The Water Board also reviewed Ralph Price Reservoir water rights, conveyance plats, and a presentation on the Dry Creek Fire near Button Rock, plus rate structure and legislative water principles.
longmont/8.where: Hygiene Fire Protection District; Ralph Price Reservoir

longmont/9.title: Composting rates and sanitation rate structure
longmont/9.summary: The Sustainability Advisory Board was asked to weigh in on compost rate changes and sanitation rate structure at Council's request. Council study sessions covered composting subsidy rate proposals and solid waste collection issues in alleys.

longmont/10.title: Platte River Power Authority noncarbon energy plan
longmont/10.summary: Platte River staff briefed the Sustainability Advisory Board on its noncarbon goals and Integrated Resource Plan. A federal emergency order kept Craig Unit 1 from retiring at the end of 2025, and the plan is to be finalized by January 2028.

longmont/11.title: Contractor's shops in MU-E zone and building fee updates
longmont/11.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission heard a citizen-initiated request to allow contractor's shops as a permitted use in the MU-E zone, with the hearing possibly continued to Nov. 18. Council also saw updates to building permit and contractor license fees.

longmont/12.title: Neighborhood proposals: Avis rental, 10930 Airport Road, 607 Emery short-term rental
longmont/12.summary: Neighborhood meeting notices covered Avis Car Rental at 206 S. Main, a single-family homes proposal at 10930 Airport Road needing plan amendments and rezoning, a replat at 160 11th Avenue, and a conditional use for a short-term rental at 607 Emery Street.
longmont/12.where: 206 S. Main; 10930 Airport Road; 160 11th Ave; 605-607 Emery Street

longmont/13.title: Police shooting review executive session
longmont/13.summary: Council scheduled an executive session on Nov. 3 to discuss the Dariss Yearby officer-involved shooting.

longmont/14.title: Show cause hearing on liquor license at 333 Main Street
longmont/14.summary: The Local Licensing Authority scheduled a show cause hearing on whether to act against a liquor license at 333 Main Street over alleged disturbances, noise and open container violations. The hearing was continued and rescheduled.

sources.body: Local Licensing Authority- CONTINUED TO DATE TBD

louisville/0.title: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance update (Ordinance 1936)
louisville/0.summary: Council took up Ordinance 1936 amending Title 17 inclusionary housing rules, with a second-reading public hearing on Aug 18 and another hearing Sept 15 with second-reading amendments. Strong Towns Louisville urged zoning reform first, by-right incentives and an exemption for small 10-12 unit projects; a resident also wrote with concerns that new market-rate units could raise prices.

louisville/1.title: 2027-2028 budget, mill levy and fee increases
louisville/1.summary: Council worked through the 2027-2028 budget from the July retreat through the City Manager's initial presentation (Sept 1), a public hearing on Oct 20 and budget and mill levy adoption set for Nov 2. Discussion covered the General Fund gap, capital plan, 2027 fees, utility rates and a decision to pull the $780,000 northeast water loop from the budget.

louisville/2.title: Centennial Valley GDP amendment and Centennial Drive affordable senior housing
louisville/2.summary: The Centennial Valley General Development Plan amendment would allow multifamily affordable housing and set building heights; it went to the parks and open space boards and the Planning Commission, which favored the project. A resident letter argued the proposed parks and open space are inadequate for a development that would grow Louisville's housing units by about 12%. A concept plan for affordable senior housing on Centennial Drive was set for Council Oct 6.

louisville/3.title: Parks, Open Space and Trails (PROS) plan and open space protections
louisville/3.summary: The draft PROS Guidebook, Long Range Plan and Trails System Plan went through the open space and parks boards and Council, with a resolution adopting the plans on the Nov 2 agenda. Louisville Open Space Advocates sent a long letter asking that the City Charter be followed, Trail 18 removed and buffers added. Residents also opposed development of 8600 Baseline and raised prairie dog concerns.

louisville/4.title: Comprehensive Plan and Development Code update
louisville/4.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the updated Comprehensive Plan, with residents voicing concerns about projected growth, traffic, water supply, evacuation routes and wildfire risk. The City accepted a state DOLA grant and awarded a contract for a Development Code update, and Council and Planning Commission discussed the Commission's role in it.

louisville/5.title: Golf course and recreation center fees for 2027
louisville/5.summary: The Recreation Advisory Board reviewed golf fee modeling showing green fees alone cannot close the golf fund deficit, and recommended 2027 golf fees and passes. It also approved 3% resident and 7% non-resident increases to Recreation and Senior Center admission fees, which went into the 2027 City Manager fee resolution. A Council member asked whether a resident golf membership rate had been considered.
louisville/5.where: Coal Creek Golf Course; Recreation & Senior Center

louisville/6.title: Sale of city property at 1501 Empire Road and 1303 Empire Road
louisville/6.summary: Council approved a purchase contract to sell 1501 Empire Road and the easterly part of 1303 Empire Road to Ripple Creek Properties LLC; the property is zoned Industrial and the subdivision would not change zoning. A November amendment extends the buyer's examination period from 60 to 100 days.

louisville/7.title: 1155 Pine Street lease/purchase and Coal Creek Junction subdivision
louisville/7.summary: Council considered Ordinance 1937 extending and amending the contract for lease and purchase of real estate at 1155 Pine Street, with a public hearing Oct 6. The Planning Commission also took up the Coal Creek Junction final plat to subdivide the site.

louisville/8.title: Grain Elevator and Grain Yard downtown funding
louisville/8.summary: The Revitalization Commission handled a tax increment financing agreement, facade and property improvement funding for the Grain Yard, and a conditional assignment of grants for the Grain Elevator at 540 County Road. It also discussed reallocating about $344,400 of unspent property improvement funds, and concerns that Front and Center construction will affect Street Fair and Front Street businesses.
louisville/8.where: Grain Elevator, 540 County Road; Front Street

louisville/9.title: Business assistance agreements for Infleqtion Quantum and Arsenal Health
louisville/9.summary: Council considered business assistance agreements of $281,114 with Infleqtion Quantum and $208,400 with Arsenal Health, plus an amended agreement with Louisville Cyclery. Staff revised the Infleqtion agreement after a Council question about clawback terms.

louisville/10.title: Historic preservation: landmark designations, grants and preservation tax
louisville/10.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission handled the landmark request for the Methodist Church at 741 Jefferson Avenue, grants for 613 Grant Avenue and the Mudrock House, and a demolition application at 181 Roosevelt Avenue. Council also put a Historic Preservation Tax on the 2026 election, and a resident architect submitted suggestions for expanding the program.
louisville/10.where: 741 Jefferson Avenue; 613 Grant Avenue; 181 Roosevelt Avenue

louisville/11.title: Sustainability, electrification and climate funding
louisville/11.summary: The Sustainability Advisory Board presented to Council on funding, building codes and a possible sustainability tax, and reviewed electrification rebates and an agreement with Power Ahead Colorado. A commenter urged Council to direct the budget toward cutting carbon emissions and electrifying city facilities, and seven businesses were awarded commercial sustainability rebates.

louisville/12.title: E-bike and e-moto regulations and traffic safety
louisville/12.summary: Council scheduled a discussion on e-bike/e-moto regulations, with a police presentation on staff's unified response to concerns and future traffic safety strategies. Council also adopted the Model Traffic Code by reference with local amendments, including a change to the speed limit provision.

louisville/13.title: Marshall Fire five-year remembrance
louisville/13.summary: Staff surveyed residents about how to mark the Marshall Fire's five-year anniversary, and results went to Council on Sept 15. Cultural Services set aside remembrance funds and discussed a mural location; the Open Space board considered recommending a small memorial on Davidson Mesa.

louisville/14.title: Utility rates and sewer backup payment policy
louisville/14.summary: Council reviewed the 2027 utility rate setting process and a revised rate presentation, and updated a policy on payments for sewer backup or water meter failure cleanup after a November 2025 backup affected a business. Refuse, recycling and compost collection fees were also raised effective Sept 1.

louisville/15.title: Boards and commissions handbook and possible consolidation
louisville/15.summary: Council discussed a Boards and Commissions Handbook, application processes and appointment terms, with some interest in combining or eliminating boards. Advisory board members discussed the effect on groups such as Parks & Public Landscaping.

lyons/0.title: Planet Bluegrass annexation and zoning at 19617 N St Vrain
lyons/0.summary: Ordinances 1225 and 1226 would annex and zone the Planet Bluegrass property at 19617 N St Vrain as a PUD. The first reading was continued repeatedly, with a request to continue it to 12/7/26. The Utilities & Engineering Board backed an impact statement, and the Economic Vitality Commission discussed parking, traffic and utilities. Town-owned property leases to Planet Bluegrass (Ordinances 1228 and 1229) were also on the Nov. 16 agenda.

lyons/1.title: 2nd and 3rd Avenue stormwater project and bond vote
lyons/1.summary: The $3.8M stormwater and sidewalk project lost a FEMA BRIC grant. A bond election was needed to borrow for it. The Ecology Advisory Board was told the ballot measure failed 3–2 and may return in 2027 as a roughly $4M project with a state loan. The board also chose to go forward with the Safe Routes to School sidewalk grant.

lyons/2.title: 2027 town budget, utility rates and electric increase
lyons/2.summary: The Board of Trustees held budget workshops and a Nov. 16 public hearing to adopt the 2027 budget. The Utilities & Engineering Board recommended rate increases of 6% for stormwater, 2.4% for water/wastewater and 12% for electric. Higher Southwest Power Pool transmission costs drive the electric increase. Time-of-use rates were also discussed.

lyons/3.title: Flock license plate reader cameras
lyons/3.summary: The trustees discussed automated license plate readers and a Flock Safety agreement on Sept. 8, Sept. 21 and Nov. 2. The agenda also included police budgets for 2025 and 2026. The documents give no outcome.

lyons/4.title: Wildfire mitigation ordinance and fire code
lyons/4.summary: The town now operates under the state fire code, so new roofs need fire-resistant materials.
