After a town hall and a survey, the trustees are weighing measures for a draft mandatory wildfire mitigation ordinance. Staff asked whether historic properties should be exempted. The survey showed high awareness of risk but limited support for mandates.

lyons/5.title: Strategic Growth and Water Supply element of the comprehensive plan
lyons/5.summary: Staff drafted a state-required addendum to the comp plan. It notes that regional housing needs recommend about 87 more units, and that the town has enough surplus water supply for that. Several boards gave feedback, including the Historic Preservation Commission on infill in historic areas.

lyons/6.title: Water rights cash-in-lieu and 402 Main Street
lyons/6.summary: Roots to Revival at 402 Main Street asked to use 1.4 Lake McIntosh shares and pay cash in lieu for additional water rights dedication. The shares were valued at about $12K each, or $16.8K total. The trustees took up a resolution to ratify the shares and accept the cash.

lyons/7.title: Sundance Film Festival task force and short-term lodging (SELL)
lyons/7.summary: Ordinance 1222 created a special event lodging license, with applications open since Aug. 1 and $1M liability insurance required. The task force shifted toward private events and curated visitor experiences. It is also considering moving under a local nonprofit, and the town directed staff to find $5,000 for beautification.

lyons/8.title: Flagstone culvert repair and historic review
lyons/8.summary: Staff are planning repairs to the historic sandstone box culvert, supported by an approximately $482,000 DOLA grant. The Historic Preservation Commission is reviewing the project and a comments memo for DOLA and History Colorado. A $154K lowest bid for the streetlight project was also discussed.

lyons/9.title: Wastewater treatment plant upgrade
lyons/9.summary: The trustees received a 60% design update on the wastewater treatment facility. The plant has a separate $5.8M need, with about $2.5M saved and a $1.7M federal grant pending. Proposed changes await state CDPHE approval.

lyons/10.title: Downtown Vacant to Vibrant incentive and Moss Rock hotel
lyons/10.summary: The Economic Vitality Commission is designing a rebate program for businesses filling vacant downtown storefronts, with sliding-scale options such as 75% of up to $5K. Separately, the urban renewal authority is reviewing redevelopment agreements for the Moss Rock hotel at 343-347 Main and Roots to Revival at 402 Main.

lyons/11.title: Housing: Carter Court, Prop 123 and off-street parking
lyons/11.summary: The county housing authority updated the trustees on Carter Court and Seward Street. The trustees took up opting into Prop 123 and a possible code change on off-street parking requirements.

lyons/12.title: Dog waste composting pilot and dark sky efforts in parks
lyons/12.summary: A dog waste composting pilot at the dog park will continue, with $4,850 approved. Dog park improvements of $9,500 were added to the parks budget. The commission is also preparing a Dark Sky application.

manzanola/0.title: 112 S. Canal brownfield cleanup and demolition
manzanola/0.summary: CDPHE awarded a Targeted Brownfields Assessment with a consultant and abatement contractor for 112 S. Canal. The town sought grants, put demolition out for bids, and picked Earth Services & Abatement as contractor; the grant contract was still pending in the fall.

manzanola/1.title: Water plant storage study, Well #2 testing and water loss
manzanola/1.summary: Council has followed a GMS water plant storage study, which moved to a preliminary engineering report with flow and chemical tests on Well #2. Staff reported 84% water loss in April, and drought water restrictions were adopted by Resolution 2026-02.

manzanola/2.title: MMOF CDOT grant of $474,041
manzanola/2.summary: The town received a $474,041 CDOT Multimodal grant, but the contract is budgeted for Colorado's 2029 budget year, later extended to 2031, because state transportation funding is underfunded. CDOT suggested looking at other grants such as Safe Routes to School and TAP.

manzanola/3.title: Southeastern Conduit vault at the water plant
manzanola/3.summary: SECWCD staff discussed placing a Southern Delivery conduit vault at the town water plant. Council also considered asking Congress to support the Conduit.

manzanola/4.title: Second Street repair and chip seal
manzanola/4.summary: Otero County was to repair Second Street at about $1,000, with a chip and seal planned for 2027 at roughly $10,000.

manzanola/5.title: Budget approval and wastewater loan payoff
manzanola/5.summary: Council took up the budget and budget resolutions in December. In November it considered paying off the 2008 wastewater loan and moving the remaining funds to the sewer fund.

manzanola/6.title: Proposition 123 housing needs assessment and senior housing lot
manzanola/6.summary: Council must approve a housing needs assessment for Proposition 123, extended through 2029, and submit it to SECED. The Park Street Senior Housing parking lot was also to be paved.

manzanola/7.title: Federal procurement policies
manzanola/7.summary: Council considered a set of procurement and federal funding compliance policies under 2 CFR 200, covering engineering, construction assurance and property acquisition.

manzanola/8.title: Equipment sales, weed ordinance and park tree work
manzanola/8.summary: The town bought a Kubota in June and considered selling or scrapping a 2012 Dodge police car and jetter truck. It took up Ordinance 2026-05 on weed and tree removal and received a $2,000 SECOG grant to trim a cottonwood in Memorial Park.

mead/0.title: Data center moratorium and Ordinance 1121 reconsideration
mead/0.summary: The Board adopted a twelve-month moratorium on data centers on August 31. Planning staff said the town had received no data center proposals. A special October 29 Board meeting listed options to reconsider Ordinance 1121 (Public Facilities zoning) or take up a conditional use permit application; the documents do not state the outcome.

mead/1.title: New Mead Police Facility, financing and site approval
mead/1.summary: The town broke ground on a new police facility on Chaparral Street in the Liberty Ranch subdivision. The Urban Renewal Authority heard a DOLA grant presentation and Piper Sandler financing options, and approved a cooperation agreement. Trustees took up the police site plan (Ordinance 1118) and a Municipal Facilities Impact Fee Fund budget amendment. A police station recap was set for November 9.

mead/2.title: 2027 budget and mill levies
mead/2.summary: The proposed 2027 budget was presented September 28 and public hearings were set for October 26. These covered the town budget, the Urban Renewal Authority, and the Hwy 66/I-25 and Elevation 25 General Improvement Districts, which also set their mill levies.

mead/3.title: Waterfront Filing No. 2 preliminary plat
mead/3.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on this proposed mixed-use development and recommended conditional approval. Commissioners focused on traffic capacity, road improvements and trail connections. They also called for broader coordination of transportation improvements across nearby developments.

mead/4.title: Annexations and Public Facilities zoning of town-owned land
mead/4.summary: The Planning Commission recommended Public Facilities initial zoning for the town-owned Valdez Annexation and recommended initial zoning for the 1785 Weld County Road 32 annexation. It also recommended Public Facilities zoning for certain town-owned properties, which Trustees took up as Ordinance 1121 on October 26.

mead/5.title: Mead Urban Renewal Authority tax increment incentive policy
mead/5.summary: Counsel proposed a formal policy for evaluating developer requests for tax increment financing reimbursement of public improvements. It sets threshold eligibility, evaluation criteria and a small project track, while leaving the Board discretion. Resolution 03-URA-2026 to approve it was on the October 26 agenda.

mead/6.title: High Plains Boulevard road project
mead/6.summary: Construction of two miles of High Plains Boulevard between WCR 32 and WCR 36 is nearly complete. It includes two travel lanes, bike lanes, roundabouts at CR 32 and CR 34, and a detached sidewalk. A celebration with the coalition and developers was scheduled.
mead/6.where: High Plains Blvd, WCR 32 to WCR 36

mead/7.title: I-25 sewer relocation and wastewater contracts
mead/7.summary: Trustees awarded the I-25 Sewer Relocation construction bid to SMH West LLC and approved a CDOT common use agreement. They also approved contracts for wastewater plant headworks rehabilitation, on-call engineering, and sewer and culvert cleaning.

mead/8.title: United Power electricity franchise agreement
mead/8.summary: The town extended its letter agreement with United Power month-to-month through January 31, 2027. Ordinance 1122, granting a new electric franchise, was on the November 9 agenda.

mead/9.title: Mead Safe Routes to School and new library
mead/9.summary: Trustees awarded the Safe Routes to School construction contract to Colorado Paving Inc. and gave conditional acceptance of the public improvements for the new High Plains Library District Mead Library, with a community opening event scheduled for October 3.

mead/10.title: Ariet's Grove Filing No. 1 preliminary plat
mead/10.summary: The Planning Commission recommended conditional approval and Trustees held a hearing on a resolution conditionally approving the plat on October 26.

meeker/0.title: Zoning variances and conditional use permits in Meeker
meeker/0.summary: Council heard a series of variance and conditional use requests. These include a 0-foot front setback at 325 Curtis Creek Drive, a reduced side setback at 891 3rd Street, a reduced side setback at 390 Market Street, an oversized sign at 43904 Highway 13, and an 8-foot fence at 172 Water. The documents list the requests but not the outcomes.

meeker/1.title: Short-term rental conditional use permit
meeker/1.summary: Council considered a conditional use permit for Chase Rule to operate a short-term rental. The agenda excerpt gives a partial address and no outcome.

meeker/2.title: Fairfield Apartments update
meeker/2.summary: Commissioner Scritchfield was scheduled to give an update on the Fairfield Apartments at the November 3 meeting. The agenda gives no further detail.

meeker/3.title: Mayor appointment process resolution
meeker/3.summary: Council was scheduled to consider a resolution setting the process for appointing a mayor.

meeker/4.title: Encroachment request on town right-of-way in Sanderson Hills
meeker/4.summary: Rebekah and Justin Grant asked to access the Town's right-of-way at Lot 2, Resubdivision of Lots 235 through 259 of the Sanderson Hills Subdivision.

meeker/5.title: Home occupation request at 440 Garfield Street
meeker/5.summary: Tevin Pelloni requested a conditional use permit for a home occupation at 440 Garfield Street.

mesa-county/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center applications
mesa-county/0.summary: On Sept. 29 the commissioners were to consider a temporary moratorium on accepting, processing and approving land use applications for data center facilities in unincorporated Mesa County. It would also suspend negotiation of county inducements for such facilities. The documents do not state the outcome.

mesa-county/1.title: 32 1/2 Road Phase II roadway project
mesa-county/1.summary: The county moved the 32 1/2 Road improvement forward: a land purchase and deed in August, a stormwater detention agreement with Housing Resources of Western Colorado (superseding a 2008 agreement), and a memorandum of understanding with Clifton Water District. A $4,606,193.95 construction contract with Mountain Valley Contracting was on the Sept. 15 agenda.

mesa-county/2.title: Sheriff's Office Flock camera presentation
mesa-county/2.summary: The Sheriff's Office division chief was scheduled to present on Flock cameras at the Aug. 18 hearing. The documents give no detail on the content or any decision.

mesa-county/3.title: Grand Junction Regional Airport FAA grants
mesa-county/3.summary: The county accepted or ratified several FAA Airport Improvement Program grants as co-sponsor with the Airport Authority. They cover terminal improvements and the runway replacement program, including a $13,265,445 grant for runway transition and taxiway conversion.

mesa-county/4.title: Appeal of short-term rental approval on Mesa Vista Road
mesa-county/4.summary: An appeal was scheduled on Sept. 15 against the administrative approval of the Beatrice Estate planning clearance, which would allow a short-term rental at 123 Mesa Vista Road. The property owner is Passion Project, LLC.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing

mesa-county/5.title: 2027 county and special district budgets
mesa-county/5.summary: Commissioners received a briefing on the proposed 2027 county budget on Oct. 6, along with briefings on several improvement districts and the pest district. A supplemental 2026 budget resolution also came up in September and November.

mesa-county/6.title: Public Health Board budget, legal counsel and evaluation
mesa-county/6.summary: The Board of Public Health held work sessions and meetings on its 2027 budget, adopting it on the Nov. 10 agenda. It also held special meetings and a closed session on hiring legal counsel and considered engaging counsel.

sources.body: Board of Public Health Special Meeting
Board of Public Health Special Meeting
Board of Public Health Work Session
Board of Public Health Special Meeting

mesa-county/7.title: North Avenue transit corridor funding
mesa-county/7.summary: The county considered an agreement of up to $1.25 million with the City of Grand Junction for improvements under the North Avenue Enhanced Transit Corridor plan.

mesa-county/8.title: Rezones and land use hearings
mesa-county/8.summary: The commissioners heard rezone and land use items including the Serrano Estates rezone at 825 26 Road, the Bailey rezone at 1083 20 Road, the Experius PUD amendment extending its lapse date to 2031, and the Smith right-of-way vacation in Loma.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing
Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing
Board of Commissioners Land Use Hearing

mesa-county/9.title: Wildfire mitigation and forest health grants
mesa-county/9.summary: The county considered an $840,000 grant application for the Mesa Creek Cross-Boundary Wildfire Mitigation Project and a letter supporting a federal forest health and wildfire risk bill.

mesa-county/10.title: Longs Park lease with School District 51
mesa-county/10.summary: The commissioners considered a lease and operating agreement with Mesa County Valley School District 51 for Longs Park.

milliken/0.title: Water bills, tiered rates and new smart meters
milliken/0.summary: Residents told the Board that water bills jumped after the Metron smart meter rollout and tiered rates; staff said rates rose about 35% on average with the base rate up about 14%. The roughly $1.25 million meter replacement project is near completion, and residents also raised records requests about the meter bid. A town-wide rate and fee study with Willdan Financial was on the Nov. 9 agenda, and 2027 rates are generally adopted in December.

milliken/1.title: Proposed paving of County Road 44 in the 2027 budget
milliken/1.summary: Residents on Weld County Road 44 spoke both for and against paving the road, citing dust, ruts and safety versus cost, traffic and rural character. Some asked that paving be removed from the 2027 budget; others pointed to an earlier IGA and service plan for Meadow Farms Filing 1 about paving responsibility.
milliken/1.where: Weld County Road 44 east of WCR 19, near Meadow Farms

milliken/2.title: 2027 town budget
milliken/2.summary: The Board of Trustees held a budget retreat and a series of work sessions on the 2027 budget starting in August. The first public budget hearing was set for Oct. 14, with final adoption at the November public hearing.

milliken/3.title: Milliken Sidewalk and ADA Project contract
milliken/3.summary: The Board considered a construction agreement with Gold Star Concrete for $1,018,200.30, with total project cost not to exceed $1,170,930.30. Grant funding falls short, so the Board discussed scope cuts, delays and cost sharing with the School District; staff recommended awarding to the lowest responsive bidder.

milliken/4.title: Strategic Growth Element of the comprehensive plan
milliken/4.summary: The Board reviewed a draft Strategic Growth Element, a required plan covering growth policies, infill and redevelopment, and greenfield development. The draft says it does not set development rights or annexation priorities. Staff also began a Water Supply Element update to the Comprehensive Plan.

milliken/5.title: Sunfield Filing 3 preliminary plat
milliken/5.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on the Sunfield Filing 3 preliminary plat, and the Board of Trustees scheduled its own hearing for Nov. 9.

milliken/6.title: Milliken Store-N-Go self-storage conditional use permit
milliken/6.summary: The Planning Commission recommended approval of a conditional use permit for a fully enclosed self-storage facility of seven buildings (over 52,000 sq ft) in the C-4 Service Business district. Staff recommended no extra conditions; CDOT approval would be needed for some improvements.

milliken/7.title: Town Hall rental program fees
milliken/7.summary: Staff proposed a hybrid rental model with higher hourly rates, a tiered fee structure with reduced rates for residents and nonprofits, higher non-resident rates, and a funeral/memorial category. The goal is to recover costs so taxpayers do not subsidize private use.

milliken/8.title: New Town Administrator hired
milliken/8.summary: The Board approved an employment agreement offering the Town Administrator job to Greg Brinck, and a resolution appointing him was set for Sept. 9. He was giving updates to the Board by October.

milliken/9.title: Milliken Housing Authority budget, Dove Valley and Prop 123
milliken/9.summary: The Housing Authority drafted and approved its 2027 budget, questioned Dove Valley operating costs and fees, discussed a Dove Valley water bill, and worked on its strategic plan, including Prop 123 meetings. It planned a presentation to the Town Board in November.

milliken/10.title: Social media and communications policy
milliken/10.summary: The Board repeatedly discussed an update to the Town's social media and communications policy after a trustee asked to add it to the agenda.

milliken/11.title: Food truck park and 1398 Irene student home partnership
milliken/11.summary: The Board took up discussions on a possible food truck park and on a student home construction partnership at 1398 Irene, and considered a Meadow Farms HOA encroachment agreement.

minturn/0.title: Police services contract with Eagle County Sheriff's Office
minturn/0.summary: Council appointed an ad-hoc committee to negotiate a Sheriff's Office police services contract starting in 2027, covering service levels, costs, terms and community concerns about automated license plate readers. The proposed terms will return to the full Council; the contract was on the Oct. 21 and Nov. 4 agendas.

minturn/1.title: Minturn shooting range grant and Forest Service permit
minturn/1.summary: Minturn won a $225,000 Colorado Parks and Wildlife grant to improve the town shooting range and address long-standing issues. The town is seeking in-kind help from Eagle County, such as road grading, and aims to have a USFS special use permit by spring 2027. A status update was on the Oct. 21 agenda, and a councilmember asked to continue the related item on Oct. 7.

minturn/2.title: Speed bumps and traffic calming, Main Street speed camera study
minturn/2.summary: Residents in the Boulder and Pine Street area asked for more speed bumps and tables, and at the Oct. 7 meeting a resident raised a 2023 petition and speed concerns. Staff is studying a Main Street speed camera and evaluating FY 2027 funding for speed bumps and radar feedback signs.
minturn/2.where: Main Street; Boulder and Pine Street area

minturn/3.title: FY 2027 town budget
minturn/3.summary: The FY 2027 budget was the subject of a public hearing on Nov. 4. Items in line for consideration include traffic calming, Beach Park retaining wall work and other capital projects.

minturn/4.title: Water moratorium ordinance, water tank design and downtown water funds
minturn/4.summary: Council considered on second reading Ordinance No. 11 amending the water moratorium, and Resolution No. 50 to repurpose CDS funds for downtown water improvements. An update from S.E.H. on water tank evaluations and design progress on Bellm Bridge was scheduled for Nov. 4.

minturn/5.title: Electric outages and Xcel Energy reliability
minturn/5.summary: Town staff met with the Colorado Energy Office and Xcel Energy about outages and reliability. At Xcel's recommendation the town sent formal correspondence requesting improvements and is monitoring Xcel's response and timelines.

minturn/6.title: ERWSD Main Street siphon rehabilitation
minturn/6.summary: Eagle River Water & Sanitation District's siphon rehabilitation is underway, with sewer bypass pumping expected to begin by Aug. 14. Traffic control remains in place on US 24/Main Street during construction.

minturn/7.title: Historic Preservation Plan update
minturn/7.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission worked on the final 2026 Historic Preservation Plan, with amendments to goals on objects and cultural resources. Members discussed asking Council about a historic district and a budget line item, and elected Ken Halliday chair and Dan Brown vice chair. The Meyer's Barn project was also updated.

minturn/8.title: Joint meeting with Eagle County on housing and e-bikes
minturn/8.summary: At a joint meeting, Minturn and the County discussed a Regional Housing Authority, with concerns about unoccupied homes, business costs and employee housing, and the need for a clear plan after past ballot measures. They also discussed e-bike rules, confusion over e-bike classes and youth riders.

minturn/9.title: Land development code definitions and Bolts Lake zoning
minturn/9.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed new definitions for the land use code, including pervious surfaces, bulk plane and affordable housing terms. Staff explained the settlement agreement and the use table for the Bolts Lake zone districts.

minturn/10.title: Silver Star Trail changes to approved plans
minturn/10.summary: Requests to change approved plans at 0024 and 0018 Silver Star Trail went to the Planning Commission on Oct. 14 and Council on Oct. 21. The 0018 item was continued to Nov. 4.

minturn/11.title: DDA investment and incentive policy
minturn/11.summary: The Downtown Development Authority board considered Resolution No. 02 adopting an Investment and Incentive Policy. It covers a small project matching grant program, large redevelopment projects and strategic property acquisition.

minturn/12.title: Highlands parcels listing strategy and conservation options
minturn/12.summary: Council planned a discussion on a strategy for listing the Highlands parcels and conservation options, with negotiations possibly handled privately.

moffat-county/0.title: Data center regulations and failed moratorium
moffat-county/0.summary: The Planning & Zoning Commission is writing data center rules for Moffat County. Residents, Yampa Valley Electric and Pure-Green Colorado spoke on a possible moratorium, and a panel discussion was held Oct. 6. On Oct. 13 Commissioner Bohrer called for a motion to adopt the Planning & Zoning Commission's recommended moratorium (Resolution 2026-103), no one responded, and the motion died.

moffat-county/1.title: Trapper Reborn project
moffat-county/1.summary: Pure-Green Colorado's CEO described the Trapper Reborn project and asked the commissioners not to pass a moratorium that could affect it. Other speakers backed the project's economic development potential.

moffat-county/2.title: Term limits referendum for November ballot
moffat-county/2.summary: The commissioners approved Resolution 2026-100, a referendum on term limits, along with an intergovernmental agreement with the Clerk's Office to put it on the November ballot.

moffat-county/3.title: 2027 county budget and related budgets
moffat-county/3.summary: A public hearing was held Oct. 13 on the proposed 2027 county budget. The Moffat Economic Development Authority's 2027 budget (Resolution 2026-129) was scheduled for adoption Nov. 10.

moffat-county/4.title: Loudy-Simpson Park master plan and shop
moffat-county/4.summary: Staff presented a Logan Simpson proposal for a Loudy-Simpson Park master plan, and a contract for the plan was on the Sept. 22 consent agenda. A contract with Masterworks Mechanical for the park shop followed in November.

moffat-county/5.title: Craig skatepark funding
moffat-county/5.summary: The Craig Skatepark Alliance and county staff won approval to apply for $25,000 grants each from the Laura Jane Musser Fund and the El Pomar Foundation. A GOCO grant application is planned for January. A services agreement with Grindline Skateparks was on the Oct. 13 consent agenda.

moffat-county/6.title: Echo Park Road closure
moffat-county/6.summary: The commissioners approved Resolution 2026-120 temporarily closing County Road 156 (Echo Park Road) in Dinosaur National Monument. Flash flood erosion left it unsafe, and the Park Service wants archaeological concerns investigated before repairs.
moffat-county/6.where: County Road 156, Echo Park Road, Dinosaur National Monument

moffat-county/7.title: Road and Bridge snow bank payment policy
moffat-county/7.summary: A Road & Bridge employee asked the commissioners twice to look into inconsistencies in the county's snow bank payment policy and asked for follow-up on his earlier request.

moffat-county/8.title: Employee health insurance board and insurance agent
moffat-county/8.summary: The commissioners reinstated the Employee Health Insurance Advisory Board and appointed five employee-elected members. They also designated local firm Mountain West Insurance as agent of record (Resolution 2026-118).

moffat-county/9.title: Vermillion/Great Divide shop project
moffat-county/9.summary: The Vermillion shop project had a contract amendment with Charchalis Construction and fuel tank removal testing and consultation approved on consent agendas.

moffat-county/10.title: Contract monitoring policy
moffat-county/10.summary: The commissioners adopted Resolution 2026-111, a contract monitoring policy setting a standard for overseeing contracts, grants, subawards and intergovernmental agreements to meet federal and state requirements.

montrose-county/0.title: Non-native wildlife ordinance 2026-01
montrose-county/0.summary: The commissioners are weighing Ordinance 2026-01, which would prohibit intentionally introducing, releasing, moving or establishing habitat for non-native wildlife species in unincorporated Montrose County. A public hearing on approval or continuance was set for Oct. 28 and came up again Nov. 5. The documents do not state the outcome.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO STREAMING AVAILABLE
Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/1.title: County resolutions on Colorado Parks and Wildlife lead ammunition and prairie dog proposals
montrose-county/1.summary: A hearing was set for Oct. 28 on a resolution opposing a citizen petition to prohibit lead ammunition for hunting. A second resolution opposes proposed CPW prairie dog regulation changes. Both would be sent to CPW as the county's public comment. A work session also listed proposed CPW changes.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/2.title: 2027 proposed county budget
montrose-county/2.summary: A public hearing on Oct. 14 presented the 2027 proposed budget to the commissioners for consideration. The documents do not give the final figures or the outcome.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/3.title: Emergency funding for West End Family Link
montrose-county/3.summary: At a special meeting in Nucla on Sept. 17, the commissioners heard a presentation and public comment on an emergency funding request from West End Family Link. Commissioner Pond moved to fund it at $75,000.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/4.title: Gold Mountain Fire FEMA support and wildfire code agreement
montrose-county/4.summary: The chair signed a letter asking for FEMA support after the 2026 Gold Mountain Fire, and the board ratified it on Sept. 2. The board also approved an agreement with Norwood Fire Protection District to share administration and enforcement of the county's Wildfire Resiliency Code. The consent agenda passed 2-1.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/5.title: Iron Will Dog Lodge special use permit
montrose-county/5.summary: The commissioners were set to consider a resolution on the Iron Will Dog Lodge special use permit (SU26-002), along with a related Strole waiver request, on Nov. 4.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/6.title: Coal Creek Estates III plat and Sunshine Road minor subdivision
montrose-county/6.summary: On Sept. 16 the county manager moved the Coal Creek Estates III Preliminary Plat (MA25-016) to follow the Sunshine Road minor subdivision item on the agenda. The documents do not give outcomes.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/7.title: County acceptance of road maintenance and road projects
montrose-county/7.summary: The board was set to accept county maintenance of 0.03 miles of 5465 Court off Banner Road and 0.22 miles of 6785 Lane and Uriah Court in Thornburgh Estates. It also approved a $487,333 B-24 bridge rail replacement contract and agreed to asphalt overlay work with the Town of Olathe. A $142,313 Public Works lot paving contract was on the Oct. 21 agenda, and a County Road Education session was scheduled.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/8.title: Montrose Regional Airport contracts and apron reconstruction
montrose-county/8.summary: The board approved an engineering amendment with Yeh and Associates for apron and taxilane reconstruction design. It also handled baggage delivery permits, a law enforcement reimbursement agreement and off-airport ground transportation agreements.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/9.title: Safe sleep program and housing-related items
montrose-county/9.summary: A work session on Oct. 5 covered a Rocky Mountain Health Plans Safe Sleep Incentive Program services agreement and Headwaters to Home. The board also assigned $1,573,936 of the county's 2026 private activity bond allocation to the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/10.title: Montrose and Ouray county line discussion
montrose-county/10.summary: The Oct. 26 work session included a discussion of the Montrose/Ouray County line. The documents give no details.

montrose/0.title: City Charter amendments on elections, term limits and appointments
montrose/0.summary: Council took up ballot language for Charter amendments: Ordinance 2727 would move municipal elections to November, 2728 sets an 8-year lifetime term limit for the at-large seat, and 2729 and 2730 give Council approval over hiring and firing the police chief and city clerk. Residents spoke both for and against at the August and September meetings.

montrose/1.title: City manager separation, interim manager and council vacancies
montrose/1.summary: After an August executive session on a confidential memo and possible independent counsel, Council approved a separation agreement with City Manager Bill Bell, ratified September 15. Ann Morgenthaler was appointed interim city manager and MURA executive director. Council also worked through the District IV and At-Large vacancies, appointing Adam Woodden to District IV and taking applications from John Brown, Danielle Godt and Cindee Williams for the At-Large seat.

montrose/2.title: Calls for a moratorium on new data centers
montrose/2.summary: At the August 18 meeting a resident asked Council to enact a moratorium on new data centers until regulations are in place. The documents show no Council action.

montrose/3.title: Rotary Park pump house replacement
montrose/3.summary: Council considered a $514,011 contract with FCI Constructors of Grand Junction to replace the park's irrigation pump house, built in the 1980s. The amount is $14,011 over the $500,000 budget, to be covered by savings from other 2026 Public Works capital projects.

montrose/4.title: Annexations and new subdivisions (Locust Road, Chipeta Lake 2, Spruce Point, El Chapin)
montrose/4.summary: Council took up the 4.2-acre Locust Road Addition annexation on second reading (Ordinance 2731). The Planning Commission heard initial zoning for the 1.14-acre Chipeta Lake 2 Addition and the Spruce Point amended preliminary plat, and reviewed a sketch plan for a 45-lot El Chapin subdivision on 6600 Road. One resident asked that Spruce Point respect established boundaries.
montrose/4.where: Locust Road; Chipeta Road; Spruce Point (6400 Road); El Chapin (6600 Road)

montrose/5.title: Comprehensive plan update and growth policies
montrose/5.summary: Staff is preparing a five-year update to the Envision 2040 comprehensive plan, including state-required housing needs assessment, housing action plan, water supply and strategic growth elements, with approval targeted by year's end. Residents urged that growth pay its own way and that the plan's standards be upheld.

montrose/6.title: Affordable housing commitment and seasonal homeless shelter funding
montrose/6.summary: Council considered a Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment. The city approved 221 units in the current cycle against a requirement of 162. Council also considered $28,597 in lodging tax funds for start-up costs for The Shepherd's Hand seasonal homeless shelter.

montrose/7.title: Student parking on residential streets near the high school
montrose/7.summary: Residents asked Council to reinstate permit-only parking on neighborhood streets near the high school and to increase police presence.

montrose/8.title: Electronic speed sign on Miami Road
montrose/8.summary: Residents asked Council to install an electronic speed indicator sign on Miami Road near Cedar Creek.

montrose/9.title: Solid waste rules, 2027 fees and landfill extension
montrose/9.summary: Council was asked to rewrite Chapter 3-1 as Solid Waste Collection Services, with separate residential and non-residential rules, scheduled paid bulk pickup and optional programs for tires, electronics and compost. It also considered Resolution 2026-18 adopting the 2027 fee schedule and a one-year extension of the landfill agreement with Bruin Waste Management.

montrose/10.title: Rio Grande and East Oak Grove roundabout art
montrose/10.summary: Council was scheduled to discuss the landscape plan and artwork for the roundabout at Rio Grande and East Oak Grove Road.
montrose/10.where: Rio Grande and East Oak Grove Road

montrose/11.title: IT, software and fire suppression purchases
montrose/11.summary: Council considered $75,000 for a gas fire suppression system in the Network Operation Center with Pye Barker, a three-year Optive firewall subscription of about $80,768, and NEOGOV HR software renewal. It also considered a Motorola Flex maintenance renewal for dispatch.

monument/0.title: Monument 2040 Comprehensive Plan and Downtown Master Plan
monument/0.summary: The Planning Commission heard the draft 2040 Comprehensive Plan and Downtown Master Plan, built on nearly two years of outreach. Residents worried that conceptual downtown redevelopment renderings clash with Monument's historic small-town character and asked for stronger architectural guidance. Town Council then held a public hearing on Resolution 78-2026 to adopt the plan, with the consultant (The Lakota Group) presenting.

monument/1.title: 2027 draft budget and use tax ballot initiative
monument/1.summary: The Citizens Service Levels Advisory Committee reviewed the preliminary 2027 budget, including stormwater impact fee needs, park security and a Monument Lake pavilion. Staff discussed use tax ballot options, including a possible $2.2M in construction use tax and about $500K more if the motor vehicle use tax rises to 3.5. Council directed staff to move ahead with the 2027 draft budget as presented.

monument/2.title: Native Sun Construction PUD amendment at 15010 Woodcarver Road
monument/2.summary: Planning Commission recommended approval of a major amendment to relocate the shop building, add a deceleration lane on Wood Carver Road, and add parking and landscaping (21 trees preserved, 66 planted). Council took up Ordinance 24-2026 on Sept 8. Commissioners asked about equipment heights, outdoor storage screening, water capacity, and stormwater from the wash bay.

monument/3.title: Falcon Commerce Center Phase 2 preliminary PUD amendment
monument/3.summary: Council re-introduced Ordinance 15-2026, continued from Aug. 3, to approve a major amendment to the preliminary PUD for the south 43 acres of Falcon Commerce Center. Staff gave a timeline of events.

monument/4.title: 7 Brew Drive Thru Coffee final PUD plan
monument/4.summary: Planning Commission reviewed the final PUD plan for a 7 Brew drive-thru coffee shop, and Council considered Ordinance 23-2026 approving it.

monument/5.title: Jackson Creek Parkway improvements and Old Denver Road traffic
monument/5.summary: Staff gave Council an update on Jackson Creek Parkway improvements. A resident raised traffic concerns on Old Denver Road during public comment, and Council considered a snowplow IGA with El Paso County that covers the new section of Beacon Lite Road. A Transportation Master Plan open house was also noticed.
monument/5.where: Jackson Creek Parkway, Old Denver Road, Beacon Lite Road

monument/6.title: Police department handgun purchase and fee schedule
monument/6.summary: Council's consent agenda included Resolution 63-2026 to buy Shadow Systems handguns and accessories for officers' on-duty use. Resolution 72-2026 revised police service fees effective Oct. 1.

monument/7.title: Town facility contracts and OpenGov software purchase
monument/7.summary: Council considered a series of contracts (Palomar, Mountain View Electric, Green Electric, Flintco) for a facility installation, plus Resolution 84-2026 to buy the OpenGov platform as a town-wide software system and Resolution 85-2026 to revise the fee schedule.

monument/8.title: Water attorney appointment and water concerns
monument/8.summary: Council approved Resolution 71-2026 appointing Nazarenus Stack & Wombacher LLC as water attorney. A councilmember also wanted a water workshop, and a new tap for two properties came up as Resolution 68-2026.

monument/9.title: Silver Key funding request and prohibited-conduct ordinance
monument/9.summary: Silver Key's CEO asked Council to consider a $25,000 contribution for services to Monument residents. Council also took up Ordinance 25-2026 regulating certain prohibited conduct, presented by police, which Council members supported for its educational components.

monument/10.title: Repeal of parking permit waiver and Heart of Monument parking lot
monument/10.summary: Council considered Ordinance 20-2026 repealing a municipal code subsection waiving parking permit requirements, and approved a change order for the Heart of Monument parking lot.

morgan-county/0.title: Data center zoning regulations
morgan-county/0.summary: The county commissioners have been working on new data center rules for the Zoning Regulations, with a Planning Commission hearing on April 21, 2026 and a commissioner hearing opened May 5 and continued repeatedly through August 4. Drafts define edge, large and accessory data centers, allow only closed-loop cooling, and are still debating setbacks and decommissioning requirements. Zoning amendments were again on the September 15 agenda.

morgan-county/1.title: Fortress solar and battery project road work enforcement
morgan-county/1.summary: The county issued a Notice of Intent to Take Enforcement Action and Order to Show Cause against Fortress over road improvements on County Roads Q and R tied to its 2024 solar and battery special use permits. Fortress says paving began without county observation of proof rolling and has chosen to crush and rebuild the road. A hearing was set for October 23, 2026.

morgan-county/2.title: County jail expansion and capital planning
morgan-county/2.summary: The 2025 annual financial report notes commissioners are reviewing the capital improvement plan and targeting a County Jail expansion. An Energy Impact Assistance Fund grant helps, and the county may ask other municipalities to help fund it. A security fence project for the Justice Center and East Point Building was also up for bid award on October 20.
morgan-county/2.where: Morgan County Jail and Justice Center, Fort Morgan

morgan-county/3.title: 2027 preliminary budget and county finances
morgan-county/3.summary: The Finance Director presented the proposed preliminary 2027 budget on November 5. The treasurer's report showed tax collections of about $64.97 million, 98.66% of taxes levied. The 2025 annual comprehensive financial report was presented in August.

morgan-county/4.title: Home Rule Charter and special election
morgan-county/4.summary: A charter commissioner presented on a Home Rule Charter for Morgan County on September 1, alongside a resolution (2026 BCC 38) calling a special election.

morgan-county/5.title: Zoning code changes and planning fee increases
morgan-county/5.summary: Commissioners considered new planning and building inspection fees, a revised 2026 fee schedule, and zoning amendments on enforcement processes. A November 5 hearing covers variances, storage units, campgrounds and RV parks, school dedications, wells and replats.

morgan-county/6.title: Junk and rubbish ordinance
morgan-county/6.summary: Ordinance No. 2, Series 2026, restricts accumulation of junk and refuse in unincorporated areas, citing rodents, fire hazards and pollution. Existing operating junk yards are exempt. It had first reading on September 15 and second reading on November 5.

morgan-county/7.title: Fort Morgan wastewater plant road use and solar lease
morgan-county/7.summary: Commissioners considered a road use agreement with Glacier Construction for the City of Fort Morgan's wastewater treatment plant expansion, plus a second amendment to a solar energy system lease and easement on about 17 acres and a related release and waiver.

morgan-county/8.title: Mission Goldwing Solar Project comments
morgan-county/8.summary: The county was asked to comment on the Mission Goldwing Solar Project in Adams County near the Morgan County line.

morgan-county/9.title: Prairie dogs on state-owned land
morgan-county/9.summary: The commissioners planned to submit comments to Colorado Parks and Wildlife about prairie dogs on state-owned land.

morrison/0.title: Farm at the Fort annexation and initial zoning
morrison/0.summary: The Town set an August 18, 2026 public hearing on annexing about 59.36 acres in unincorporated Jefferson County known as the Farm at the Fort. A separate hearing covered initial zoning to Residential Estate (RE) and Mixed-Use Neighborhood (MX-N), on applications by Morrison Redevelopment, LP and Revesco Properties. Residents were invited to speak at both hearings.
morrison/0.where: Farm at the Fort, unincorporated Jefferson County

morrison/1.title: Lodging tax changes and November ballot questions
morrison/1.summary: Ordinance 562 aligned the lodging tax exemption with the 2012 voter-approved ballot language, and the Board set its effective date to October 1, 2026. Voters will also see two ballot questions: removing the exemption for small lodging facilities (about $125,000 a year) and raising the lodging tax rate from 6% to 8% (about $500,000 a year).

morrison/2.title: 2027 town budget and Capital Improvement Plan
morrison/2.summary: The draft 2027 budget includes a 15.85% health insurance renewal increase, a proposed 3.6% cost-of-living raise, and lodging tax revenue expected to pass property tax. Hearings on the budget and the 2027 Capital Improvement Plan are set for November 4 and November 17, 2026, when adoption is expected. A hotel sales-tax incentive (ESTIP) and a change to who pays online bill-pay fees are also in the draft.

morrison/3.title: Mandatory drought watering restrictions
morrison/3.summary: Because of drought, all Morrison water customers have been under mandatory outdoor watering limits since April 2, 2026. Watering is allowed no more than two days a week and not between 10 AM and 6 PM, and wasting water is prohibited.

morrison/4.title: Raw water diversion and utility agreements
morrison/4.summary: The Board went into executive session on raw water diversion negotiations with its water engineer. The 2027 budget includes about $296,213 for the overall raw water project in the Utility Fund. The Board also had a Green Tree Metro District sewer service agreement on its October 20 agenda. A resident thanked the Utility Director for his response to water concerns.

morrison/5.title: East Planning Area pre-development agreement
morrison/5.summary: On October 6 the Board considered agreements related to the East Planning Area and moved to approve a pre-development agreement. The documents give no further details.

morrison/6.title: Parking: overnight parking and Interstate parking
morrison/6.summary: The Board held a discussion-only item on overnight parking on September 15 after a resident from Bear Creek Ave. asked for clarification. Interstate parking came up again on October 6.

morrison/7.title: Municipal code updates: garden sheds, motels, floodplain and nuisance abatement
morrison/7.summary: Ordinance 566 allows garden sheds up to 120 sq ft as an accessory use in residential zones, permits motels in the HD district, and changes floodplain elevation rules and the definition of substantial improvement. Ordinance 567, adopted October 6, speeds up abatement of nuisances on public property.

morrison/8.title: Town Manager employment, new staff position and personnel rules
morrison/8.summary: The Board held executive sessions on the Town Manager employment agreement and a special meeting requested by the Town Manager was noticed for October 7. Agenda items on October 20 included the agreement, a new full-time position, amended Board rules of procedure, and Ordinance 568 repealing the code chapter on town employee plans.

mountain-view/0.title: R3 Zoning District Update (R3/R4 rezoning and General Plan amendments)
mountain-view/0.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission was set to consider on Oct 7 recommending adoption of the R3 Zoning District Update. It would certify an environmental review, amend the General Plan map, and rezone areas to R4 in 14 change areas and to new R3-A, R3-B and R3-C districts, implementing state housing laws.

mountain-view/1.title: Rowhouse project at 924-940 San Rafael Avenue
mountain-view/1.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission is to hear a gatekeeper project replacing two industrial buildings with a 36-unit rowhouse development using State Density Bonus Law. It needs a rezoning from MM (General Industrial) to R3-2, a General Plan amendment, a PUD permit, removal of two Heritage trees and a tentative map.

mountain-view/2.title: Historic Preservation Ordinance and Historic Register update
mountain-view/2.summary: A public hearing at the Environmental Planning Commission on Aug 19 covered amendments to the zoning code on historic resources and a zoning map change updating the historic register. Council had the second reading to adopt both ordinances on Oct 13. Public comments were attached to the staff report.

mountain-view/3.title: LinkedIn development agreement amendment
mountain-view/3.summary: Council held a public hearing on Oct 13 on a first amendment to the development agreement for LinkedIn's sites. On Oct 27 it was set to adopt the ordinance and appropriate a $1.6 million public benefit fee to the Affordable Housing Fund.
mountain-view/3.where: 700-810 East Middlefield Road and 1100-1200 Maude Avenue

mountain-view/4.title: Rengstorff Complete Streets Study and Active Transportation Plan
mountain-view/4.summary: Staff presented the Rengstorff Complete Streets Study (bike lane gaps, road diets, sidewalk access) and the final Active Transportation Plan. The bike/ped committee recommended the plan 5-0 with added language on smaller-scale projects. It then went to the Council Transportation Committee for a recommendation on adoption.

mountain-view/5.title: Castro Street pedestrian mall interim improvements
mountain-view/5.summary: Staff presented a concept layout for Interim Pedestrian Mall Improvements at the Castro/California intersection (Project 23-49). It was reviewed by the Bicycle/Pedestrian Advisory Committee and the Council Transportation Committee, which was to recommend a design concept to Council. The Downtown Committee also got Castro Street updates.

mountain-view/6.title: Heritage tree removal appeals and ordinance update
mountain-view/6.summary: The Urban Forestry Board denied an appeal at 961 Eichler Drive, overturned staff to allow removal of one tree at 777 San Carrizo Way, and denied an appeal at 1473 Tyler Park Way. Commissioners also began input on updating the Heritage Tree Ordinance, citing permitting conflicts between departments and alignment with the Biodiversity and Urban Forest Plan.
mountain-view/6.where: 961 Eichler Dr, 777 San Carrizo Way, 1473 Tyler Park Way

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Commission and Urban Forestry Board
Parks and Recreation Commission and Urban Forestry Board

mountain-view/7.title: Rent stabilization appeals
mountain-view/7.summary: The Rental Housing Committee heard a landlord appeal (Solis) against tenant Jean Bell and approved the tentative appeal decision in full on Aug 27. Another hearing officer decision, Petition C25260032, was set for appeal on Oct 22, and staff sought feedback on the one-time utility adjustment petition process.

mountain-view/8.title: Shoreline athletic field renovation and Google environmental reimbursement
mountain-view/8.summary: Council, acting as the Shoreline Regional Park Community board, was to approve an $880,000 contract with Tetra Tech for athletic field renovations. It was also to approve agreements with Google for reimbursement of past environmental work and ongoing monitoring, appropriating about $4.97 million.

mountain-view/9.title: Affordable housing funding and bonds (96 West El Camino Real, 334 San Antonio Road)
mountain-view/9.summary: Council took up $388,515 in state PLHA funds for 96 West El Camino Real and a homeownership pilot, plus tax-exempt bond financing for that project. On Oct 27 it considered similar bond financing for 334 San Antonio Road.
mountain-view/9.where: 96 West El Camino Real; 334 San Antonio Road

mountain-view/10.title: SR 237/Middlefield interchange and Public Safety Building
mountain-view/10.summary: Council was to approve the design concept for the State Route 237 and Middlefield Road interchange improvements (Project 19-65). It was also to authorize pre-qualification of bidders for Package 2 of the Public Safety Building (Project 20-49).
mountain-view/10.where: SR 237 and Middlefield Road; Public Safety Building

mountain-view/11.title: Ambulance billing fees and Pathways to Housing progress report
mountain-view/11.summary: On Oct 13 Council was to adopt revised ambulance billing and user fees for the Fire Department. It also was to accept the first annual progress report on the Pathways to Housing homeless response strategy.

mountain-view/12.title: Thompson Mini Park grant application
mountain-view/12.summary: Council was asked to authorize an application for up to $2.3 million from the Statewide Park Development and Community Revitalization Program for Thompson Mini Park (Project 26-35). A second community meeting on the park was upcoming.

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Commission and Urban Forestry Board

nederland/0.title: Rezoning 242 & 252 E 5th St from General Commercial to Medium Density Residential
nederland/0.summary: LandShark Investments LLC wants to rezone two sloped lots from General Commercial to Medium Density Residential to build two roughly 2,100 sq ft A-frame homes. At its Oct. 21 hearing the Planning Commission found the application met code criteria and recommended approval of Ordinance 895. Neighbors raised concerns about losing commercial flexibility and spot zoning, while another resident supported it.

nederland/1.title: Temporary use permit rules (Ordinance 893)
nederland/1.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a draft ordinance creating staff-reviewed temporary use permits, generally limited to 90 days, revocable for health or safety problems, with a processing fee to be set by resolution. Neighbor notification would not be automatic but staff could require it. A resident submitted public comment.

nederland/2.title: Outdoor sales, eating and drinking use table amendment (Ordinance 894)
nederland/2.summary: The Planning Commission considered changes to the use group table to allow outdoor sales, eating and drinking, including safety standards for outdoor commercial activities near roadways. A commissioner moved to recommend approval of Ordinance 894 after a resident spoke in support.

nederland/3.title: Moving Board of Zoning Adjustment duties to Planning Commission (Ordinance 896)
nederland/3.summary: Ordinance 896 would dissolve the Board of Zoning Adjustment and shift its functions to the Planning Commission. The commission discussed the low number of variance applications and difficulty maintaining a separate volunteer board.

nederland/4.title: Flex zoning for housing and redevelopment
nederland/4.summary: The Planning Commission began discussing flex zoning, a concept named in the Comprehensive Plan and Downtown Subarea Plan. Options include more housing types, mixed uses, affordable housing incentives, and an overlay. The Wolf Tongue industrial area and General Commercial properties near East Street Garage and Mountain Auto were identified as candidates.
nederland/4.where: Wolf Tongue industrial area and East Street Garage area

nederland/5.title: Eldora spending resolution (Resolution 2026-31)
nederland/5.summary: The Board of Trustees took up Resolution 2026-31 on Eldora spending at its Nov. 9 meeting. Several residents submitted public comment on it, including Dallas Masters and Karen Blakemore.

nederland/6.title: Fiscal Year 2027 budget
nederland/6.summary: The Board of Trustees held a budget discussion for FY27 on Nov. 9. Residents including Dallas Masters and Kathleen Chippi commented.

nederland/7.title: Interim Town Manager agreement amendment
nederland/7.summary: The Board of Trustees considered Resolution 2026-30, a first amendment to the Interim Town Manager employment agreement with Gordon.

nederland/8.title: Chipeta Park playground replacement and PROST update
nederland/8.summary: The parks advisory board continued discussing a vision, grant opportunities and priorities for replacing the Chipeta Park playground. It also worked on final revisions to the PROST plan update and a timeline for returning it to the Board.

sources.body: PROSAB - Nederland Parks, Recreation, and Open Space Advisory Board

nederland/9.title: Amendments to ADU code (Ordinance 892)
nederland/9.summary: The Planning Commission recommended approval of draft Ordinance 892, amending section 16-33 of the municipal code on accessory dwelling units.

new-castle/0.title: Community Market plastic reduction and bag fee fund
new-castle/0.summary: The Climate and Environment Commission is planning compostable cups and recycling at the Community Market and a plastic pledge for the community. About $12,000 remains in the plastic bag fee fund, which the town can use for recycling and cleanup costs.

new-castle/1.title: Data center information discussion
new-castle/1.summary: Town Council scheduled a discussion of general data center information at its November 3, 2026 meeting. The documents give no further detail on any proposal.

new-castle/2.title: 2026 budget, 2027 budget and trash fees
new-castle/2.summary: Council held workshops on the 2026 budget on Oct. 20 and the 2027 budget on Nov. 3. Mountain Waste is gathering landfill fee data that will drive 2027 trash and recycling fees.

new-castle/3.title: Building, planning and development update
new-castle/3.summary: Town Planner Paul Smith reported about 40 of 80 expected apartment units permitted, Coal Seam hotel/restaurant approved in April, and a New Castle Center (Walters Center) amended PUD expected in fall 2026. TC Midwest plans road and infrastructure work in fall/winter 2026.
new-castle/3.where: New Castle Center, Lakota and Castle Valley Ranch areas

new-castle/4.title: EV charging in Burning Mountain PUD Phase II
new-castle/4.summary: Council, sitting as the Board of Zoning, was to consider an EV charging state use designation in the Burning Mountain PUD (Phase II) zoning district.

new-castle/5.title: Police Department training and updates
new-castle/5.summary: Chief Stu Curry reported on increased officer training, largely funded by Colorado POST grants to limit town cost. Police matters were discussed in the August and September council meetings, including regional chief meetings.

new-castle/6.title: Senior housing residents' concerns
new-castle/6.summary: A resident spoke for residents of Canyon Senior Housing about concerns and asked about town ordinances. Administrator Reynolds said council can take it up at an upcoming work session.

new-castle/7.title: Historic Preservation Commission survey grants and CLG audit
new-castle/7.summary: The commission is pursuing grants to survey historic properties using Sanborn fire insurance maps, a videography project, and approved its Certified Local Government audit. The chair said some projects fall outside the commission's bylaws.

new-castle/8.title: Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act
new-castle/8.summary: Council had a workshop discussion on the Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act on Sept. 15.

new-castle/9.title: Town events: Burning Mountain Festival parade and fall cleanup
new-castle/9.summary: Council is planning parade logistics for the Burning Mountain Festival and an Oct. 10 trash pick-up day with fall cleanup.

new-castle/10.title: AI use policy
new-castle/10.summary: Council was to discuss and consider an artificial intelligence use policy on Nov. 3, 2026.

norwood/0.title: Town-wide 15 mph speed limit
norwood/0.summary: The board discussed lowering the speed limit in the spring and summer, then considered an ordinance in July setting a 15 mph limit on all town streets unless otherwise posted. A further ordinance was on the August 12 agenda, but the documents do not state the outcome.

norwood/1.title: Moratorium on medium and large-scale development and land use code rewrite
norwood/1.summary: The board considered extending the emergency temporary moratorium on medium and large-scale development (Ordinance 0813, 2025). It also contracted KLJ for a land use code update and a master plan, and a Land Use Code amendment ordinance was scheduled for October. A joint work session covered the master plan and annexation.

norwood/2.title: Norwood Public School property purchase and rezone
norwood/2.summary: The town tracked its purchase of the Norwood Public School property. A public hearing and ordinance were scheduled on May 13 to rezone 2028 Maverick Way from Agriculture to a Public zoning district.

norwood/3.title: Short-term rental rules
norwood/3.summary: Short-term rentals were a recurring discussion item from July through October. The documents do not give specifics of any proposed rules.

norwood/4.title: Employee compensation and retention incentives
norwood/4.summary: The board considered a resolution and ordinance authorizing additional compensation and retention incentives for employees, with legal review of compensation in May. A second ordinance on the subject came up in July.

norwood/5.title: Water treatment plant land, raw water and water commission
norwood/5.summary: The board and Water Commission met about State Land Board property for the water treatment plant. They also worked on raw water board rules, grant authority for the Water Commission, commission appointments and terms, and a drainage study and system design by SGM.

norwood/6.title: Pocket park construction and dedication
norwood/6.summary: The town took a bid from RMC Builders for the pocket park at 1575 Grand Ave. Signage and an update followed, and a dedication was set for September.

norwood/7.title: Sidewalks, school traffic and CDOT projects
norwood/7.summary: The town approved job bids for the CDOT Safer Sidewalks to School project and an MOU with CDOT. It later discussed school traffic and the sidewalk project, and heard about upcoming CDOT projects.

norwood/8.title: Removal for cause hearing
norwood/8.summary: The board adopted a resolution in August setting a public hearing to consider removing an official for cause, and amended it in September. The October 15 hearing was cancelled. The documents do not name the person or give the reason.

norwood/9.title: Wildlife and wildfire ordinances, fireworks
norwood/9.summary: The board discussed wildlife and wildfire ordinances in January and February. Fireworks, including a Noel Night or New Year's Eve show and 2026 plans, came up several times.

norwood/10.title: 2027 draft budget
norwood/10.summary: The 2027 draft budget was taken up in October and again on November 4.

norwood/11.title: EV charging, streetlights and dark sky rules
norwood/11.summary: The board discussed EV charging station rates and install budget, streetlight dark sky compliance, and updated Dark Sky Coalition rules.

nunn/0.title: North Weld Water Services Agreement and Master Water Plan
nunn/0.summary: The Town attorney has been reviewing and amending the water services agreement with North Weld County Water District, with a final version to go to the Board before approval. The Town also awarded a Master Water Plan grant, chose an engineer bid in August 2026, and is working on a grant to find water loss.

nunn/1.title: Water taps, excess water use ordinance and 2027 water rates
nunn/1.summary: In fall 2026 the Board took up water tap approvals with water share and tap fees, an excessive water use ordinance for properties over their water unit, and 2027 water rates and fees. Water loss and added meters were earlier concerns, as were hydrant locks and a bulk fill station.

nunn/2.title: Clayton Homes and Blue Spruce developments, 4th Street lot line variance
nunn/2.summary: Clayton Homes wants to build 18 homes. The Board has discussed plant investments and tap fees for large developments, approved permits for lots 2 and 3 of the RLD subdivision, and held a September 2026 hearing on a variance at 1467 4th Street after a house at 1457 4th Street was placed too close to the lot line. A development agreement with Blue Spruce Development on 4th Street is under review, and they must provide water shares.

nunn/3.title: CDBG Senior Center/Community Center grant and Town Hall improvements
nunn/3.summary: The Town got a CDBG grant of $206,739.34 for the senior and community center, and asbestos abatement bids ranged from $56,000 to $161,000. The Board voted on how to complete the work, including interior painting and a trophy case, and on a project manager.

nunn/4.title: Wildfire resiliency code and 2024 building code adoption
nunn/4.summary: The Board adopted Ordinance 329 for the 2024 International Building Code in April 2026. It is working on adopting the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which the fire district must review, and plans a hearing notice and draft ordinance.

nunn/5.title: Safer Streets grant, speed study and Master Drainage Plan
nunn/5.summary: The Town chose an engineering firm for the Safer Streets grant, ran a speed study, and gathered resident input through an interactive map and outreach events. The Safer Streets plan and Master Drainage Plan are to be posted online for 30 days for public comment. Weld County road help on CR 31 is also under discussion.

nunn/6.title: Sunrise Solar project at CR 29.5
nunn/6.summary: The Board reviewed a permit application for a 20-acre solar project at 49600 CR 29.5, with a 10-foot fence. It asked for written plans on dust mitigation, construction truck routes and an eco plan, and expects 50% plans in mid-August. Chalk Bluffs Energy Project also presented in January 2026.

nunn/7.title: 2027 budget, mill levy and police funding
nunn/7.summary: The 2026 mill levy and budget were adopted in December 2025. The 2027 budget draft was reviewed in October 2026. The police department sought less-lethal pepper ball guns at $969 each, tasers, vehicle upgrades or lease, and a Byrne JAG grant with a match of up to $5,000.

nunn/8.title: RV and ADU ordinance
nunn/8.summary: The Board began reviewing an ordinance on RVs and accessory dwelling units in fall 2026.

nunn/9.title: Marijuana license renewals and new manufacturing application
nunn/9.summary: The Board handled several marijuana cultivation and manufacturing license renewals. It also reviewed a new manufacturing application, which still needs state approval and then a local license vote.

nunn/10.title: Bus stop shelter on Highway 85
nunn/10.summary: The Board discussed and voted on an additional bus stop shelter on the east side of Highway 85.

nunn/11.title: Preliminary concept plan for 20 acres, former Antelope Run
nunn/11.summary: The Board was to review a preliminary concept plan from Robert Kearny for 20 acres of the former Antelope Run property.

oak-creek/0.title: New 2% sales tax chapter for capital improvements (Ordinance No. 678)
oak-creek/0.summary: The Town Board discussed an ordinance adopting a new Chapter 3.02 of the municipal code covering the town's 2.0% sales tax, to be used for construction and rehabilitation of capital improvements. It was discussed in August and September and put up for approval as Ordinance No. 678 on October 8.

oak-creek/1.title: 2027 budget and capital improvement plan
oak-creek/1.summary: The board reviewed the first draft of the 2027 annual budget on October 8 and continued budget and 2027 Capital Improvement Plan discussions on November 12.

oak-creek/2.title: Lot 15, Sierra View Subdivision development agreement with MACOGA, LLC
oak-creek/2.summary: The board considered a development agreement for Lot 15 in Sierra View, took legal advice in executive session on October 22, and then considered a Development Improvement Agreement. The new agreement would end and replace the April 2025 Improvements Agreement and requires a $5,000 deposit from the developer.

oak-creek/3.title: Bulk water dispensing station upgrades
oak-creek/3.summary: The board discussed upgrades to the town's bulk water dispensing station, then took up buying a new control panel and a proposal to build a new shell for the station.

oak-creek/4.title: Trash hauling rate increases from Apex Twin Enviro
oak-creek/4.summary: The board scheduled a discussion with Apex Twin Enviro about trash hauling rate increases starting in November 2026.

oak-creek/5.title: Dog park proposal and SOROCO Youth Council grant
oak-creek/5.summary: The SOROCO Youth Action Council asked for a letter of support for a grant to build a dog park in Oak Creek and presented the proposed project to the board on October 8.

oak-creek/6.title: Grants for Oak Creek Mountain Park flow trail and DOLA energy impact funds
oak-creek/6.summary: The board considered a $125,000 Colorado Parks and Wildlife trail grant application to finish a downhill flow trail in Oak Creek Mountain Park. On November 12 it also considered a DOLA Energy Impact Assistance grant application of up to $200,000 and discussed a Charge Ahead Colorado grant.

oak-creek/7.title: Routt County Sheriff's Office law enforcement agreement
oak-creek/7.summary: The board discussed an agreement with the Routt County Sheriff's Office for law enforcement services in town.

oak-creek/8.title: Interim town clerk/treasurer and payroll outsourcing
oak-creek/8.summary: The board appointed an interim clerk/treasurer by resolution in October and again in November. It also considered outsourcing payroll to Caselle.

oak-creek/9.title: South Routt Medical Center expansion
oak-creek/9.summary: The Planning Commission and Town Board held public hearings on a South Routt Medical Center Health Service Plan application to add 880 square feet of institutional space.

oak-creek/10.title: Bell Avenue drainage improvement project
oak-creek/10.summary: The board reviewed bids for the Bell Avenue drainage improvement project.

oak-creek/11.title: South Routt Housing Authority funding request
oak-creek/11.summary: The South Routt Housing Authority asked the town for $13,000 in operations funding.

oak-creek/12.title: Nuisance abatement and construction management standards
oak-creek/12.summary: The board discussed nuisance abatement actions in town on October 22 and possible adoption of construction management standards on November 12.

ophir/0.title: Ban on short-term rentals (Ordinance 2026-7)
ophir/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission took up an ordinance amending Section 303.1 of the Land Use Code to prohibit leasing homes as short-term rentals, citing town services, neighbors and limited housing stock. P&Z discussed how long a rental period should count, with one member suggesting anything under 63 days, and recommended the ordinance 3-0 as written in October.

ophir/1.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code and new exterior material rules
ophir/1.summary: Ophir adopted the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which state law required by May. P&Z reviewed wildfire-resistant siding, such as wood-styled cement board, and in October considered new exterior material requirements for siding, garage doors, decking and fences that comply with the code.

ophir/2.title: Revegetation ordinance and parking plan
ophir/2.summary: P&Z reviewed the Ophir Environmental Commission's proposed revegetation ordinance, including an approved seed list and a parking plan that would limit parking to Ophir rights of way. P&Z recommended approving the revegetation code 5-0, with the construction fencing requirement removed.

ophir/3.title: Dark Sky / lighting ordinance
ophir/3.summary: P&Z recommended approval of a Dark Sky/Lighting Ordinance 5-0 in March 2026.

ophir/4.title: Variance for 2/12 roof pitch and reduced side setbacks on Aurum Street
ophir/4.summary: An applicant (Slator) requested variances for Lots 1 and 2, Block 2 on Aurum Street: side yard setbacks reduced from 15 ft to 10 ft and a 2/12 roof pitch, to help reduce building height. P&Z reviewed the request in March 2026, and the minutes mention approval of the variance by the General Assembly.

ophir/5.title: Low Energy & Carbon Code presentation
ophir/5.summary: EcoAction Partners were scheduled to give P&Z a 30-minute presentation with Q&A on a Low Energy and Carbon Code in June 2026.

ophir/6.title: Building permit reviews: Bobtail, Granite and Aurum streets
ophir/6.summary: P&Z reviewed building plans for the Aplin and Kondracki home on Bobtail Street, the Croke residence on Granite Street and the Cooper residence on Aurum Street. P&Z recommended approving the Croke plans 4-0, with exterior material samples to be provided.

ophir/7.title: Fence at 112 Bobtail Street
ophir/7.summary: P&Z considered whether a fence on Lots 5 and 6, Block 4 is a permitted accessory use to the home on Lots 7 and 8. It decided new fencing needed no variance or Special Use Permit, then reviewed fencing materials for the new fence at 112 Bobtail Street in October.

ordway/0.title: Addies Restaurant annexation at 17484 Highway 96
ordway/0.summary: Trustees took up an annexation petition filed by Toni Evans (Addies Restaurant) in August, and Planning and Zoning recommended annexation. Ordinances 673 and 674 on annexation and zoning had a second reading on Oct. 5, but were repealed Oct. 21. Council then set a Nov. 30, 2026 public hearing on the annexation.

ordway/1.title: Water moratorium, restrictions and water supply
ordway/1.summary: Council denied a water restrictions resolution (2026-06) in April, then approved Resolution 2026-07 in June, a moratorium on additional water services. Water reports and a town resident water restructuring discussion also came up, along with the SE Colorado Water Conservancy allocation of 64.75 AF.

ordway/2.title: Town attorney contract loss and CIRSA insurance claim
ordway/2.summary: Documents include a CIRSA coverage letter and a settlement agreement tied to a former town attorney's amendment of a water rate contract, with losses beginning in 2022. The Town's losses and the malpractice claim are described, but the outcome is not clear from the documents.

ordway/3.title: 428 E. 3rd Street town property sale and foreclosure
ordway/3.summary: Council authorized sale of town-owned property in March, including 428 East 3rd Street, then discussed the property in executive session in May. In June it discussed restarting foreclosure on the property.

ordway/4.title: Historic preservation and Certified Local Government
ordway/4.summary: Council moved to establish a Certified Local Government and a Historic Preservation Advisory Authority (Ordinances 668, 669, 671) and gave updates on the CLG process. A further historic ordinance (675) had a first reading in October.

ordway/5.title: Affordable housing development agreement and tax certificate purchases
ordway/5.summary: In October the Town considered an agreement with a development company on future affordable housing. It also approved negotiating tax certificates for properties at 305, 317 and 319 Arkansas and 326 Idaho, and approved a demolition application at 318 E 3rd.

ordway/6.title: Mobile park holding negotiations ended
ordway/6.summary: Council discussed a sewer tap for a mobile park in June and in October moved to discontinue negotiations with Mobile Park Holding LLC.

ordway/7.title: Cemetery board and cemetery grant
ordway/7.summary: Council passed an ordinance (672) creating a Cemetery Board for Ordway Cemetery and gave an update on moving ahead with a cemetery grant.

ordway/8.title: Fire department county invoices and funding
ordway/8.summary: Council discussed an invoice from the county to the Fire Department in June. The Fire Department will pay past-due invoices with a subsidy. Workers' compensation and Air Med Care membership also came up.

ordway/9.title: Community Library agreement
ordway/9.summary: Council discussed the library in April and approved a revised Community Library IGA in September.

ouray-county/0.title: Land Use Code rewrite: zoning section and definitions
ouray-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission is working through a revised county Land Use Code under Resolution 2024-029, with Section 2 drafts followed by Section 3 (Zoning) and Section 13, and a public hearing planned once drafts are done. Proposed changes include new definitions and limits for accessory dwelling units, yurts, campgrounds, commercial outdoor recreation, short-term rentals and agricultural structures, and a possible 'Commercial Storefront' use in the Colona Zone.

ouray-county/1.title: Water-wise landscaping requirements in the Land Use Code
ouray-county/1.summary: Draft Section 3.11 would add state-driven water-wise landscaping rules for new development, with a broad definition of invasive plants and exceptions such as artificial turf on athletic fields of play that still need clarification.

ouray-county/2.title: Tribal consultation for renewable energy projects in zoning code
ouray-county/2.summary: Staff say they reached out to Tribes about state-law consultation requirements for renewable energy projects and will discuss scope and proposed code language if the Tribes reply.

ouray-county/3.title: Curry subdivision at 1615 County Road 1
ouray-county/3.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on a combined Preliminary and Final Development Plan from Kilpin and Sandra Curry to divide a parcel into 2 lots.

ouray-county/4.title: Pastor subdivision exemption at 6549 County Road 24
ouray-county/4.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing to recommend to the county commissioners on Clifford Pastor's request for an exemption to split a parcel into 2 lots.

ouray-county/5.title: Joint Planning agreement with the City and annexation authority
ouray-county/5.summary: Staff noted that 2022 changes to the Joint Planning IGA requested by the City, related to annexation authority, created legal and planning concerns that could force zoning section changes on the fly.

pagosa-springs/0.title: Ponderosa Mountain planned development (Hwy 160 and Goldmine Drive)
pagosa-springs/0.summary: Modern Community Builders LLC applied for a 70-acre, three-phase planned development with commercial lodging, housing and deed-restricted workforce housing (90%-130% AMI). The Planning Commission reviewed the sketch plan in September, Council took first reading on Oct. 20 after continuing it from Oct. 6, and second reading, as amended, was scheduled for Nov. 3.

pagosa-springs/1.title: Data center moratorium (Ordinance 1037)
pagosa-springs/1.summary: Council took up Ordinance 1037 on second reading, a moratorium on accepting or processing permit and land development applications that include a data center. The Land Use Development Code has no data center use classification, and staff want time to codify one while watching data center development in Colorado and nationally.

pagosa-springs/2.title: 2027 town budget, fee schedule and capital plan
pagosa-springs/2.summary: Council adopted the 2027 budget (Resolution 2026-21) after a public hearing, with a 1.561 mill levy generating $173,145 and a 5-year capital plan covering the community center roof, vehicles and park improvements. Town sales tax receipts have come in below projections, down 0.78% in July and 2.83% in August.

pagosa-springs/3.title: Sewer system repairs and new wastewater treatment plant
pagosa-springs/3.summary: The Sanitation GID is replacing sewer lines (McCabe Creek project completed, Rosita Street underway), buying surge tanks and pumps, and seeking a $900,000 grant for the 1st Street lift station, with a $3 million loan approved. It is also procuring an owner's advisor and design-build team for a new wastewater treatment facility, and a sewer sales tax passed earlier.
pagosa-springs/3.where: Pagosa Springs sewer system, 1st Street lift station

pagosa-springs/4.title: Sanitation GID 2027 budget and sewer rate increases
