pagosa-springs/4.summary: The Sanitation GID adopted its 2027 budget with $6,057,941 in expenditures and a 0.904 mill levy generating $81,008. The fee schedule raises commercial sewer rates and connection fees.

pagosa-springs/5.title: G&I Sanitation trash collection franchise (Ordinance 1039)
pagosa-springs/5.summary: Council granted G&I Sanitation Services a five-year franchise for refuse collection using town streets and alleys. A public hearing was also held on the rates G&I proposes to charge.

pagosa-springs/6.title: Talisman Drive area rezoning to Multi-unit Town Center (Ordinance 1040)
pagosa-springs/6.summary: Ordinance 1040 rezones Cornerstone Lofts and Talisman Pointe units on Talisman, Eaton and Village Drives to Multi-unit Town Center. Planning Commission recommended approval Aug. 25, and Council passed it on first and second reading.
pagosa-springs/6.where: Talisman Drive, Eaton Drive, Village Drive

pagosa-springs/7.title: Housing Action Plan and Proposition 123 credits
pagosa-springs/7.summary: Town and County held joint work sessions on the Housing Action Plan, and Council approved an intergovernmental agreement on Proposition 123 shared affordable housing credits. Council also reviewed town-owned properties and appointed members to a Housing Committee.

pagosa-springs/8.title: Development moratorium request and Apache Street speeding
pagosa-springs/8.summary: Resident Rachel Suh asked Council to approve a large-scale development moratorium because of infrastructure needs. Tammy Walters asked for a speed bump and deer crossing sign on Apache Street, citing speeding from park use, pickleball and school traffic.

pagosa-springs/9.title: Dark Sky Lighting Management Plan
pagosa-springs/9.summary: The Dark Sky Steering Committee held a work session on a Lighting Management Plan that exceeds current Land Use Development Code standards. It limits artificial light at night, requires exterior lighting plans for new development, and sets rules such as no flashing lights and no lit trails.

pagosa-springs/10.title: Kids Camp ended by Town; park naming and new park projects
pagosa-springs/10.summary: The Town will stop operating Kids Camp, which carried about $40,000 in annual subsidy, and is discussing with PCI a summer program. Council named the former Bob's LP property at 1040 E US 160 San Juan River Park, and Yamaguchi South Bike Park construction continues.

pagosa-springs/11.title: Canceled July 4 fireworks rescheduled for Old Fashion Christmas
pagosa-springs/11.summary: Fireworks were canceled in July due to extreme fire risk. The Acme contract would forfeit the $32,000 cost unless a show is held in 2026, so Council voted to hold it during Old Fashion Christmas.

pagosa-springs/12.title: Town Manager David Harris contract extension
pagosa-springs/12.summary: After an executive session on his evaluation and employment agreement, Council moved to extend Town Manager David Harris's contract. Martinez and Mayor Pierce will help craft the extension.

pagosa-springs/13.title: Downtown development reviews: Healing Waters, courthouse parking lot, Town Terrace
pagosa-springs/13.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled reviews of the Healing Waters redevelopment, the 449 San Juan Street LLC courthouse and parking lot enhancement (449, 473, 497 San Juan Street), and a density bonus for Town Terrace at 262 Pagosa Street.

palisade/0.title: Draft 2027 Town of Palisade budget
palisade/0.summary: Staff presented the draft 2027 budget to the Board of Trustees as required by state law. The board was asked to set the public hearing to adopt the final budget for November 10, 2026.

palisade/1.title: 2027 special event calendar and blackout dates (Resolution 2026-17)
palisade/1.summary: The Board of Trustees was to consider Resolution 2026-17, approving the 2027 special event calendar and blackout dates.

palisade/2.title: Watershed wildfire mitigation presentation from Colorado State Forest Service
palisade/2.summary: The Colorado State Forest Service was scheduled to present on watershed wildfire mitigation and coordination with the town.

palisade/3.title: Tourism Advisory Commission interviews and appointment
palisade/3.summary: The board was to interview candidates and appoint a commissioner to the Tourism Advisory Commission by roll call vote.

palisade/4.title: Fall Town Cleanup Day and Trick-or-Treat Street events
palisade/4.summary: Fall Town Cleanup Day is Saturday, October 17 from 8 am to noon at the Riverbend Park parking lot, or until dumpsters are full. Trick-or-Treat Street and Touch a Truck is Friday, October 30.

palmer-lake/0.title: Temporary data center moratorium (Resolution 31-2026)
palmer-lake/0.summary: The Board of Trustees had Resolution 31-2026 on its September 10 agenda for discussion and possible action on a temporary moratorium on data centers. The documents do not state the outcome.

palmer-lake/1.title: Buc-ee's annexation withdrawal and EcoSpa development legal talks
palmer-lake/1.summary: The Board met in executive session on negotiations with the landowner's counsel and counsel for Buc-ee's following withdrawal of the annexation request. Later agendas show legal advice on the EcoSpa development at 350 Highway 105, and a Buc-ee's-related item was pulled from the consent agenda on Nov 12.

palmer-lake/2.title: Town-wide bear-proof trash ordinance (Ordinance 6-2026)
palmer-lake/2.summary: The Planning Commission discussed a mandatory, town-wide bear-proof container requirement, certified receptacles and CPW grants, and residents asked for strict enforcement. The Board had the Bear Mitigation and Enforcement ordinance 6-2026 on its Oct 22 agenda.

palmer-lake/3.title: Stage one water emergency and watering restrictions
palmer-lake/3.summary: The town remains under a stage one water emergency with an outdoor watering ban that cut demand by 25% and allowed a shift to the Denver well. Monument Creek is too low to serve as a production source and there is no firm end date to the water call. A resident criticized how the town communicated the restrictions.

palmer-lake/4.title: 2026 amended budget and draft 2027 budget
palmer-lake/4.summary: Town Administrator Patrick Davidson froze non-essential spending and new capital projects while preparing 2027 projections. The Board held budget workshops and reviewed the amended 2026 budget (Resolution 45-2026) and draft 2027 budget (Resolution 44-2026), with a master fee schedule amendment (Resolution 34-2026) earlier. Possible consolidation of the Water, Roads and Parks departments was also raised.

palmer-lake/5.title: Trustee Moseley removal hearing and legal costs
palmer-lake/5.summary: The town retained a hearing officer and is arranging a presenting officer for hearings concerning Trustee Roger Moseley, with a removal hearing tentatively set for Nov 16. The Board is also dealing with Moseley v. Town of Palmer Lake (Colorado False Claims Act) and policies on using the town attorney and legal costs.

palmer-lake/6.title: Parks and Trails projects and 2027 budget priorities
palmer-lake/6.summary: The Parks and Trails Commission ranked 2027 projects, favoring stable funding like the Conservation Trust Fund, and proposed a third Air Force Academy student-designed bridge. Other items include Elephant Rock pavilion renovation, Centennial Park pickleball court flooding and pump track, playground inspections, a community garden proposal, the Strip Park project and motorized vehicles on trails.
palmer-lake/6.where: Centennial Park, Elephant Rock and town trails

palmer-lake/7.title: Creek Week and Fountain Creek watershed cleanup
palmer-lake/7.summary: Trustees proclaimed Sept 26 to Oct 4, 2026 as Creek Week after a Fountain Creek Watershed District presentation. Palmer Lake planned a joint litter pickup and noxious weed mitigation event.
palmer-lake/7.where: Palmer Lake and Fountain Creek watershed

palmer-lake/8.title: Lakeview lots conservation easement and Town lease with option to purchase
palmer-lake/8.summary: The Board agenda included a conservation easement and donation of about 140 platted lots in Lakeview. The Board also met in executive session on a proposed lease with option to purchase.

palmer-lake/9.title: Possible fire protection ballot measure
palmer-lake/9.summary: The town administrator is researching a possible ballot measure on fire protection involving the Palmer Lake Fire Department and Monument Fire. Because it involves taxation, a special election may not be allowed and it may have to wait until November 2027.

palmer-lake/10.title: Planning Commission items: Fowler Branch land use, plat amendment, Calverts sign
palmer-lake/10.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled a Fowler Branch land use matter, a plat amendment adjusting Lot 8 to make it larger, and a sign application for Calverts. The applicant on one item requested a continuance.

paonia/0.title: Short-term rental rules and the Common Ground Ordinance
paonia/0.summary: An ad hoc committee has met repeatedly since August to edit the proposed Common Ground Ordinance on short-term rentals. It has leaned toward registration with no numerical cap at first, three-year registrations, self-certified safety, a local contact, liability insurance and tax compliance, and it is still debating an 8% saturation threshold for whole-home rentals. Public survey responses and written comments have been mixed, citing housing, noise, parking and tax fairness.

paonia/1.title: Stage 2 water restrictions and water supply concerns
paonia/1.summary: On Aug. 18 the Board adopted Stage 2 water restrictions (Resolution 19-26) after high water use dropped tank levels about four feet over a weekend, allowing limited hand or drip watering. Later meetings tracked tank levels and production, and the Board took up Resolution 22-26 rescinding the restrictions on Oct. 27. Planning staff are also preparing for possible water moratorium and tap availability processes, and the Board met with the water attorney in executive session on water rights.

paonia/2.title: Zoning code rewrite, estate zoning density, ADUs and subdivision rules
paonia/2.summary: The Town is rewriting its zoning, subdivision and related codes to carry out the 2025 Comprehensive Plan, with smaller lots, ADUs by right, infill, impact fees and streamlined review. Staff also proposed fixing an inconsistency in Estate Zoning Table 16-2 and allowing 1.5 to two acres per dwelling. The Planning Commission is looking at ADU rules and sidewalks in new subdivisions, and a rezoning application from David Warren went to public hearing.

paonia/3.title: 2027 budget work sessions
paonia/3.summary: The 2027 budget was presented Oct. 27 and the Board asked for weekly budget work sessions separate from other meetings. Sessions were held in October and November, including a discussion of a solid waste enterprise. Staff also suggested creating a Community Development position.

paonia/4.title: New police chief appointment
paonia/4.summary: Residents spoke in support of Sergeant Henderson, and the Board appointed him as the new Chief of Police on Oct. 27. The Board also approved radios for the police department, and a patrol truck purchase was on a Sept. 30 agenda.

paonia/5.title: Town Administrator search and Board vacancy
paonia/5.summary: The Town is searching for a permanent Town Administrator, with an executive search firm profile up for approval Sept. 30 while Greg Sund serves as interim. The Board also appointed a trustee after hearing from two candidates and declared another vacancy by Resolution 24-26.

paonia/6.title: Recyclops free recycling service and Colorado EPR
paonia/6.summary: The Board heard from Recyclops about the state's Extended Producer Responsibility program and a proposal for free recycling service. Trustees approved the proposal on Nov. 10 on conditions: a state contract, liability insurance, and an agreement with the local recycler Cory's. A new solid waste disposal ordinance was also on the Sept. 8 agenda.

paonia/7.title: Water plant, sewer and street infrastructure projects
paonia/7.summary: The Board approved a RESPEC amendment for the Raw Water Monitoring Project, a $188,502.58 purchase of electric water plant valves and a sewer pipe CCTV scoping bid. It also considered a county agreement for a West Fourth Street overlay and a storm and sanitary sewer repair project. Sewer tap fee waiver ordinances and a Consor safety action plan covering roads like Samuel Wade Road were also on the agenda.

paonia/8.title: Former Twin Lakes property and Berg Foundation
paonia/8.summary: The Carl E. Berg Foundation presented to the Board in September and again on Nov. 10 about the former Twin Lakes property. A Colorado Parks & Wildlife conservation easement and a pathway license were also on the Nov. 10 agenda.

paonia/9.title: Street lights, dark skies and trail lights
paonia/9.summary: The Board discussed removing street lights and later gave direction on dark skies and trail lights. Separate items covered Town Hall solar panels and roof replacement.

paonia/10.title: Meeting procedures and meeting times
paonia/10.summary: The Board considered Ordinance 07-26 amending meeting procedures and Resolution 23-26 changing the regular meeting time, amending the start to 5:30. A commuter spoke about meeting times, and others raised concerns that public comments were not taken seriously at the ad hoc meetings.

parachute/0.title: Data center regulations (Ordinance 838-2026)
parachute/0.summary: The Town Council has a public hearing on Ordinance No. 838-2026 on Oct. 15, 2026. It would amend Title 15 of the municipal code to regulate data centers and technology uses. The agenda lists a cover memo but the documents give no outcome.

parachute/1.title: 1st Street / Highway 6 'Parachute Moves' reconstruction and grants
parachute/1.summary: The town has applied for federal funds (USDOT BUILD, HUD, congressionally directed spending) for the Highway 6 and 1st Street mobility and safety project. It did not get the $6.4 million BUILD grant in 2026 but received a $600,000 DOLA CDBG grant, and plans to try again next year.

parachute/2.title: 2027 budget and new revenue ideas
parachute/2.summary: Staff presented the 2027 draft budget in a September workshop and a public hearing on the budget is set for Oct. 15. The town needs more money for transit (PATS), wages and streets and is considering options such as a lodging fee, a tobacco tax, or sales tax ballot measures, some of which would need voter approval.

parachute/3.title: Parachute Area Transit System (PATS) funding
parachute/3.summary: The town approved a service agreement with Glenwood Downtowner for transit operations, supported transit grant applications and approved a Flix Bus license agreement for a bus stop. The mayor and town manager planned to discuss PATS funding with the county commissioners on Oct. 5.

parachute/4.title: Water system: raw water tank, loan refinance and Stage 2 restrictions
parachute/4.summary: Council backed a DOLA grant for the raw water tank replacement and approved an ordinance amending the water enterprise loan with Alpine Bank. Stage 2 water restrictions remained in place into summer, and public works began the Revelle Springs raw water line replacement.

parachute/5.title: Affordable housing expedited review and regional housing needs
parachute/5.summary: Ordinance 837-2026 would add expedited review for affordable housing under Prop 123 and update the land use review chart; it is up for a public hearing Oct. 15. Council also heard a regional housing needs assessment in July.

parachute/6.title: Purchase of 147 1st Street from Qwest/Lumen
parachute/6.summary: Council approved a contract to buy the property at 147 1st Street from Qwest Corporation. By May the sale had closed and the town owned it.

parachute/7.title: Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act and South Bridge support
parachute/7.summary: Council considered a resolution supporting federal bills S.5101 and H.R. 9826 to protect the Glenwood Hot Springs. Glenwood Springs also asked for a letter of support for its South Bridge project.

parachute/8.title: Garfield County Library District ballot issue 6B
parachute/8.summary: Council considered a resolution supporting the Garfield County Library District's 6B ballot measure.

parachute/9.title: Pet limits ordinance
parachute/9.summary: Council amended Ordinance 831-2025 on animal rules to remove household pet limits before approving it. It also updates the warning procedure and the fine for impounded strays.

parachute/10.title: Wildland-urban interface fire code and turf/landscaping rules
parachute/10.summary: Council adopted a revised Wildland Urban Interface Fire Code (Ordinance 836-2026). It also took up Ordinance 835-2026 limiting nonfunctional artificial turf and invasive plants in new development.

parachute/11.title: Community center and senior center future use
parachute/11.summary: The Valley Senior Center president asked council to make the facility more of a community center and spoke of the need for funding. In July council reviewed a draft Parachute Community Center management plan covering pricing, reservations and security.

park-county/0.title: Camp Sycamore conference and retreat center permit (PZ-2026-0198)
park-county/0.summary: An applicant sought a conditional use permit for a conference and retreat center in a residential zone, with church camps, weddings, corporate retreats and camping for up to 250 people. The Advisory Board on the Environment raised wildlife, wetland erosion and Ranger Station Rd. traffic and parking concerns. After public comment from several residents, the Planning Commission moved on Oct. 28 to recommend denial.

sources.body: Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments

park-county/1.title: Regenerative agrotourism camping at 634 County Road 62, Grant
park-county/1.summary: A conditional use permit (A26-0021) for a regenerative agrotourism business with commercial camping, plus a related minor subdivision, was reviewed from August through October. Commissioners asked for conditions including proof of water rights, a drainage and erosion plan, review of septic under CR 62 and a flood evacuation plan. Resolutions 2026-50 and 2026-51 were approved Oct. 6.

sources.body: Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments
Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments

park-county/2.title: Lostfork PUD amendment at Hwy 285 and County Road 62
park-county/2.summary: The applicant asked to fold an adjacent lot at 373 County Rd 62 into its PUD at 49355 Hwy 285, Grant. Commissioners approved it Oct. 20 with conditions including a look at Geneva Creek waterways, no buildings on wetlands, a CDOT road evaluation and septic and building permits. Resolution 2026-53 followed on Oct. 27.

sources.body: Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments
Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments

park-county/3.title: 2027 county budget
park-county/3.summary: Commissioners reviewed the 2026 budget and held departmental presentations on the 2027 proposed budget through September to November. The proposed 2027 budget was moved to Oct. 15, when two commissioners voted to adopt it. The Land and Water Trust Fund also reviewed its 2027 budget.

sources.body: Land and Water Trust Fund Board
Land and Water Trust Fund Board

park-county/4.title: County manager termination and legal services change
park-county/4.summary: The commissioners ratified Resolution 2026-47 terminating the county manager, then corrected its statutory citations in Resolution 2026-48. On Oct. 30 they voted not to renew the contract with Evans Legal Group, and a new legal services contract was on the Nov. 10 agenda.

park-county/5.title: Emergency culvert repairs on County Road 43 and Deer Creek
park-county/5.summary: Commissioners used Land and Water Trust Fund discretionary money (Resolution 2026-49) for an emergency Deer Creek culvert repair. They also approved a bid for emergency replacement of twin 72-inch culverts at County Road 43 and 1034. The CR43 repairs were slated for a community update.

sources.body: Land and Water Trust Fund Board

park-county/6.title: Paris Mill and Old Courthouse preservation work
park-county/6.summary: The county approved a construction agreement with High Country Haulers for Paris Mill work after asking about bid numbers and whether the firm would do the work or broker it. Heritage board notes cover foundation grant work at Paris Mill and basement work at the Old Courthouse, plus a county historic preservation plan update seeking public survey responses.

sources.body: South Park National Heritage Area Board

park-county/7.title: South Park International Dark Sky designation
park-county/7.summary: The commissioners reviewed a letter of support for the South Park Dark Sky effort. The heritage area board reported the application is submitted, focused on Eleven Mile State Park, with letters of support being gathered.
park-county/7.where: Eleven Mile State Park / South Park

sources.body: South Park National Heritage Area Board
South Park National Heritage Area Board

park-county/8.title: Environmental blight ordinance (Ordinance 6, 2026)
park-county/8.summary: Commissioners approved the final reading of Ordinance 6 (2026), which prohibits accumulation of environmental blight in unincorporated Park County and replaces the 1991 ordinance.

park-county/9.title: Chaffee County inmate housing agreement
park-county/9.summary: Commissioners approved an agreement to house Park County inmates at the Chaffee County Detention Center at a daily rate of $100 per inmate. A rescinding and replacement agreement was on the Nov. 10 agenda.

park-county/10.title: McMillan rezoning (PZ-2026-0191) and fire hazard concerns
park-county/10.summary: A request to rezone a property from Residential drew environmental board concerns about possible firewood processing and fire hazard inside town limits. The applicant requested a continuance to the Nov. 17 commissioners meeting.

sources.body: Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments

park-county/11.title: Summit County bus service agreement
park-county/11.summary: Commissioners continued reviewing a proposed intergovernmental agreement with Summit County bus service.

park-county/12.title: Google North state-assessed property and Colorado Springs Utilities
park-county/12.summary: Commissioners discussed a Google North, Inc. state-assessed property matter and heard a presentation from Colorado Springs Utilities. The documents give no further detail.

park-county/13.title: Overlook St right-of-way vacation (PZ-2026-0160)
park-county/13.summary: A request by the county and Michael Fleming to vacate 14 feet of the 30-foot Overlook St right-of-way at 128 Overlook St was remanded to the Planning Department after a hearing.
park-county/13.where: 128 Overlook St, Harris Park Estates Unit 2

parker/0.title: Axon drone-as-first-responder and license plate reader program
parker/0.summary: The Police Department proposed joining Axon's countywide Drone as First Responder and License Plate Reader programs, which would raise the Axon contract by $175,000 a year. Council discussion centered on transparency, accountability and video retention. A resident separately asked the Town to remove Flock cameras around Parker.

parker/1.title: Parker Road and Mainstreet intersection redesign
parker/1.summary: Town staff and consultant Kimley-Horn identified a Dual Quadrant Roadway as the preferred alternative for the Parker Road (CO-83) and Mainstreet intersection. They asked Council for direction to keep advancing the 10% conceptual design, which aims to improve traffic flow, pedestrian safety and downtown redevelopment while limiting impacts to O'Brien Park.

parker/2.title: Future of Mainstreet: safety, speeding and pedestrian-only proposal
parker/2.summary: Residents urged a traffic study for speeding on Mainstreet between Jordan Road and Twenty Mile Road. Others suggested making Mainstreet pedestrian-only for safety and social gatherings.

parker/3.title: 2027 Town budget and property tax levy
parker/3.summary: Council held a budget workshop on Oct. 2 and a study session on Oct. 26 on the 2027 Proposed Budget, published Oct. 13. First readings of the 2026 property tax levy and revised 2026 budget came Nov. 2, with adoption set for Nov. 16. New special funds for risk management and the My Mainstreet GID were also introduced, and staff proposed redesigning the Town's property and liability insurance.

parker/4.title: Parker 2050 Comprehensive Plan adopted
parker/4.summary: After a Planning Commission hearing on Sept. 10, Council adopted the Town of Parker 2050 Comprehensive Plan on Sept. 21 (Resolution 26-060). The Planning Commission also took up the 2026 Three-Mile Area Plan on Oct. 22.

parker/5.title: Salisbury Regional Park Phase 2
parker/5.summary: Council approved a site plan amendment for Phase 2 of the 91-acre Salisbury Regional Park, adding tennis, pickleball and basketball courts, an inclusive playground and spray ground, a bike park, fitness area and parking. A water pipeline easement for the Parker Water and Sanitation District was also approved. One resident asked about parking.
parker/5.where: East side of Motsenbocker Road, north of Hess Road

parker/6.title: Security guard, massage facility and merchant patrol licensing updates
parker/6.summary: The town is overhauling its 1994 security guard (merchant patrol) ordinance, last amended in 2004, with new fees and investigation processes. Council also readopted massage facility licensing rules under state law and set license fees.

parker/7.title: Twenty Mile Road improvements and property acquisition
parker/7.summary: Council introduced an ordinance stating the Town's intent to acquire property interests to build and improve Twenty Mile Road, and directed staff to notify affected owners.

parker/8.title: Parker Heritage Center plan and tribal history recognition
parker/8.summary: Council reviewed an Interpretive Plan to reimagine the Parker Heritage Center with Douglas County and Parker History. The 2026 budget has $100,000 for it plus a $7,500 grant. Council also heard a presentation on honoring the area's Tribal history.

parker/9.title: Parker Senior Center update and feasibility study
parker/9.summary: Council received an update on the Senior Center's facility needs, including drainage, flooring and parking lot repairs, and on a recently completed feasibility study. No funding was requested.

parker/10.title: Downtown Parker and Chambers BID 2027 budgets
parker/10.summary: The two Business Improvement Districts presented 2027 operating plans and budgets. Staff recommended Council approve them on Oct. 19. A separate item considered allowing deer-exclusion fencing taller than the current limit for plant nurseries.

parker/11.title: Parker Road and Hilltop Road intersection improvements and resurfacing contracts
parker/11.summary: Council awarded a $1,339,679.75 contract to Denver Dirt Works for the Parker Road and Hilltop Road intersection and approved a $607,070.35 increase to the 2026 resurfacing program contract with Amrize West Central.
parker/11.where: Parker Road and Hilltop Road; townwide streets

phillips-county/0.title: Wind, solar, battery storage and data center regulations
phillips-county/0.summary: The county commissioners had an agenda item on regulations for wind energy, solar, battery energy storage and data center facilities on Aug. 20. A Land Use Code public hearing was cancelled that day. The documents do not say what was decided.

phillips-county/1.title: 2027 county budget work sessions
phillips-county/1.summary: Commissioners scheduled 2027 budget work sessions after their meetings from September through November. A 2027 sales tax MOU for control of confidential data also came up on Sept. 29.

phillips-county/2.title: Floodplain ordinance
phillips-county/2.summary: A floodplain ordinance had its first reading on Oct. 19 and its second reading on Oct. 30. The documents do not give its contents.

phillips-county/3.title: Housing needs assessment and Proposition 123 recertification
phillips-county/3.summary: The county sought qualifications from firms for a Housing Needs Assessment and Water Supply Element on Oct. 9. On Oct. 30 it took up Proposition 123 recertification, which relates to affordable housing commitments.

phillips-county/4.title: Landfill equipment purchase and rates
phillips-county/4.summary: The landfill manager presented an equipment purchase on Aug. 20. Landfill rates were on the Aug. 31 agenda.

phillips-county/5.title: Viaero roadway occupancy agreements
phillips-county/5.summary: Roadway occupancy agreements with Viaero were on the Aug. 31 and Oct. 9 agendas. Such agreements cover the company's use of county road right-of-way.

phillips-county/6.title: Brightwater Cattle Co. on County Road 38 and minor land use change
phillips-county/6.summary: The commissioners heard a Brightwater Cattle Co. item on County Road 38 on Oct. 30. A public hearing on a minor land use change for Jason Roberts was held Sept. 21.

phillips-county/7.title: Road and Bridge propane contracts and equipment
phillips-county/7.summary: Road and Bridge brought a CHS propane contract and a cutting edges equipment purchase on Sept. 29. Propane contracts returned Oct. 9.

phillips-county/8.title: Fairgrounds entrance asphalt replacement
phillips-county/8.summary: The commissioners considered a project payment for replacing asphalt at the fairgrounds entrance on Oct. 19.

pitkin/0.title: 2026 Zoning Code adoption, RV parks and planned developments
pitkin/0.summary: The Board held public hearings on adopting a new 2026 Zoning Code in January and February 2026. Residents raised concerns about the RV park section and the planned unit development language. The town attorney was to remove the RV Park section and the board agreed to strike "mixed uses" from the planned development section. A sign section was also discussed at a resident's request. The documents do not show the final adoption vote.

pitkin/1.title: Western Slope Towers / Gunnison Met Rec radio tower lease
pitkin/1.summary: The Board considered a lease agreement with Gunnison Met Rec and Western Slope Towers to market tower services at the town's tower site. The mayor was concerned that the proposed 18 months at no charge and the rent amount were too low, and the 2,500 sq ft site description was questioned. Residents commented in January, and the site cleanup was to be added to the contract. In February the board reviewed the agreement again with no public comment, and the contract came up again in April.

pitkin/2.title: 2025 budget amendment, 2026 budget and mill levy
pitkin/2.summary: After public hearings on November 17, 2025, the board adopted an amended 2025 budget and the 2026 budget by Resolution 7 on December 11. It also adopted Resolution 8 levying property taxes for 2026. The amendment included a $7,000 increase for street maintenance. In April the mayor noted a large increase in sales tax revenue and asked for more detailed financial reports.

pitkin/3.title: OWTS (septic) regulations update
pitkin/3.summary: The board held a public hearing on November 19, 2025 and adopted Ordinance No. 1 of 2025 updating on-site wastewater treatment system regulations to match the state's Regulation 43. A new Environmental Health Agent, Joshua Ackerman, was appointed in November. Four properties had been sent final certified-mail notices.

pitkin/4.title: Wildfire resiliency, energy and building codes
pitkin/4.summary: The town held work sessions on a Wildfire Resiliency Code and plans public hearings on the Zoning, Wildfire, Energy and Building Codes starting in January 2026. A wildfire mitigation seminar was also on the April update list.

pitkin/5.title: Pond maintenance agreement with Colorado Parks and Wildlife
pitkin/5.summary: The board considered a five-year operations and maintenance cost-share agreement with CPW for a pond that CPW would keep stocking. The mayor reported concerns that the pond could be drained into the ditch. A resident commented.

pitkin/6.title: Fire/irrigation ditch cleaning RFP
pitkin/6.summary: The town sought bids for cleaning and digging about 600 feet of fire and irrigation ditches. The board reviewed the quotes, and the streets and ditches commissioner reported on his work.

pitkin/7.title: 428 State Street fence permit
pitkin/7.summary: The board reviewed a previously denied fence permit request for 428 State Street and approved it, with no public comment.

pitkin/8.title: Open board seats and town appointments
pitkin/8.summary: The board declared two board positions open through Resolution 4 of 2026, posted an open Zoning Board seat, and reappointed the town clerk/treasurer and town attorney.

platteville/0.title: Housing needs assessment, expedited affordable housing review and Proposition 123 commitment
platteville/0.summary: The Oct. 20, 2026 agenda lists three housing items: Resolution 2026-20 adopting a Housing Needs Assessment (with a public hearing), Resolution 2026-21 on expedited review policies for affordable housing projects, and Resolution 2026-22 on the town's Proposition 123 commitment for 2027-2029. The documents do not state the outcome.

pueblo-county/0.title: Aspen Acres Fire disaster declaration and flood recovery
pueblo-county/0.summary: The commissioners renewed the local disaster emergency for the Aspen Acres Fire (started June 29, 2026; over 101,965 acres affected) at nearly every meeting. They accepted a USDA watershed grant for flood and debris-flow recovery (project total $18,336,812) and hired Wilson and Company ($300,000 design) and RockSol and Phoenix Eye Consulting for engineering and oversight. They also approved a $500,000 MOU for mitigation projects and a FEMA lease at 201 W. 8th Street.

pueblo-county/1.title: Data center zoning standards
pueblo-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission held work sessions on August 19 and September 16 on draft use-specific standards for data centers under the Unified Development Code. The drafts address noise and cooling, and staff added requirements that developers show how they will pay for their share of utility infrastructure improvements. They also cover decommissioning timelines and road use agreements. The goal is a code amendment for Planning Commission and county commissioner action.

pueblo-county/2.title: 2027 budget cuts, layoffs and hiring freeze
pueblo-county/2.summary: The county is dealing with a budget shortfall, with a 2027 budget process, a financial outlook presentation, and repeated closed sessions on personnel and operating cuts across the Assessor, DA, Treasurer, Sheriff and Clerk offices. The board adopted a resolution eliminating BOCC staff positions (effective date later moved to December 19, 2026), formally declared no outside funding requests for 2027, and approved a 2027 pay plan and benefits. It also put the budget department under temporary oversight and amended the 2026 budget.

pueblo-county/3.title: Pueblo West roads sales tax and road transition
pueblo-county/3.summary: The board held a district meeting on the 2023 intergovernmental agreement for the Pueblo West roads sales tax and the transition of road services to the county. Cabree Cleveland was appointed to the Pueblo West Roads Sales Tax Oversight Committee as a joint member, with the tax coming from ballot question 6C (a temporary 1% sales tax for road maintenance).

pueblo-county/4.title: Solar projects and House Bill 1041 permits
pueblo-county/4.summary: Commissioners heard several 1041 permit items: a permit for 3 Corners Connector LLC, withdrawal of solar permit SLI-23-7, and an extension of SLI-23-6, pushing construction start to the third quarter of 2029. Stormwater maintenance agreements were approved for Highland Solar I and Thunder Wolf II, and closed sessions covered solar agreements with AES Solar and Solon.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use
Board of County Commissioners Land Use

pueblo-county/5.title: Runyon Sports Complex lease
pueblo-county/5.summary: The board discussed in closed sessions a lease with the Runyon Sports Complex Commission and contracts for bleachers and artificial turf, and then approved the lease agreement on October 22.

pueblo-county/6.title: Certificates of participation and county property financing
pueblo-county/6.summary: The county worked on lease-purchase financing, including bond counsel analysis, reduced collateral for certificates of participation, and a first amendment to a lease purchase for a block near West 11th Street. The Capital Construction Corporation board was changed to county staff, property was transferred to the county, and the county designated property for its TABOR emergency reserve. A resolution declared intent to issue revenue bonds, and a private activity bond presentation was heard.

pueblo-county/7.title: Jail construction contract with JE Dunn
pueblo-county/7.summary: The board discussed the jail construction contract between the county and JE Dunn in closed sessions on September 1 and October 27.

pueblo-county/8.title: Land use cases: special use permits, rezonings and violations
pueblo-county/8.summary: Planning commissioners and the board heard items such as a vehicle sales and rental special use for Toby and Rose Miller, rescission of Commnet's tower permit at 4800 North Creek Road in Beulah, a zoning violation case on Fields Road in Avondale, a 0.53-acre rezoning to SR2, and rescission of a marijuana and light industrial PUD. The Fremont Paving & Redi-Mix gravel and asphalt permit (1,030 acres) was reviewed.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Land Use
Board of County Commissioners Land Use
Board of County Commissioners Land Use

pueblo-county/9.title: PACOG transportation planning and trails
pueblo-county/9.summary: The Pueblo Area Council of Governments took up its 2027 budget, federal funding assignments for highway safety and signals along CO96A, the Medal of Honor Blvd. trail project, a bicycle and pedestrian master plan, and the Bustang expansion.

pueblo-county/10.title: Economic development: county revitalization authority and PEDCO
pueblo-county/10.summary: Staff presented a tax increment financing plan using a county revitalization authority and an economic development campaign. The chief administrative officer was appointed to the PEDCO board, and closed sessions covered economic development strategy and a marijuana excise tax agreement with the Pueblo Hispanic Education Foundation.

pueblo-county/11.title: Xcel Energy Carbon Free Future advisory seat
pueblo-county/11.summary: The county considered its role in appointing a Pueblo community member to Xcel Energy's Carbon Free Future Development Program advisory board and approved a letter of recommendation on September 24.

pueblo-county/12.title: Parks projects: Rye Mountain forest thinning and playgrounds
pueblo-county/12.summary: The board considered a Summit Logging contract for forest thinning and fuels reduction at Rye Mountain Park and approved a Playcore/GameTime playground agreement for Fulton Heights Community Center (up to $102,466.47).
pueblo-county/12.where: Rye Mountain Park; Fulton Heights Community Center

pueblo-county/13.title: Pueblo West and county lead cleanup comment
pueblo-county/13.summary: The board approved a letter responding to an EPA proposal to change a lead cleanup level and encouraging participation in public comment and open houses.

pueblo/0.title: 2027 city budget, property tax mill levy and public hearing
pueblo/0.summary: Council heard 2027 budget presentations from IT, Law, Finance and Parks in August and reviewed a recommended 2027 budget of $117,785,907, with sales tax (3.7% rate) making up 66.8% of general taxes. Nine residents spoke at the October 26 public hearing, and on November 9 council took first presentation of ordinances setting the 2027 mill levy and appropriations.

pueblo/1.title: Opposition to Black Hills Energy electric rate increase
pueblo/1.summary: Council passed a resolution opposing a proposed Black Hills Colorado Electric rate increase and added ratepayer costs of its 2026 electric resource plan, to be sent to the Colorado Public Utilities Commission (Proceeding No. 26A-0333E). Council also discussed the 2026 rate case in executive session.

pueblo/2.title: Lime Road and St. Charles Industrial Park development
pueblo/2.summary: Staff presented options for Lime Road, the only route into St. Charles Industrial Park: about $20M for reinforced concrete or $5M for asphalt, with a traffic study needed. Council earlier moved $8M to infrastructure for the park and discussed a potential economic development project there.
pueblo/2.where: Lime Road / St. Charles Industrial Park

pueblo/3.title: Da Vinci Museum request for half-cent sales tax funds
pueblo/3.summary: Council reviewed the Leonardo da Vinci Museum of North America's application for funding from the half-cent sales tax fund, an RTA project that replaced the Professional Bull Riders University. Materials note prior council approval of more than $14 million and up to $3 million in additional eligible funding.

pueblo/4.title: Economic development partner RFP and Project Tortuga
pueblo/4.summary: Council held several work sessions following up on a request for proposals for an economic development partner. Closed sessions also covered a potential economic development agreement called Project Tortuga, Project Falcon, Project Manta and a PEDCO v. City of Pueblo legal matter.

pueblo/5.title: Pueblo Masterplan Communities annexation and Jackson Ranch zoning
pueblo/5.summary: Council found the petition to annex the 89.93-acre Pueblo Masterplan Communities Annexation No. 1 valid and sent it to Planning and Zoning for review. It also took first presentation of ordinances zoning parcels of the Jackson Ranch annexation area, including 250.1 acres to Agricultural One.
pueblo/5.where: Pueblo Masterplan Communities; Jackson Ranch annexation area

pueblo/6.title: Airport agreements and aviation asset defense funding
pueblo/6.summary: Council created an Airport Policy Advisory board, took up an airline operating agreement, and approved a $300,000 transfer for an Aviation Asset Defense project, which was then brought back for a motion to reconsider. Closed sessions mentioned City of Pueblo v. Airport litigation and hangar and Skyway lease agreements.

pueblo/7.title: 24-month moratorium ordinance
pueblo/7.summary: Council took first presentation of an ordinance imposing a 24-month moratorium on accepting applications for and issuing certain new licenses. The type of license is not shown in the condensed agenda.

pueblo/8.title: Pueblo Mountain Park and city parks
pueblo/8.summary: Council scheduled a work session on next steps for Pueblo Mountain Park, and a resident spoke about city parks and the park at the October 13 meeting. Elmwood Golf Course concrete improvements were also awarded a $148,337.95 contract.
pueblo/8.where: Pueblo Mountain Park; Elmwood Golf Course

pueblo/9.title: EPA smelter cleanup in Eilers and Bessemer
pueblo/9.summary: An EPA project manager briefed council on Superfund cleanup of former smelter contamination in the Eilers and Bessemer neighborhoods. The public comment period closed October 15 and EPA is preparing a responsiveness summary, with Benedict Park revitalization also discussed.
pueblo/9.where: Eilers and Bessemer neighborhoods; Benedict Park

pueblo/10.title: Library funding mill levy and automated enforcement
pueblo/10.summary: The Library Foundation told council that the library's funding under the 2019 initiative is not a new tax or rate increase. Council also took up an ordinance on automated enforcement in the Police Department and a police staffing amendment.

pueblo/11.title: RTA steering committee and housing authority update
pueblo/11.summary: Council reviewed a draft for forming a Regional Transportation Authority steering committee with voting seats for governments, business and community members, plus technical advisors. It also heard the Housing Authority's 2025 annual report, with 715 public housing units and 1,169 vouchers in use.

rangely/0.title: Geothermal energy campus and proposed data center
rangely/0.summary: Council took up the Energy Campus Development & Municipal Participation Study (stage 2 of Rangely's geothermal development). Residents including Tanner Nielsen and Camille raised concerns about a possible data center, its water use, noise, jobs and secrecy. Tanner asked for a moratorium on data centers, and an NDA ban for public officials was raised in October.

rangely/1.title: Stage 3 water restrictions and White River water supply
rangely/1.summary: Rangely entered Stage 3 water restrictions, and the water conservancy district released 10 cfs from Kenney Reservoir to help; the town later returned to stage 1. Council also considered Resolution 2026-07 declaring a municipal water urgency and authorizing negotiation, but not execution, of a conditional storage agreement for the White River Regional Water Supply Project.

rangely/2.title: 2027 budget and capital projects
rangely/2.summary: Council held budget and capital project work sessions and approved the draft 2027 budget as presented on Oct. 13. A Main Street beautification project was also mentioned during budgeting.

rangely/3.title: Town Manager's outside employment and independent hearing officers
rangely/3.summary: A resident raised concerns about the Town Manager, and council discussed his employment outside the Town. On Oct. 29 council held a special virtual meeting on Resolution 2026-08, creating two to three independent hearing officers to hear employee grievances over discipline and terminations by the Town Manager.

rangely/4.title: Wastewater lagoon liner repairs
rangely/4.summary: Staff reported the lagoon liners at the wastewater plant need repair, with water found underneath the current liner and the other liners also needing replacement. Grants are being sought to help with the expense.

rangely/5.title: Local historic designation for 826 E. Main Street
rangely/5.summary: Council was asked to designate 826 E. Main Street as a local historic property.

rangely/6.title: Bell Street parking and crosswalk safety
rangely/6.summary: Residents and council discussed the Bell Street crosswalk and signs, and a No Parking area near the park was extended by 50 feet. Council member Tim Webber worried about the No Parking zone during events.

rangely/7.title: Asbestos removal project on Birch
rangely/7.summary: An asbestos project on Birch was about to begin, and later additional asbestos was found. The manager said the grant would cover it.

rangely/8.title: Interim Police Chief and police staffing
rangely/8.summary: Joseph McGuire was sworn in as Interim Chief of Police in October. The police department was interviewing for dispatcher positions in November.

rico/0.title: Letter of support for Montelores Bridge restoration trail grant
rico/0.summary: The Dolores Ranger District asked the Town of Rico for a letter of support for its 2027 Colorado Parks and Wildlife Non-Motorized Trail Grant application, seeking about $80,000 to repair the Montelores Bridge. The Forest Service wants letters by September 15, 2026, and the Town's support would be limited to endorsing the project. The Council was set to consider approving the letter on September 2, 2026.

ridgway/0.title: Beaver Creek Diversion Restoration and infiltration gallery
ridgway/0.summary: The town's water diversion project on Beaver Creek ran into design and cost problems. Council raised the RESPEC engineering contract to $657,312 in January and in June awarded the redesigned infiltration gallery to Meridian Contracting for up to $641,386. The project is funded by NRCS and other grants plus a Colorado Water Conservation Board loan, with total cost near $4 million.

ridgway/1.title: Wastewater Treatment Plant renovation and siting
ridgway/1.summary: Council reviewed the needs assessment for renovating the wastewater plant, with a pre-public hearing in May. Siting and treatment options are being discussed in September and at the October budget retreat. A resident urged building the new plant for a 50 to 60 year life.

ridgway/2.title: Housing Action Plan, workforce housing and Proposition 123
ridgway/2.summary: The town drafted a Housing Action Plan required by state law, with goals on workforce housing, ADUs, infill and land banking. The plan is slated for adoption by resolution in October. Council also reviewed regional housing services run by Home Trust of Ouray County, a down payment assistance MOU with the Telluride Foundation, and a Proposition 123 commitment.

ridgway/3.title: 2026 and 2027 town budgets
ridgway/3.summary: Council adopted the 2026 budget and property tax levies in December after workshops, which included a citizen proposal called Keep Ridgway Creative and community grants totaling $98,205. Work on the 2027 budget began with a draft in October and a budget retreat on Oct 31 covering pay, capital projects and nonprofit funding requests.

ridgway/4.title: Water supply planning and water restrictions
ridgway/4.summary: A resident asked how planning accounts for water as the town grows, and staff pointed to a public process on future supply. The town is drafting a Water Supply Element of the Master Plan and modifying its Water Conservation and Management Plan. Council is considering rescinding Stage 2 mandatory water restrictions.

ridgway/5.title: Tourism strategy and loss of lodging to workforce housing
ridgway/5.summary: After the town's lodge was converted to workforce housing, lodging tax and sales tax revenue fell. A Destination Development Mentor Program report and a draft destination marketing plan lay out strategies to address limited lodging.

ridgway/6.title: Wildfire code and fire restrictions
ridgway/6.summary: Council introduced an ordinance adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code with amendments. Later in the year it also acted on Stage 1 and Stage 2 fire restrictions and a disaster declaration support letter.

ridgway/7.title: Vehicle idling ordinance
ridgway/7.summary: Council took up an ordinance to limit vehicle idling in December. In July a resident asked the council to reconsider addressing the proposed idling ordinance.

ridgway/8.title: Riverbend Townhomes and other development applications
ridgway/8.summary: Council is to hear a site plan for Riverbend Townhomes on Liddell Drive, an amended plat in Riverview Business Park, and an earlier amended plat in Northridge Subdivision. Pre-approved accessory dwelling unit designs are also being contracted.
ridgway/8.where: Liddell Drive and Riverview Business Park

ridgway/9.title: Lawsuit over land use code
ridgway/9.summary: Council considered filing a complaint for declaratory and injunctive relief, with discussion of defending the land use code and not setting a precedent.

ridgway/10.title: Council rules of procedure and decorum
ridgway/10.summary: Council discussed adopting formal meeting rules, including public comment limits, keeping comments on topic and managing meeting length. The topic was sent back for future consideration.

ridgway/11.title: Street closures for events and Clinton Street business concerns
ridgway/11.summary: Council approved several street closures for events, including Clinton Street for a filming and Pride. A business owner said he was not notified enough about an upcoming Clinton Street closure and asked for talks with business owners before approvals.

ridgway/12.title: Athletic Park Bike Park and recreation projects
ridgway/12.summary: The Athletic Park Coalition is asking for town funds for professional design of a bike park. Council also is considering a letter of support for a proposed recreation fee.

rifle/0.title: Data center / Bulk Resource Consumer permit rules (Ordinance No. 21)
rifle/0.summary: Rifle is drafting a conditional use permit pathway for data centers and other 'bulk resource consumers' limited to industrial districts, requiring utility, water, noise, fiscal and decommissioning analyses and allowing denial if there is no net public benefit. Planning Commission discussed it in August and September, Council discussed it Oct. 14, and Ordinance No. 21 (Chapter 16 standards) was set for first reading Nov. 4.

rifle/1.title: Draft 2026 Comprehensive Plan
rifle/1.summary: Staff presented a draft update of the 2019 comprehensive plan to the Planning Commission (Oct. 27) and City Council (Nov. 4). The draft projects a need for roughly 1,800 to 2,200 additional housing units over 20 years, and still needs the state-required water supply and strategic growth elements.

rifle/2.title: Municipal code text amendments: warehouses, ADUs, site plans, variances
rifle/2.summary: Staff proposed splitting the warehouse definition into Local and Regional types allowed in light industrial and industrial zones, plus changes to ADU size, height, lot line and variance application rules. The ADU ordinance (No. 20) was on the Nov. 4 Council agenda, and the Planning Commission also took up site plan requirements.

rifle/3.title: Planning Commission hearings on specific properties
rifle/3.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled hearings on a conditional use permit for 799 Buckhorn, a variance for 758 Railroad Ave, a minor subdivision of 1317 E 17th St, and rezone PLN 2026-023 from Tourist.

rifle/4.title: GRIT downtown grants, façade program and wayfinding
rifle/4.summary: The GRIT board handled façade grants funded by lodging tax for ProMex Bakery (233 Railroad Ave) and the Rifle CoWork. The $40,000 program had $18,043.75 left, so the two requests would exceed it by $1,329.88, and members discussed covering the gap from beautification savings. The board also discussed a $40,000 downtown wayfinding contract, a Third Street shade structure estimated at $20,000-$30,000, a participatory budgeting pilot, and the 2027 GRIT budget.
rifle/4.where: Downtown Rifle, Railroad Ave and Third Street

sources.body: Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board
Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board
Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board

rifle/5.title: Centennial Park riparian restoration and RESTORE grant
rifle/5.summary: The city is partnering with the Middle Colorado Watershed Council on a $130,000 federal RESTORE grant application toward construction documents for Centennial Park improvements. The Parks board gave a unanimous letter of support, and Council was to consider applying on Nov. 4. The Parks board also heard about Rifle Creek watershed habitat restoration and Raynard Ditch invasive removal and fire mitigation.

rifle/6.title: Rifle Community Foundation restructuring and grants
rifle/6.summary: After the resignation of board president Kasey Nipsel, the foundation discussed simplifying operations to focus on grant review and recommended that Council restructure it under City administration. It also reviewed about a dozen grant requests, including $30,000 for Discovery Cafe, and a new electronic grant application.

rifle/7.title: Rifle Mountain Park plaque and skate park comment
rifle/7.summary: Parks board considered a request from Jim Bell for a recognition plaque by an apple tree between the ice caves in Rifle Mountain Park, reviewing the city naming policy, and discussed bike racks bought by the Rifle Climbing Coalition. Public comment on the skate park was submitted by email.

rifle/8.title: Roan Plateau natural gas leasing update
rifle/8.summary: Wilderness Workshop was scheduled to give City Council an update on natural gas leasing on the Roan Plateau.

rifle/9.title: Railroad Rehabilitation Project DOLA grant
rifle/9.summary: The Parks board was asked for a letter of support for the city's DOLA EIAF grant application for the Railroad Rehabilitation Project.

routt-county/0.title: Yampa Valley Gravel Pit special use permit (PL20260026)
routt-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission took up the Yampa Valley Gravel Pit special use permit to expand the permit boundary of an old pit on the north side of County Road 65. The commissioners considered it on Sept. 29 with written public comment on file, and on Oct. 13 the Chair was asked to sign the permit. In November the county also approved buying a Connex box for the gravel pit.

routt-county/1.title: 2027 county budget and health insurance costs
routt-county/1.summary: Commissioners held a series of 2027 budget presentations from Public Works, Facilities Management and the District Attorney, and reviewed the proposed budget on Sept. 21 and 22. They also reviewed county dues and outside funding requests, the 2027 health and dental insurance plan, the Tri-County District Attorney budget and the 2025 audit.

routt-county/2.title: Purchase of Development Rights: Nottingham Ranch and Monger Homestead conservation easements
routt-county/2.summary: The commissioners were asked to approve $3,000,000 toward a conservation easement on Nottingham Ranch (PDR Project 222) and $1,200,000 for the Monger Homestead (Project 224). Projects 224 and 225 also went through closed-session Tier reviews.

sources.body: Purchase of Development Rights Board Meetings

routt-county/3.title: Lodging tax advertising and marketing panel setup
routt-county/3.summary: The new Advertising and Marketing Local Tourism Panel is setting up bylaws, conflict-of-interest rules and a grant program for the 10 percent share of lodging tax. About $141,000 in qualifying revenue has been reported so far, and eligibility, matching funds and application cycles are undecided.

sources.body: Advertising and Marketing Local Tourism Panel
Advertising and Marketing Local Tourism Panel

routt-county/4.title: Milner wastewater matter and Sparks Residence wastewater variance
routt-county/4.summary: The commissioners twice heard a Milner wastewater item, with an executive session on a legal or negotiation matter. They also considered a variance request for the wastewater treatment system at the Sparks Residence.

routt-county/5.title: Yampa Valley Housing Authority board and housing bond volume cap
routt-county/5.summary: The commissioners approved delegation agreements and an inducement resolution (2026-062) that let the Yampa Valley Housing Authority use the county's private activity bond volume cap through CHFA. In November they considered applications from 12 candidates for the YVHA board.

routt-county/6.title: Fire restrictions
routt-county/6.summary: The county returned to Stage 1 fire restrictions under Ordinance 2026-001 in early September and rescinded them on Sept. 29.

routt-county/7.title: Yampa Valley Regional Airport terminal expansion grant
routt-county/7.summary: The commissioners approved Amendment 3 to the FAA Airport Improvement Program grant for the West Terminal Expansion. The Airport Commission continued to get capital and budget updates.

routt-county/8.title: Instream flow water rights on Lost Dog Creek and Butcher Creek
routt-county/8.summary: The Colorado Water Conservation Board gave the commissioners a presentation on proposed instream flow water rights on Lost Dog Creek and a second creek. The county also commented on the draft regional 208 water quality management plan.
routt-county/8.where: Lost Dog Creek and Butcher Creek

routt-county/9.title: County Annex HVAC problems
routt-county/9.summary: Facilities staff reported HVAC problems recently found in the Routt County Annex and sought direction on replacing the system.

routt-county/10.title: Historic preservation grants and Certified Local Government status
routt-county/10.summary: The Museum and Heritage board and commissioners reviewed fall capacity-building grants, including $48,500 for a South Routt historic survey, $10,711.55 for the Hayden Heritage Center and $3,646 for Oak Creek and Phippsburg. The Historic Preservation Board worked on a resolution to make the county a Certified Local Government and reviewed a permit for 54200 CR 62.

routt-county/11.title: Sheriff's office and detention center projects
routt-county/11.summary: The commissioners approved a contract for a body scanner and a detention center remodel, agreements with CMC for sheriff training, and a Peace Officer Training and Support Fund resolution.

routt-county/12.title: North Routt recreation strategic plan and trails grant
routt-county/12.summary: The commissioners approved a consultant for the North Routt County recreation strategic plan (RFP 891). They also ratified a letter supporting a Colorado Parks and Wildlife non-motorized trails grant.

rye/0.title: Water treatment plant, water tank and sewer main line projects
rye/0.summary: The December 10, 2025 agenda includes updates on the water treatment plant and main infrastructure, including water tank work, the sewer main line replacement capital project, and brainstorming on removing silt and reeds from the inlet. The agenda gives no outcomes.

rye/1.title: 2026 budget and 2025 supplemental appropriation
rye/1.summary: Council was set to consider a 2025 supplemental budget and appropriation (Resolution 2025-7) and adopt the 2026 budget (Resolution 2025-8) at its December 10, 2025 meeting.

rye/2.title: Intergovernmental agreements with Pueblo County and Colorado City Metro
rye/2.summary: The agenda lists an agreement with Pueblo County on road maintenance and a three-party agreement with Pueblo County and Colorado City Metropolitan District for a satellite office. No terms are given in the agenda.

rye/3.title: Dumpster right-of-way service fees and ordinance violation lien
rye/3.summary: Council's agenda includes dumpster right-of-way service fees and a lien on Account #69 for unpaid 2022 ordinance violation fees.

salida/0.title: 1st & D Space-to-Create affordable workforce housing project
salida/0.summary: Council approved an MOU with Trellis Housing Partners, LLC for an affordable workforce rental project at 233 E. First Street and 102 D Street, with final terms to be settled. A November 2 agenda includes a resolution authorizing the sale of the property at 102 D Street and 233 E. First Street, subject to an upcoming ordinance.
salida/0.where: 233 E. First Street and 102 D Street

salida/1.title: Energy code update (2021 IECC amendments, Ordinance 2026-23)
salida/1.summary: Council passed Ordinance 2026-23 on first reading on August 18, updating the city's adoption of the 2021 International Energy Conservation Code amendments. A September 15 public hearing drew five speakers: Madelyne Felsch, Felicia Houston, Craig Nielson, Alex Buck and Ken Fogle.

salida/2.title: Short-term rental license rules (Ordinance 2026-22)
salida/2.summary: Council held a second reading on changes to short-term rental license use requirements. Paula Givan and Nancy Wallace spoke on the active use requirement; council approved the residency requirement amendment and removed the active use amendment.

salida/3.title: Land Use Code amendments and follow-up work
salida/3.summary: Council held a public hearing on Ordinance 2026-21 amending the Land Use Code (Chapter 16) on August 18, with no comments. The Planning Commission then held a September 28 work session on remaining issues, including separate rules for cottage housing and co-housing, such as the 1,500 sq ft unit cap and one unit per lot.

salida/4.title: Mountain Mail building renovation at 121-129 E. 2nd Street
salida/4.summary: Shavano Holding Co. LLC seeks a Major Certificate of Approval from the Historic Preservation Commission to renovate the old Mountain Mail building. The plan includes a rooftop patio, two upper-floor residences, ground floor retail, two egress windows, and demolition of a deteriorated rear structure.

salida/5.title: 2027 budget and community priorities survey
salida/5.summary: Council discussed the 2027 preliminary budget in October and November, plus a community budget survey. A November 16 agenda pairs continued budget talks with results of the Community Priorities Survey.

salida/6.title: Regional housing collaboration, Proposition 123 and housing needs assessment
salida/6.summary: Council took up an MOU on regional Proposition 123 affordable housing collaboration with Buena Vista, Poncha Springs, Chaffee County and Chaffee Housing Authority. A Regional Housing Needs Assessment and an MOU with the Chaffee Housing Authority were also on the November 2 agenda. Council also approved a Chaffee Housing Trust fee transfer for 8 deed-restricted units in Two Rivers.

salida/7.title: Comprehensive Plan update and water supply and growth elements
salida/7.summary: Council supported a Local Planning Capacity grant application for a 2027 Comprehensive Plan update. The Planning Commission was to discuss Comprehensive Plan amendments for Water Supply and Strategic Growth elements on October 26.

salida/8.title: Regional sustainability program and recycling/waste policies
salida/8.summary: Staff updated council on the grant-funded regional sustainability contractor, covering energy code work, EV readiness, a greenhouse gas inventory and outside funding. Possible future council items include recycling space requirements for multifamily buildings and waste hauler licensing.

salida/9.title: Mesa Tank project award
salida/9.summary: Council moved the Mesa Tank Project award off the consent agenda for separate consideration on October 6. Details of the decision are not in the documents.

salida/10.title: 5-H LLC R-2 zoning question on the November ballot
salida/10.summary: Council adopted a resolution expressing support for the 5-H LLC R-2 zoning question on the November 3, 2026 ballot.

salida/11.title: 610 Walnut Street dangerous building notice
salida/11.summary: Council went into executive session on contracts tied to the Chaffee County Building Safety Department's Notice to Vacate and Notice of Demolition of Dangerous Building at 610 Walnut Street.

san-juan-county/0.title: 2027 Town-County law enforcement contract with the Sheriff
san-juan-county/0.summary: The agenda includes the 2027 contract under which the San Juan County Sheriff patrols the Town of Silverton, enforces town code and investigates traffic accidents, running January 1 to December 31, 2027. The Town's budgeted payment was $340,000 in 2025 (about $31,516 a month) and $31,993 a month in 2026; the contract is dated December 15, 2026.

san-juan-county/1.title: 2027 budgets for the Sheriff, Fire and Rescue Authority and governmental services agreement
san-juan-county/1.summary: The November 12 agenda lists the 2027 San Juan County Sheriff budget, the Silverton San Juan Fire and Rescue Authority budget, the Town-County governmental services agreement, and sales and property tax revenues. Details of decisions are not given in the agenda.

san-juan-county/2.title: Stage Two Fire Ban
san-juan-county/2.summary: The council took up Resolution 2026-07 on a Stage Two fire ban at its June 29 meeting. The agenda does not state the outcome.

san-miguel-county/0.title: Natural resources Land Use Code rewrite: forestry, oil & gas, geothermal
san-miguel-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed new Land Use Code sections on forestry practices (including streamlining wildfire mitigation), oil and gas operations, and deep geothermal operations, with Sheep Mountain Alliance commenting on forestry. The commissioners then scheduled Resolutions 2026-40 through 2026-43 for public hearings on Oct. 21 to adopt the amendments.

san-miguel-county/1.title: Affordable housing code update and employee housing impact fee
san-miguel-county/1.summary: The county is rewriting its Land Use Code to make affordable and workforce housing easier to build, funded by a Prop 123 grant, with stakeholder roundtables on density bonuses, ADUs and a Community Housing Zone. Planning Commission work sessions also looked at the Employee Housing Impact Mitigation Fee, which applies to new construction in the Telluride R-1 school district area.

san-miguel-county/2.title: Mountain Village affordable housing setback variance on County Road 63L
san-miguel-county/2.summary: The Board of Adjustment considered a request from the Town of Mountain Village to cut the setback from the County Road 63L right-of-way from 20 feet to 7 feet on a 56.34-acre Community Housing zoned parcel. The town says this keeps housing farther from the riparian corridor and wetlands, and staff recommended a five-year approval.

san-miguel-county/3.title: Placerville Park rezoning around the fire station
san-miguel-county/3.summary: San Miguel County asked the Planning Commission to recommend rezoning part of Placerville Park around the fire station from Forestry, Agriculture and Open to a Public zone. Telluride Fire Protection District is also giving a project update on Placerville Station 3.

san-miguel-county/4.title: Bridal Veil Falls low water flow and black swifts
san-miguel-county/4.summary: Citizens raised concern that Town diversions dropped flow at Bridal Veil Falls to about 1 CFS versus the 6.5 CFS required, threatening nesting black swifts. The Open Space Commission noted no management prescriptions for minimum flows exist, pointed to the Forest Service and US Fish & Wildlife, and considered it resolved for now as the birds migrate.

san-miguel-county/5.title: County parks and open space projects and new manager
san-miguel-county/5.summary: The Open Space Commission followed Galloping Goose Park (target completion around Oct. 29), Mill Creek Park, Placerville schoolhouse masonry work and the Down Valley park properties, where fire mitigation and a management plan are priorities. New Parks and Open Space Manager J.D. Wise was introduced, and the commission is preparing 2027 priorities and budget cuts.
san-miguel-county/5.where: Galloping Goose Park, Mill Creek Park, Down Valley Park

san-miguel-county/6.title: Noxious weed grant funds and enforcement
san-miguel-county/6.summary: The Noxious Weed Advisory Board discussed how to allocate a $5,800 Colorado Department of Agriculture Noxious Weed Fund grant, with Julie Kolb to draft allocation options. It also discussed enforcement against landowners and 2027 grant outlook, while commissioners set the 2027 Vegetation Control and Management fee schedule.

san-miguel-county/7.title: San Miguel Basin Fair Board budget shortfall and possible separation from county
san-miguel-county/7.summary: The Fair Board reported a $13,000 budget shortfall due to low livestock sale revenue and deferred equipment purchases until the budget balances. County Manager Mike Bordogna raised separating the Fair Board as a nonprofit, and the board discussed 2027 junior livestock sale rule changes.

san-miguel-county/8.title: Highway 145 multimodal improvements and Down Valley planning
san-miguel-county/8.summary: Commissioners followed up on requests to CDOT for multimodal improvements in Sawpit and Placerville, signage at Juniper Village Road, and Norwood Hill rockfall project timing. They also tracked the Down Valley Master Plan RFP and fire mitigation on county-owned Down Valley property.

san-miguel-county/9.title: Telluride Pines water system CDBG application and community funding
san-miguel-county/9.summary: Commissioners considered co-sponsoring a Colorado CDBG Public Facilities application for Telluride Pines HOA to restore safe and reliable water. They also took up 2027 Community Support Funding, including West End Family Link ($12,000) and the Norwood Community Garden.

san-miguel-county/10.title: Gondola replacement cost-sharing agreement for 2027
san-miguel-county/10.summary: The board considered the chair's signature on the fourth supplement to the five-entity intergovernmental agreement sharing the 2027 planning and development budget for the gondola replacement project.

severance/0.title: 2027 budget, property tax levy and fee schedule
severance/0.summary: On Nov. 10 the Town Council was scheduled to hold a public hearing on the Fiscal Year 2027 budget and to act on the 2027 property tax levy and appropriation. The same meeting covered the town fee schedule, water and wastewater rates, an amended Transportation Utility Fee, and a change to development impact fees.

severance/1.title: Water, wastewater and transportation utility rates and impact fees
severance/1.summary: Council was to consider Resolution 2026-38R setting water and wastewater rates and infrastructure investment fees. It was also to consider Resolution 2026-39R amending the Transportation Utility Fee and Ordinance 2026-20 changing development impact fees.

severance/2.title: 2027 Capital Improvement Program
severance/2.summary: Council reviewed the final draft of the 10-year capital plan, of which only 2027 projects get funded in the 2027 budget. New or updated items include a 2036 Police Department addition, more money for water acquisition, and more for Town Park improvements including a restroom. A Town Projects & Budget session was also set for Oct. 13.

severance/3.title: Metropolitan district service plans: Bower North and Northgate Lakes
severance/3.summary: Council scheduled public hearings on Ordinances 2026-11 and 2026-12 to approve consolidated service plans for the Bower North Metropolitan District and the Northgate Lakes Metropolitan District.
severance/3.where: Bower North and Northgate Lakes districts

severance/4.title: Land use code amendments: oil and gas setbacks, setbacks in Town Core, and fast-track amendments
severance/4.summary: The Planning Commission took up several code changes. One aligns oil and gas setbacks with Weld County regulations. Another corrects setbacks in the Town Core and Development Node zones. A third lets Town Council adopt time-sensitive code amendments without a prior Planning Commission recommendation. The Commission also approved procedures for suspending land use applications at an applicant's request and rules on electric service infrastructure for new development, and an early grading permit change followed.

severance/5.title: Comprehensive Plan update
severance/5.summary: The Comprehensive Plan Advisory Committee is reviewing draft chapters, a sample design and an engagement plan and schedule. Feedback from council members stressed small-town and agricultural feel, sales tax generation, economic development and more housing diversity.

severance/6.title: Platte Valley Veterinary Clinic site plan
severance/6.summary: The Planning Commission considered Resolution PC2026-01R approving, with conditions, a site plan for the Platte Valley Veterinary Clinic.

severance/7.title: Community grants: SHS After Prom and Chamber
severance/7.summary: The Citizen Advisory Board approved a $2,000 grant request from Severance High School After Prom for 2027, up from $1,000 in February 2026. The Town Council votes on the funding, and a Severance Chamber grant application was also on the agenda.
severance/7.where: Severance High School, 1200 Hidden Valley Parkway

severance/8.title: Interim town attorney appointment
severance/8.summary: Council was asked to appoint an interim town attorney and approve an amended engagement agreement through Resolution 2026-29R.

severance/9.title: Youth Council projects and Severance Days Teen Day
severance/9.summary: The Youth Council is planning a Teen Day for the 2027 Severance Days and discussing service projects, Senior Prom participation and a suicide awareness walk.

sheridan/0.title: 2027 budget and 2026 budget amendment
sheridan/0.summary: Council and the Redevelopment Agency reviewed 2027 proposed budgets (general fund, capital, open space, stormwater, volunteer fire, Sheridan Celebrates, SRA). Public hearings on Sept. 28 drew no speakers; Ordinances 14-2026 and 15-2026 amending 2026 and adopting 2027 came back for second reading Oct. 12, and the SRA took up Resolutions 4 and 5-2026.

sheridan/1.title: Proposed 0.50% sales and use tax increase referred to voters
sheridan/1.summary: Council considered Ordinance 13-2026 on second reading, referring to city voters a 0.50% increase in the city sales and use tax for public purposes. The documents do not state the outcome.

sheridan/2.title: 2200 W. Radcliff Ave subdivision plats
sheridan/2.summary: Planning Commission and Council held hearings on preliminary and final plats for four industrial parcels at 2200 W. Radcliff Ave (applicant Iron Woman). Platting is required before building permits, no development is proposed, and staff recommended approval with an added 19-foot right-of-way dedication.

sheridan/3.title: 2500 W. Hampden Ave subdivision
sheridan/3.summary: Planning Commission heard preliminary and final plat applications from Garrett Companies for 2500 W. Hampden Ave. Council's Nov. 9 agenda includes the preliminary plat, final plat and a subdivision improvements agreement.

sheridan/4.title: Housing: Sheridan Housing Implementation Plan, ADU rules and Housing Authority
sheridan/4.summary: Staff are updating the ADU code to comply with state legislation (HB24-1152) and will return later in the year. A consultant is presenting final Sheridan Housing Implementation Plan (SHIP) recommendations, and Council work sessions covered the Sheridan Housing Authority.

sheridan/5.title: Brownfields grant, South Santa Fe planning and Flying Saucer RV Park
sheridan/5.summary: Planning staff reported a federal EPA Brownfields Grant award, the renewed South Metro Enterprise Zone, South Santa Fe planning and linkages projects, and a subdivision application for the Flying Saucer RV Park.

sheridan/6.title: Trash and recycling equal space ordinance
sheridan/6.summary: Sustainability Coordinator Mel Englund is expected to introduce a potential equal space ordinance for trash and recycling to the Planning Commission in October.

sheridan/7.title: Crisis services contract, police equipment and opioid settlement
sheridan/7.summary: Council agendas include an agreement with AllHealth Network for crisis services (Res. 28-2026), a police equipment purchase agreement (Res. 29-2026), and approval of Colorado opioid settlements (Res. 34-2026).

sheridan/8.title: Comcast cable franchise and roads concerns
sheridan/8.summary: The City Manager reported that the Comcast cable franchise agreement expired in 2024. A council member said residents raised road concerns, and DRCOG is moving to reduce congestion and expand E-470.

silt/0.title: Request for proposals for Silt Senior Housing property management
silt/0.summary: The Town of Silt is seeking a qualified property management company to manage the Silt Senior Housing property. Companies are invited to review the RFP and submit comments, proposed services and pricing, after which the town would award the contract to the selected company.

silver-cliff/0.title: Workforce housing and IGA with Westcliffe
silver-cliff/0.summary: The Board considered a Workforce Housing intergovernmental agreement with Westcliffe in September and October, with the attorney needing an electronic copy of the draft to adjust it. A multijurisdictional housing authority briefing is set for November 3. Planning Commission also reviewed an affordable housing interior lot line request and site plans for multi-building housing.

silver-cliff/1.title: Park improvements and vacation of streets and alleys at Silver Cliff Community Park
silver-cliff/1.summary: In June the Board reviewed proposals and moved to award the park improvements project covering dirt work, curb and handicap parking at the playground, and pickleball site preparation. A GOCO grant account and park donations fund the work. The Planning Commission took up vacating lot lines at Silver Cliff Park, and the Board set a public hearing on vacating streets and alleys at the park for Dec 3, 2026.

silver-cliff/2.title: Excessive noise ordinance (Ordinance 01-2026)
