silver-cliff/2.summary: Amendment of the town's excessive noise section (Sec. 10-9-30) was tabled in April, then went through second reading and a public hearing for consideration in June.

silver-cliff/3.title: 2027 budget and 2026 budget amendment
silver-cliff/3.summary: The proposed 2027 budget was presented in October with no decisions, and budget workshop dates were to be set. Ordinance 06/2026 amending the 2026 budget is on the November agenda. An Altitude Fitness funding request was deferred to the budget workshop.

silver-cliff/4.title: Title 16 zoning update and Dutch Pantry parking rezoning
silver-cliff/4.summary: The Planning Commission worked on a municipal code and Title 16 zoning update, and the Board held first reading of Ordinance 03-2026 amending Title 16. Matt Hershberger asked to buy land for additional parking for Dutch Pantry, which would need rezoning from R3 to B1.

silver-cliff/5.title: Prop 123 resolution and grants
silver-cliff/5.summary: The Board considered Resolution 06-2026 on Prop 123 housing funds in June. It also accepted a Black Hills Energy grant (Resolution 05-2026) and another grant under Resolution 04-2026.

silver-cliff/6.title: CloudBreak decommissioning bond
silver-cliff/6.summary: The Board considered approving a decommissioning bond for CloudBreak in April.

silver-cliff/7.title: Wildfire resiliency building code mandate
silver-cliff/7.summary: The town attorney briefed the Board on the state's wildfire-urban-interface building code requirements.

silver-cliff/8.title: 2027 Custer County Sheriff agreement and Humane Society contract
silver-cliff/8.summary: The Board is to consider the 2027 IGA with the Custer County Sheriff's Office in November. In October it considered an agreement with Fremont County Humane.

silver-cliff/9.title: Naming the baseball field
silver-cliff/9.summary: A trustee proposed naming the baseball field after a coach; the attorney suggested an ordinance for naming. Consideration is on the November agenda.

silver-plume/0.title: 2027 budget work sessions
silver-plume/0.summary: The budget committee held a third-quarter review of the 2026 general ledger against budget and began work sessions on the 2027 budget, including a line-item breakdown, areas of concern, and a proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 3. A second work session was to be scheduled. Budget updates also appeared on the regular Town Board agendas.

silver-plume/1.title: Camping ordinance public hearing
silver-plume/1.summary: The Town Board scheduled a public hearing on Sept. 14 for second and final reading of Ordinance 359 and a related ordinance regulating camping within Silver Plume town limits.

silver-plume/2.title: 2027 utility rate increase proposal
silver-plume/2.summary: On Nov. 9 the Board was to discuss and decide on a proposed 2027 utility rate increase brought forward by the Budget Committee.

silver-plume/3.title: Taylor Kennedy land purchase wrap-up
silver-plume/3.summary: The Board planned a wrap-up discussion of the Taylor Kennedy land purchase, with special guest Cindy Neely.

silver-plume/4.title: CCFA intergovernmental agreement amendment
silver-plume/4.summary: The Board was set to consider an amendment to the intergovernmental agreement with CCFA on Nov. 9.

silver-plume/5.title: Town shop door replacement quote
silver-plume/5.summary: The Board was to review a quote and decide on replacing the door at the town shop.

snowmass-village/0.title: Ritz Carlton (Viewline/Wildwood) redevelopment sketch plan
snowmass-village/0.summary: Elevate Snowmass LLC proposes a major redevelopment with 167 lodge units, about 125 workforce housing units in the Wildwood area, and a 252-space subgrade garage, requiring a PUD amendment and rezoning. The Planning Commission reviewed it in segments and on Oct. 7 adopted Resolution No. 4 with conditions recommending approval; Town Council takes it up starting Nov. 9 and 16, with a housing review set for Dec. 21 and a draft resolution Jan. 4, 2027. A resident, Alan May, raised concerns about height, massing, traffic, parking and deliveries on Fall Lane, and advisory boards worry about scale.

snowmass-village/1.title: Housing mitigation nexus study and employee housing requirements
snowmass-village/1.summary: The Town raised the developer employee-housing mitigation rate from 60% to 100% and hired EPS to update employee generation rates and fee-in-lieu calculations. Council generally agreed to update rates, add residential remodels as a mitigating activity, and use a fee based on $945/SF, and asked for more information on operations and maintenance rates.

snowmass-village/2.title: Draw Site workforce housing project
snowmass-village/2.summary: Council reviewed next steps as owners for the Draw Site workforce housing project; the 2027 budget includes $76.1 million for construction. Council was to direct staff on next steps on Oct. 19.

snowmass-village/3.title: 2027 Town budget
snowmass-village/3.summary: Staff presented a tight 2027 budget after a low-snow 2026 ski season, with $107.9 million in capital project expenditures. Council reviewed it Oct. 5, 12 and 19 with the Financial Advisory Board and tourism comments, and adoption by resolution was set for Nov. 4. A hearing on the 2027 Road Maintenance Mill Levy expenditures was also on the Nov. 4 agenda.

snowmass-village/4.title: Transit Center project at Snowmass Mall
snowmass-village/4.summary: The Town is weighing a new transit center and RFTA improvements at the Snowmass Mall, with estimates of $42M to $60M. The Part-Time Resident Advisory Board agreed some improvement is needed but questioned the cost, timing given the Ritz redevelopment, and the distribution of funding, and drafted a letter opposing the proposed grand entrance and calling for an alternative.

snowmass-village/5.title: Cavern Springs mobile home park funding and Workforce Housing Advisory Board
snowmass-village/5.summary: Council moved Ordinance 15 appropriating funds for the Cavern Springs Mobile Home Park and Resolution 23 on an IGA, housing covenants and a grant agreement. It also considered Ordinance 16 creating a Workforce Housing Advisory Board.

snowmass-village/6.title: Wildfire mitigation MOU with Roaring Fork Fire Rescue and rebate program
snowmass-village/6.summary: Council considered adopting an MOU with the Roaring Fork Fire Rescue Authority on wildfire mitigation. Separately, the Environmental Advisory Board discussed a wildfire mitigation rebate program to be administered by the RFV Wildfire Collaborative, since the fire authority lacks capacity, and the Town offers a $1,000 fire mitigation rebate.

snowmass-village/7.title: Pesticide use and integrated pest management plan
snowmass-village/7.summary: Council discussed pesticide application, and advisory boards asked for a more detailed noxious weed spraying plan and better signage on trails. The Environmental Advisory Board was to review a draft Integrated Pest Management Plan in November.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board

snowmass-village/8.title: SHOP final plan and PUD amendment
snowmass-village/8.summary: Council heard the SHOP Final Plan and PUD Amendment, with first reading Sept. 8 and second reading of Ordinance 14 on Oct. 5.

snowmass-village/9.title: Workforce housing construction hours regulation
snowmass-village/9.summary: Council discussed current housing regulations and proposed Ordinance 17 on workforce housing hours, with first reading Nov. 4.

snowmass-village/10.title: Rodeo grounds bleachers
snowmass-village/10.summary: Council was to give discussion and direction on the Rodeo Grounds bleachers on Nov. 16.

snowmass-village/11.title: Wood Road lane closure and construction impacts
snowmass-village/11.summary: Part-Time Resident Advisory Board members raised concerns about a single-lane closure on Wood Road for a developer permit, expected to reopen in December, and the idea of time limits and penalties on long building permits.

snowmass-village/12.title: Show cause hearings for delinquent sales tax on liquor licenses
snowmass-village/12.summary: The Liquor Authority scheduled show cause hearings for licensees accused of failing to remit sales taxes to the Town, which could lead to suspension or revocation of licenses.

sources.body: Liquor Authority Hearing & Local Marijuana Licensing Authority Hearing

snowmass-village/13.title: Winter parking plan and playground renovation
snowmass-village/13.summary: Council considered the 2026/2027 Winter Parking Plan. The parks board discussed theming the Town Park playground renovation.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board
Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board

starkville/0.title: FY 2026-27 city budget, 34-mill tax rate and new police positions
starkville/0.summary: The Board approved the proposed 2027 budget items at an Aug. 25 special meeting, including a resolution setting the millage rate at 34 mills, pay adjustments for general fund employees, and Park and Recreation fee increases. It also funded police fleet additions and new positions: a sergeant, a code enforcement officer, an additional officer and a part-time parking enforcement officer. Contributions to the library, JL King Center, community theater, SMART system and animal shelter spay/neuter vouchers were also approved.

starkville/1.title: Electric Department 2% rate increase and pole replacement plan
starkville/1.summary: Staff presented a proposed 2% rate increase across all rate classes starting November 2026, the first since October 2016. It would raise about $650,000 a year and help fund a capital plan including replacing 856 wood poles, LED street lighting, and a grid resiliency grant project, with the proposed FY26-27 budget showing a $375,000 shortfall.

starkville/2.title: Airport runway extension and hangar grants
starkville/2.summary: The Board accepted MDOT matching offers of 2.5% on FAA grants for runway, taxiway and lighting extension work. It later took up change orders and new FAA grant applications for Corporate Hangar #3 and Phase III of the runway and taxiway extension plus overlay.

starkville/3.title: Pafford Emergency Services contract renewal
starkville/3.summary: Pafford Emergency Services representatives presented on renewing their contract with the City at the Aug. 28 work session.

starkville/4.title: Pat Station Road / Highway 12 East residential development variance and special exception
starkville/4.summary: A proposed residential development near Pat Station Road and Highway 12 East needed a building height variance (VA 26-07) and a special exception (SE 26-11). The Board of Adjustments and Planning Commission heard them, and they went to the Board of Aldermen on Nov. 3.
starkville/4.where: Pat Station Road and Highway 12 East

starkville/5.title: Hotel parking exception on Mill Street
starkville/5.summary: The Planning Commission considered special exception SE 26-12 on parking requirements for a proposed hotel on the east side of Mill Street, east of the Cotton Mill Road intersection.
starkville/5.where: Mill Street at Cotton Mill Road

starkville/6.title: Housing special exceptions and rezoning: manufactured home, townhouses, rezoning
starkville/6.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a special exception for a manufactured home west of 1487 Bluefield Road, a townhouse development on a vacant lot at 104 Curtis Circle (SE 26-13), and rezoning request RZ 26-02.

starkville/7.title: Subdivision plats: Sterling Ridge and others
starkville/7.summary: The Board considered a phased preliminary plat for Sterling Ridge at Mockingbird Road and Highway 182, and final plats including Fowler Subdivision, College View #2, Adelaide Phase IIIA and IIIB, and QTRDOG minor subdivision.
starkville/7.where: Mockingbird Rd/Hwy 182; Herbert St; Ryan Ave; E. Gillespie St

starkville/8.title: Highway 12 and Garrard Road roundabout and road projects
starkville/8.summary: The Board approved Neel-Schaffer for engineering and inspection of the Safe Streets for All roundabout at Highway 12 and Garrard Road. It also approved rail spur crossing easements for a Southwire connection to CC Clark Road, and handled streetscape and University Drive work.
starkville/8.where: Highway 12 and Garrard Road; CC Clark Road

starkville/9.title: Henderson Road and Sand Road sewer CDBG project
starkville/9.summary: Golden Triangle Planning and Development was scheduled to brief the Board on a CDBG project to provide sewer for the Henderson Road and Sand Road area, with related agreements on the sewer and lagoon project.

starkville/10.title: Extension of local tourism and beverage taxes
starkville/10.summary: The Board approved a resolution asking the 2027 Mississippi Legislature to extend the economic development, tourism and convention taxes on non-alcoholic beverage gross revenue and the hotel/motel tax.

starkville/11.title: Police sale of abandoned firearms to buy sighting devices
starkville/11.summary: The Board approved the police department converting abandoned property firearms for sale to Southern Connection, the higher of two bids, to buy sighting and light devices.

steamboat-springs/0.title: Slate Creek / Brown Ranch development roadmap and budget
steamboat-springs/0.summary: The Slate Creek Steering Committee met repeatedly in October and November to review the development roadmap, timeline, project scope and budget. The agendas tie the work to the Brown Ranch plan and annexation proposal.

steamboat-springs/1.title: 2027 city budget and two-mill property tax levy
steamboat-springs/1.summary: Council held a budget retreat on Oct 6 and passed the 2027 Budget on first reading Oct 20 by 5/1, with second reading on Nov 10. A two-mill property tax levy ordinance also came up on first reading Nov 10.

steamboat-springs/2.title: Child care centers allowed by right in commercial zones
steamboat-springs/2.summary: A Community Development Code text amendment lets large and small child care centers be built by right in commercial zoning. Planning Commission heard it, Council approved first reading 7/0 on Oct 20, and second reading was set for Nov 10.

steamboat-springs/3.title: The Forge at Burgess Creek preliminary plat
steamboat-springs/3.summary: A preliminary plat and major variance for 2.32 acres of unplatted land in the 1900 block of Burgess Creek Road went to Planning Commission and then to Council for resolution approval on Oct 20.

steamboat-springs/4.title: Terrain at Walton Creek short-term rental overlay zone
steamboat-springs/4.summary: Planning Commission considered a zone map amendment to change the short-term rental overlay zoning at the Terrain at Walton Creek property.

steamboat-springs/5.title: Downtown Plan implementation and parking text amendment
steamboat-springs/5.summary: Planning Commission worked on code changes implementing Downtown Plan goal LUZ 6.3, which would exempt same-grade structured parking from Floor Area Ratio calculations. It was discussed at an Oct 26 work session and a Nov 12 hearing. A Water Supply Element was also presented at the work session.

steamboat-springs/6.title: Base area redevelopment: URA projects and 2027 budget
steamboat-springs/6.summary: The Urban Redevelopment Authority advisory committee and the Redevelopment Authority reviewed Complete Streets Segment 4B Phase II, Mount Werner Road/Circle projects, and the 2027 budget and project activity plan.

steamboat-springs/7.title: Regional transportation sales tax ballot question
steamboat-springs/7.summary: Council considered a resolution supporting the Yampa Valley Regional Transportation Authority ballot question for a one-half percent sales tax.

steamboat-springs/8.title: Golf course 2027 rates and overhead allocation
steamboat-springs/8.summary: The Golf Management Committee discussed allocated overhead and 2027 golf rates.

steamboat-springs/9.title: Public records research and retrieval fees
steamboat-springs/9.summary: Council took up a resolution amending the administrative regulation on research and retrieval fees for public records.

steamboat-springs/10.title: Historic preservation: Rodeo Grounds tax exemption and Crowell-Marshall House
steamboat-springs/10.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission reviewed a sales tax refund certification for rehabilitation at the Rodeo Grounds and a demolition case. Council approved a building permit for the permanent placement of the Crowell-Marshall House.

sterling/0.title: Proposed street improvement sales tax on the November 3 ballot
sterling/0.summary: Council took up Resolution 8-2-26 for a November 3, 2026 election on a 1% sales and use tax. Residents John Tyson and Lee Roth asked for more information, a sunset clause, exceptions, and combining the $400,000 already budgeted for street repair with any new tax money.

sterling/1.title: 2027 budget and property tax levy
sterling/1.summary: Council held a public hearing on the proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 27. On Nov. 10 it considered the resolution adopting the budget and an ordinance setting the property tax levy. A tentative budget workshop was set for Sept. 25.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/10-27-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202610261608010

sterling/2.title: Waterline replacement projects and change orders
sterling/2.summary: Council accepted a bid from Hard Rock Civil for the 2026 Waterline Replacement Project #26-001. It later approved a change order for the North 10th Avenue waterline and one for the 2025 project #25-006. On Nov. 10 it considered an emergency on-call utility contract with Concrete Specialties.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/10-27-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202610261608010

sterling/3.title: Wastewater Treatment Facility Replacement change order
sterling/3.summary: Council considered Resolution 10-7-26 approving Change Order No. 1 and extra contingency funding for the Sterling Wastewater Treatment Facility Replacement Project.

sterling/4.title: Veterinary clinics allowed as conditional use
sterling/4.summary: Ordinance No. 8 amends the zoning code to allow veterinary clinics as a conditional use in a district. It had a public hearing on second reading, and Council discussed adding the use by conditional use application.

sterling/5.title: Rezoning 917 Hamilton Street to Community Business
sterling/5.summary: Ordinance No. 10 rezones 917 Hamilton Street from High Density Residential (R-3) to Community Business (CB). It moved from first reading to a second-reading public hearing, at which no one spoke.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/09-22-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202609211636560

sterling/6.title: Shipping container rules and neighbor complaints
sterling/6.summary: A resident said the new shipping container updates have unintended problems and do not properly address community business zoning. Another resident raised concerns that were not being adequately addressed.

sterling/7.title: Police Department Armory renovation and expansion
sterling/7.summary: Council considered Resolution 9-3-26 approving a professional engineering design services agreement for the Police Department Armory renovation and expansion.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/09-22-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202609211636560

sterling/8.title: Master Plan update and DOLA planning grant
sterling/8.summary: Council authorized a funding request to the Colorado Department of Local Affairs Local Planning Capacity Grant Program to update the city's Master Plan.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/09-22-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202609211636560

sterling/9.title: Hotel tax fund spending for tourism and downtown
sterling/9.summary: Council considered Citizen's Advisory Board recommendations to spend up to $10,000 from the Hotel Tax Fund on an update. It also considered up to $45,000 for lighted holiday garland wraps and storage for West Main Street. Downtown sidewalks were also raised.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/10-27-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202610261608010
http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/09-22-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202609211636560

sterling/10.title: Speeding near Pioneer Park and loud mufflers
sterling/10.summary: A resident near Pioneer Park complained about fast traffic that makes it hard to cross the street and enjoy the park. Another resident reported loud mufflers early morning and late at night, and the city manager will pass it to the police.

sterling/11.title: Municipal court fines and fees
sterling/11.summary: Council planned a work session on court fines and fees after the Aug. 25 meeting.

summit-county/0.title: Quikrete concrete and asphalt batch plant appeal at 28755 State Hwy 9
summit-county/0.summary: The Board of County Commissioners heard an appeal of the Lower Blue Planning Commission decision on PLN26-004, a Class 4 conditional use permit for milling and concrete and asphalt batch plant operations on a 151-acre portion of a 605-acre A-1 parcel. The packet includes public comments, a stormwater plan, a landscape plan and a draft resolution; the documents do not state the outcome.

summit-county/1.title: Verizon wireless facility appeal at 6631 Heeney Road
summit-county/1.summary: The Board took up an appeal of the Planning Commission decision on PLN26-009 and PLN26-010, a Class 4 conditional use permit and site plan for a new Verizon wireless telecommunication facility on Heeney Road (CR 30). Public comments are in the packet along with draft resolutions; the outcome is not stated.

summit-county/2.title: 2027 county budget
summit-county/2.summary: The county presented its 2027 draft budget and held public hearings for comment on it in October and November. Work sessions covered the coroner, human services, Strong Future funds (early childhood, behavioral health, recycling, wildfire) and a Q3 2026 budget amendment.

summit-county/3.title: SCRAP landfill tipping fee increase
summit-county/3.summary: Commissioners considered a new tipping fee schedule for the SCRAP landfill for 2027, based on a rate study. A resolution and fee schedule were in the packet.

summit-county/4.title: Snake River wastewater plant rates and tax lien
summit-county/4.summary: The county reviewed a Snake River wastewater utility rate study in work sessions, with Q&A comparing other agencies' rate factors. The Board also considered certifying indebtedness to the Snake River Sewer Fund for the treatment plant.

summit-county/5.title: Proposition 123 housing credits IGA with Keystone for Soda Creek project
summit-county/5.summary: The Board considered an intergovernmental agreement with the Town of Keystone on allocating Proposition 123 housing credits to the Soda Creek project.

summit-county/6.title: Summit Gulch claims option agreement in Upper Blue Basin
summit-county/6.summary: The Board was asked to approve exercising an option agreement for the Summit Gulch Claims in the Upper Blue Basin.

summit-county/7.title: County Road 506 full maintenance
summit-county/7.summary: The Board considered a resolution on whether the county should take on full maintenance of CR 506 for 2026.

summit-county/8.title: Background checks for massage facility personnel
summit-county/8.summary: Commissioners considered a proposed resolution requiring background checks for massage facility personnel.

summit-county/9.title: Community Services Block Grant needs assessment and Head Start grant
summit-county/9.summary: The Board considered authorizing the Chair to approve the 3-year CSBG community needs assessment and 2027-2029 community action plan, and a Head Start supplemental grant application.

superior/0.title: Marshall Fire Remembrance Project and 5-year anniversary event
superior/0.summary: The Town is designing a Marshall Fire Remembrance (place to gather, pet remembrance, dispersed components) with Davis Partnerships + LandDesign. Council approved an agreement with Colorado Gives Foundation as fiscal partner and a fundraising advisor, Make Philanthropy Work. Louisville is contributing $25,000, and a 5-year anniversary Resilience Celebration is set for Friday, Dec. 18, 6-8pm, to kick off fundraising.

sources.body: Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)

superior/1.title: 2027 Town budget, fee schedule and property tax levy
superior/1.summary: Council held budget review sessions in late August and September, then on Oct. 12 held public hearings and approved the 2027 budget, fee schedule and property tax levy. Related budgets for the Superior/McCaslin Interchange Metro District, Urban Renewal Authority and Metro District No. 1 were also approved. The budget adds a full-time Park Ranger.

superior/2.title: Zaharias property PUD amendment (Rock Creek Ranch)
superior/2.summary: The Planning Commission heard the Twenty-Fifth Amendment to the Rock Creek Ranch Planned Development Plan for the Zaharias property, presented by applicant Garrett Companies, and recommended approval after resident comment. Town Council then held its public hearing on the ordinance on Sept. 14.

superior/3.title: Pirate Park playground redesign
superior/3.summary: PARC and Council received updates on the Pirate Park playground project with Altitude Recreation. Final design milestone was reached in October, and construction is expected to begin in spring 2027.

superior/4.title: McCaslin Boulevard multi-use trail and CPW trail grant
superior/4.summary: The Town is applying for a Colorado Parks and Wildlife non-motorized trail grant to plan a trail segment along McCaslin Blvd from the Water Treatment Plant south. PARC discussed supporting it, and Council approved the grant submission on Oct. 26.

superior/5.title: Coyote Ridge trails and open space management plans
superior/5.summary: Pointe Strategies finished Phase 1 of the Coyote Ridge trail recommendations, and OSAC approved new trail names. The Town is also updating its Prairie Dog Management Plan and Wildfire Mitigation Plan, with grant-funded goat grazing planned from 2027 and a Wildlife Management Plan in progress.
superior/5.where: Coyote Ridge and Town open space

superior/6.title: 88th Street bicycle and pedestrian improvements
superior/6.summary: Council approved an intergovernmental agreement with CDOT for the 88th Street Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvements Project.

superior/7.title: Water supply and waterwise landscaping
superior/7.summary: Council adopted a Waterwise Landscape Transformation Roadmap with a tool to prioritize reducing non-functional turfgrass, and approved an amendment to the Northern Water Southern Water Supply Project allotment.

superior/8.title: Boulder County early childhood care mill levy and child care initiative
superior/8.summary: Council discussed the Boulder County Child Care Investment Initiative and approved a resolution supporting the county's Early Childhood Care and Education mill levy increase ballot measure.

superior/9.title: 2024 International Fire Code adoption
superior/9.summary: Council adopted by reference the 2024 International Fire Code as Ordinance 80 on second reading, after Chief Webb spoke on it; it was continued from an August meeting.

superior/10.title: CAPS public art: ARTery, Circle Park and swing benches
superior/10.summary: The arts committee is extending the ARTery public art path through Circle Park and behind Safeway. It proposed purchasing Noblewins swing benches (about $12,000 each) and art, and took the plan to Council on Oct. 26.

sources.body: Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)

superior/11.title: Proposition 123 housing agreement with Boulder County
superior/11.summary: Council approved an intergovernmental agreement with Boulder County for housing development to implement Proposition 123, and a rebate agreement with the Impact Development Fund.

teller-county/0.title: Cripple Creek & Victor Gold Mine Development Plan Amendment 14
teller-county/0.summary: Staff recommended approval with conditions of Amendment 14 to the Cresson Project mine plan, which covers an employee parking lot along County Road 821 and a temporary access road in Grassy Valley. The state DRMS conditionally approved it Oct. 1, 2025, and county approval is still required. Commissioners discussed it in a work session Oct. 27 and a resolution was on the Nov. 12 agenda; public comment is included in the packet.
teller-county/0.where: Cripple Creek Mining Overlay District, County Road 821

teller-county/1.title: Quantum Tech compliance agreement for revoked permit at 10180 West
teller-county/1.summary: After the Planning Commission revoked Quantum Tech's 1995 conditional use permit for a construction storage yard on May 12, and the Board of Adjustment acted July 9, the county reached a compliance agreement. It gives Quantum 90 days to remove non-permitted operations while keeping office use, and any future use would need a new CUP application. Commissioners ratified it on Sept. 10 agenda.

teller-county/2.title: Short-term rental regulation and tax administration
teller-county/2.summary: The Board took up the second reading of Ordinance #23 regulating short-term rentals in unincorporated Teller County. It also considered ratifying an agreement with Neumo Group, LLC to administer short-term rental taxes and licenses.

teller-county/3.title: 2027 county budget and 2026 budget amendments
teller-county/3.summary: Commissioners held budget work sessions, including capital plan and financial strategic planning, and received the 2027 proposed budget presentation on Oct. 8. They also amended the 2026 General, Jail, Road and Bridge, and Social Services fund budgets, including monthly moves from holding departments as personnel needs change.

teller-county/4.title: Stage II to Stage I fire ban
teller-county/4.summary: With fire season ongoing, the Board considered a resolution moving the county from a Stage II fire ban to a Stage I ban, and ratified it on Sept. 10. Earlier discussion noted Stage II remained in effect and water rights were being called due to low river flows.

teller-county/5.title: Proposed changes to building code and contractor licensing
teller-county/5.summary: A work session on Aug. 25 covered proposed changes to county building code, including contractor license classes, annual fees ($50 to $150) and licensing for septic (OWTS) installers, cleaners and maintenance contractors.

teller-county/6.title: Jail underground repair contract increase
teller-county/6.summary: A change order raised the Mid-Colorado Construction contract for jail underground repair investigation and logistics from a not-to-exceed $40,000 to $100,000 and extended it to June 30, 2027. The Board considered ratifying it Oct. 8.

teller-county/7.title: Pinestone Ranch project and Rosemont Reservoir variance
teller-county/7.summary: Palmer Land Trust was scheduled to discuss the Pinestone Ranch project with commissioners on Oct. 13. A separate board also discussed a variance for Rosemont Reservoir.

teller-county/8.title: Public health programs and grants
teller-county/8.summary: The Board of Health discussed rising suicides among men ages 45-65, the Rural Health Transformation Grant, a non-emergent oxygen program with five emergency oxygen units, and reflective address signs funded by grants. It also discussed childcare facility permits and the new Tamale Act.

telluride/0.title: Carhenge Redevelopment Project review
telluride/0.summary: The Historic & Architectural Review Commission has three Preliminary Large-Scale applications for the Carhenge site (Buildings A–C, D1–D2, E1–E3), after earlier continuances from July and August 2026. Town Council also considered a resolution on a preliminary large-scale subdivision consolidating Lots 34 and 34B, Backman Village Subdivision.
telluride/0.where: Lots 34 and 34B, Backman Village Subdivision (Carhenge lot)

telluride/1.title: Telluride Housing Authority waitlist policy and rental housing rules
telluride/1.summary: The Housing Authority and its subcommittee are reworking the employee rental housing waitlist rules (§105 and 106.1) after a recent suspension of the waitlist. They are also considering bedroom-size exceptions for households, a partial 2027 rental rate increase, and a policy on primary residency for children of multiple custodial parents (adopted with amendments: 20% cutoff, through age 18).

telluride/2.title: Deed restriction amendments for Fino affordable units
telluride/2.summary: The Housing Authority considered a resolution to amend deed restrictions on Town-built affordable units at 215 East Colorado Avenue (Units 1A and others). Staff described it as a last-resort request to amend the contract, not an exception, and the Town Council was also to consider authorizing it.

telluride/3.title: 2027 budget, real estate transfer tax suspension and grant funding
telluride/3.summary: Town Council took up first reading of an ordinance suspending a portion of Real Estate Transfer Tax revenue handling for the 2027 budget year. The Open Space Commission discussed the 2027 budget with the Town Manager, and the community grants commission sent Council a letter on its 2027 grant budget request.

sources.body: Commission for Community Assistance, Arts & Special Events

telluride/4.title: Gondola replacement project funding
telluride/4.summary: Town Council and the regional transportation authority (SMART) are considering the 2027 amendment to the gondola project development cost-sharing agreement for the Gondola Replacement Project, with project updates at each meeting.

sources.body: San Miguel Authority for Regional Transportation
San Miguel Authority for Regional Transportation

telluride/5.title: Ban on fuel-burning landscape equipment
telluride/5.summary: The Ecology Commission is discussing a draft ordinance banning combustion lawn and garden equipment, a step called for in the 2022 Climate Action Plan. Staff will connect the commission with Town staff who operate such equipment to gather feedback before recommendations go to Council.

telluride/6.title: 2027 Climate Action Plan update
telluride/6.summary: The Ecology Commission is reviewing the 2022 Climate Action Plan one focus area at a time, including materials, community resilience, municipal operations and buildings, to recommend its required five-year update. Town Council will also consider updates to the Telluride Energy Mitigation Program.

telluride/7.title: Ethics complaint and a Code of Conduct for Council
telluride/7.summary: After the Ethics Commission considered a complaint against a councilmember's conduct during a public meeting, it is weighing a recommendation to Town Council on a Code of Conduct. Options include building it into the Ethics Code or a stand-alone code with penalties like removal from boards.

telluride/8.title: Town Park campground and shower fees for 2027
telluride/8.summary: The Parks & Recreation Commission considered 2027 campground fee increases of $2–$5 a night, averaging about 8%, projected to raise $203,304, and shower fees projected to raise $62,500 (up 25%). It also discussed the 5-year capital improvement fund and Town Park Oval improvements.

telluride/9.title: Valley Floor goat grazing pilot and winter use plan
telluride/9.summary: A resident wrote to the Open Space Commission asking for results, costs and future of the Valley Floor goat grazing pilot. The commission also reviewed the 2026/27 Winter Use Operational Plan covering grooming, trails and signage.

telluride/10.title: Two-night concert proposed for Town Park
telluride/10.summary: Town Council discussed a proposed major two-night concert in Town Park, alongside a review of 2026 special events on Town property.

telluride/11.title: Historic review of individual projects and parking payment-in-lieu
telluride/11.summary: The Historic & Architectural Review Commission has items including 448 Tomboy Road, 785 Primrose, 214 S Fir, and a payment-in-lieu of parking for one space at 510 W Columbia/129 N Townsend, which also has a minor subdivision to vacate an internal lot line. Council also had an appeal on the Stender Residence on North Aspen Street.
telluride/11.where: 510 W Columbia Ave; 448 Tomboy Rd; 785 Primrose

thornton/0.title: Data center moratorium discussions
thornton/0.summary: City Council discussed a possible data center moratorium at the Aug. 25 council update and again at the Sept. 1 planning session, with a data center presentation each time. The documents do not state a decision.

thornton/1.title: 2027 city budget, pay plans and tax levy
thornton/1.summary: Council reviewed the preliminary 2027 budget recommendation in September. On Oct. 27 it held a public hearing on adopting the 2027 budget, the appropriations ordinance, the Career Service and Excluded pay plans, and the first reading of the property tax levy. Companion budgets for TASHCO, the Thornton Development Authority, the 136th Avenue GID and E911 were also on the Oct. 27 agendas.

thornton/2.title: 2027 water, sewer and stormwater rate increases
thornton/2.summary: Council reviewed proposed 2027 utility rate and fee adjustments for the Water, Sewer and Stormwater funds, effective Jan. 1, 2027. The Old Hire Fire Pension Board also asked that a cost-of-living adjustment be included in the 2027 budget.

thornton/3.title: Creekside Gardens Annexation at East 140th Avenue and Washington Street
thornton/3.summary: Council held a public hearing on Aug. 25 on annexing about 26 acres at the southwest corner of East 140th Avenue and Washington Street, with zoning and a conceptual site plan. The annexation and zoning ordinances were on the Sept. 8 agenda for second reading, and the land would be assigned to Ward 4.
thornton/3.where: Southwest corner of East 140th Avenue and Washington Street

thornton/4.title: Bellflower Annexation near East 140th Avenue and Holly Street
thornton/4.summary: The Planning Commission considered annexation, zoning and a conceptual site plan for a residential development on about 39 acres near East 140th Avenue and Holly Street on Oct. 20. Council scheduled a public hearing on the annexation, zoning and site plan for Nov. 10, with the land assigned to Ward 3.
thornton/4.where: North of East 140th Avenue and east of Holly Street

thornton/5.title: Welby Station rezoning at East 88th Avenue and Welby Road
thornton/5.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on Sept. 15 on rezoning about 55 acres at the northeast and northwest corners of East 88th Avenue and Welby Road. Council took up the zoning ordinance in a public hearing on Oct. 13.

thornton/6.title: Parks and Recreation Master Plan and Arts and Culture Master Plan
thornton/6.summary: Council reviewed the 2026 Parks, Recreation & Community Programs Master Plan and the Arts and Culture Master Plan 2026-2030 on Sept. 8. A resolution adopting the Parks and Recreation Master Plan was on the Sept. 22 council agenda.

thornton/7.title: Small-lot housing and residential design standards
thornton/7.summary: Council held a planning session discussion on residential housing and design standards, including small-lot housing. Planning Commission also took up housekeeping amendments to the development code in October.

thornton/8.title: Parterre subdivision legal strategy
thornton/8.summary: Council went into executive session on Sept. 8 for legal advice and negotiator instructions about the development of the Parterre subdivision. No outcome is stated.

thornton/9.title: Interim City Attorney and City Attorney recruitment
thornton/9.summary: Council interviewed internal candidates for Interim City Attorney and discussed a potential employment agreement in August. In October it met in executive session on selecting a vendor for the City Attorney recruitment and on performance of the Municipal Judge, Interim City Attorney and City Manager.

thornton/10.title: Redevelopment Request for Qualifications negotiations
thornton/10.summary: Council held executive sessions on Sept. 22 and Sept. 29 to set negotiating strategy on respondents to a Request for Qualifications for a redevelopment project. The documents do not name the site.

thornton/11.title: Marijuana licensing code amendments
thornton/11.summary: Council reviewed draft amendments to the city's marijuana licensing code at an Oct. 27 council update.

thornton/12.title: Public hearing conduct and security at council meetings
thornton/12.summary: On Oct. 13 Council went into executive session for legal advice on speakers' constitutional rights and maintaining order during public hearings, and on security arrangements.

thornton/13.title: Station area plans and E-470 presentation
thornton/13.summary: Council discussed visioning for the York at 144th and North Thornton at Colorado 7 station areas and heard an E-470 Public Highway Authority presentation. The STAMP plan was also updated to the BTAC advisory group.
thornton/13.where: York St/144th Ave and Colorado 7 station areas

thornton/14.title: Annexation plan for land in Adams and Weld Counties
thornton/14.summary: On Oct. 13 Council considered a resolution designating a plan under the Municipal Annexation Act for land in Adams and Weld Counties.

thornton/15.title: Liquor license hearings: Waldo's Chicken and Beer, Paddock Lounge, Love Sushi, and event permit
thornton/15.summary: The Local Licensing Authority held hearings on new licenses for Waldo's Chicken and Beer (9675 Washington St), Paddock Lounge (16059 Grant St) and Love Sushi (9740 Grant St). It also heard a special events permit for First Street Plaza at Eastlake N-Line Station, where residents spoke in opposition.
thornton/15.where: Washington St, Grant St, First Street Plaza

timnath/0.title: 2027 Town budget and 2026 budget amendment
timnath/0.summary: Council held 2027 budget work sessions on Oct. 13 and 27, reviewing the draft budget, five-year capital plan and strategic plan allocations. On Nov. 10 it held first reading of the 2027 budget ordinance (No. 19) and a 2026 budget amendment (No. 20), with public hearings set for Dec. 8, 2026.

timnath/1.title: Peanut Park (Timnath Ranch North Park) master plan and funding
timnath/1.summary: The Parks committee reviewed master planning for Peanut Park, including a resident poll on amenities and drainage and size challenges. The five-year capital plan includes $6 million for the park next year, not guaranteed until the budget is approved, so the work will likely be phased. A resident asked Council for a public timeline, funding plan and geographic equity for northern Timnath parks.
timnath/1.where: Peanut Park / Timnath Ranch North Park

timnath/2.title: Timnath Landing GID bond issuance
timnath/2.summary: The Timnath Landing General Improvement District board took first reading of an ordinance authorizing Series 2026A and subordinate 2026B limited tax general obligation bonds to fund public improvements and reimburse the developer and Town. The ordinance re-authorizes one approved in December 2025; the public hearing was set for Oct. 27, 2026. The board also accepted the 2025 audit.

sources.body: Timnath Landing General Improvement District Board
Timnath Landing General Improvement District Board

timnath/3.title: Costco fuel facility expansion
timnath/3.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a site plan to expand the Costco fuel canopy at 4665 Weitzel Street from about 3,884 to 10,216 square feet and double fueling positions from 16 to 32. Discussion focused on traffic circulation and a median extension to remove unsafe southbound movements; staff recommended approval with standard conditions.

timnath/4.title: Draft Comprehensive Plan and Land Use Code amendments
timnath/4.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the working draft of the Timnath Comprehensive Plan. It was also updated on Council decisions on Land Use Code changes covering wastewater and graywater, Larimer County flood maps, neighborhood meeting notices, subdivision procedures, plats and fencing materials.

timnath/5.title: Recreation Center design and Community Park projects
timnath/5.summary: The Rec Center project finished schematic design and is being reviewed with Adolfson & Peterson Construction and a third-party architect before moving into design development. The Community Park entrance project is nearly complete, with flood irrigation removed to save water, and a kayak kiosk was installed in April.

timnath/6.title: Roads and roundabout concerns near Harmony Road and Parkway
timnath/6.summary: Residents spoke at the Nov. 10 Council meeting about a project near Harmony Road and Weld County Road 15, road construction in front of the community, and opposition to a roundabout on the Parkway.
timnath/6.where: Harmony Road / Weld County Road 15 / Parkway

timnath/7.title: Town compensation study
timnath/7.summary: A work session on Aug. 25 covered a compensation study meant to help the Town attract and retain staff. Staff plan to incorporate the recommendations into the budget.

washington-county/0.title: Landfill resolution (Resolution 34-2026)
washington-county/0.summary: The board scheduled a 2:30 landfill resolution on Aug. 18 and took up Resolution 34-2026 on the landfill on Sept. 1. A landfill capital purchase also came up Aug. 25. The documents do not state the outcome.

washington-county/1.title: Wind moratorium extension (Resolution 49-2026)
washington-county/1.summary: The board considered extending the county's moratorium on wind development through Resolution 49-2026 on Sept. 29. The documents do not state the outcome.

washington-county/2.title: RAISE grant request for proposals and bids
washington-county/2.summary: The county drafted an RFP for a RAISE grant and later opened and discussed bids on Oct. 6 and Oct. 20. On Nov. 3 SEH presented on the RAISE grant bid.

washington-county/3.title: Comprehensive Plan consultant selection
washington-county/3.summary: The county drafted an RFP for a new comprehensive plan from August onward, opened bids Oct. 27, discussed the plan Nov. 3, and had a comprehensive plan contract on the Nov. 10 agenda.

washington-county/4.title: County clinic roof and clinic bids
washington-county/4.summary: The board approved an APEX agreement for the clinic roof on its Aug. 25 agenda, then opened clinic bids Oct. 6 and Oct. 20. Clinic bids were discussed again Oct. 27, Nov. 3 and Nov. 10.

washington-county/5.title: 2027 health benefits and health pool rates
washington-county/5.summary: The board reviewed 2027 health pool rates on Sept. 22 and took up Resolution 50-2026 on 2027 health benefits repeatedly from Sept. 29 through Oct. 27.

washington-county/6.title: PILT agreement and conflict waiver
washington-county/6.summary: The board discussed a conflict waiver and a PILT (payment in lieu of taxes) agreement on Oct. 13, and the PILT agreement again Oct. 20 and Nov. 3.

washington-county/7.title: Budget review sessions
washington-county/7.summary: The board scheduled departmental budget review sessions on Nov. 3 and Nov. 10.

washington-county/8.title: Courthouse and EMS building surveillance system
washington-county/8.summary: The board reviewed proposals for a surveillance system for the courthouse and EMS building on Aug. 18 for discussion and decision. A CamNet service contract followed on Sept. 8.

washington-county/9.title: Fiber/telecom agreements with Level 3 and Williams Communications
washington-county/9.summary: The board took up Resolutions 52-2026 and 53-2026 for Level 3 Communications and Williams Communications on Oct. 20. A railroad letter was also on the Aug. 18 agenda.

washington-county/10.title: Planning and zoning fee schedule (Resolution 48-2026)
washington-county/10.summary: The board considered a new Washington County fee schedule for planning and zoning on Sept. 1.

weld-county/0.title: Weld County Justice Center project and jail upgrades
weld-county/0.summary: The county is building a new Justice Center on Block 66. It approved a construction manager/general contractor bid in September, signed an agreement with J.E. Dunn Construction Group in October, and handled a stormwater agreement, parking garage plan review, and a temporary parking lot. Separate bids cover jail pod renovations, lighting, and shower replacements.

weld-county/1.title: Emergency Ordinance 264 lease-purchase financing
weld-county/1.summary: The commissioners took up Emergency Ordinance No. 264 on Nov. 2 and again on Nov. 4. It authorizes a ground and improvement lease, a lease purchase agreement and related financing documents. The summaries do not state the outcome.

weld-county/2.title: 2027 county budget and annual fee changes
weld-county/2.summary: Ordinance #263 to adopt the county budget had its first reading Nov. 9. A code ordinance updating annual fees (2026-09) also had a first reading, and an ordinance on liquor code updates, dance licenses and fees (2026-19) moved from first to second reading.

weld-county/3.title: Weld County Code rewrite: zoning, cisterns and right-of-way permits
weld-county/3.summary: Code Ordinance 2026-04 rewriting the administration, areas of state interest and zoning chapters had its final reading Aug. 24. Ordinances 2026-12 (cistern usage permit criteria) and 2026-13 (right-of-way use permits) went through three readings, ending Oct. 26. More code ordinances (2026-20, 2026-21) began in November.

weld-county/4.title: BURNCO gravel mining permit amendment near Greeley
weld-county/4.summary: The commissioners heard a first major amended Use by Special Review permit for BURNCO Colorado and the Groundwater Management Subdistrict's water activity enterprise on Aug. 19. The approval item came up on Aug. 24 and the hearing certificates on Sept. 2.
weld-county/4.where: North of County Road 58, near Weld County Parkway and County Road 49

weld-county/5.title: Rule Farm Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3 service plan
weld-county/5.summary: The county accepted the service plan filing for the proposed Rule Farm Metropolitan Districts on Aug. 26. It went to hearing Sept. 23 and was approved by resolution Sept. 30.
weld-county/5.where: North of County Road 2, east of County Road 21

weld-county/6.title: Solar farms and Latham annexation deed
weld-county/6.summary: The board heard Use by Special Review permits for two solar energy facilities, one on County Road 35 near AA Street (Chickadee Solar) and one on County Road 46, on Oct. 21. In September it also took up a quit claim deed tied to the Latham Solar Farm annexations.

weld-county/7.title: Oil and gas leases, 1041 permits and the Oil and Gas Department
weld-county/7.summary: The county auctioned and approved a large-tract oil and gas lease of 40.685 acres in August. It extended three more leases in September and signed road maintenance agreements for two Noble Energy 1041 WOGLA permits. On Sept. 30 it considered dissolving the Weld County Department of Oil and Gas Energy, and on Nov. 2 it hired a backup hearing officer for 1041 permits.

weld-county/8.title: Housing Choice Voucher transfer to Greeley Housing Authority
weld-county/8.summary: The commissioners, sitting as the Housing Authority Board, considered voluntarily transferring the county's Housing Choice Voucher program to the Housing Authority of the City of Greeley. It was brought up Aug. 24 and approved by resolution Aug. 26.

weld-county/9.title: Road projects: roundabouts, signals and bridges
weld-county/9.summary: The county is buying right-of-way and easements for roundabouts at County Roads 74/31 and 13/50. It is installing streetlights, a traffic signal at State Highway 52 and CR 37, and improvements at SH 392 and CR 35. It also applied for a bridge replacement grant and awarded a Bridge 19/46.5A contract, and approved many temporary road closures.

weld-county/10.title: Pawnee Grasslands FLAP grant and Weld County airport grants
weld-county/10.summary: The county considered a Federal Lands Access Program grant application for safety and experience on Pawnee Grasslands. It also considered an airport improvement grant for taxiway extension and runway rehabilitation.

weld-county/11.title: Dispatch agreements and law enforcement agreements
weld-county/11.summary: The county signed public safety communications dispatch services agreements with Eaton, Greeley, Johnstown, Mead and Windsor, plus Ault police and the Briggsdale and Fort Lupton fire districts. It also approved a Justice Assistance Grant MOU and a Kersey police agreement.

weld-county/12.title: Show cause hearings on permit compliance
weld-county/12.summary: The board held show cause hearings on whether permittees comply with permit standards: a mineral resource permit (PCSC26-0007) on Sept. 2 and a water skiing facility permit (PCSC23-0011) on Oct. 7. A probable cause hearing on PCSC21-0008 was also scheduled Oct. 21.

weld-county/13.title: Elections: Amendment 83 resolution and coordinated election agreements
weld-county/13.summary: The board considered a resolution supporting Amendment 83 and set up an intergovernmental agreement with Firestone for coordinated elections. It also amended a voting system agreement and set a fiscal agent for state election grant funds.

wellington/0.title: Flock license plate reader cameras and the Larimer County Sheriff's contract
wellington/0.summary: The Larimer County Sheriff presented on Flock automated license plate reader cameras at five Wellington locations, including Highway 1/CR 9 and 6th Street/Cleveland Avenue. The Sheriff's Office did not win the grant it sought, and $17,000 was set aside in the 2026 budget. A resident thanked the Board for asking to remove ALPR items from the 2027 budget, which was reviewed with dispatch services.

wellington/1.title: FY2027 budget, property tax levy and sewer fund loan
wellington/1.summary: Staff presented the 2027 budget with department cuts, delayed capital projects and a proposed $2,000,000 loan from the General Fund to the Sewer Fund to delay a sewer rate adjustment. A budget workday was held Oct 2, and a hearing on the budget, 2026 property tax levy and appropriations was set for Nov 10.

wellington/2.title: North Poudre Irrigation Company water agreements and water master plan
wellington/2.summary: The Board approved a new water supply agreement with North Poudre Irrigation Company replacing the 1983 agreement, with step-down payments in the first four years and the ability to store or convey future water. It also approved a storage and carriage operations agreement and adopted the 2025-2026 Water Distribution System Master Plan.

wellington/3.title: Cleveland Avenue downtown construction project
wellington/3.summary: The Board got an update on the Cleveland Avenue project, aimed at better lighting, more on-street parking and new storm drainage on Cleveland Avenue and 5th Street. Coulson Excavating is the contractor; $1.8M and $1.35M grants must be spent by 12/31/2026. Crews have dealt with waterline lowerings and sewer service conflicts.

wellington/4.title: Metropolitan district model service plan and review policy
wellington/4.summary: The Board held work sessions on a model service plan and review criteria for metropolitan district proposals, including what counts as sufficient public benefit, mill levy limits (a 60-mill combined cap was discussed) and consolidation of districts.

wellington/5.title: Housing needs assessment and affordable housing
wellington/5.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed and moved toward accepting the Housing Needs & Affordability Assessment, which identifies housing gaps. NoCo Foundation spoke to the Board about housing needs, and the Board adopted an economic development incentive policy that touches affordable housing.

wellington/6.title: Comprehensive Plan water supply and strategic growth elements
wellington/6.summary: To comply with state SB24-174, the Town is adding Water Supply and Strategic Growth elements to its Comprehensive Plan with consultant Logan Simpson, discussed by the Planning Commission and Board of Trustees in November.

wellington/7.title: Floodplain code amendments
wellington/7.summary: The Planning Commission recommended and the Board approved Ordinance 13-2026 amending the floodplain rules to align with a FEMA model ordinance and updated flood maps, which moved some property owners into the floodplain. No public comment was given.

wellington/8.title: Building and fire code update
wellington/8.summary: The Board adopted Ordinance 11-2026 updating the building, residential and fire codes to align with the Wellington Fire Protection District's 2024 fire code and including electric-ready and solar-ready provisions.

wellington/9.title: PROST master plan, community center study and park improvements
wellington/9.summary: The parks board toured east side parks (Sunrise, Park Meadows, Wellville), discussed signage, a veterans garden, and implementation of the PROST Master Plan and Community Center Feasibility Study. A Girl Scout proposed an ADA-accessible playground at Sunrise Park.
wellington/9.where: Sunrise Park, Park Meadows, Wellville Park, Centennial Park

sources.body: Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board
Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board

wellington/10.title: Xcel Energy wildfire power shutoffs
wellington/10.summary: Xcel presented on Public Safety Power Shutoffs and wildfire mitigation, noting undergrounding plans; the Board asked about the town's water and wastewater plants as critical facilities.

wellington/11.title: Water Treatment Plant administration and lab building contract
wellington/11.summary: The Board was scheduled on Nov 10 to consider awarding the construction contract for the Water Treatment Plant Administration and Lab Building.

westcliffe/0.title: Data center moratorium (Ordinance 2-2026)
westcliffe/0.summary: After a June discussion of data centers straining the electrical grid and water supply, the Town drafted a moratorium. First reading was July 21, and the Council approved Ordinance 2-2026 on Aug. 18 as an emergency ordinance, effective immediately. No one spoke at the public hearing.

westcliffe/1.title: Main Street parking, safety and crosswalk
westcliffe/1.summary: The Mayor raised closing Main Street between 2nd and 3rd in summers because of over-length vehicles and people crossing outside crosswalks. A workshop is planned. The Town bought two signs (up to $1,000) for the Rosita Street lot and approved a temporary painted crosswalk near 104 Main St. A permanent crosswalk is to be budgeted next year. A stop sign at Main and Adams Blvd is also on the October agenda.
westcliffe/1.where: Main Street between 2nd and 3rd Streets; Rosita lot; Main St. and Adams Blvd

westcliffe/2.title: Prop 123 affordable housing, Housing Needs Assessment and IGA with Silver Cliff
westcliffe/2.summary: The Town considered the final Housing Needs Assessment. It approved an intergovernmental agreement with Silver Cliff on Prop 123 so Westcliffe can count some of Silver Cliff's affordable housing numbers, since it missed the three-year requirement. Residents asked numerous questions about the Prop 123 grant in September, and a Custer County workforce housing report is on the October agenda.

westcliffe/3.title: Water/sewer expansion south of town and reservoir project
westcliffe/3.summary: The Council approved a public statement for trustees and staff to use when residents ask about the water/sewer expansion south of town. It says the project improves the chance private lots get built on. In August the reservoir project was awarded to Mountain Valley Excavation, starting in September with completion hoped by May. The wastewater pilot study was 70% complete.

westcliffe/4.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code rejected and wildfire plan adopted
westcliffe/4.summary: The Council adopted the Custer County Community Wildfire Protection Plan in January, replacing a 2007 plan. In March it denied Ordinance 1-2026 adopting the state Wildfire Resiliency Code. The Fire Department, Silver Cliff and the County had not adopted it, and the attorney noted possible insurance and permitting risks.

westcliffe/5.title: Park shade structures instead of tree planting amid drought
westcliffe/5.summary: Because of drought and water shortage concerns, the Council dropped 2026 tree planting. It approved up to $40,000 for shade structures of about $3,000-$4,000 each. Bids for Memorial Park structures were moving forward in August.

westcliffe/6.title: Overnight camping ordinance update
westcliffe/6.summary: A trustee wants to revamp the Town camping ordinance to match Silver Cliff's, citing more overnight camping linked to rising homelessness. The current ordinance refers only to parks.

westcliffe/7.title: Tourism funding: Highway 69 welcome signs and holiday decor
westcliffe/7.summary: The Council gave $5,000 for Highway 69 welcome signs to get travelers to stop in town, with Mr. Shy opposed and approval contingent on the auditor. It also gave $3,500 for the holiday wreath contest and business holiday decor. The attorney said a statutory town cannot donate to the Altitude Fitness pool resurfacing and it must go through the grant process.

westcliffe/8.title: 2026 budget and mill levy
westcliffe/8.summary: After a public hearing with no comment, the Council approved the 2026 budget, appropriation and mill levy ordinances (5, 6 and 7-2025) in one motion on Dec. 9. A 2027 budget workshop was set for Aug. 28.

westcliffe/9.title: Façade Grant program
westcliffe/9.summary: The Council approved 2026 Façade Grant awards, cutting the Wildflower Hotel's award to $3,542. It rewrote application rules: reimbursement only, in-town business license, brick-and-mortar, and signs capped at $1,000. It also let a 2025 recipient finish work past the deadline.

westcliffe/10.title: Street sweeper purchase and town truck replacement
westcliffe/10.summary: The Council approved buying a street sweeper after a trial period, with discussion of renting it to businesses. Earlier the public works lead sought to buy a truck to replace aging Town trucks.

westcliffe/11.title: Farmer's Market at Jess Price Park and Bluff Park observatory hours
westcliffe/11.summary: The Council approved Resolution 4-2025 supporting the Farmer's Market on Town land at Jess Price Park, drafted as a resolution to avoid creating a leasehold. It also approved an MOU for extended Bluff Park hours at the Smokey Jack Observatory.

westminster/0.title: Data center regulation and neighboring-jurisdiction proposals
westminster/0.summary: After Council adopted Resolution No. 20 on July 27, 2026 supporting a zoning interpretation that data centers are a prohibited land use, it held an October 19 study session on strengthening Unified Development Code language. Council also discussed concerns about data centers proposed just outside city limits, including water use and extraterritorial utility service.

westminster/1.title: Automated license plate readers (Flock cameras) discontinuation
westminster/1.summary: Police presented on automated license plate readers at an October 5 study session. On October 26 Council considered Resolution No. 46 discontinuing the technology, and residents including Jessica Johnson spoke against Flock cameras, citing data retention, cybersecurity and privacy.

westminster/2.title: Proposed 2027 budget
westminster/2.summary: Staff presented the proposed 2027 budget, held a public hearing on September 14, and Council gave feedback at a September 21 study session. Charter requires adoption by October 26, and second readings were scheduled for that date. Related 2027 budgets for the Economic Development Authority and General Improvement Districts were heard October 12.

westminster/3.title: Affordable housing density bonus, down payment assistance and Prop 123
westminster/3.summary: Council took up a density bonus and revised affordable housing definition with a parking provision (Councillor's Bills 39 and 36), a proposed Down Payment Assistance Program offering up to 20 percent of purchase price, Housing LIFT agreements, and Proposition 123 expedited review policies. Rights of first refusal for multifamily housing were also assigned to regional housing partners.

westminster/4.title: Event center moratorium and ordinance
westminster/4.summary: Council enacted a six-month moratorium on new event centers in multi-tenant commercial developments or within 300 feet of residential areas due to impacts on public safety, water and sewer, parking and neighboring uses. Staff presented revised recommendations for Councillor's Bill No. 19 on October 5 after engaging operators.

westminster/5.title: Stormwater, water, sewer rate and fee changes
westminster/5.summary: Council held a hearing on 2027 and 2028 stormwater fee changes and considered ordinances implementing water, sewer and reclaimed water rates and stormwater fees (Councillor's Bills 40 and 43).

westminster/6.title: Homelessness response and Navigation Center agreements
westminster/6.summary: Council received a homelessness update and approved intergovernmental agreements with Jefferson County and several cities, including for the Navigation Center in Lakewood. A resident urged considering a navigation center closer to Westminster.

westminster/7.title: Butterfly Pavilion expansion support
westminster/7.summary: Butterfly Pavilion proposed a four-phase, roughly $44 million expansion growing from 27,000 to about 38,796 sq ft, and requested $250,000 for pre-development. Council considered an economic development agreement (Councillor's Bill 56) on first reading November 9.

westminster/8.title: Kaiser North redevelopment plan amendment
westminster/8.summary: Council held a public hearing and first reading on a Comprehensive Plan amendment and Preliminary Development Plan amendment for the Kaiser North redevelopment.

westminster/9.title: Childcare market study and provider tax rebate
westminster/9.summary: A market study found a need for licensed childcare spaces for 3,695 children and that affordability is a major barrier. Council considered a Child Care Provider Property Tax Rebate Program.

westminster/10.title: Waste hauler licensing and recycling code changes
westminster/10.summary: Council considered updates to hauler licensing, a Skip the Stuff ordinance and a construction and deconstruction ordinance, building on a CU Boulder study and Colorado's producer responsibility program for recycling.

westminster/11.title: Holly Park and Block B-6 property deals
westminster/11.summary: The Economic Development Authority approved purchase and development agreements for Holly Park with Pumpkin Ridge Holdings and discussed in executive session the possible sale of authority-owned property on Block B-6. Council also considered an economic development agreement with Cooper's Hawk.

sources.body: Westminster Economic Development Authority Post Meeting Study Session

westminster/12.title: Renter concerns and housing conditions
westminster/12.summary: A Westminster renter spoke about rising rents and mold, urging healthy housing standards. Council also considered a residential property maintenance code update.

windsor/0.title: Data center discussions with Weld County
windsor/0.summary: Town and recreation boards discussed a joint work session on a proposed data center in unincorporated Weld County, outside Windsor and Greeley. Concerns included electricity and water use, written comments were being accepted, and a public hearing was expected in a couple of months unless annexation came up first; the Town Board later described the discussion as productive and cordial.

windsor/1.title: 2027 town budget and staffing requests
windsor/1.summary: Staff are preparing a balanced 2027 budget with property tax, oil and gas revenues projected to decline. Requests for a Deputy Police Chief, Deputy Town Attorney and Transportation Planner/Engineer were not recommended, while two Police Lieutenants were requested. Board follow-up included $1.2M for LaBue Park design and $60,000 for a community project.

windsor/2.title: Crossroads/Colorado Blvd roundabout construction phasing
windsor/2.summary: Contractor AB Underground asked to fully close Crossroads Boulevard east of Colorado Boulevard during Phase 2, saying the original plan to keep two-way traffic is too constrained and unsafe. The closure could speed the project and allow the NISP water casing to be installed in one operation; the Town Board reviewed it on Sept. 21.

windsor/3.title: 2027 water, sewer and stormwater rates and NISP costs
windsor/3.summary: The Water and Sewer Board reviewed the Stantec 2027 rate study and forwarded a recommendation of approval of proposed utility rates to the Town Board. A member raised concerns about rising NISP costs, debt coverage and interest rates. The Town's share of the Glade Inlet Canal Diversion project is about 15%, and a $3M federal grant application could save Windsor roughly $450,000.

windsor/4.title: New sign code and conditional use permit changes
windsor/4.summary: The Town replaced its sign regulations (Ordinance 2026-1753), including limits on wall and projecting signs and murals only in the central business district. The Planning Commission also recommended changes to conditional use permit rules, and no public comment was received at the hearings.

windsor/5.title: Hollister Lake Metropolitan District and Windsor Lake Road extension
windsor/5.summary: The Town Board reviewed a service plan for the Hollister Lake Metropolitan District and Ordinance 2026-1754 approving it. Separately, the Board accepted right-of-way dedications and easements for the Windsor Lake Road (Weld County Road 70) extension connecting Hollister Lake Road to SH 257.

windsor/6.title: Housing: Proposition 123, Housing Action Plan and down payment assistance
windsor/6.summary: The Town Board considered a resolution of intent to commit to Proposition 123 affordable housing, a draft Housing Action Plan, and findings on a possible down payment assistance program. Funding for a 2027 program is being held in reserve pending DOLA or NoCo Foundation grants.

windsor/7.title: Proposed police shooting range
windsor/7.summary: Budget follow-up documents discuss a police firearms range, with the Board limiting funding to $37,000 in 2027. Staff plan a first-quarter 2027 work session on location and design; the consultant noted the floodplain location limits building and the range could meet nearly all local firearms training needs.

windsor/8.title: Open space purchase near the wastewater plant and Kodak
windsor/8.summary: The Town bought roughly 70 acres (the Herman property) as open space, and another purchase of land with ditch water and four historic structures was under contract at a total of $6.2M ($3M water, $3.2M land). Funding comes from the Park Improvement Fund, to be reimbursed from the open space sales tax.
windsor/8.where: Near the sewer plant and Kodak open space

windsor/9.title: Rec center tax survey
windsor/9.summary: A Magellan survey found about 48% approval for a 0.8% tax increase for an additional rec center, with 50% at 0.5% if partnered with Severance. Officials said they would wait a year or two before returning to voters.

windsor/10.title: Annexation of the GWIP property and Greeley dispute
windsor/10.summary: The Mayor referred to a public hearing on annexation of the GWIP property, and the Nov. 9 agenda lists litigation including The City of Greeley v. Town of Windsor. The documents give no outcomes.

windsor/11.title: Wireless tower at Timberline Church
windsor/11.summary: The Planning Commission and Town Board considered a 50-foot stealth silo wireless tower and conditional use permit at 29918 County Road 17, owned by Timberline Church.

windsor/12.title: Downtown parking management plan
windsor/12.summary: Staff presented annual parking data under the Downtown Parking Management Plan adopted June 2025. Occupancy stayed under 85% but approached capacity near Main and Walnut during evenings and events, with municipal code changes under consideration.
windsor/12.where: Downtown Windsor, Main and Walnut Streets

windsor/13.title: American Legion funding request for ADA access
windsor/13.summary: American Legion Post 109 asked the Town for financial help with ADA improvements to its building, which sits about five feet above grade.

winter-park/0.title: Town of Winter Park 2027 budget
winter-park/0.summary: Town Council is scheduled to hold a public hearing on Resolution 2355, which would adopt the 2027 budget and make appropriations for the calendar year beginning January 1, 2027. The Transit Advisory Committee is also reviewing the 2027 transit operating budget.

winter-park/1.title: Housing Authority purchases on Wheeler Road
winter-park/1.summary: Council, acting as the Winter Park Housing Authority, is to consider Resolution 37 authorizing a purchase and sale agreement for 34 Wheeler Road. The packet also lists Resolution 38 and a purchase agreement for 56 Wheeler Road. A closed session on buying or selling Town-owned property is also scheduled.

winter-park/2.title: Sojourn development agreement amendment and ADU deed restrictions
winter-park/2.summary: Council is to consider Resolution 2356, a second amendment to the Development Improvement Agreement for the Sojourn development. It would also authorize release of accessory dwelling unit deed restrictions.

winter-park/3.title: Urban Renewal Authority tax increment deals (fire district and Cooper Creek Village)
winter-park/3.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority is to consider Resolution 25, a tax increment revenue agreement with the East Grand County Fire Protection District No. 4. It also plans a closed session to set negotiating strategy on a tax increment sharing agreement with the Cooper Creek Village Metro Districts. A separate Resolution 26 would hire Northland Securities for professional services.
winter-park/3.where: Winter Park Urban Renewal Authority area

winter-park/4.title: Thermal energy network design contract
winter-park/4.summary: Council is to consider Resolution 2354, accepting a proposal from GreyEdge Group for 10 percent design services for a Town thermal energy network and awarding the contract.

winter-park/5.title: Downtown aerial transit system portal and design guidelines
winter-park/5.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority is scheduled to hear a presentation on the Downtown Aerial Transit System (ATS) portal design. The Planning Commission is reviewing a 75% draft of the Winter Park Downtown Design Guidelines.

winter-park/6.title: Planning Commission development reviews
winter-park/6.summary: The Planning Commission has several projects on its agendas: a preliminary plat at 47 Village Drive, a master sign program for Arrow at Winter Park on US Highway 40, and site plans at 40 Ski Idlewild Road and 100 Trademark Drive. It will also review a plat exemption at 215 Dreamcatcher South and discuss the ROAM Neighborhood Park. The Board of Adjustment will hear a setback variance request at 23 Maple Road.
winter-park/6.where: 47 Village Drive; 40 Ski Idlewild Road; 100 Trademark Drive; 78746 US Hwy 40; 23 Maple Road

woodland-park/0.title: Eagle Fire Lodge rezoning and apartment conversion at 777 E. US Highway 24
woodland-park/0.summary: Applicant Rick Dilsavor of Cedarwood Development seeks to rezone the former Eagle Fire Lodge motel from PUD to Multi Dwelling Urban Residential and get a conditional use permit to turn its 25 lodging units into 25 market-rate long-term rentals. The rezone would require 25 additional multifamily water taps under the City's Water Tap Management Plan. Planning Commission heard it October 8; Council took ordinances 1539 and 1540 on initial posting November 5 with a hearing set for November 19.

woodland-park/1.title: Proposed temporary moratorium on residential development applications
woodland-park/1.summary: City Council took Ordinance 1541 on initial posting on November 5. It would temporarily halt submission, acceptance, processing and approval of development, zoning and land use applications for residential development in the city. A public hearing is set for November 19, 2026.

woodland-park/2.title: "Public Safety Facilities" added to the Unified Development Code
woodland-park/2.summary: The city is amending the Unified Development Code to create a new use type, "Public Safety Facilities," to be handled under the Special Use Permit process and defined in the code. The Planning Commission discussed it in September and October, and Council held a hearing on Ordinance 1536 on November 5.

woodland-park/3.title: 2027 budget for the city and the Downtown Development Authority
woodland-park/3.summary: The DDA board reviewed its 2027 budget, with projected 2027 expenditures of about $1.74 million against $1.19 million in revenue. Line items include $50,000 for beautification, $275,000 for TIF agreements (raised for the TAVA agreement) and $200,000 for micro-grants. The DDA resolution recommends approval to City Council, and the city's 2027 budget was on the November 5 Council agenda with public comment allowed.

woodland-park/4.title: DDA micro-grant program for downtown businesses
woodland-park/4.summary: DDA staff reported about $48,337 in micro-grants paid out so far, with $30,000 more up for approval and about $175,000 expected by year-end. Two recipients withdrew. One applicant received two grants this year, but going forward the limit will be one grant per applicant.

woodland-park/5.title: Local historic landmark designation for 116 W. Lake Avenue
woodland-park/5.summary: Steve Plutt and Murray WP Cabin, LLC asked to designate 116 W. Lake Avenue a Local Historic Landmark. The Historical Preservation Committee held a hearing on September 1, with a City Council public hearing scheduled for October 1, 2026.

woodland-park/6.title: Historic preservation projects: Junction House, Templeton Cemetery and Bergstrom Park
woodland-park/6.summary: The Historical Preservation Committee tracks active projects including the Junction House/Roberts House grant, where city staff said Brownfields grants can fund planning services, the Templeton Cemetery restoration plan, a preservation plan, and Bergstrom Park Reimagined. Council said the Bergstrom design is already agreed. The committee is also preparing its 2027 work plan and budget.

woodland-park/7.title: Main Street programs, grants and Oktoberfest
woodland-park/7.summary: The Main Street board is planning Oktoberfest volunteer coordination and hoping for a $2,500 AARP grant. It could be matched with DOLA mini-grant funds; Main Street already received $5,000 from DOLA. Council also scheduled a State of Main Street presentation on November 5.

woodland-park/8.title: Zoning correction at 1420 and 1430 Red Haven Place
woodland-park/8.summary: Mark McNab of MBI Contractors and owner Ventus, LLC requested a zoning correction for property in the Paradise Subdivision. The Planning Commission hearing was set for November 12, with a Council hearing to follow.

wray/0.title: Zoning and subdivision code rewrite (Ordinances 656 and 657)
wray/0.summary: Council held a public hearing in April and passed first readings in May on rewrites of Title 18 (Zoning) and Title 16 (Subdivision). The Planning Commission recommended both as part of the Innovative Housing Strategies grant work. Second readings were on the June 9 agenda.

wray/1.title: Wray Civic Center construction contract
